2.3.1.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, how did the goddess Satī, daughter of Dakṣa, who gave up her body at her father's sacrifice, become the daughter of the mountain, the Mother of the world? ॥1॥
2.3.1.2: And how, having performed extremely fierce austerity, did she obtain Śiva as her husband? Tell me, who am asking, this properly and in detail. ॥2॥
2.3.1.3: Brahmā said: Listen, O tiger among sages, to the excellent story of Śiva, purifying, supreme, divine, auspicious, and removing all sins. ॥3॥
2.3.1.4: When the goddess Dākṣāyaṇī, the supreme Goddess, joyfully sported playfully with Hara on the Himālaya, ॥4॥
2.3.1.5: Menā, the beloved of Himācala, full of all prosperity, thinking, this is my daughter, served her with a mother's affection. ॥5॥
2.3.1.6: When Dākṣāyaṇī, the supreme Goddess, having gone to that sacrifice and been disrespected by her father Dakṣa, became angry and abandoned her own body, ॥6॥
2.3.1.7: then indeed, O sage, that Menakā, the beloved of Himācala, desired to propitiate that goddess dwelling in Śiva's world. ॥7॥
2.3.1.8: Satī, having resolved in her heart that she would be her daughter, after abandoning her body set her mind on becoming the daughter of Himavat. ॥8॥
2.3.1.9: When the time came, that goddess Satī, praised by all the gods, who had abandoned her body, lovingly became again the daughter of Menakā. ॥9॥
2.3.1.10: That goddess, by name Pārvatī, having performed most unbearable austerity on the instruction of Nārada, again obtained Śiva as her husband. ॥10॥
2.3.1.11: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O Creator, O greatly wise one, best of speakers, tell me of Menakā's origin and likewise the story of her marriage. ॥11॥
2.3.1.12: Blessed indeed is the goddess Menakā, in whom Satī was born as daughter; therefore that faithful wife is honoured and blessed by all. ॥12॥
2.3.1.13: Brahmā said: Listen, O sage Nārada, to the origin of Pārvatī's mother, and to her marriage and story, which purify and increase devotion. ॥13॥
2.3.1.14: In the northern direction, O best of sages, there is the great lord of mountains, Himavat, a mountain of great splendour, possessed of prosperity. ॥14॥
2.3.1.15: His twofold form is well known, by the distinction of mobile and immobile. I shall describe briefly his subtle nature. ॥15॥
2.3.1.16: He stands having plunged into the eastern and western oceans, a delightful mine of various gems, like a measuring rod of the earth. ॥16॥
2.3.1.17: Covered with various trees, beautifully adorned with many peaks, always frequented by happy animals such as lions and tigers, ॥17॥
2.3.1.18: a store of snow, very formidable, variegated with many wonders, resorted to by gods, seers, Siddhas and sages, very dear to Śiva, ॥18॥
2.3.1.19: a place of austerity, very pure in nature, purifying for the great-souled, greatly bestowing success in austerity, an auspicious mine of various minerals. ॥19॥
2.3.1.20: He indeed has a divine form, delightful, beautiful in every limb, a portion of Viṣṇu, unchanging, king of the kings of mountains, dear to the good. ॥20॥
2.3.1.21: That mountain, for the continuance of his lineage and for the increase of dharma, wished to marry, desiring the welfare of the ancestors and gods. ॥21॥
2.3.1.22: At that time, O lord of sages, the gods, having fully considered their own interest, approached the divine Pitṛs and lovingly spoke. ॥22॥
2.3.1.23: The gods said: All of you Pitṛs, with pleased minds, listen to our words; if you desire the gods' task, it must be done quickly just so. ॥23॥
2.3.1.24: Your eldest daughter named Menā, of auspicious form — marry her with great affection to the mountain named Hima. ॥24॥
2.3.1.25: Thus there will be great gain in every way for all, for you and for the immortals, and removal of sorrow at every step. ॥25॥
2.3.1.26: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the immortals, the Pitṛs reflected, and remembering the curse on their daughters, said Om (yes) to those words. ॥26॥
2.3.1.27: They gave their own daughter Menā with proper rites to the mountain Hima; there was a great festival at that most auspicious wedding. ॥27॥
2.3.1.28: Those gods headed by Hari, and all the other sages too, came there, remembering in their minds Bhava, Vāmadeva. ॥28॥
2.3.1.29: They had the festival celebrated, giving gifts in many ways; having highly praised the divine Pitṛs, they praised Himācala. ॥29॥
2.3.1.30: All those gods, together with the lords of sages, filled with great joy, went to their respective abodes, remembering Śiva and Śivā. ॥30॥
2.3.1.31: Having received abundant dowry and duly married his beloved, the lord of mountains came to his own home and rejoiced. ॥31॥
2.3.1.32: Brahmā said: O lord of sages, I have lovingly told you of the happy marriage of the mountain Hima with Menā, which gives joy. What more do you wish to hear? ॥32॥
2.3.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The description of the marriage of Himācala, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥1॥
2.3.2.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi (Brahmā), O wise one, now tell me with due care of the origin of Menā. Relate the curse as well, and dispel my doubt. ॥1॥
2.3.2.2: Brahmā said: Listen, Nārada, with great delight, to the origin of Menā, told with discernment. I shall tell it as discussed together with the sages, O best of sons, O greatly wise one. ॥2॥
2.3.2.3: My son named Dakṣa, who was spoken of earlier, O sage — to him were born daughters numbering sixty, the causes of creation. ॥3॥
2.3.2.4: He married them to excellent husbands such as Kaśyapa. All that is known to you; now hear what is relevant, Nārada. ॥4॥
2.3.2.5: Among them, he gave the daughter named Svadhā to the Pitṛs. To her were born three daughters, fortunate, embodiments of dharma. ॥5॥
2.3.2.6: Hear from me their purifying names, O lord of sages, which always remove obstacles and bestow great auspiciousness. ॥6॥
2.3.2.7: The eldest daughter was named Menā, the middle one Dhanyā, and the last Kalāvatī. All these daughters were mind-born of the Pitṛs. ॥7॥
2.3.2.8: They were not born from a womb; by common usage they are regarded as daughters of Svadhā. By uttering their auspicious names a person would obtain all desires. ॥8॥
2.3.2.9: They are worthy of the world's worship, ever mothers of the worlds, givers of supreme joy, supreme yoginīs, treasuries of knowledge, moving through the three worlds. ॥9॥
2.3.2.10: Once, O lord of sages, those three sisters went to Śvetadvīpa, the world of Viṣṇu, for the sake of seeing him. ॥10॥
2.3.2.11: Full of devotion, having bowed to Viṣṇu and praised him, they stayed there by his command. A great assembly had gathered there. ॥11॥
2.3.2.12: At that very time, O sage, the Siddhas Sanaka and the others, sons of Brahmā, went there; having bowed to Hari and praised him, they stayed by his command. ॥12॥
2.3.2.13: Seeing the sages Sanaka and the others, all those present quickly rose; and the sages bowed to those stationed there, the gods and others revered by the worlds. ॥13॥
2.3.2.14: But those three sisters did not rise there, O sage, deluded by the Māyā of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self, helpless under fate. ॥14॥
2.3.2.15: Śiva's Māyā is mightiest, the deluder of all worlds. The whole universe depends on it; it is proclaimed as Śiva's will. ॥15॥
2.3.2.16: That same is called prārabdha (destiny already set in motion); it has many names. Everything happens by Śiva's will alone; there should be no deliberation on this. ॥16॥
2.3.2.17: Having come under its sway, they did not even bow to them; amazed, merely gazing, they just remained seated there. ॥17॥
2.3.2.18: Seeing their conduct thus, the lords of sages Sanaka and the others, though men of wisdom, became exceedingly and unbearably angry. ॥18॥
2.3.2.19: There, deluded by Śiva's will, the lord of yogins Sanatkumāra, full of anger, spoke to them, giving a punishing curse. ॥19॥
2.3.2.20: Sanatkumāra said: You three sisters are foolish, devoid of true understanding, ignorant of the essence of the Vedas, even though you are surely daughters of the Pitṛs. ॥20॥
2.3.2.21: Proud ones, you did not rise to greet us, nor even offer salutation. Deluded by this human-like disposition, may you be removed far from heaven. ॥21॥
2.3.2.22: May all three of you, deluded by ignorance, be born as human women. By the power of your own deed, receive such a fruit. ॥22॥
2.3.2.23: Brahmā said: Hearing this, those three virtuous women, greatly alarmed, fell at his feet and spoke with bowed heads. ॥23॥
2.3.2.24: The daughters of the Pitṛs said: O best of sages, ocean of compassion, be gracious now. We, deluded, did not make obeisance to you with true feeling. ॥24॥
2.3.2.25: We have received its fruit, O brahmin; the fault is not yours, great sage. Show us favour in this, so that we may regain our heavenly state. ॥25॥
2.3.2.26: Brahmā said: Hearing their words, dear son, the sage, now pleased at heart and prompted by Śiva's Māyā, then declared the release from the curse. ॥26॥
2.3.2.27: Sanatkumāra said: O three daughters of the Pitṛs, listen with glad hearts to my words, which destroy grief and always bring you happiness. ॥27॥
2.3.2.28: Let the eldest become the beloved wife of the mountain Himālaya, a portion of Viṣṇu; her daughter will be Pārvatī. ॥28॥
2.3.2.29: The second, Dhanyā, will be the yoginī wife of Janaka; her daughter, Mahālakṣmī, will be known by the name Sītā. ॥29॥
2.3.2.30: The youngest, Kalāvatī, will be the wife of the vaiśya Vṛṣabhāna; her daughter will be Rādhā, at the end of the Dvāpara age. ॥30॥
2.3.2.31: The yoginī Menakā, together with her husband and by the boon of Pārvatī, will go in that very body to Kailāsa, the supreme abode. ॥31॥
2.3.2.32: And Dhanyā, with Sītā, and Sīradhvaja of Janaka's line, liberated while living, a great yogin, will go to Vaikuṇṭha. ॥32॥
2.3.2.33: Kalāvatī, wife of Vṛṣabhāna, liberated while living, will joyfully go with her daughter to Goloka; there is no doubt. ॥33॥
2.3.2.34: Without adversity, whose greatness will arise, and where? When the sorrow of the virtuous has passed, rare happiness may arise. ॥34॥
2.3.2.35: You are all daughters of the Pitṛs, delighting in heaven; and by the sight of Viṣṇu your karma has been exhausted. ॥35॥
2.3.2.36: Having said this, the lord of sages, his anger gone, spoke again, remembering in his mind Śiva, the giver of knowledge, of enjoyment and liberation. ॥36॥
2.3.2.37: Hear lovingly further words of mine, ever bringing happiness. You are blessed, dear to Śiva, to be honoured and worshipped constantly. ॥37॥
2.3.2.38: Menā's daughter, the goddess Pārvatī, Mother of the universe, having performed extremely arduous austerity, will become the beloved of Śambhu. ॥38॥
2.3.2.39: Dhanyā's daughter, known as Sītā, will be Rāma's wife; adopting worldly conduct, she will sport with Rāma. ॥39॥
2.3.2.40: Kalāvatī's daughter Rādhā, herself a dweller of Goloka, bound by secret love, will be Kṛṣṇa's wife. ॥40॥
2.3.2.41: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, the venerable sage Sanatkumāra, praised by them together with his brothers, vanished right there. ॥41॥
2.3.2.42: Those three sisters, dear one, the mind-born daughters of the Pitṛs, freed of sin and having obtained happiness, quickly went to their own abode. ॥42॥
2.3.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The description of the former history, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥2॥
2.3.3.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi (Brahmā), wise one of great intellect, best of speakers, tell me: what happened after that? Tell me the deeds of Śiva, the true guru of Viṣṇu. ॥1॥
2.3.3.2: This wondrous and auspicious story of Menā's earlier life has been told, and the marriage too has been fully heard. Now tell the supreme story that follows. ॥2॥
2.3.3.3: Having married Menā, what did that mountain do after that? How was Pārvatī, the Mother of the world, born of her? ॥3॥
2.3.3.4: Having performed a most unbearable austerity, how did she obtain Hara as husband? Relate all this, the glory of Śaṅkara, in detail. ॥4॥
2.3.3.5: Brahmā said: O sage, listen with great delight to the auspicious, excellent glory of Śaṅkara, by hearing which even a slayer of a brāhmaṇa is purified and obtains all his desires. ॥5॥
2.3.3.6: When the mountain, having celebrated the marriage with Menā, went home, then a great festival arose in the three worlds, O Nārada. ॥6॥
2.3.3.7: Himācala too, greatly delighted, held a supreme festival. With a good mind he honoured the brāhmaṇas, his kinsfolk, and others. ॥7॥
2.3.3.8: All the twice-born, satisfied, gave him excellent words of blessing and went to their own abodes; so too did the kinsfolk and the others. ॥8॥
2.3.3.9: Himācala too, much delighted, sported with Menā in his pleasant home, and elsewhere in fine places, even in Nandana and other groves. ॥9॥
2.3.3.10: At that time, O sage, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, and the great-souled sages, came to the mountain's presence. ॥10॥
2.3.3.11: Seeing those gods arrive, the mountain bowed joyfully; the great one honoured them with devotion, praising his own good fortune. ॥11॥
2.3.3.12: With joined palms and bowed head he praised them with deep devotion. A great thrill arose on the mountain's body, and tears of love fell. ॥12॥
2.3.3.13: Then, having bowed, the Snow Mountain, delighted and serene of mind, humbly prostrate, spoke, O sage, to the gods headed by Viṣṇu. ॥13॥
2.3.3.14: Himavān said: Today my birth is fruitful, fruitful my very great austerity; today my knowledge is fruitful, today my rites are fruitful. ॥14॥
2.3.3.15: Today I have become blessed; blessed is my whole land; blessed my lineage and my wife; everything is blessed, without doubt. ॥15॥
2.3.3.16: since you have all come together at once. Regarding me as your own servant, kindly command me as is fitting. ॥16॥
2.3.3.17: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the mountain, the gods headed by Hari were then pleased, considering their own purpose accomplished, and spoke. ॥17॥
2.3.3.18: The gods said: O Himācala, of great wisdom, hear our beneficial words. We shall gladly tell you why we have all come. ॥18॥
2.3.3.19: O mountain, Umā, the Mother of the world, who formerly was born as Dakṣa's daughter, became Rudra's wife and sported on earth for a very long time. ॥19॥
2.3.3.20: Receiving disrespect from her father, Satī, remembering her own vow, abandoned that body and then Ambikā went to her own abode. ॥20॥
2.3.3.21: That story is known in the world, and to you also, O Snow Mountain. If it comes about thus, that she is born to you, there would indeed be great gain for the host of gods, ॥21॥
2.3.3.22: for all, and for you as well; all those gods would be under your sway. ॥22॥
2.3.3.23: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Hari and the others, the lord of mountains, pleased at heart, said with respect, so be it. ॥23॥
2.3.3.24: Then, having instructed him with great respect in the procedure for it, they themselves went for refuge to Umā, Śaṅkara's consort. ॥24॥
2.3.3.25: Staying in a pleasant place, the gods remembered the Mother of the world in their minds; bowing there many times, they praised her with faith. ॥25॥
2.3.3.26: The gods said: O Goddess Umā, Mother of the worlds, dweller in Śivaloka, beloved of Sadāśiva, O Durgā, O Maheśvarī, we bow to you. ॥26॥
2.3.3.27: With devotion we bow to you, the glorious Power, purifying, peaceful, nourishment itself, supremely purifying, whose form is the Great (mahat) and the Unmanifest. ॥27॥
2.3.3.28: We bow to you, Śivā, maker of auspiciousness, pure, gross and subtle, the supreme refuge, well pleased by inner knowledge and true knowledge. ॥28॥
2.3.3.29: You are faith, you are steadfastness, you are prosperity (śrī); you alone pervade all things. You are the radiance residing in the sun, illuminating your own manifest world. ॥29॥
2.3.3.30: She who abides in the structure of the cosmic egg and in the living beings of the world, she who nourishes the world from Brahmā down to a blade of grass — to her we bow. ॥30॥
2.3.3.31: You are Gāyatrī, the Mother of the Vedas; you are Sāvitrī and Sarasvatī; you are the livelihood (vārtā) of all the worlds; you are the threefold Veda, embodying dharma. ॥31॥
2.3.3.32: You are sleep in all beings, you alone are hunger and satisfaction; thirst, loveliness, lustre, contentment — ever the giver of all joy. ॥32॥
2.3.3.33: You are Lakṣmī for the doers of merit, you are ever Jyeṣṭhā (misfortune) for the sinful; you are peace for all the worlds, you are the nurse who sustains life. ॥33॥
2.3.3.34: You are the essential nature of the five elements, and the one who makes their essence; you are the policy of those who uphold policy, embodying resolute effort. ॥34॥
2.3.3.35: You are the chant of the Sāmaveda, the binding knot and oblation of the Yajus formulas, likewise the metre (mātrā) of the Ṛgveda, and the supreme goal of the Atharvaveda. ॥35॥
2.3.3.36: She who is the power of the entire host of gods, consisting of tamas, visible only through the qualities of the Creator, and through the expansion of rajas having the single form of existence — she, heard of by us as the bringer of welfare, is praised here. ॥36॥
2.3.3.37: We bow indeed to her who is the boat that carries one across the sorrows of embodied existence in the terrible ocean of saṃsāra, who is without the sacred thread, who is skilled in the sport of upholding eight-limbed yoga, and who delights in dwelling on the Vindhya mountain. ॥37॥
2.3.3.38: She who, by sustaining them, ever spreads comforts in the nose, eyes, mouth, arms, chest and mind of a creature, who, the gracious one, goes by the name of Sleep for the beings of the world — may she be gracious to us for the preservation of the world's continuance. ॥38॥
2.3.3.39: Brahmā said: Having thus praised Maheśānī, Umā the Mother of the world, Satī, all of them, their minds full of love, stood waiting, eager for her vision. ॥39॥
2.3.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The praise by the gods, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥3॥
2.3.4.1: Brahmā said: Thus praised by the gods, the Goddess Durgā, destroyer of the distress of hardships, the Mother of the world, appeared before the gods. ॥1॥
2.3.4.2: She was seated in a divine chariot made of jewels, supremely wondrous, fitted with networks of little bells, excellent, with a soft cushioned seat. ॥2॥
2.3.4.3: She shone with lovely limbs whose radiance surpassed that of ten million suns; she stood in the midst of a mass of her own splendour, of excellent form and of unequalled beauty. ॥3॥
2.3.4.4: She is incomparable, the Great Māyā, the consort who sports with Sadāśiva, possessed of the three guṇas yet beyond the guṇas, eternal, dwelling in Śivaloka. ॥4॥
2.3.4.5: She is the mother of the three gods, Caṇḍī, Śivā, destroyer of all distress, mother of all, the Great Sleep, the deliverer of all her own people. ॥5॥
2.3.4.6: But owing to the power of that mass of radiance, Śivā was scarcely seen by the gods; so those gods, longing for a sight of her, praised her again. ॥6॥
2.3.4.7: Then all the hosts of gods, headed by Viṣṇu, desirous of seeing her, having obtained her grace there, beheld that Mother of the world. ॥7॥
2.3.4.8: A flood of bliss arose for all the dwellers of heaven; again and again they bowed to her and praised her in particular. ॥8॥
2.3.4.9: The gods said: O Śivā, O Śarvāṇī, O auspicious one, O Mother of the world, O Maheśvarī, we gods bow to you in every way, you who destroy all distress. ॥9॥
2.3.4.10: O Mistress of the gods, the Vedas and the śāstras do not know you completely; your greatness and the meditation on you lie beyond speech and mind, O Śivā. ॥10॥
2.3.4.11: Even the Śruti, ever filled with awe, speaks of you only by excluding what you are not; what then to say of others? ॥11॥
2.3.4.12: Many devotees know you, having obtained your grace through devotion; for devotees who have taken refuge in you there is no fear or the like anywhere. ॥12॥
2.3.4.13: O Ambikā, being well pleased, hear the petition of those who are ever your servants; O Devī, O Mahādevī, we set it forth humbly. ॥13॥
2.3.4.14: Formerly, having become Dakṣa's daughter, you were born as the beloved of Hara, and you removed the great affliction of Brahmā and of others. ॥14॥
2.3.4.15: Having met with disrespect from your father, you gave up your body because of a vow and went to your own world; and Hara too suffered sorrow. ॥15॥
2.3.4.16: That task of the gods has not been fully accomplished, O Maheśvarī; distressed, we sages and gods have come to you for refuge. ॥16॥
2.3.4.17: O Maheśānī, fulfil the desire of the immortals, so that the word of Sanatkumāra may bear fruit, O Śivā. ॥17॥
2.3.4.18: Descending to the earth, O Devī, become Rudra's wife again; perform your sport as befits, so that the immortals may attain happiness. ॥18॥
2.3.4.19: May Rudra too, dwelling on Mount Kailāsa, be happy, O Devī; may all be happy; may sorrow perish completely. ॥19॥
2.3.4.20: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, all the immortals headed by Viṣṇu, overflowing with love, fell silent and stood with their bodies bowed in devotion. ॥20॥
2.3.4.21: Śivā too became very pleased on hearing the praise of the immortals; then, considering its purpose and remembering her own lord Śiva, ॥21॥
2.3.4.22: the Goddess Umā, compassionate and loving to her devotees, then smiled and, addressing those gods headed by Viṣṇu, spoke. ॥22॥
2.3.4.23: Umā said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods and sages, be free of distress. All of you, listen to my words: I am pleased, there is no doubt. ॥23॥
2.3.4.24: My deeds everywhere bring happiness to the three worlds; all that — the delusion of Dakṣa and the rest — was done by me in this way. ॥24॥
2.3.4.25: I shall take a full incarnation on earth, there is no doubt. There are many reasons for this too; I shall tell them with great regard. ॥25॥
2.3.4.26: Formerly, O gods, Himācala and Menā, with very great devotion, served me, then in the body of Satī, like a father and mother. ॥26॥
2.3.4.27: Now too they serve me constantly with deep devotion — Menā especially, wishing me to be her daughter; there is no doubt of this. ॥27॥
2.3.4.28: Let Rudra go there, and you too take incarnation in Himavat's house; therefore I too shall descend, and there will be an end of sorrow. ॥28॥
2.3.4.29: All of you, go to your own abodes and enjoy happiness for long. Descending and becoming Menā's daughter, I shall bestow great happiness. ॥29॥
2.3.4.30: I shall become Hara's wife — this is my own closely guarded intention. For Śiva's sport is wondrous, deluding even the wise. ॥30॥
2.3.4.31: O gods, from the time when I, Dakṣa's daughter, having gone to his sacrifice and seen the disrespect shown by my father to my lord, abandoned my own body, ॥31॥
2.3.4.32: from then on that lord Rudra, called Kālāgni, quickly became sky-clad, wholly absorbed in thinking of me. ॥32॥
2.3.4.33: Reflecting thus: Seeing my anger at the sacrifice, Satī, who had gone there to her father's, gave up her body out of love, being a knower of dharma, ॥33॥
2.3.4.34: Maheśvara abandoned his fitting abode and assumed an unworldly guise; he could not bear separation from Satī, who was of my form. ॥34॥
2.3.4.35: On my account he became greatly grieved, wearing a wretched guise; from then on he renounced the highest pleasure born of desire. ॥35॥
2.3.4.36: Hear something more, O Viṣṇu, O Vidhi, O sages and gods: the sport of the great lord Maheśa, which protects the worlds. ॥36॥
2.3.4.37: Making a garland of my bones with great love, distraught by separation, he found peace nowhere; though awakened, he remained alone. ॥37॥
2.3.4.38: That lord wept aloud here and there as though helpless; wandering everywhere at all times, he did not discern the proper from the improper. ॥38॥
2.3.4.39: Thus the lord Hara performed his sport, showing the state of lovers; he spoke words like a lover, as if distraught by separation. ॥39॥
2.3.4.40: In reality the Supreme Lord is unchanging, never dejected, unconquered; Śiva the master is perfectly complete, the ruler of Māyā, the lord of all. ॥40॥
2.3.4.41: Otherwise, what purpose would he have with delusion, or with desire? That Lord is not quickly tainted by Māyā through any modification of mind whatsoever. ॥41॥
2.3.4.42: Rudra, the all-pervading one, greatly desires to take my hand in marriage. Therefore, O gods, I shall take an incarnation on earth, in the house of Menā and Himācala. ॥42॥
2.3.4.43: And therefore I shall descend, for the sake of pleasing Rudra, in Menā, the wife of the Himālaya mountain, adopting the worldly course of birth. ॥43॥
2.3.4.44: Becoming a devotee dear to Rudra and performing extremely hard austerity, I shall accomplish the task of the gods — truly, truly, there is no doubt. ॥44॥
2.3.4.45: Go, all of you, to your own homes and worship Bhava constantly. By his grace all sorrow perishes; there is no doubt. ॥45॥
2.3.4.46: By the grace of the compassionate one there will always be auspiciousness. And because I am his wife, I shall be worthy of salutation and worship in the three worlds. ॥46॥
2.3.4.47: Brahmā said: Having said this, that Mother of the world, Śivā, vanished then while the gods looked on, O dear one, and quickly reached her own world. ॥47॥
2.3.4.48: All the gods headed by Viṣṇu, and the sages, filled with joy, bowed in that direction and went to their respective abodes. ॥48॥
2.3.4.49: Thus the noble story of Durgā has been described to you, O lord of sages; it always gives happiness to men and bestows both enjoyment and liberation. ॥49॥
2.3.4.50: Whoever, with a concentrated mind, constantly listens to this or makes others listen, or reads it or has it read, would obtain all his desires. ॥50॥
2.3.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The consoling of the gods, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥4॥
2.3.5.1: Nārada said: When the goddess Durgā had vanished and the hosts of immortals had gone to their own homes, what happened after that? ॥1॥
2.3.5.2: How did Menā and the lord of mountains perform supreme austerity? And how was a daughter born to him in Menā? Tell me that, dear father. ॥2॥
2.3.5.3: Brahmā said: O best of brahmins, best of sons, listen to that great story. Having bowed to Śaṅkara with devotion, I shall narrate it, which increases devotion. ॥3॥
2.3.5.4: Dear son, when the host of gods headed by Hari had departed after giving instruction, the lord of mountains and Menakā too performed supreme austerity. ॥4॥
2.3.5.5: Meditating day and night on Śivā and Śambhu, the couple worshipped them properly and constantly with a mind filled with devotion. ॥5॥
2.3.5.6: She, the mountain's beloved, with great joy worshipped the goddess together with Śiva, and always gave gifts to brahmins for the sake of pleasing her. ॥6॥
2.3.5.7: Beginning in the month of Caitra, for twenty-seven years, desiring offspring, she devotedly worshipped Śivā every day. ॥7॥
2.3.5.8: Having fasted on the eighth lunar day, she made offerings on the ninth with sweet balls, rice-flour cakes for oblation, milk-rice, fragrances and flowers. ॥8॥
2.3.5.9: At the Gaṅgā in Oṣadhiprastha she made an earthen image of Umā and worshipped it with offerings of various articles. ॥9॥
2.3.5.10: Sometimes she went without food, sometimes she kept vows, sometimes she lived on air, sometimes she subsisted on water. ॥10॥
2.3.5.11: With her mind fixed on Śivā, Menakā, radiant with pure splendour, lovingly passed twenty-seven years. ॥11॥
2.3.5.12: At the end of twenty-seven years, Umā, the mother of the world, who pervades the world, beloved of Śaṅkara, became exceedingly pleased. ॥12॥
2.3.5.13: To show favour to Menā, that supreme goddess, delighted by her deep devotion, appeared before her. ॥13॥
2.3.5.14: Endowed with divine limbs, standing in the midst of a halo of light, she, having become visible, smilingly spoke to Menā. ॥14॥
2.3.5.15: The Goddess said: Ask for a boon, O great virtuous lady, whatever is in your mind. I am well pleased with your austerity, O beloved of the mountain. ॥15॥
2.3.5.16: Whatever you have prayed for, Menā, through austerity, vows and meditation, all that you desire, whenever it may be, I shall give you. ॥16॥
2.3.5.17: Then Menakā, seeing the goddess Kālikā visibly present, bowed down and spoke these words. ॥17॥
2.3.5.18: Menā said: O goddess, now I have seen your form directly. I wish to praise you; be pleased, O Kālikā. ॥18॥
2.3.5.19: Brahmā said: Then Kālikā, who enchants all, thus addressed by Menā, with a delighted heart embraced Menakā with both arms. ॥19॥
2.3.5.20: Then Menakā, having attained great knowledge, devotedly praised with pleasing words the auspicious Kālikā who had become visible. ॥20॥
2.3.5.21: Menā said: I bow to the great Māyā, the sustainer of the world, Caṇḍikā, upholder of the worlds, the great goddess who grants all desires and aims. ॥21॥
2.3.5.22: I always bow to her who causes eternal bliss, Māyā, Yoganidrā, mother of the world, the perfected one, garlanded with auspicious essence. ॥22॥
2.3.5.23: I bow to the grandmother, ever blissful, destroyer of devotees' grief, the adornment of women and the form of intelligence in living beings. ॥23॥
2.3.5.24: You are the cause of cutting the bonds of ascetics; how can your power be sung by women like me? You are the destructive power of the Atharvaveda; ever fulfil my cherished desire. ॥24॥
2.3.5.25: The group of elements is joined together by their respective subtle elements (tanmātras), eternal and non-eternal, devoid of states, transcendent. You are ever their power, of eternal form; in time you become a woman, endowed with yoga and all-capable. ॥25॥
2.3.5.26: You alone are the womb and supporter of the worlds; you alone are the eternal Prakṛti beyond; by whom even the form of Brahman is brought under control—you, the eternal one, be gracious to me today, O mother. ॥26॥
2.3.5.27: You are the fierce power residing in fire; you are the burning power of the sun's rays; you are the gladdening abundant moonlight—you, Caṇḍī, I praise and bow to. ॥27॥
2.3.5.28: You are the true beloved of women, and you are the eternal goal of celibates; you are the desire of all the worlds, and you are Māyā, as the Māyā of Hari. ॥28॥
2.3.5.29: The goddess who, assuming desired forms, is the maker consisting of creation, preservation and destruction, the cause of the bodies of Brahmā, Acyuta and Sthāṇu—you, be gracious today; again, salutation to you. ॥29॥
2.3.5.30: Brahmā said: Then, thus praised, Durgā Kālikā again said to the lady Menakā: Choose what you desire. ॥30॥
2.3.5.31: Umā said: You are as dear to me as my life, O delight of Himācala. Whatever you wish I shall surely give; there is nothing I cannot give. ॥31॥
2.3.5.32: Hearing these nectar-like words of Maheśānī, Menakā, the mountain's beloved, fully satisfied, spoke. ॥32॥
2.3.5.33: Menā said: O Śivā, victory, victory to you! O wise one, O Maheśvarī, O Bhavāmbikā, if I am worthy of a boon from you, I choose again an excellent boon. ॥33॥
2.3.5.34: First, O mother of the world, may I have a hundred sons, long-lived, valiant, endowed with prosperity and success. ॥34॥
2.3.5.35: Afterwards likewise one daughter, rich in beauty and virtues, bringing joy to both families, worshipped in the three worlds. ॥35॥
2.3.5.36: O Śivā, become my daughter for the sake of the gods' purpose; and become Rudra's wife, and so perform your divine play, O Bhavāmbikā. ॥36॥
2.3.5.37: Brahmā said: Hearing what Menakā said, the goddess, gracious-minded, spoke with a smile, fulfilling her wish. ॥37॥
2.3.5.38: The Goddess said: May a hundred valiant sons be born to you; among them one mighty chief will be born first. ॥38॥
2.3.5.39: Pleased by your devotion, I shall be born as your daughter; served by all the gods, I shall accomplish the gods' task. ॥39॥
2.3.5.40: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, Kālikā, sustainer of the world, the supreme goddess Śivā, vanished right there while Menakā looked on. ॥40॥
2.3.5.41: Menakā too, having obtained from Maheśānī the boon she desired, attained boundless joy, O dear one, and the hardship of her austerity also vanished. ॥41॥
2.3.5.42: Bowing toward that direction, the virtuous lady, her mind greatly delighted, uttering the cry of victory, entered her own abode. ॥42॥
2.3.5.43: Then she told her husband of that excellent boon, in fine words repeated again, as though it were confirmed by its own signs. ॥43॥
2.3.5.44: Hearing that speech of Menā, the lord of mountains became delighted, and with affection he praised his beloved, who was devoted to devotion to Śivā. ॥44॥
2.3.5.45: Then, in the course of time, when their union had taken place, O sage, Menā conceived, and the embryo grew day by day. ॥45॥
2.3.5.46: She bore an excellent, wondrous son named Maināka, fit to be enjoyed by the nāga maidens, who formed a true friendship with the ocean. ॥46॥
2.3.5.47: He, who even when Vṛtra's foe Indra was enraged and cutting off the mountains' wings, O divine sage, remained winged and of excellent form, knowing the pain of those wounded by the thunderbolt. ॥47॥
2.3.5.48: He was the foremost of a hundred sons, of great strength and valour, the one alone established as lord of mountains among the mountains born of Himavat himself. ॥48॥
2.3.5.49: A wondrous great festival took place there in Himācala's city; the couple's joy overflowed and their hardships came to an end. ॥49॥
2.3.5.50: He gave gifts to the twice-born and bestowed wealth on others as well; the love of the two for the pair of feet of Śivā and Śiva grew greater. ॥50॥
2.3.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The description of Menā's obtaining a boon, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥5॥
2.3.6.1: Brahmā said: Then that couple, with devotion and reverence, called to mind Bhavāmbikā there, so that she might be born to them for the sake of accomplishing the gods' task. ॥1॥
2.3.6.2: Then that Caṇḍikā, who long ago had abandoned her body through yoga at the sacrifice of her father, wished by her own will to be born again from the mountain's wife. ॥2॥
2.3.6.3: To make her own word true, the gracious Maheśvarī, granter of all desires, then entered the mind of the mountain with her full portion. ॥3॥
2.3.6.4: Then he shone exceedingly, full of joy, with an unprecedented splendour, unassailable like fire, a mass of radiance, great-souled. ॥4॥
2.3.6.5: Then the mountain, by virtue of his concentrated meditation, at the proper time placed that complete portion of Śivā into his own most auspicious beloved. ॥5॥
2.3.6.6: Through the grace of the Goddess, the mine of compassion, who abode in his mind, the mountain's wife conceived an embryo that brought joy to the mountain. ॥6॥
2.3.6.7: Menā, the mountain's beloved, shone all the more brightly for being the refuge of her in whom all the worlds dwell, ever encircled by a halo of radiance. ॥7॥
2.3.6.8: And Menā bore the signs of pregnancy-craving, which gave rise to joy for her husband, the auspicious and longed-for cause of the gods' bliss. ॥8॥
2.3.6.9: Owing to the languor of her body she wore only some of her ornaments, and her face was pale as lodhra; she was like a night at the waning of the moon, of faint light, its few stars hard to make out. ॥9॥
2.3.6.10: O sage, the lord of mountains, smelling in private her face fragrant with the scent of earth, found no satiety; that became an excess of love. ॥10॥
2.3.6.11: For which things does Menā long? Out of shyness she tells me nothing she desires — so the mountain asked her friends again and again. ॥11॥
2.3.6.12: Whatever the mountain-queen, gripped by craving, asked for, she soon saw it brought; indeed nothing he desired was unattainable for him, even in heaven. ॥12॥
2.3.6.13: Her limbs growing fuller, having passed beyond the discomfort of craving, Menā shone like a young creeper abounding in freshly formed leaves. ॥13॥
2.3.6.14: The mountain regarded his pregnant queen as like the earth bearing treasure within, like the śamī tree with fire hidden inside. ॥14॥
2.3.6.15: The wise one performed the rites prescribed by scripture, befitting his love for his beloved, the loftiness of his mind, and his self-earned wealth. ॥15॥
2.3.6.16: In due time he, delighted, saw Menā about to give birth, in the birth-chamber attended by physicians, like the sky laden with clouds. ॥16॥
2.3.6.17: Seeing his beloved of auspicious limbs, who then bore in her womb the Mother of the World and was full of great radiance, the lord of mountains rejoiced greatly. ॥17॥
2.3.6.18: At that time, O sage, the gods, Viṣṇu and the others, and the sages assembled and praised Śivā, who was in the womb. ॥18॥
2.3.6.19: The gods said: O Durgā, victory, victory to you! O wise one, Mother of the World, Maheśvarī, O you of true vows, devoted to truth, threefold truth, embodiment of truth, ॥19॥
2.3.6.20: O you who abide in truth, who are well pleased by truth, source of truth, arisen from truth, whose mouth is truth and whose eye is truth — we have come to you for refuge. ॥20॥
2.3.6.21: O beloved of Śiva, Maheśānī, destroyer of the gods' sorrow, you are the Mother of the three worlds, Śarvāṇī, all-pervading, loving to your devotees. ॥21॥
2.3.6.22: Manifest yourself, O Ruler of the three worlds, and accomplish the gods' task; for by your grace, O Maheśvarī, all of us have a protector. ॥22॥
2.3.6.23: Through you all beings become happy and attain the highest happiness; without you nothing at all shines, even in the three worlds. ॥23॥
2.3.6.24: Brahmā said: Having thus offered abundant praise to Maheśānī abiding in the womb, the gods, glad at heart, then went each to his own abode. ॥24॥
2.3.6.25: When the ninth month had passed and the tenth month was complete, Kālikā, the Mother of the World, abiding in the womb, began to move toward birth. ॥25॥
2.3.6.26: Then it was a most auspicious time: the constellations, planets and stars were calm, the sky became clear, and there was brightness in all directions. ॥26॥
2.3.6.27: The earth, with its forests, villages and oceans, was full of auspiciousness; in lakes, rivers and wells lotuses bloomed. ॥27॥
2.3.6.28: Various breezes pleasant to the touch blew, O lord of sages; all the good rejoiced, and sorrow quickly befell the wicked. ॥28॥
2.3.6.29: The immortals came into the sky and beat kettledrums; a shower of flowers fell there, and the best of the Gandharvas sang. ॥29॥
2.3.6.30: The Vidyādhara women and likewise the Apsarases danced in the sky; then there was a great festival of the gods and others in the heavens. ॥30॥
2.3.6.31: At that moment the Goddess, the primal Śakti, Śivā, who had been Satī, appeared before Menā in her own form. ॥31॥
2.3.6.32: In the spring season, in the month of Madhu, on the ninth day, under the Mṛga asterism, at midnight she was born, like Gaṅgā from the orb of the moon. ॥32॥
2.3.6.33: At that time Śivā, in that very form of hers, came forth from Menakā's womb and was born, like Lakṣmī from the ocean. ॥33॥
2.3.6.34: Then, when she was born, Bhava became pleased; a favourable wind blew, deep, fragrant and auspicious. ॥34॥
2.3.6.35: There was a shower of flowers, preceded by a shower of rain; the sacred fires blazed up serenely, and the clouds then thundered. ॥35॥
2.3.6.36: As she was being born, every kind of wealth came about there in Himavat's city, and all sorrow perished. ॥36॥
2.3.6.37: At that moment all the gods, Viṣṇu and the rest, came there joyfully and with love, and beheld the Mother of the World. ॥37॥
2.3.6.38: They praised her — Śivā, the Mother, Kālikā, beloved of Śiva, of divine form, the Great Māyā, dweller in Śiva's world. ॥38॥
2.3.6.39: The gods said: O Mother of the World, Great Goddess, bestower of all attainments, you indeed accomplish the gods' task; therefore we ever bow to you. ॥39॥
2.3.6.40: In every way bring about the welfare of the gods, O you who love your devotees. You have fulfilled Menā's heart's desire; fulfil Hara's too. ॥40॥
2.3.6.41: Brahmā said: Having thus praised Śivā and bowed deeply to her, the gods led by Viṣṇu went, delighted, each to his own abode, extolling her supreme state. ॥41॥
2.3.6.42: O Nārada, seeing the goddess thus born, dark in complexion, with the lustre of a blue lotus petal, Menakā was filled with joy. ॥42॥
2.3.6.43: Then, beholding her divine form, the beloved of the mountain gained understanding; recognising her as the supreme Goddess, she praised her, exceedingly delighted. ॥43॥
2.3.6.44: Menā said: O Mother of the world, O Great Goddess, you have shown great compassion, in that you have appeared before me in radiance, O Ambikā. ॥44॥
2.3.6.45: You are the first of all powers, the mother of the three worlds, O Śivā; ever beloved of Śiva, O Goddess, supreme, praised by all the gods. ॥45॥
2.3.6.46: Be gracious, O Great Goddess; abide in my meditation. Instead of this form, take before my eyes a form like that of a daughter. ॥46॥
2.3.6.47: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Menā, the mountain's wife, the goddess Śivā, well pleased, replied to the mountain's beloved. ॥47॥
2.3.6.48: The Goddess said: O Menā, formerly you, devoted, served me well; greatly pleased by your devotion, I came near you to grant a boon. ॥48॥
2.3.6.49: Hearing my words bidding you ask a boon, you chose this boon: Become my daughter, O Great Goddess, and accomplish the welfare of the gods. ॥49॥
2.3.6.50: Having thus granted you the boon, I went with respect to my own abode; when the time came, I became your daughter, O beloved of the mountain. ॥50॥
2.3.6.51: I have assumed this divine form today so that you may remember me; otherwise, through the mortal condition, you would have ignorance regarding me. ॥51॥
2.3.6.52: You two, thinking of me again and again, either as a daughter or as divine, and bearing affection for me, will attain my supreme state. ॥52॥
2.3.6.53: I shall accomplish the gods' task, performing a wondrous play on earth; I shall become Śambhu's wife and shall deliver the virtuous. ॥53॥
2.3.6.54: Brahmā said: Having said this, Śivā Ambikā fell silent, and by her own māyā, while the mother looked on with love, she at once took on the body of an infant daughter. ॥54॥
2.3.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The description of the birth of Pārvatī, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥6॥
2.3.7.1: Brahmā said: Then, in front of Menā, she of great radiance, having become her daughter, began to cry there, adopting the way of the world. ॥1॥
2.3.7.2: Around the lying-in bed, by her excellent, widely spreading brilliance, the midnight lamps at once became dimmed in their light, O sage. ॥2॥
2.3.7.3: Hearing that charming crying, all the women of the household rejoiced and came there in haste, full of affection. ॥3॥
2.3.7.4: Then an attendant of the inner apartments quickly announced to the mountain-king the birth of Pārvatī, which was joyful, auspicious, and would accomplish the gods' purpose. ॥4॥
2.3.7.5: For that attendant of the inner apartments who swiftly brought the good news of a daughter's birth, there was nothing that king of mountains would not give, not even his white royal parasol. ॥5॥
2.3.7.6: The mountain went there joyfully with his family priest and excellent brāhmaṇas, and saw that daughter shining with beautiful radiance. ॥6॥
2.3.7.7: Seeing such a girl, dark like the petal of a blue lotus, radiant and most lovely, the lord of mountains rejoiced greatly. ॥7॥
2.3.7.8: And all rejoiced there—the citizens, men and women. Then there was a great festival, and musical instruments sounded abundantly. ॥8॥
2.3.7.9: There was auspicious singing; courtesans danced. And having performed the birth rite (jātakarma), he gave gifts to the twice-born. ॥9॥
2.3.7.10: Then, coming to the gate, Himācala, glad at heart, held a very great festival and gave wealth to mendicants. ॥10॥
2.3.7.11: Then, at an auspicious moment, Himavān together with the sages gave his daughter joy-bestowing names, beginning with Kālī. ॥11॥
2.3.7.12: Then he gladly and respectfully gave many gifts to the brāhmaṇas, and had various festivities held, accompanied by song. ॥12॥
2.3.7.13: Having thus held abundant festivities, and gazing at Kālī again and again, the mountain, together with his wife, found delight, though he already had many sons. ॥13॥
2.3.7.14: There, in the house of the king of mountains, the goddess Śivā grew, like the Gaṅgā in the rainy season, or like moonlight in autumn. ॥14॥
2.3.7.15: Thus that goddess Kālikā, lovely-limbed and beautiful to behold, took on day by day a growing charm, like a digit of the moon's disc. ॥15॥
2.3.7.16: Her kinsfolk called her, who was dear to her relatives and endowed with the virtue of good conduct, by the name Pārvatī, befitting her family. ॥16॥
2.3.7.17: Kālikā, forbidden by her mother from practising austerity with the words u mā (O, don't), the fair-faced one later came to be known in the world as Umā, O sage. ॥17॥
2.3.7.18: The gaze of the mountain, though he had sons, found no satiety in that child named Pārvatī, endowed with every good fortune. ॥18॥
2.3.7.19: For though spring has endless flowers, the swarm of bees has a special attachment to the mango tree, the fragrant sahakāra, O lord of sages. ॥19॥
2.3.7.20: By her the mountain Himālaya became both purified and adorned, just as a wise man is by refined speech. ॥20॥
2.3.7.21: As the lamp of a house shines by its flame of great radiance, as the celestial path by the three-pathed Gaṅgā, so the mountain shone by the mountain-born girl. ॥21॥
2.3.7.22: In childhood, amid her friends, she played again and again with balls, dolls, and sand-altars on the banks of the Gaṅgā. ॥22॥
2.3.7.23: Then, when the time for instruction came, O sage, the goddess Śivā studied the sciences with great delight and a controlled mind under a good teacher. ॥23॥
2.3.7.24: The knowledge of her former birth came to her, as in autumn the row of swans comes to the heavenly river, and as at night their own luminosity comes to the great herbs. ॥24॥
2.3.7.25: Thus some part of Śivā's play has been well described. I shall tell another episode of her play; listen with love, O sage. ॥25॥
2.3.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The description of the childhood play of Pārvatī, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥7॥
2.3.8.1: Brahmā said: Once you, a knower of Śiva and the best among those who know Śiva's divine play, went with affection to the house of Himācala, impelled by Śiva. ॥1॥
2.3.8.2: O sage Nārada, on seeing you, the lord of mountains bowed and worshipped you; and calling his own daughter, he made her fall at your feet. ॥2॥
2.3.8.3: O lord of sages, bowing to you again, the snowy mountain, with joined palms and head deeply bowed, considering himself fortunate, spoke to you. ॥3॥
2.3.8.4: Himavān said: O sage Nārada, wise one, best of Brahmā's sons, O lord, you are all-knowing, compassionate, and devoted to helping others. ॥4॥
2.3.8.5: Tell me my daughter's horoscope, with the good and bad qualities arising from it. Whose beloved will my fortunate daughter become? ॥5॥
2.3.8.6: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Himādri, the lord of mountains, O best of sages, you examined Kālikā's hand and especially all her limbs. ॥6॥
2.3.8.7: Dear son, you, Nārada—playful, skilled in speech, wise, knowing the whole matter, and pleased at heart—spoke to the mountain. ॥7॥
2.3.8.8: Nārada said: O Menā, O king of mountains, this daughter of yours has grown like the first digit of the moon, endowed with all auspicious marks. ॥8॥
2.3.8.9: She will give the utmost happiness to her husband and increase the fame of her parents; a great chaste woman, she will always bring great joy to all women. ॥9॥
2.3.8.10: O mountain, all the marks on your daughter's hand are auspicious; but there is one unusual line—hear its result truly. ॥10॥
2.3.8.11: Her husband, it seems, will be like this: a yogin, naked, without qualities, free of desire, without mother or father, without pride, and of inauspicious attire. ॥11॥
2.3.8.12: Brahmā said: Hearing your words and taking them to be true, the couple, Menā and Himācala, both became distressed. ॥12॥
2.3.8.13: But Śivā, the Mother of the world, hearing such words of yours and recognising Śiva from those marks, rejoiced greatly in her heart, O sage. ॥13॥
2.3.8.14: Reflecting that Nārada's words cannot be false, Śivā then conceived in her heart a deep love for Śiva's pair of feet. ॥14॥
2.3.8.15: Then the mountain, grieved at heart, said to you, Nārada: O sage, what remedy should I adopt? Great sorrow has arisen. ॥15॥
2.3.8.16: Hearing that, O sage, you, the maker of great wonders and skilled in speech, spoke, delighting Himācala with auspicious words. ॥16॥
2.3.8.17: Nārada said: O mountain, listen with affection to my words: they are true, not false. The lines of the hand are Brahmā's writing; they certainly never prove false. ॥17॥
2.3.8.18: O mountain, her husband will be such—there is no doubt. Hear with pleasure the remedy for it, by following which you will attain happiness. ॥18॥
2.3.8.19: Such a bridegroom is Śambhu, the Lord who assumes forms in play; in him all the ill marks are equal to good qualities. ॥19॥
2.3.8.20: In a mighty lord a defect does not cause sorrow; it causes great sorrow only in one who is not a lord. The sun, fire and the Gaṅgā should be known as examples of this. ॥20॥
2.3.8.21: Therefore, with discernment, give your daughter Śivā to Śiva. Śiva is the lord of all, worthy of service, changeless, the imperishable Lord. ॥21॥
2.3.8.22: That Śiva, quick to be gracious, will undoubtedly accept her; he is attained especially through austerity, if Śivā performs austerity. ॥22॥
2.3.8.23: For that Śiva, the lord of all, is fully capable in every way; he can shatter even the thunderbolt, has Brahmā under his control, and bestows happiness. ॥23॥
2.3.8.24: Brahmā said: Having said this, dear son, you—playful sage and knower of Brahman—again spoke to the king of mountains, delighting him with auspicious words. ॥24॥
2.3.8.25: She will become the beloved of Śambhu, ever agreeable to Hara, a great chaste woman of good vows, increasing her parents' happiness. ॥25॥
2.3.8.26: Through austerity she will bring Śambhu's mind under her control, and he too will marry no other woman except her. ॥26॥
2.3.8.27: Love like that of these two has never been anyone's, nor will be, nor exists now. ॥27॥
2.3.8.28: Through these two, O best of mountains, the tasks of the gods that must be done, and whatever ones had died, will be revived again and again. ॥28॥
2.3.8.29: Through this daughter of yours, O mountain, Hara will become Ardhanārīśvara; and joyfully the two will be united once again. ॥29॥
2.3.8.30: This daughter of yours, having pleased Maheśa, the lord of all, by the power of austerity, will take half of Hara's body. ॥30॥
2.3.8.31: Having pleased Hara by austerity, this daughter of yours will become golden-fair, gleaming like gold, fairest like lightning. ॥31॥
2.3.8.32: This maiden will win fame by the name Gaurī, and will be worshipped by all the hosts of gods, as well as by Hari, Brahmā and others. ॥32॥
2.3.8.33: O best of mountains, you should not give her to anyone else here. And this secret of the gods must never be revealed. ॥33॥
2.3.8.34: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of yours, O divine sage Nārada, Himavān, skilled in speech, spoke to you, O sage. ॥34॥
2.3.8.35: Himavān said: O wise sage Nārada, I make a certain request; listen to it with affection, and so bring me joy. ॥35॥
2.3.8.36: It is heard that Mahādeva has renounced all attachment, is self-controlled, and constantly practises austerity, beyond the reach even of the gods. ॥36॥
2.3.8.37: O divine sage, how will he, established on the path of meditation, divert his mind fixed on the supreme Brahman? About this I have great doubt. ॥37॥
2.3.8.38: He contemplates his own form called Sadāśiva—the imperishable supreme Brahman, like the flame of a lamp, changeless, beyond the unborn Brahmā, ॥38॥
2.3.8.39: which is both without and with qualities, undifferentiated and free of activity. Hence he sees it everywhere and does not look at anything external. ॥39॥
2.3.8.40: So it is constantly heard about him, O sage, from the mouths of the Kinnaras who come here with great affection. Is that surely a false report? ॥40॥
2.3.8.41: In particular, it is heard that Hara himself, in person and by name, made a vow in the past. Hear it as I relate it. ॥41॥
2.3.8.42: O Dākṣāyaṇī, O beloved Satī, apart from you I will not choose another; I will not take anyone as a wife. I tell you this truly. ॥42॥
2.3.8.43: Thus a vow was made by him with Satī long ago. Now that she is dead, how will he himself take another? ॥43॥
2.3.8.44: Brahmā said: Having said this, the mountain fell silent in front of you. Hearing that, O divine sage, you then spoke in accordance with the real truth. ॥44॥
2.3.8.45: Nārada said: you need not worry, O king of mountains, O wise one. This daughter of yours, Kālī, was indeed born formerly as Dakṣa's daughter. ॥45॥
2.3.8.46: Her name was Satī, ever bestowing all auspiciousness. That Satī, being Dakṣa's daughter, became the beloved of Rudra. ॥46॥
2.3.8.47: Then, at her father's sacrifice, having met with disrespect, and seeing that of Śaṅkara too, Satī, on seeing it, became enraged and gave up her body. ॥47॥
2.3.8.48: That very one, Ambikā Śivā, has been born again in your house. This Pārvatī will become Hara's wife; there is no doubt. ॥48॥
2.3.8.49: All this, O sage, you told the mountain in detail — Pārvatī's former form and her story, which increases delight. ॥49॥
2.3.8.50: Having heard from the sage's mouth that entire former history of Kālī, the mountain, together with his sons and wife, was then freed of doubt. ॥50॥
2.3.8.51: Then Kālī, having heard the account from Nārada's mouth, lowered her face in shyness, her face broadened with a smile. ॥51॥
2.3.8.52: Having heard her story, the mountain touched her with his hand, and kissing her on the head again and again, seated her beside his own seat. ॥52॥
2.3.8.53: Then, O sage, seeing her again seated there, you spoke, delighting the king of mountains and Menakā together with their sons. ॥53॥
2.3.8.54: But what need would she have of a throne, O king of mountains? Hence her seat will always be on Śambhu's lap. ॥54॥
2.3.8.55: Having obtained the seat on Hara's lap, your daughter will remain there forever, where no one's sight or mind can reach. ॥55॥
2.3.8.56: Brahmā said: Having spoken these noble words to the lord of mountains, O Nārada, you went joyfully to heaven at that very moment. The lord of mountains too, his heart filled with lovely delight, went to his own home, rich in every prosperity. ॥56॥
2.3.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The description of the dialogue of Nārada and Himālaya, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥8॥
2.3.9.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi, dear father, best of Śiva's devotees, O wise one, out of compassion you have narrated a wondrous story, and my delight has grown all the more. ॥1॥
2.3.9.2: O Vidhi, after I, of divine vision, had gone to my own abode, what happened then, dear father? Kindly tell me that now. ॥2॥
2.3.9.3: Brahmā said: O sage, after you had gone to heaven and some time had passed, Menā one day approached the mountain Himālaya and bowed to him. ॥3॥
2.3.9.4: Standing there humbly, the mountain's beloved, that virtuous lady whose daughter was dear to her as life, spoke to her own lord, the king of mountains. ॥4॥
2.3.9.5: Menā said: Owing to a woman's nature, I have not properly understood the sage's words. Arrange the marriage of our daughter with a handsome bridegroom. ॥5॥
2.3.9.6: Then that wedding would in every way bring unprecedented happiness; and the bridegroom of Girijā should have good marks and be born of a good family. ॥6॥
2.3.9.7: My daughter is dear to me as life; act so that the beloved girl may be happy and delighted on obtaining a worthy husband. Salutation to you. ॥7॥
2.3.9.8: Brahmā said: Having said this, Menā, her face wet with tears, then fell at her husband's feet. Raising her up, the mountain, foremost of the wise, spoke fittingly. ॥8॥
2.3.9.9: Himavān said: Listen, O goddess Menakā; I speak what is true, in reality. Give up your confusion: the sage's words are never false. ॥9॥
2.3.9.10: If you have affection for your daughter, instruct her respectfully that she should perform austerity for Śaṅkara with devotion and a steady mind. ॥10॥
2.3.9.11: If Śiva, pleased, takes Kālī's hand, O Menakā, everything will be auspicious and the inauspiciousness spoken of by Nārada will vanish. ॥11॥
2.3.9.12: All inauspicious things are ever auspicious in Śiva. Therefore quickly instruct our daughter in austerity for attaining Śiva. ॥12॥
2.3.9.13: Brahmā said: Hearing the mountain's words, Menā became very pleased and went near her daughter to instruct her to take up austerity. ॥13॥
2.3.9.14: But seeing her daughter's very delicate body, Menakā was pained, and both her eyes quickly filled with tears. ॥14॥
2.3.9.15: The mountain's beloved could not instruct her daughter in that; Pārvatī quickly understood her mother's intention. ॥15॥
2.3.9.16: Then that goddess Kālikā, the all-knowing supreme ruler, at once spoke to her mother, comforting her again and again. ॥16॥
2.3.9.17: Pārvatī said: Mother, O very wise one, listen: last night, at the hour of Brahmā (before dawn), I saw a dream. I shall tell it; be kind and hear it. ॥17॥
2.3.9.18: A brahmin ascetic, compassionate, lovingly instructed me, mother, to perform intense austerity for Śiva. ॥18॥
2.3.9.19: Brahmā said: Hearing that, Menakā quickly called her husband there and told him in full the dream her daughter had seen. ॥19॥
2.3.9.20: Then, hearing the daughter's dream from Menakā, the lord of mountains, greatly pleased, spoke, addressing his beloved with these words. ॥20॥
2.3.9.21: Himavān said: O beloved, at the end of the latter part of the night I too saw a dream. Listen to it with great delight; I shall tell it with due respect. ॥21॥
2.3.9.22: A supreme ascetic, bearing the bodily marks of the bridegroom described by Nārada, came gladly to the outskirts of our city to perform austerity. ॥22॥
2.3.9.23: Very pleased, I went there taking my daughter. I recognised him as Śambhu, the lord, the bridegroom spoken of by Nārada. ॥23॥
2.3.9.24: Having instructed my daughter to serve that ascetic, I requested him to accept her service; but at that time he did not agree to it. ॥24॥
2.3.9.25: A very great debate arose, in keeping with Sāṅkhya and Vedānta. Then, by his permission, my daughter remained there. ॥25॥
2.3.9.26: Holding that desire in her heart, she served him with devotion. This is the dream I saw, which I have told you, O fair-faced one. ॥26॥
2.3.9.27: Therefore, O Menā, beloved, its outcome should be watched for some time. This alone is fitting here; know this from me for certain. ॥27॥
2.3.9.28: Brahmā said: Having said this, O lord of sages, the king of mountains and Menakā remained, with pure minds, watching for its outcome. ॥28॥
2.3.9.29: When a few days had thus passed, the supreme lord, refuge of the good, the creator, greatly agitated by separation from Satī, was wandering everywhere. ॥29॥
2.3.9.30: The lord came there gladly, accompanied by a few attendants (gaṇas), to perform austerity, his mind distraught by separation from his beloved Satī. ॥30॥
2.3.9.31: He performed his own austerity there; Pārvatī, devoted to serving him, together with her two friends, was constantly engaged then to please him. ॥31॥
2.3.9.32: Though pierced with arrows by Smara (Kāma), sent by the gods to infatuate him, Lord Śambhu did not undergo any change. ॥32॥
2.3.9.33: Burning Smara right there with his fiery eye, and recalling my words, he, angry with me, then vanished. ॥33॥
2.3.9.34: Then after some time, having destroyed Girijā's pride and being propitiated by her intense austerity, Maheśvara became pleased. ॥34॥
2.3.9.35: Following worldly custom, Rudra, propitiated by Viṣṇu, married Kālī; from that came great auspiciousness. ॥35॥
2.3.9.36: Thus, dear son, I have told you in brief this supreme, divine story of the all-pervading Śaṅkara. What more do you wish to hear? ॥36॥
2.3.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The description of Śiva's deeds in brief, preceded by the description of a dream, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥9॥
2.3.10.1: Nārada said: O disciple of Viṣṇu, O most fortunate one, O Vidhi (Brahmā), best of Śiva's devotees, O lord, you should kindly tell me in detail this sport (līlā) of Śiva. ॥1॥
2.3.10.2: What deeds did Śambhu, afflicted by separation from Satī, perform? And when did he go to the excellent plateau of Himavat to perform austerities? ॥2॥
2.3.10.3: How did the dispute between Śivā and Śiva arise, and how did the destruction of Kāma take place? How did Pārvatī, having performed austerities, attain Śiva, Śambhu? ॥3॥
2.3.10.4: O Brahman, you should tell me all that, and also any other supreme, auspicious, good deeds of Śiva that bring great bliss. ॥4॥
2.3.10.5: Sūta said: Hearing this question of Nārada, Vidhi, the foremost of the lords of the worlds, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, spoke with great delight. ॥5॥
2.3.10.6: Brahmā said: O divine sage, foremost among Śiva's devotees, listen with reverence to his glory, which is purifying, auspicious, excellent, and increases devotion. ॥6॥
2.3.10.7: Having come to his own mountain, Śambhu, distressed by separation from his beloved, remembered in his heart his dear goddess Satī, dearer to him than life. ॥7॥
2.3.10.8: Addressing the Gaṇas and grieving for her, he described with great love her qualities that increased affection, displaying the way of worldly people. ॥8॥
2.3.10.9: Then, abandoning the good path of householder life, he became sky-clad (naked); and he, skilled in divine sport, again wandered through all the worlds. ॥9॥
2.3.10.10: Grieved by separation from Satī, he found no sight of her anywhere; and Śaṅkara, who brings welfare to his devotees, came back to the mountain. ॥10॥
2.3.10.11: Concentrating his mind with effort, he entered meditative absorption (samādhi), the destroyer of sorrow, and beheld his own imperishable true form. ॥11॥
2.3.10.12: Thus Sthāṇu remained for a very long time, the three guṇas dissolved—changeless, the supreme Brahman, lord of Māyā, the Lord himself. ॥12॥
2.3.10.13: Then, when countless years had passed, he gave up samādhi; what happened then quickly, that episode I shall tell you. ॥13॥
2.3.10.14: A drop born of exertion (sweat) fell from the Lord's forehead onto the earth; there it quickly became a child. ॥14॥
2.3.10.15: O sage, he was four-armed, reddish in hue, of charming form, with unearthly radiance, splendid, brilliant, and unbearable to others. ॥15॥
2.3.10.16: That child cried there before the supreme Lord, who was engaged in worldly conduct, just like an ordinary son. ॥16॥
2.3.10.17: Then the Earth, reflecting with her good intellect and fearing Śaṅkara, assumed the form of a fair woman and appeared right there. ॥17॥
2.3.10.18: Quickly lifting that excellent child, she placed him on her lap and lovingly suckled him with her breast milk, the milk that welled up in her. ॥18॥
2.3.10.19: She kissed his face with affection and, smiling, played with the child—herself truly a mother, devoted to the welfare of the supreme Lord. ॥19॥
2.3.10.20: Seeing that deed, Śambhu Hara—playful, the skilled agent of creation, the indweller—knowing her to be the Earth, laughed and then spoke. ॥20॥
2.3.10.21: Blessed are you, O Earth; lovingly nurture this excellent son of mine, born upon you from the sweat of me, the greatly radiant one. ॥21॥
2.3.10.22: O Earth, though this child, who will do what is dear to you, is born of my sweat, he shall be famed by your name and ever be free from the three afflictions. ॥22॥
2.3.10.23: This child will indeed be virtuous and a giver of land to you; he will also be a giver of joy to me. Take him as you wish. ॥23॥
2.3.10.24: Brahmā said: Having said this, Rudra—his mind somewhat freed from the grief of separation, following worldly custom, changeless, dear to the good—fell silent. ॥24॥
2.3.10.25: And the Earth, having received Śiva's command, quickly went with the son to her own abode and attained supreme happiness. ॥25॥
2.3.10.26: That child, obtaining the name Bhauma and quickly becoming a youth, served Lord Śaṅkara for a long time in Kāśī. ॥26॥
2.3.10.27: By the grace of Viśveśvara, the Earth-born one attained the status of a planet and quickly went to an excellent divine world beyond the world of Śukra. ॥27॥
2.3.10.28: Thus has been told Śambhu's deed connected with separation from Satī. Now, O sage, listen with reverence to Śambhu's practice of austerity. ॥28॥
2.3.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The description of the birth of Bhauma and of Śiva's sport, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥10॥
2.3.11.1: Brahmā said: When that daughter of the mountain, the Śakti worshipped by the worlds, Satī reborn, was growing up and had become eight years old in Himālaya's house, ॥1॥
2.3.11.2: Giriśa, who was distressed by separation from Satī, learned of her birth and, holding that wondrous one within his heart, rejoiced exceedingly, O Nārada. ॥2॥
2.3.11.3: Meanwhile Śambhu, adopting worldly conduct, wished to perform penance in order to concentrate his mind properly. ॥3॥
2.3.11.4: Taking with him some excellent and tranquil gaṇas, Nandin and others, he went to Gaṅgāvatāra, the excellent plateau of Himavat. ॥4॥
2.3.11.5: where, long ago, the Gaṅgā, flowing from Brahmā's city, fell down — the supreme purifier, for the destruction of all masses of sin, O sage. ॥5॥
2.3.11.6: Staying there, the self-controlled Hara began his penance; untiring, he meditated one-pointedly on his own Self, ॥6॥
2.3.11.7: which is consciousness, arising from knowledge, eternal, of the form of light, free from affliction, pervading the universe, consciousness and bliss, devoid of duality, without support. ॥7॥
2.3.11.8: While Hara was engrossed in meditation, some Pramathas too became intent on meditation, as did other gaṇas such as Nandin and Bhṛṅgin. ॥8॥
2.3.11.9: Then some gaṇas served Śambhu, the supreme Self; remaining silent, they made no sound at all; and some became door-keepers. ॥9॥
2.3.11.10: Meanwhile the snowy mountain Himavat, having heard of Śaṅkara's arrival at Oṣadhiprastha, went there respectfully. ॥10॥
2.3.11.11: The lord of mountains, with his attendants, bowed to the lord Rudra, worshipped him, and, greatly pleased, praised him with joined palms. ॥11॥
2.3.11.12: Himavān said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Kapardin, Śaṅkara, O Lord, by you alone, the lord of the world, the three worlds are protected. ॥12॥
2.3.11.13: Obeisance to you, O Lord of the gods of gods, who bear the form of a yogin; obeisance to you who are without attributes, who have attributes, who sport in the world. ॥13॥
2.3.11.14: O Śambhu, obeisance to you, dweller on Kailāsa, who roam through all worlds, the supreme lord, who take forms in play, the trident-bearer. ॥14॥
2.3.11.15: Obeisance to you, the receptacle of perfect qualities, free from modification; to the desireless, the one beyond striving, the steadfast, the supreme Self. ॥15॥
2.3.11.16: Obeisance to you whose enjoyment is not external, O lover of people; O master of the three guṇas, Lord of Māyā, obeisance to Brahman, the supreme Self. ॥16॥
2.3.11.17: To you who are served by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others, who have the form of Viṣṇu and Brahmā, the sole bestower on Viṣṇu and Brahmā — O lover of devotees, obeisance be to you. ॥17॥
2.3.11.18: O you who delight in penance, O abode of penance, obeisance to you, giver of the fruit of good penance, fond of penance, tranquil, having the form of Brahman. ॥18॥
2.3.11.19: Obeisance be to you who engage in worldly dealings and follow the customs of the world, who have attributes, the supreme lord, the supreme Self. ॥19॥
2.3.11.20: Your sport, O Maheśāna, is unknowable and gives happiness to the good. You are by nature subject to your devotees; controlled by devotees, you perform actions. ॥20॥
2.3.11.21: Through the rising of my good fortune you have come here, O Lord. You have made me one who has a protector; you are rightly described as kind to the lowly. ॥21॥
2.3.11.22: Today my birth is fruitful, my life is fruitful; today everything of mine is fruitful, since you have come here. ॥22॥
2.3.11.23: Knowing me to be your steadfast servant, give me your command, O Maheśvara, and I shall serve you with great love, with mind fixed on nothing else. ॥23॥
2.3.11.24: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the lord of mountains, Maheśvara opened his eyes slightly and saw the mountain with his attendants. ॥24॥
2.3.11.25: Seeing that king of mountains thus with his attendants, the bull-bannered lord of the world, abiding in meditative yoga, spoke as if smiling. ॥25॥
2.3.11.26: Maheśvara said: I have come in secret to perform penance on your ridge. Arrange it so that no one comes near. ॥26॥
2.3.11.27: You are great-souled, an abode of penance, and the constant refuge of sages, of gods, of rākṣasas and of other great beings; ॥27॥
2.3.11.28: always the dwelling of the twice-born and others, ever purified by the Gaṅgā, benefactor of all, the overlord and master of mountains. ॥28॥
2.3.11.29: Relying on you, well pleased and self-controlled, O king of mountains, I shall practise penance here at the place of the Gaṅgā's descent. ॥29॥
2.3.11.30: O protector of mountains, best of mountains, make every effort now by which my penance here may be free of obstacles. ॥30॥
2.3.11.31: This alone is the highest service to me, O best of mountains. Go to your home with true affection and accomplish this with care. ॥31॥
2.3.11.32: Brahmā said: Having said this, the lord of the worlds, the creator, fell silent. Then the king of mountains affectionately said this to Śambhu. ॥32॥
2.3.11.33: Himavān said: You have been worshipped by me, O lord of the world, O supreme Lord, with a welcome. What shall I request of you, who today dwell in my realm? ॥33॥
2.3.11.34: Indeed, even by great penance you are not attained by the gods who strive with effort, O Maheśāna; yet that very you has come here of your own accord. ॥34॥
2.3.11.35: There is no one superior to me, no one more meritorious than me, since your Honour has come onto my ridge for penance. ॥35॥
2.3.11.36: I consider myself greater than the lord of the gods, O supreme Lord, for by coming here with your attendants you have made me a recipient of your grace. ॥36॥
2.3.11.37: Perform your supreme penance free of obstacles, O lord of the gods, as you are independent. I shall render service accordingly; I am ever your servant, O Lord. ॥37॥
2.3.11.38: Brahmā said: Having said this, that king of mountains quickly returned to his own house and respectfully related the whole account to his beloved. ॥38॥
2.3.11.39: Summoning all his attendants who were being led there and his own followers, O Nārada, the lord of mountains spoke to them truthfully. ॥39॥
2.3.11.40: Himavān said: From today onward, by my command, let no one go to Gaṅgāvatāraṇa, my plateau. This I declare truly. ॥40॥
2.3.11.41: If any person goes there, I shall punish that great scoundrel severely; this I have declared truly. ॥41॥
2.3.11.42: O sage, having quickly restrained all his attendants in this way, the mountain Himavat made a careful effort; listen to it, I shall tell you. ॥42॥
2.3.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The description of the meeting of Śiva and the mountain, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥11॥
2.3.12.1: Brahmā said: Then the lord of the mountains, delighted, took a collection of fine flowers and fruits and, accompanied by his daughter, went into the presence of Hara. ॥1॥
2.3.12.2: Having gone and bowed to the Lord of the three worlds, who was intent on meditation, he offered to him wholeheartedly his wondrous daughter Kālī. ॥2॥
2.3.12.3: Placing all the fruits, flowers and other things before him, and putting his daughter in front, the king of mountains said this to Śambhu. ॥3॥
2.3.12.4: Himavān said: O Lord, my daughter, eager to serve you, the moon-crested one, has been brought here out of her desire to worship you. ॥4॥
2.3.12.5: Let her, together with her two friends, serve you, Śaṅkara, constantly. Permit her, O Lord, if you have favour towards me. ॥5॥
2.3.12.6: Brahmā said: Then Śaṅkara looked at her, who had just reached early youth, whose lustre was like the petals of a blooming blue lotus, and whose face resembled the full moon; ॥6॥
2.3.12.7: who shone with an auspicious attire, the abode of every grace; whose neck was like a conch, whose eyes were large, and who was radiant with a pair of lovely ears; ॥7॥
2.3.12.8: charming with her two arms, long and slender to their ends like lotus-stalks; bearing breasts like lotus buds, full, plump and firm; ॥8॥
2.3.12.9: bearing them, slender-waisted, beautified by the three folds at her middle, and resplendent with two feet like land-lotuses; ॥9॥
2.3.12.10: able, merely by being seen, to dislodge even the minds of sages bound fast in the cage of meditation; the crest-jewel of all womankind. ॥10॥
2.3.12.11: Having seen her thus, dear one, captivating even to meditators, one who in her very form augments the power of tantras and mantras, assuming forms at will, ॥11॥
2.3.12.12: the great yogin quickly closed his eyes and meditated on his own supreme form, the highest reality, beyond the three guṇas, imperishable. ॥12॥
2.3.12.13: Seeing then the all-pervading Lord of all, engaged in austerity with eyes closed, with matted locks, adorned with the digit of the moon, knowable through Vedānta, seated on the supreme seat, ॥13॥
2.3.12.14: Himācala bowed again with his head; he, though of undaunted spirit, fell into doubt. Then the lord of mountains, foremost among those skilled in speech, addressed words to the sole friend of the world. ॥14॥
2.3.12.15: Himavān said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, mine of compassion, Śaṅkara, open your eyes, O all-pervading one, and look at me who have come to you for refuge. ॥15॥
2.3.12.16: O Śiva, Śarva, Maheśāna, O Lord who brings joy to the world, I bow to you, Mahādeva, who removes all calamities. ॥16॥
2.3.12.17: O Lord of gods, the Vedas and the scriptures do not know you completely. Your greatness ever transcends the path of speech and mind. ॥17॥
2.3.12.18: Through the exclusion of what is not you, all of Śruti ever describes you hesitantly, with awe; what then is to be said of others? ॥18॥
2.3.12.19: Many devotees know you, having obtained your grace through devotion. For devotees who have taken refuge in you there is no delusion or the like anywhere. ॥19॥
2.3.12.20: Now, out of kindness to me, hear the request of me, your own servant. By your command, O God, dear one, I relate it out of my humility. ॥20॥
2.3.12.21: I am fortunate, Mahādeva, by your grace, Śaṅkara. Regarding me as your own servant, O Lord, show kindness; salutations to you. ॥21॥
2.3.12.22: And every day I shall come to see you, O Lord, together with this daughter; O master, please grant your permission. ॥22॥
2.3.12.23: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of his, Maheśvara opened his eyes; abandoning meditation and reflecting, the God of gods spoke these words. ॥23॥
2.3.12.24: Maheśvara said: You may come daily to see me, O mountain, but leave the maiden at home; otherwise there is no seeing me. ॥24॥
2.3.12.25: Brahmā said: Hearing such words of Maheśa, the mountain, father of Śivā, bowing his neck, replied thus to Giriśa. ॥25॥
2.3.12.26: Himavān said: Why should I not come together with her? Let that be told. Is she unfit for service? I do not know the reason for this. ॥26॥
2.3.12.27: Brahmā said: Then Śambhu, whose banner bears the bull, laughing, spoke to the mountain, showing especially the worldly conduct appropriate for unworthy yogins. ॥27॥
2.3.12.28: Śambhu said: This maiden, with fine hips, slender, moon-faced and beautiful, must not be brought near me; I forbid it again and again. ॥28॥
2.3.12.29: Woman is held by the learned, masters of the Veda, to be a form of Māyā; a young woman especially is an obstacle to ascetics. ॥29॥
2.3.12.30: I am an ascetic and a yogin, ever untouched by Māyā. What need have I of a young woman, O bearer of the earth? ॥30॥
2.3.12.31: You should not speak thus again, O refuge of the best ascetics, since you are skilled in Vedic dharma, foremost among the wise, and learned. ॥31॥
2.3.12.32: O mountain, from association with her sensual desire quickly arises; detachment perishes, and thereby true austerity falls away. ॥32॥
2.3.12.33: Therefore, O mountain, an ascetic should not keep company with women, for that company is the root of great sensual attachment and the destroyer of knowledge and detachment. ॥33॥
2.3.12.34: Brahmā said: Having said this and much more to that lord of mountains, Maheśvara, the great yogin, the Lord, foremost among great yogins, fell silent. ॥34॥
2.3.12.35: Hearing these words of Śambhu—untroubled, free of desire and harsh—Kālī's father was startled, O celestial sage, and, somewhat perturbed by them, remained silent. ॥35॥
2.3.12.36: Hearing the words spoken by the ascetic, and perceiving the lord of mountains thus startled, Bhavānī then bowed to Śiva and spoke clear words. ॥36॥
2.3.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The description of the dialogue of Śiva and Himācala, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥12॥
2.3.13.1: Bhavānī said: O yogin, hear from me, O all-pervading lord, O one skilled among the wise, the answer to what you, an ascetic, said to the king of mountains. ॥1॥
2.3.13.2: O Śambhu, you perform extensive austerity because you are endowed with the power of austerity. This resolve to practise austerity has arisen in you, the great-souled one, through that power. ॥2॥
2.3.13.3: That power should be known as Prakṛti, the source of all actions whatsoever. By her everything is created, preserved and destroyed. ॥3॥
2.3.13.4: Who are you, and who is subtle Prakṛti? O Lord, let that be reflected upon. And without Prakṛti, how could Maheśvara exist in the form of the liṅga? ॥4॥
2.3.13.5: It is through Prakṛti that you are ever worthy of worship, of homage and of meditation by living beings. Having reflected on this in your heart, let all that be stated. ॥5॥
2.3.13.6: Brahmā said: Having heard those words of Pārvatī, Maheśa, intent on bestowing great favour, laughed heartily and, with a pleased mind, spoke these words. ॥6॥
2.3.13.7: Maheśvara said: By supreme austerity alone I destroy Prakṛti. In truth I, Śambhu, remain free from Prakṛti. ॥7॥
2.3.13.8: Therefore the virtuous should never embrace Prakṛti; they should remain free from change and removed from worldly conduct. ॥8॥
2.3.13.9: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Śambhu, dear one, in the manner of worldly usage, Kālī smiled inwardly and spoke sweet words. ॥9॥
2.3.13.10: Kālī said: O yogin, Śaṅkara, Lord, the words you have spoken — how are they not Prakṛti? How then are you beyond her? ॥10॥
2.3.13.11: Having considered this, you should state it truly, exactly as it is. All this is continuously bound by Prakṛti. ॥11॥
2.3.13.12: Therefore you should not speak, nor do anything at all. Know with your mind that all speaking and all making belong to Prakṛti. ॥12॥
2.3.13.13: What you hear, what you eat, what you see, what you do — all that is the effect of Prakṛti. False talk is meaningless. ॥13॥
2.3.13.14: If you are beyond Prakṛti, then why, O Śambhu, O Lord, are you now performing austerity on this mountain Himavat? ॥14॥
2.3.13.15: You have been swallowed by Prakṛti; you do not know your own self, O Hara. If you know your own self, O Lord, why do you perform austerity? ॥15॥
