2.3.13.16: O yogin, what is the use of my arguing with you in words? Where there is direct perception, the wise do not regard inference as a means of proof. ॥16॥
2.3.13.17: As long as things fall within the range of the senses of embodied beings, so long should the wise regard all of it, with their intellect, as belonging to Prakṛti. ॥17॥
2.3.13.18: What is the use of saying much, O lord of yogins? Hear my supreme word: I am she Prakṛti and you are Puruṣa. This is true, true; there is no doubt. ॥18॥
2.3.13.19: It is by my grace that you are regarded as possessing qualities and form. Without me you are inactive and cannot do anything at all. ॥19॥
2.3.13.20: You are always dependent on another, though self-controlled, performing various actions. How then are you changeless, and how are you not tainted by me? ॥20॥
2.3.13.21: If your statement that you are beyond Prakṛti is true, then, O Śaṅkara, you need not fear being near me. ॥21॥
2.3.13.22: Brahmā said: Having heard her words, expressed according to the Sāṃkhya doctrine, Śiva, who is established in the Vedānta view, spoke to Śivā. ॥22॥
2.3.13.23: Śrī Śiva said: If you speak thus, O Girijā, holding to Sāṃkhya, then render me daily service that is not forbidden, O sweet-spoken one. ॥23॥
2.3.13.24: If I am Brahman, untainted by Māyā, the Supreme Lord, knowable through Vedānta, the master of Māyā, what will you do then? ॥24॥
2.3.13.25: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus to Girijā, the Lord, who delights his devotees and bestows grace on them, addressed the mountain. ॥25॥
2.3.13.26: Śrī Śiva said: Right here, O mountain, on your excellent and most lovely plateau, I, by supreme austerity, move upon the earth, clearly beholding the blissful nature that is the state of the highest truth. ॥26॥
2.3.13.27: O lord of mountains, you should grant me permission to perform austerity; without permission no austerity can be performed. ॥27॥
2.3.13.28: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the trident-bearing god of gods, Himavat bowed to Śambhu and spoke these words. ॥28॥
2.3.13.29: Himavān said: The whole world, with gods, demons and humans, is indeed yours. What can I, being insignificant, say to you, O Mahādeva? ॥29॥
2.3.13.30: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Himavat, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, smiled and respectfully said to the king of mountains: Go. ॥30॥
2.3.13.31: Permitted by Śaṅkara, Himavat went to his own home; and together with Girijā he remained coming daily for darśana of the Lord. ॥31॥
2.3.13.32: Even without her father, that Kālī, intent on devotion, went daily with her two friends to Śaṅkara's presence to serve him. ॥32॥
2.3.13.33: No gaṇa, Nandīśvara or any other, stopped her, dear one, by Maheśa's command, each being pure and obedient to his order. ॥33॥
2.3.13.34: This dialogue between Śiva and Śivā, voicing the Sāṃkhya and Vedānta views, who are truly non-different, has been narrated; on careful reflection it is ever auspicious and gives happiness. ॥34॥
2.3.13.35: At the word of the king of mountains, Śaṅkara, who is beyond the senses, accepted his daughter close by his side, also out of regard for him. ॥35॥
2.3.13.36: The lord of beings said these words to Kālī with her two friends: Let her serve me daily and go home; let her stay here without fear. ॥36॥
2.3.13.37: Having spoken thus, Hara — the changeless great yogin, the Lord who performs many sports — accepted that goddess for his service. ॥37॥
2.3.13.38: This indeed is the great steadfastness of the steadfast and of true ascetics: that even on encountering circumstances full of obstacles, they are not overcome by those obstacles. ॥38॥
2.3.13.39: Then the king of mountains, having returned to his city with his attendants, rejoiced greatly in his mind together with his beloved, O lord of sages. ॥39॥
2.3.13.40: And Hara, through the yoga of meditation, with an undisturbed mind, remained intent on reverently contemplating the Supreme Self. ॥40॥
2.3.13.41: Kālī, accompanied by her two friends, served the moon-crested Mahādeva every day, keeping to her coming and going. ॥41॥
2.3.13.42: Having washed Śambhu's feet, she drank the water from his feet, and with a cloth purified by fire she wiped his body. ॥42॥
2.3.13.43: Having duly worshipped Hara with the sixteen offerings and bowed to him again and again, she would daily go back to her father's house. ॥43॥
2.3.13.44: O best of sages, while Śivā thus served Śaṅkara, who was intent on meditation, a long time passed. ॥44॥
2.3.13.45: Sometimes Kālī, together with her two friends, sang in Śaṅkara's hermitage a beautiful song, well set to rhythm, that heightens love. ॥45॥
2.3.13.46: Sometimes she herself brought kuśa grass, flowers and fuel-sticks, and then stayed there, cleaning the place with her two friends. ॥46॥
2.3.13.47: Sometimes, staying restrained in the dwelling of the moon-bearer, she, full of longing, gazed intently at the moon-crested one and was filled with wonder. ॥47॥
2.3.13.48: Then the Lord of beings, with the ardour of his austerity, having seen her standing nearby free of attachment, reflected: She abides in a body made of the elements. ॥48॥
2.3.13.49: Giriśa did not take as wife Kālī, who stood near him, a treasury of great beauty, enchanting even to sages. ॥49॥
2.3.13.50: Mahādeva, again seeing her thus with controlled senses and ever devoted to serving him, compassionately reflected. ॥50॥
2.3.13.51: Only when this Kālī performs the vow of austerity will I accept her, free of the seed of pride. ॥51॥
2.3.13.52: Brahmā said: Having thus reflected, the Lord of beings quickly took to meditation; the Lord, great master of yogins and performer of great sport, became absorbed. ॥52॥
2.3.13.53: Then, O sage, in the heart of Śiva, the Supreme Self absorbed in meditation, no other thought whatever remained. ॥53॥
2.3.13.54: But Kālī served Śambhu day after day with true devotion, constantly contemplating the form of that great one. ॥54॥
2.3.13.55: Hara, intent on meditation, daily saw Kālī standing steadily; having forgotten his former thought, though seeing her, he did not see her. ॥55॥
2.3.13.56: Meanwhile the gods headed by Śakra, and those sages, at Brahmā's command respectfully sent Smara there, ॥56॥
2.3.13.57: so as to bring about through him, by means of desire, the union of Kālī with Rudra, for they were oppressed by Tāraka, the asura of great might. ॥57॥
2.3.13.58: Going there, Smara employed all his own means; Hara was not disturbed in the least, and he reduced him to ashes. ॥58॥
2.3.13.59: Pārvatī too, O sage, became free of pride at his direction; then, having performed great austerity, the virtuous one obtained Śiva as husband. ॥59॥
2.3.13.60: Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord both became very joyful, and, devoted to helping others, they accomplished the task of the gods. ॥60॥
2.3.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The description of the dialogue of Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥13॥
2.3.14.1: Nārada said: O disciple of Viṣṇu, great devotee of Śiva, O Vidhi (Brahmā), you have told well this supreme account of Śivā and of Śiva. ॥1॥
2.3.14.2: O Brahman, who is the asura Tāraka, by whom the gods were oppressed? Whose son was he? Tell me, and tell his story, which is connected with Śiva. ॥2॥
2.3.14.3: And how did Śaṅkara, the self-controlled one, reduce Smara to ashes? Tell that too with great kindness — that wondrous deed of the Lord. ॥3॥
2.3.14.4: How did Śivā perform extremely fierce penance for the sake of happiness? How did the primordial Śakti, supreme beyond the world, obtain Śambhu as her husband? ॥4॥
2.3.14.5: O greatly wise one, tell all this completely and in detail to me, your own son, who has faith and whose soul is devoted to Śiva. ॥5॥
2.3.14.6: Brahmā said: O best of sons, greatly wise, divine sage of praiseworthy vows: remembering Śaṅkara, I shall tell it; hear that whole account. ॥6॥
2.3.14.7: First, O Nārada, hear well the origin of Tāraka himself, for whose slaying a great effort was made by the gods who took refuge in Śiva. ॥7॥
2.3.14.8: My son is Marīci; Kaśyapa is his son. He had thirteen wives, who were daughters of Dakṣa. ॥8॥
2.3.14.9: Diti was the eldest of his wives; she bore two sons: Hiraṇyakaśipu the elder, and then Hiraṇyākṣa the younger. ॥9॥
2.3.14.10: Those two daityas, who caused great misery, were slain by Viṣṇu in the forms of Man-lion and Boar; then the gods, freed from fear, attained happiness. ॥10॥
2.3.14.11: Diti was grief-stricken; she went to Kaśyapa for refuge. Serving him again with devotion, that woman of good vows conceived an embryo. ॥11॥
2.3.14.12: Learning of it, the great Indra too, very energetic, having found an opening, entered there and cut her embryo again and again with his thunderbolt. ॥12॥
2.3.14.13: By the power of her vow, that embryo did not die. As she slept, by the working of fate, it became seven times seven sons. ॥13॥
2.3.14.14: Those sons all became gods, known by name as the Maruts. Then, made his own by Indra, king of the gods, they went to heaven. ॥14॥
2.3.14.15: Again Diti, remorseful over her own deed, resorted to her husband and, by supreme service, made that sage well pleased. ॥15॥
2.3.14.16: Kaśyapa said: Perform penance, having become pure, for ten thousand years of Brahmā. If that is accomplished first, then you will have a son. ॥16॥
2.3.14.17: O sage, that penance was completed thus by Diti with faith. Then, receiving an embryo from her husband, she bore such a son. ॥17॥
2.3.14.18: That son of Diti was named Vajrāṅga, equal to the immortals, a hero whose body matched his name (adamantine), very valiant and mighty from his very birth. ॥18॥
2.3.14.19: At his mother's command, that son at once seized the lord of the gods by force and inflicted various punishments on the gods as well. ॥19॥
2.3.14.20: Diti attained great joy seeing the wretched plight of Śakra and the others; and the immortals, Śakra and the rest, met with sorrow on account of their own deeds. ॥20॥
2.3.14.21: Then I, ever devoted to the welfare of the gods, quickly came there with Kaśyapa and, with conciliatory words, had the gods released from him. ॥21॥
2.3.14.22: Having released the gods, that Vajrāṅga — a devotee of Śiva, very pure-souled, unperturbed and serene-minded — then spoke respectfully. ॥22॥
2.3.14.23: Vajrāṅga said: Indra is wicked, a killer of my mother's offspring, a pursuer of his own interest. He has received his reward today; let him now rule his own kingdom. ॥23॥
2.3.14.24: O Brahman, all this I did under the compulsion of my mother's command; I have no desire to enjoy any world at all. ॥24॥
2.3.14.25: O Vidhi, best of knowers of the Vedas, tell me the essence of truth, by which I may be ever happy, unperturbed and serene-minded. ॥25॥
2.3.14.26: Hearing that, O sage, I said: The sāttvic disposition is called the essence of truth. And with affection I created an excellent woman. ॥26॥
2.3.14.27: Having given her, named Varāṅgī, to that son of Diti, I went, well pleased, to my own abode; and Kaśyapa, his father, too went. ॥27॥
2.3.14.28: Then that daitya Vajrāṅga, adopting the sāttvic disposition and abandoning the demonic one, free of enmity, attained happiness. ॥28॥
2.3.14.29: But in Varāṅgī's heart the sāttvic disposition did not arise. Full of desire, that virtuous woman served her husband with faith in various ways. ॥29॥
2.3.14.30: Then, from her service, the great lord Vajrāṅga, her husband, soon became pleased, and he then spoke these words. ॥30॥
2.3.14.31: Vajrāṅga said: What do you wish, beloved? Tell me — what is in your mind? Hearing that, she bowed to her husband and told him her heart's desire. ॥31॥
2.3.14.32: Varāṅgī said: If you are pleased, O good husband, give me a son of great might, a conqueror of the three worlds, who will bring distress to Hari. ॥32॥
2.3.14.33: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of his beloved, he became astonished and troubled. That wise one, sāttvic and free of enmity, spoke within his heart: ॥33॥
2.3.14.34: My beloved desires hostility with the gods, but it does not please me. What shall I do? Where shall I go? How may my pledge not be destroyed? ॥34॥
2.3.14.35: If my beloved's desire is fulfilled, the three worlds, and the gods and sages as well, will again be greatly afflicted. ॥35॥
2.3.14.36: If my beloved's desire is not fulfilled, then hell will be my lot. Either way there is loss of dharma — so he had heard from tradition. ॥36॥
2.3.14.37: Thus, O sage, Vajrāṅga wavered in this dilemma of dharma, and there he weighed with his intellect the strength and weakness of the two alternatives. ॥37॥
2.3.14.38: By Śiva's will, O sage, that wise one accepted the woman's words, and the king of daityas said to his beloved, so be it. ॥38॥
2.3.14.39: For that purpose he, with senses controlled, performed another intense and difficult penance for many years, directing it with great devotion to me. ॥39॥
2.3.14.40: Seeing that great penance, I went to grant him a boon, and with a well-pleased mind I said to him: Ask for a boon. ॥40॥
2.3.14.41: Then Vajrāṅga, seeing me, the lord, pleased and standing in the sky, bowed down deeply, praised me much, and chose a boon that was dear to his beloved and for her benefit. ॥41॥
2.3.14.42: Vajrāṅga said: O lord, grant my own wife a son who will bring her great benefit — mighty in strength, of great valour, highly capable, and a treasure-house of austerity. ॥42॥
2.3.14.43: Brahmā said: Having heard his words, O sage, I said, so be it. Having granted that, I went to my own abode, troubled in mind, remembering Śiva. ॥43॥
2.3.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The description of the birth and austerity of Vajrāṅga, in the account of the birth of Tāraka, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥14॥
2.3.15.1: Brahmā said: Then Varāṅgī, with devotion, conceived an embryo from him, as arranged before; and it grew within her womb over many years with great radiance. ॥1॥
2.3.15.2: Then, when the time was complete, Varāṅgī gave birth to a son of huge body and great valour, blazing so as to light up the ten directions. ॥2॥
2.3.15.3: At that very moment, as that son of Varāṅgī—the bringer of grief to the gods—was being born, great portents arose, causes of sorrow. ॥3॥
2.3.15.4: In heaven, on earth and in the mid-air they appeared, terrifying to all the worlds, heralds of calamity; dear son, I shall tell you of those three kinds. ॥4॥
2.3.15.5: Thunderbolts fell along with meteors, with great, terrifying crashes; and fierce comets, bringers of misery, rose up. ॥5॥
2.3.15.6: The earth with its mountains shook; all the directions blazed; all the rivers, and the oceans especially, were agitated. ॥6॥
2.3.15.7: A wind harsh to the touch blew, uttering dreadful howls, uprooting great trees—an army of whirlwinds with dust for its banner. ॥7॥
2.3.15.8: Again and again halos appeared around the sun and moon, together with Rāhu, O best of brahmins—heralds of great terror, robbers of happiness. ॥8॥
2.3.15.9: Then, at that time, from the caves of the mountains arose rumblings, omens of fear, like the rattling of chariots. ॥9॥
2.3.15.10: Inauspicious she-jackals, vomiting fire from their mouths, howled hideously within the villages, amid the cries of jackals and owls. ॥10॥
2.3.15.11: Here and there dogs, raising their necks, let out various cries, now like singing, now like weeping. ॥11॥
2.3.15.12: Then, dear son, asses, frenzied and wild with braying, ran about hither and thither in herds, striking the earth with their hooves. ॥12॥
2.3.15.13: Birds, their minds terrified by the asses' braying, flew up from their nests, and screeching, with agitated hearts, found rest nowhere. ॥13॥
2.3.15.14: Overwhelmed by fear, the animals in pen and forest discharged dung and urine; they wandered about as though beaten and found no rest. ॥14॥
2.3.15.15: The cows, terrified, with tearful eyes and stricken with fear, yielded blood when milked; and the clouds there became frightening, raining pus. ॥15॥
2.3.15.16: There the images of the gods wept, as though about to fly up; trees fell without wind; and a war of the planets took place in the sky. ॥16॥
2.3.15.17: These and many other portents arose, O best of sages; the ignorant people there thought it was the dissolution of the universe. ॥17॥
2.3.15.18: Then the Prajāpati Kaśyapa, after due reflection, gave that mighty asura the name Tāraka. ॥18॥
2.3.15.19: That great hero, his innate manliness swiftly becoming manifest, grew with a body harder than stone, like the lord of mountains. ॥19॥
2.3.15.20: Then that high-minded daitya Tāraka, of great strength and prowess, asked his mother's permission to perform penance. ॥20॥
2.3.15.21: Having obtained permission, that great master of illusion, who deludes even the illusionists, set his mind on penance in order to conquer all the gods. ॥21॥
2.3.15.22: Going to the forest of Madhu, obedient to his elder's command, he performed according to rule an extremely severe penance directed to Vidhi (Brahmā). ॥22॥
2.3.15.23: With arms raised, standing on one foot, gazing at the sun with his eyes, firm of mind and firm of vow, he performed penance for a hundred years. ॥23॥
2.3.15.24: Touching the ground with his big toe, and in the same state, that resolute lord Tāraka, king of asuras, performed penance for another hundred years. ॥24॥
2.3.15.25: For a hundred years he consumed only water, for a hundred years lived on air, for a hundred years stood in water, and for a hundred more practised austerity on the bare ground. ॥25॥
2.3.15.26: Likewise for a hundred years in fire, for a hundred years head downwards, and for a hundred years standing on the ground on the palm of his hand. ॥26॥
2.3.15.27: For a hundred years, O sage, hanging by his feet from the branch of a tree, head downwards, he drank the smoke of a pure fire. ॥27॥
2.3.15.28: Thus that king of daityas, aiming at his desire, performed according to rule an excellent penance of the hardest kind, unbearable even to those who merely hear of it. ॥28॥
2.3.15.29: As he performed penance there in this way, a great radiance issued from his head, spreading everywhere and causing great calamity, O sage. ॥29॥
2.3.15.30: By it those worlds of the gods were almost burnt up, and all the divine sages, O sage, fell into distress on every side. ॥30॥
2.3.15.31: Then Indra, lord of the gods, was seized with great fear: Someone is performing penance now; surely he will assail my position. ॥31॥
2.3.15.32: This mighty one will destroy the universe untimely. Fallen into such doubt, they could reach no certainty. ॥32॥
2.3.15.33: Then all those gods and sages, after consulting well among themselves, frightened and dejected, went to my world and approached me. ॥33॥
2.3.15.34: Bowing to me and praising me well, all of them, troubled in mind, with joined palms, reported to me everything that had happened. ॥34॥
2.3.15.35: Having fully ascertained the whole cause of it with clear understanding, I went to grant a boon to where that asura was performing penance. ॥35॥
2.3.15.36: I spoke to him these words, O sage: Ask for a boon. You have performed intense penance; there is nothing that cannot be given to you. ॥36॥
2.3.15.37: Hearing these words of mine, the great asura Tāraka bowed to me, praised me well, and chose an exceedingly terrible boon. ॥37॥
2.3.15.38: Tāraka said: When you, the giver of boons, are pleased, what could be impossible for me? Therefore I ask a boon of you; hear it from me, O Grandsire. ॥38॥
2.3.15.39: If you are pleased, O lord of the gods, if a boon is to be given to me, then, showing mercy towards me, grant me two boons. ॥39॥
2.3.15.40: In this entire world created by you, O great lord, let there surely be no man at all as strong as I am. ॥40॥
2.3.15.41: When a son born of Śiva's seed, having become commander of the army, hurls a weapon at me, then alone may my death occur. ॥41॥
2.3.15.42: Thus addressed then by that demon, O lord of sages, I granted such a boon and quickly went to my own world. ॥42॥
2.3.15.43: That demon too, having obtained the excellent boon desired in his mind, became exceedingly delighted and went to the city called Śoṇita. ॥43॥
2.3.15.44: Then that great demon, together with the asuras, was consecrated to the kingship of the three worlds by Śukra, preceptor of the demons, at my command. ॥44॥
2.3.15.45: Thereafter that great demon became the ruler of the three worlds; he enforced his own command, oppressing all beings, moving and unmoving. ॥45॥
2.3.15.46: That Tāraka ruled the three worlds according to rule, and protected the subjects while oppressing the gods and others. ॥46॥
2.3.15.47: Then that demon Tāraka took the jewels of Indra and the other guardians of the worlds, which they gave of their own accord out of fear of him. ॥47॥
2.3.15.48: Out of fear of him Indra surrendered Airāvata to him; Kubera then gave the nine treasures. ॥48॥
2.3.15.49: By Varuṇa white horses were given, by the sages likewise the wish-granting cow; and by Indra the divine Uccaiḥśravas was surrendered to him out of fear. ॥49॥
2.3.15.50: Wherever that demon saw any excellent thing, he seized it by force; the three worlds became bereft of their essence. ॥50॥
2.3.15.51: And likewise the oceans gave him jewels out of fear, O sage. The earth yielded crops without ploughing, and all subjects had their desires fulfilled. ॥51॥
2.3.15.52: The sun shone in such a way that it caused him no discomfort; the moon was visible with full radiance, and the wind was favourable in every way. ॥52॥
2.3.15.53: Whatever wealth belonged to the gods, to the ancestors and to others, all of it was seized by that wicked demon. ॥53॥
2.3.15.54: Having subdued the three worlds, he himself became Indra. He was the unrivalled lord, and, self-controlled, he exercised a wondrous rule. ॥54॥
2.3.15.55: Having expelled all the gods, he then installed the demons in their places; he himself set the divine beings to their own tasks. ॥55॥
2.3.15.56: Then all the gods, led by Śakra, afflicted by him, helpless and greatly distressed, came to me for refuge, O sage. ॥56॥
2.3.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The description of the austerity and reign of the asura Tāraka, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥15॥
2.3.16.1: Brahmā said: Then all those gods, oppressed by Tāraka, bowed deeply to the lord of creatures Brahmā and praised him with supreme devotion. ॥1॥
2.3.16.2: Having heard the gods' praise, true and heart-touching, I became exceedingly pleased and replied to the dwellers of heaven. ॥2॥
2.3.16.3: Welcome. Are your own offices free of obstacles, O gods? For what purpose have you all come here? Tell me. ॥3॥
2.3.16.4: Hearing these words of mine, all those dwellers of heaven, humbled and wretched, oppressed by Tāraka, bowed and spoke to me. ॥4॥
2.3.16.5: The gods said: O Lord of the worlds, the demon Tāraka, made arrogant by your boon, has driven us out by force and himself seized our places by violence. ॥5॥
2.3.16.6: Is the misery that has befallen us not known to you? Destroy that misery quickly; we have come to you for refuge. ॥6॥
2.3.16.7: Day and night he torments us wherever we stay; even as we flee, wherever we go we see Tāraka. ॥7॥
2.3.16.8: And by the misery that has arisen for us from Tāraka, O Lord of all, all of us, dear father, are oppressed and utterly distraught. ॥8॥
2.3.16.9: Agni, Yama, Varuṇa, Nirṛti and Vāyu, and the other guardians of the quarters too — all are under his control. ॥9॥
2.3.16.10: All of them, behaving like humans, together with all their retinues, serve that great demon; never are they independent. ॥10॥
2.3.16.11: Thus afflicted by him, the gods are always under his sway; all are devoted to doing his will, living as his dependents. ॥11॥
2.3.16.12: All the women there were, and the hosts of Apsarases as well — that mighty demon Tāraka has seized them all. ॥12॥
2.3.16.13: Sacrifices are not performed, ascetics do not practise austerities; nothing such as charity and righteous duty goes on in the worlds. ॥13॥
2.3.16.14: His general is Krauñca, a greatly sinful Dānava; he has gone to the nether world and torments its creatures ceaselessly. ॥14॥
2.3.16.15: By that sinful, pitiless Tāraka this entire triad of worlds of ours has been seized by force, O creator of the universe. ॥15॥
2.3.16.16: We shall go to whatever place you assign. Though we dwelt at ease, we have been driven from it by that enemy of the gods, O Lord of the worlds. ॥16॥
2.3.16.17: You alone are our refuge, ruler, sustainer and protector. All of us are burnt in the fire called Tāraka and are utterly distressed. ॥17॥
2.3.16.18: By him all our fierce means have been rendered powerless, as potent medicines fail in a sannipāta disorder. ॥18॥
2.3.16.19: Hari's discus Sudarśana, in which lay our hope of victory, became blunted on his neck, as if a flower had been offered there. ॥19॥
2.3.16.20: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the gods, O sage, I replied to all the gods with words suited to the occasion. ॥20॥
2.3.16.21: Brahmā said: It is by my own word that the demon named Tāraka has grown powerful; it is not proper that he be slain by me, O dwellers of heaven. ॥21॥
2.3.16.22: Hence his slaying by me is not fitting, since he attained growth through me; even a poison tree, once one has reared it oneself, it is improper to cut down oneself. ॥22॥
2.3.16.23: Śaṅkara is able to accomplish your whole task; but even when urged, he cannot himself counter him directly. ॥23॥
2.3.16.24: Tāraka will come to ruin by his own sin. I shall give you counsel so that you may make the arrangements. ॥24॥
2.3.16.25: Tāraka cannot be slain by me, nor by Hari, nor by Hara, nor by anyone else or by the gods, because of my boon — this is spoken in truth. ॥25॥
2.3.16.26: If there were a son born of Śiva's seed, O gods, he alone, and no other, would be the slayer of the demon named Tāraka. ॥26॥
2.3.16.27: Carry out the means I tell you, O best of gods; by the grace of Mahādeva it will surely succeed. ॥27॥
2.3.16.28: Satī, daughter of Dakṣa, who formerly gave up her body, has been born from Menakā's womb; that story is known to you. ॥28॥
2.3.16.29: Giriśa will certainly take her hand in marriage; even so, O dwellers of heaven, you should work out a means for it. ॥29॥
2.3.16.30: Act with great effort so that Śiva's seed may be made to fall into that Pārvatī, born of Menakā. ॥30॥
2.3.16.31: She alone is able to make that Śambhu, whose seed is held upward, release his seed; no other woman whatever can do so, even by force. ॥31॥
2.3.16.32: That daughter of the king of mountains, now in the full bloom of youth, constantly serves Hara as he performs austerities on the Himālaya. ॥32॥
2.3.16.33: At the word of Himavat, her own father, and by her own insistence, Kālī the auspicious one, together with two friends, serves the Supreme Lord who is absorbed in meditation. ॥33॥
2.3.16.34: Though she, the most beautiful woman in the three worlds, worships him right before him, Maheśa, intent on meditation, does not waver even in mind. ॥34॥
2.3.16.35: Act with effort, O gods, so that before long the moon-crested one may desire Kālī as his wife. ॥35॥
2.3.16.36: Now I shall go to the demon's abode and restrain that Tāraka from his wicked obstinacy. Go to your own places, O immortals. ॥36॥
2.3.16.37: Having said this to the gods, I quickly approached the demon named Tāraka, greeted him very cordially, and spoke thus: ॥37॥
2.3.16.38: Brahmā said: You are ruling this heaven of ours, the very essence of splendour, as your kingdom; yet you desire more than that for which you performed great austerity. ॥38॥
2.3.16.39: The boon I gave was a lesser one; sovereignty over heaven was not granted by me. Therefore, leaving heaven, rule a kingdom on earth. ॥39॥
2.3.16.40: All the deeds befitting the gods will take place right there for you, O best of Asuras; there need be no hesitation about this. ॥40॥
2.3.16.41: Having spoken thus and having admonished that asura, I, the lord of all beings, remembered Śivā together with Śiva and vanished from there. ॥41॥
2.3.16.42: Tāraka too, abandoning heaven, then went to the earth; staying in the city called Śoṇita, he ruled over the entire kingdom. ॥42॥
2.3.16.43: All the gods too, having heard those words of mine, bowed low to me and went gladly to Śakra's abode, well composed, together with Śakra. ॥43॥
2.3.16.44: Having gone there, met, and deliberated among themselves, all those gods affectionately spoke these words to Maghavan. ॥44॥
2.3.16.45: The gods said: O Maghavan, you must carry out all that Brahmā has said, so that Śambhu's longing for Śivā may arise through Kāma. ॥45॥
2.3.16.46: Brahmā said: Having thus reported the whole account to the lord of the gods, those gods went joyfully from there, each to his own place. ॥46॥
2.3.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The description of the consoling of the gods, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥16॥
2.3.17.1: Brahmā said: When those gods had gone, Śakra, sorely afflicted by the wicked demon Tāraka, called Smara (Kāma) to mind. ॥1॥
2.3.17.2: At that very moment Kāma came, together with Vasanta, the lover of Rati, proud, accompanied by Rati, the lord who conquers the three worlds. ॥2॥
2.3.17.3: Then, having bowed and standing before him, Smara, high-spirited, dear one, with joined palms spoke to Śakra. ॥3॥
2.3.17.4: Kāma said: What task has arisen for you? For what reason have I been remembered? Tell it, O lord of the gods; I have come to accomplish it. ॥4॥
2.3.17.5: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of Kandarpa, the lord of the gods spoke with affection, praising him, saying, well said, well said. ॥5॥
2.3.17.6: Śakra said: Your undertaking is good, since you are ready to accomplish the task that has come upon me. You are blessed, O Makaradhvaja. ॥6॥
2.3.17.7: Hear my words on the matter at hand; I will tell you before you. Whatever task is mine is also yours, not otherwise. ॥7॥
2.3.17.8: I do have many friends, and very great ones; but, O Smara, a true friend equal to you is nowhere at all. ॥8॥
2.3.17.9: For my victory, dear one, a pair has been made: the excellent thunderbolt and you. The thunderbolt may prove fruitless, but you never. ॥9॥
2.3.17.10: Who indeed is dearer than the one from whom benefit arises? Therefore you, the best of friends, should accomplish my task. ॥10॥
2.3.17.11: A sorrow has arisen for me, born of time and otherwise incurable; no one at all can remove it except you. ॥11॥
2.3.17.12: The test of a giver comes in famine, of a hero in battle, of a friend in time of calamity, and of women and of a family in times of helplessness. ॥12॥
2.3.17.13: The test of humility is in conduct; of the truthful, when a crisis has come; and likewise of true affection, behind one's back, dear one. This truth has been declared, not otherwise. ॥13॥
2.3.17.14: Now that a calamity has come upon me which no one else can avert, today your test will take place, O best of friends. ॥14॥
2.3.17.15: This task, bringing happiness, is not mine alone; rather it is the task of all the gods and others—there is no doubt. ॥15॥
2.3.17.16: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Maghavan, Makaradhvaja, smiling sweetly, spoke words deep with affection. ॥16॥
2.3.17.17: Kāma said: Why do you speak like this? I give you no answer in words. In the world a true helper is seen in deeds, not spoken of; mere talk is artificial. ॥17॥
2.3.17.18: He who talks much in a crisis—what task will he accomplish? Even so, great king, I will speak; listen, O lord. ॥18॥
2.3.17.19: Whoever performs fierce austerity to drag you from your position, that enemy of yours I will bring down completely, O friend. ॥19॥
2.3.17.20: In an instant, with the sidelong glance of a lovely woman, I will make gods, sages, Dānavas and the rest fall; men do not even count for me. ॥20॥
2.3.17.21: Let the thunderbolt and the many other weapons stay far away; what task will they accomplish for you when I, your friend, am at hand? ॥21॥
2.3.17.22: I could make even Brahmā or Hari fall, no doubt; others do not count at all. I could bring down even Hara. ॥22॥
2.3.17.23: My arrows are only five, soft, and made of flowers; my bow, curved in three places, is made of flowers; its string is formed of bees. ॥23॥
2.3.17.24: My strength is my dear beloved Rati; Vasanta is known as my minister. I possess fivefold strength, O god, and my friend is the moon, the treasury of nectar. ॥24॥
2.3.17.25: My commander is Śṛṅgāra (erotic sentiment), and amorous gestures and moods are my soldiers. All of them are soft, O Śakra, and I too am of that kind. ॥25॥
2.3.17.26: A wise man should employ for a task whoever can accomplish it. Whatever task is suited to me—assign all of it to me. ॥26॥
2.3.17.27: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of his, Śakra was delighted, and, bowing with his speech, addressed Kāma, the bringer of joy to lovers. ॥27॥
2.3.17.28: Śakra said: The task that I have conceived in my mind, dear Manobhava, you are able to accomplish; it cannot come about through anyone else. ॥28॥
2.3.17.29: Listen, Kāma, best of friends; I will tell you truly the purpose for which the longing for you arose in me today, O Manobhava. ॥29॥
2.3.17.30: The great demon named Tāraka, having obtained a wondrous boon from Brahmā, has become invincible and a cause of suffering to all. ॥30॥
2.3.17.31: By him the world is oppressed and dharma has been destroyed in many ways; all the gods are distressed, and likewise all the sages. ॥31॥
2.3.17.32: All the gods fought with him according to their strength, but earlier all their weapons proved futile there. ॥32॥
2.3.17.33: The noose of the lord of waters (Varuṇa) was broken; and Hari's discus Sudarśana, hurled by Viṣṇu at his neck, was blunted. ॥33॥
2.3.17.34: The lord of creatures (Brahmā) has declared that this wicked one's death will come from a boy born of the seed of Śambhu, the great lord of yogins. ॥34॥
2.3.17.35: This task must be carried out well by you with great effort; then, O best of friends, supreme happiness will come to us gods. ॥35॥
2.3.17.36: Therefore, remembering in your heart the duty of friendship, you should now accomplish what I too have planned, which brings happiness to all the worlds. ॥36॥
2.3.17.37: That Śambhu has undertaken supreme austerity on the king of mountains; that lord, the independent Supreme Lord, is not moved even by desire. ॥37॥
2.3.17.38: I have heard that near him, for the sake of the gods, Pārvatī, with her companions, remains serving him, as commanded by her father. ॥38॥
2.3.17.39: You must surely act, O Māra, so that in that self-controlled Śiva an intense attraction for her arises. ॥39॥
2.3.17.40: Having done this, you will have succeeded; all suffering will perish, and your glory in the world will be lasting—not otherwise. ॥40॥
2.3.17.41: Brahmā said: Thus addressed, Kāma, his lotus-face blossoming with joy, lovingly said to the lord of the gods: I will do it; there is no doubt. ॥41॥
2.3.17.42: Having spoken these words to him, Kāma, deluded by Śiva's māyā, promptly accepted that command of Indra, saying, so be it, Om. ॥42॥
2.3.17.43: Greatly pleased, together with his wife and accompanied by Vasanta, he went to the place where the lord of yogins himself was performing supreme austerity. ॥43॥
2.3.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The description of the dialogue of Śakra and Kāma, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥17॥
2.3.18.1: Brahmā said: Having gone there, the proud Smara, deluded by Śiva's māyā, that enchanter, stood there, first of all spreading forth the nature of Madhu the spring. ॥1॥
2.3.18.2: And the nature of spring spread everywhere in Maheśa's place of austerity, on the Oṣadhiprastha, O lord of sages. ॥2॥
2.3.18.3: And the forests of trees there became especially full of blossoms through its power, O great sage, O lord of sages. ॥3॥
2.3.18.4: The blossoms of the mango trees in the groves of aśoka shone, fragrant and greatly kindling love. ॥4॥
2.3.18.5: And the white lotus blossoms, swarmed over by bees, became especially productive of the onset of passion. ॥5॥
2.3.18.6: The sweet warbling of the cuckoos, which strongly kindles desire, was exceedingly delightful, charming and most pleasing. ॥6॥
2.3.18.7: Likewise, O sage, there arose the various hums of the bees, charming to all and also kindling desire. ॥7॥
2.3.18.8: The clear radiance of the moon, spread all around, became like a go-between for amorous men and women. ॥8॥
2.3.18.9: At that time the light of the season served to urge on lovers sulking in pride; and a pleasant breeze blew, O good one, yet unwelcome to one separated from the beloved. ॥9॥
2.3.18.10: Thus the spread of spring, causing possession by passion, then became exceedingly hard to bear there for the sages dwelling in the forest. ॥10॥
2.3.18.11: Then, O sage, even in insentient beings there arose attachment to desire; what need is there to tell the tale of sentient creatures? ॥11॥
2.3.18.12: Thus that Madhu, kindling desire in all living beings, displayed his own power, which was most hard to bear. ॥12॥
2.3.18.13: Seeing then, dear one, what Madhu had produced out of season, Hara, the Lord who had taken a body through his own play, considered it a great wonder. ॥13॥
2.3.18.14: Then that performer of divine play, Hara, the master of the self-controlled, the Lord who removes sorrow, practised there austerity that was supremely difficult. ॥14॥
2.3.18.15: When spring had spread there, Kāma, accompanied by Rati, drew the mango-blossom arrow and stood at his left side. ॥15॥
2.3.18.16: He spread his power, deluding all people. Who indeed, seeing Kāma then united with Rati, would not be deluded? ॥16॥
2.3.18.17: When the two had thus begun their love-sport, Śṛṅgāra (the erotic sentiment) too, with his attendants, endowed with amorous gestures and moods, entered there into Hara's presence. ॥17॥
2.3.18.18: Madana, who moves within the mind, dwelt there visible outside; he did not then see in Śambhu any weak spot through which he could enter. ॥18॥
2.3.18.19: And when Smara found no opening in that best of yogins, Mahādeva, he became confounded by great fear. ॥19॥
2.3.18.20: Who indeed is able to approach Śaṅkara, absorbed in meditation, possessing a forehead-eye like a fire with blazing flames? ॥20॥
2.3.18.21: Meanwhile, Śivā, accompanied by her two friends, went there for the worship of Śiva, carrying flowers of many kinds. ॥21॥
2.3.18.22: Whatever great beauty is described by people on earth, all that, and more, is certainly present in that Pārvatī. ॥22॥
2.3.18.23: When she wore the lovely flowers of the season, how could that beauty of hers be described even in hundreds of years? ॥23॥
2.3.18.24: When that daughter of the mountain came near Śiva, at that very moment Śaṅkara, leaving his meditation, remained so for an instant. ॥24॥
2.3.18.25: Finding that opening, Madana first, with the arrow Harṣaṇa, excited the Moon-crested One standing nearby. ॥25॥
2.3.18.26: Then, O sage, Pārvatī, endowed with amorous moods and feelings, went to Hara, in aid of Kāma, together with Spring. ॥26॥
2.3.18.27: At that very moment, drawing that bow, Smara, well composed, swiftly released the flower-arrow at the Trident-bearer, to arouse his liking. ॥27॥
2.3.18.28: Just as she came constantly every day, so now she came to Śiva; having bowed to him and performed his worship, she stood before him. ॥28॥
2.3.18.29: That Pārvatī was seen there by the Lord Giriśa as she then, from a woman's nature and with great bashfulness, revealed her limbs. ॥29॥
2.3.18.30: Recalling well the boon given to her formerly by Vidhi Brahmā, Lord Śiva too described her limbs with delight, O sage. ॥30॥
2.3.18.31: Śiva said: Is this a face, or the moon? Are these eyes, or blue lotuses? And these two eyebrows are the bows of the great-souled Kandarpa. ॥31॥
2.3.18.32: Is this a lower lip, or a bimba fruit? Is this a nose, or a parrot's beak? Is this a voice, or the cooing of a cuckoo? Is this a waist, or an altar? ॥32॥
2.3.18.33: How can her gait be described? How can her form be described again and again? And how can her flowers be described, and likewise again her garments? ॥33॥
2.3.18.34: Whatever lovely grace there is in creation has been fashioned in one place in her. All her limbs are charming in every way; there is no doubt. ॥34॥
2.3.18.35: Ah, most blessed is this Pārvatī of wondrous form! There is no woman in the three worlds so beautiful as to equal her. ॥35॥
2.3.18.36: She is a treasure of great loveliness, bearing wondrous limbs, an enchantress even of sages, increasing great joy. ॥36॥
2.3.18.37: Brahmā said: Having thus described her limbs again and again, Hara, under the influence of the boon given by Vidhi, then fell silent. ॥37॥
2.3.18.38: When Śaṅkara moved his hand toward the edge of her garment, she, out of a woman's nature, abashed, went some distance away. ॥38॥
2.3.18.39: Revealing her own limbs and glancing again and again with lovely looks, Śivā, from great joy, broke into a sweet smile, O sage. ॥39॥
2.3.18.40: Seeing such behaviour then, Śambhu became infatuated, and Maheśvara, of great divine play, spoke these words. ॥40॥
2.3.18.41: By merely seeing her, great bliss arises in abundance. If I were to embrace her, what joy would there be then? ॥41॥
2.3.18.42: Having reflected thus for just a moment and then having honoured Girijā, that great yogin, awakened to himself and wholly dispassionate, spoke as follows. ॥42॥
2.3.18.43: What has happened, what strange conduct? Have I fallen into delusion? Even though I am the master and the Lord, today I have been disturbed by Kāma. ॥43॥
2.3.18.44: If I, the Lord, should indeed desire to touch another's body, then what will any other petty, powerless being not do? ॥44॥
2.3.18.45: Having thus attained dispassion, the Supreme Lord, the Self of all, checked that sitting of Pārvatī's upon the couch. How could he fall here? ॥45॥
2.3.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The description of the disturbance caused by Kāma, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥18॥
2.3.19.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O Creator, O greatly fortunate one, what happened after that? Graciously tell me that sin-destroying story. ॥1॥
2.3.19.2: Brahmā said: Listen, dear child, to that story of what happened after that. Out of affection for you I shall narrate Śiva's joy-bringing sport. ॥2॥
2.3.19.3: Seeing the disturbance of his composure, the great yogin Maheśvara, greatly astonished, then reflected thus in his mind. ॥3॥
2.3.19.4: Śiva said: Why have obstacles arisen while I am performing supreme austerity? What evil-doer here has made my mind agitated? ॥4॥
2.3.19.5: I have indeed lovingly made an improper description concerning another's woman. A violation of dharma has occurred here; the boundary of the Veda has been transgressed. ॥5॥
2.3.19.6: Brahmā said: Having reflected thus, the great yogin, the Supreme Lord, the refuge of the good, then, suspicious, looked around in all directions. ॥6॥
2.3.19.7: He saw Kāma standing on his left side with his arrow drawn, eager to shoot his own arrow, proud and deluded in mind. ॥7॥
2.3.19.8: Seeing Kāma in that state, O Nārada, a tumult of anger arose instantly in Girīśa, the Supreme Self. ॥8॥
2.3.19.9: Kāma, standing in the sky and holding that bow with its arrow, discharged at Śaṅkara, O sage, his irresistible, unfailing missile. ॥9॥
2.3.19.10: But that unfailing missile became futile against the Supreme Self; it then subsided before that enraged Supreme Lord. ॥10॥
2.3.19.11: When his own missile had become futile against Śiva, Manmatha was quickly seized by fear, and standing before him, seeing the lord Mṛtyuñjaya, he trembled. ॥11॥
2.3.19.12: His effort being fruitless, that Smara, overwhelmed with fear, O tiger among sages, called to mind all the gods headed by Śakra. ॥12॥
2.3.19.13: Being intently remembered by Kāma, O lord of sages, all those gods headed by Śakra came, bowed to Śambhu, and praised him. ॥13॥
2.3.19.14: While the gods were offering praise, from the third eye of the greatly enraged Hara there then issued forth a great fire, ॥14॥
2.3.19.15: From that eye situated in the middle of the forehead, that swiftly arisen fire blazed with upward flames, shining, with a radiance like the fire of dissolution. ॥15॥
2.3.19.16: Swiftly flying up into the sky and dropping onto the surface of the earth, whirling round and round about itself, it fell all over the earth. ॥16॥
2.3.19.17: O good one, it reduced Madana to ashes even while the gods were still crying, forgive, forgive. ॥17॥
2.3.19.18: When that heroic Smara was slain, the gods fell into grief; overwhelmed, they wept, crying loudly: What has happened? ॥18॥
2.3.19.19: Then the daughter of the king of mountains, pale of limb and distraught in mind, went to her own house taking her companions with her. ॥19॥
2.3.19.20: Then Rati there became unconscious for a moment; through the grief born of her husband's death she fell as if dead. ॥20॥
2.3.19.21: When consciousness returned, Rati, utterly distraught, lamented there, uttering various words. ॥21॥
2.3.19.22: Rati said: What shall I do? Where shall I go? What have the gods done here? Having summoned my proud lord, they had him destroyed. ॥22॥
2.3.19.23: Alas, alas, my protector Smara, my lord, dear as life, giver of joy! What is this that has happened here? Alas, alas, beloved, beloved! ॥23॥
2.3.19.24: Brahmā said: Lamenting thus and uttering many words, she then beat her hands and feet and tore at her hair. ॥24॥
2.3.19.25: Hearing her lament then, all the forest creatures there became sorrowful, O Nārada, and even the immobile beings. ॥25॥
2.3.19.26: Meanwhile, all the gods there headed by Śakra, remembering Maheśvara, consoled Rati and spoke to her. ॥26॥
2.3.19.27: The gods said: Take some of the ashes and guard them carefully; give up fear. That Lord will revive him, and you will regain your beloved. ॥27॥
2.3.19.28: No one is the giver of happiness, nor anyone the giver of sorrow; everyone experiences what he himself has done. You blame the gods in vain. ॥28॥
2.3.19.29: Brahmā said: Having thus consoled Rati, all the gods approached Śiva and, having fully propitiated Śiva with devotion, spoke these words. ॥29॥
2.3.19.30: The gods said: O Blessed One, O Lord, O Maheśāna, affectionate to those who seek refuge, be merciful and listen to this auspicious speech of ours. ॥30॥
2.3.19.31: O Śaṅkara, consider well and kindly the deed of Kāma. What Kāma did here was not for his own sake, O Maheśvara. ॥31॥
2.3.19.32: O all-pervading one, that deed was caused to be done by all of us gods oppressed by the wicked Tāraka. O Lord, Śaṅkara, know it not to be otherwise. ॥32॥
2.3.19.33: O god, Rati, all alone and grief-stricken, is lamenting. O Giriśa, O giver of all, console her. ॥33॥
2.3.19.34: O Śaṅkara, if you have slain that Smara, then with this anger you intend to destroy everyone, along with the gods. ॥34॥
2.3.19.35: Seeing the grief of that Rati, the gods are almost ruined. Therefore you must remove Rati's sorrow. ॥35॥
2.3.19.36: Brahmā said: Having heard their words, the Blessed Śiva was pleased and spoke these words to all the gods. ॥36॥
2.3.19.37: Śiva said: O gods and all sages, listen attentively to my words. What has happened through my anger will remain so; it cannot be otherwise. ॥37॥
2.3.19.38: The mighty Kāma, Rati's husband, shall remain bodiless (anaṅga) only until Kṛṣṇa, the husband of Rukmiṇī, descends upon the earth. ॥38॥
2.3.19.39: When, dwelling in Dvārakā, he begets sons, then Kṛṣṇa will beget Kāma in Rukmiṇī. ॥39॥
2.3.19.40: He will be named Pradyumna; there is no doubt. And as soon as that son is born, Śambara will carry him off. ॥40॥
2.3.19.41: Śambara, the foremost of the Dānavas, having carried him off and thrown him into the ocean, and deluded, believing him dead without reason, will go to his own city. ॥41॥
2.3.19.42: Meanwhile, O Rati, you should stay in his city as you please; right there you will obtain your own husband, reborn as Pradyumna. ॥42॥
2.3.19.43: There Kāma, named Pradyumna, having met her and slain Śambara in battle, will be happy with his own beloved, O gods. ॥43॥
2.3.19.44: And taking whatever wealth was his (Śambara's), he will go back to the city together with her, O gods; my word is true. ॥44॥
2.3.19.45: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Śambhu, the gods, somewhat relieved at heart, bowed to him and, with folded hands and bodies bent low, spoke. ॥45॥
2.3.19.46: The gods said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, ocean of compassion, Lord, quickly revive Kāma; save Rati's life, O Hara. ॥46॥
2.3.19.47: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the immortals, the Supreme Lord, pleased, the ocean of compassion, the Lord of all, spoke again. ॥47॥
2.3.19.48: Śiva said: O gods, I am well pleased, and I shall revive him in due course. That Kāma, having become my attendant (gaṇa), will roam about forever. ॥48॥
2.3.19.49: This account must not be told before anyone, O gods. Go to your own abodes; I shall destroy your sorrow in every way. ॥49॥
2.3.19.50: Brahmā said: Having said this, Rudra vanished then while the gods were praising him. All the gods became well pleased, their amazement gone. ॥50॥
2.3.19.51: Then, abiding by Rudra's word, they consoled her, told her his message, and went each to his own abode, O sage. ॥51॥
2.3.19.52: Kāma's wife then went to the city indicated to her, awaiting the time appointed by Rudra, O lord of sages. ॥52॥
2.3.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The description of the destruction of Kāma, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥19॥
2.3.20.1: Nārada said: O Creator, where did that flame of fire that arose from Hara's eye go? Tell me that story of the moon-crested Śiva. ॥1॥
2.3.20.2: Brahmā said: When the fire of Śambhu's third eye had swiftly reduced Kāma to ashes, it then blazed on all sides, without purpose. ॥2॥
2.3.20.3: A great cry of distress arose in the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings. All the gods and sages, dear son, quickly came to me for refuge. ॥3॥
2.3.20.4: Agitated, they all bowed down deeply, praised me well, joined their hands, and with faces lowered reported that distress to me. ॥4॥
2.3.20.5: Hearing that, I remembered Śiva, reflected carefully on its cause, and went there with a humble mind for the protection of the three worlds. ॥5॥
2.3.20.6: That fire, eager to burn everything, blazing intensely with garlands of flames, was quickly checked by me through the great power obtained by Śambhu's grace. ॥6॥
2.3.20.7: Then, O sage, I drew away that fire made of wrath, eager to burn the three worlds, giving it the form of the submarine mare-fire with a gentle flaming mouth. ॥7॥
2.3.20.8: Taking that fire in the body of the mare-fire, by Śiva's will I, the lord of the worlds, went to the ocean for the welfare of the people. ॥8॥
2.3.20.9: Seeing me arrive, O sage, the Ocean, assuming a human form, came into my presence with joined palms. ॥9॥
2.3.20.10: Then the Ocean bowed deeply to me and praised me according to rule, and with great affection he spoke to me, the grandfather of all the worlds. ॥10॥
2.3.20.11: The Ocean said: For what purpose have you come here, O Brahmā, lord of all? Instruct me about that kindly, regarding me as your own servant. ॥11॥
2.3.20.12: Then, having heard the Ocean's words spoken with affection, I remembered Śaṅkara and spoke, bringing about the welfare of the world. ॥12॥
2.3.20.13: Brahmā said: Listen, dear one, highly intelligent one, bringer of welfare to all worlds. O Ocean, impelled in my heart by Śiva's will, I speak with affection. ॥13॥
2.3.20.14: This is the wrath of Maheśa, a mighty power in the form of the mare-fire. Having quickly burnt Kāma, it then became eager to burn everything. ॥14॥
2.3.20.15: By Śaṅkara's will I was quickly entreated by the afflicted gods; coming there swiftly, dear one, I checked that fire. ॥15॥
2.3.20.16: It assumed the form of the mare-fire; taking it, I have come here. O abode of waters, I, the merciful one, direct you: ॥16॥
2.3.20.17: This wrath of Maheśa, which has taken the form of the mare-fire with a flaming mouth, must be held by you until the dissolution of beings. ॥17॥
2.3.20.18: When I come here and dwell here, O lord of rivers, then this wondrous wrath of Śaṅkara should be released by you. ॥18॥
2.3.20.19: Your water will always be its food. It must be held with care so that it does not come out. ॥19॥
2.3.20.20: Thus addressed by me, the Ocean then firmly agreed to take in the fierce mare-fire, which could not be held by anyone else. ॥20॥
2.3.20.21: Then that fire in the body of the mare-fire entered the ocean, burning its floods of water, blazing with garlands of flames. ॥21॥
2.3.20.22: Then, with a contented mind, I went to my own abode, O sage; and the Ocean, of divine form, bowed to me and disappeared. ॥22॥
2.3.20.23: The whole world regained its well-being, freed from the fear arising from that; the gods and the sages became happy, O great sage. ॥23॥
2.3.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The description of the story of the submarine fire, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
2.3.21.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi, dear father, greatly wise one, disciple of Viṣṇu, maker of the three worlds: this wondrous story of the great-souled Śaṅkara has been told by you. ॥1॥
2.3.21.2: When Smara had been reduced to ashes by the fire of Śambhu's third eye, and when that fire had entered the ocean, tell me what happened after that. ॥2॥
2.3.21.3: What did the goddess Pārvatī, daughter of the mountain, do then? Where did she go with her two friends? Tell me that now, O treasure of compassion. ॥3॥
2.3.21.4: Brahmā said: Listen, dear son, greatly wise one, with reverence to the deeds of the moon-crested one, the bestower of great grace, my own Lord. ॥4॥
2.3.21.5: When the fire born from Śambhu's eye burned Madana, a great and wondrous sound arose, by which the sky was filled. ॥5॥
2.3.21.6: Frightened by that great sound, and having seen Kāma burned, she went, distraught, to her own home together with her two friends. ॥6॥
2.3.21.7: At that sound Himavat, together with his household, was astonished and deeply distressed, remembering his daughter who had gone there. ॥7॥
2.3.21.8: The lord of mountains fell into grief on seeing his daughter so agitated; the lord of mountains approached her as she wept from separation from Śambhu. ॥8॥
2.3.21.9: Having approached, wiping her two eyes with his hand, he said, do not fear, Śivā; do not weep, and then took hold of her. ॥9॥
2.3.21.10: Himavat, lord of mountains, quickly placed his daughter on his lap and then brought her to his own abode, consoling her in her great distress. ॥10॥
2.3.21.11: When Hara, having burned Smara, had vanished, Śivā, through separation from him, became extremely distressed and found comfort nowhere. ॥11॥
2.3.21.12: Then, having gone to her father's house and met her mother, Śivā, the daughter of the mountain, felt as though she had been born again. ॥12॥
2.3.21.13: She reproached her own beauty and then said, alas, I am ruined! Even when counselled by her friends, the daughter of the mountain-king would not be consoled. ॥13॥
2.3.21.14: Whether sleeping or drinking, bathing or walking, or standing among her friends, Śivā found no happiness at all. ॥14॥
2.3.21.15: Fie on my beauty, and likewise on my birth and my deeds! So she kept saying, constantly remembering Hara's actions. ॥15॥
2.3.21.16: Thus Pārvatī, her mind tormented by separation from Śambhu, found no happiness whatever, and kept saying, Śiva, Śiva. ॥16॥
2.3.21.17: Dwelling in her father's house, her mind fixed on the bearer of Pināka, Śivā grieved, dear son, and swooned again and again. ॥17॥
2.3.21.18: Then the king of mountains, and Menakā too, and all their sons headed by Maināka, steadfast in spirit, consoled her; yet she did not forget Hara. ॥18॥
2.3.21.19: Then, O wise divine sage, you, sent by Indra the slayer of Bala, came of your own free will to the tableland of Himavat. ॥19॥
2.3.21.20: Then you were honoured by that great-souled mountain, and, seated on an excellent seat, you asked him about his welfare. ॥20॥
2.3.21.21: Then the lord of mountains related from the beginning his daughter's story, including her service to Hara and the burning of Kāma by Hara. ॥21॥
2.3.21.22: Having heard this, O sage, you said to that lord of mountains: Worship Śiva. Then, taking leave of him, you rose, remembering Śiva in your mind. ॥22॥
2.3.21.23: Leaving him, you went quickly to that Kālī in private, O sage—you, the benefactor of the world, wise and dear to Śiva. ॥23॥
2.3.21.24: Approaching Kālī and addressing her, intent on her welfare, you, the best of all the wise, spoke true words with respect. ॥24॥
2.3.21.25: Nārada said: Listen, Kālī, to my words; devoted to compassion, I speak the truth—what is wholly beneficial to you, free of fault, and grants good desires. ॥25॥
2.3.21.26: Because Mahādeva was served by you here without austerity, while you were proud, he who shows grace to the humble destroyed that pride. ॥26॥
2.3.21.27: And that Lord of yours, Maheśvara the great yogin, being dispassionate, burned Smara and left you, O Śivā—though he is loving to his devotees. ॥27॥
2.3.21.28: Therefore, devoted to good austerity, worship the Lord for a long time. When you are refined by austerity, Rudra will make you his consort. ॥28॥
2.3.21.29: And you too will never abandon Śaṅkara Śambhu; O goddess, you will not obstinately accept any husband other than Śiva. ॥29॥
2.3.21.30: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of yours, O sage, that daughter of the mountain, Kālī, breathing a little more freely, joyfully spoke to you with folded hands. ॥30॥
2.3.21.31: Śivā said: O all-knowing one, benefactor of the worlds, O lord, O sage, give me a mantra for the worship of Rudra. ॥31॥
2.3.21.32: No rite of anyone succeeds without a true guru; I heard this eternal scriptural teaching long ago, and it is true. ॥32॥
2.3.21.33: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Pārvatī, you, best of sages, imparted to her according to rule the five-syllabled mantra of Śambhu. ॥33॥
2.3.21.34: And, O sage, arousing faith in her, you told her of the power of that king of mantras, which surpasses all. ॥34॥
2.3.21.35: Nārada said: Listen, O goddess, to the supremely wondrous power of this mantra, by the mere hearing of which Śaṅkara is greatly pleased. ॥35॥
2.3.21.36: This mantra is the overlord of all mantras and fulfils desires; it bestows enjoyment and liberation and is exceedingly dear to Śaṅkara. ॥36॥
2.3.21.37: O fortunate one, when this is repeated according to rule, Śiva, thus worshipped, will surely and swiftly appear before you without delay. ॥37॥
2.3.21.38: Meditating on his form and abiding in observances, repeat the five-syllabled mantra, O Śivā; Śiva will quickly be pleased. ॥38॥
2.3.21.39: Thus perform austerity, O virtuous one; Maheśvara is to be won by austerity. Through austerity alone is the fruit obtained by all, never in any other way. ॥39॥
2.3.21.40: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus to Kālī, O Nārada, you, dear to Śiva, wandering at will and devoted to the welfare of the gods, went to heaven. ॥40॥
2.3.21.41: Then Pārvatī, having heard your words, O Nārada, was greatly delighted, and then received the five-syllabled mantra, the most excellent of all. ॥41॥
2.3.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The instruction of Nārada, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥21॥
2.3.22.1: Brahmā said: O divine sage, when you had gone, Pārvatī, glad at heart, judged that Hara could be won through penance, and she set her mind on penance. ॥1॥
2.3.22.2: Then, taking along her two friends, Jayā and Vijayā, she asked leave of her mother and her father through the two friends. ॥2॥
2.3.22.3: First, going to her father Himavat, lord of mountains, and bowing low, she, full of humility, asked him. ॥3॥
2.3.22.4: The two friends said: O Himavat, let your daughter's words be heard, which are now being told: she herself wishes to bring fulfilment to her body and likewise to her beauty, ॥4॥
2.3.22.5: and indeed to this family of yours—she wishes to make them fruitful. He is to be won through penance; otherwise he would not come within sight. ॥5॥
2.3.22.6: Therefore, O best of mountains, permission should now be given by you, respectfully, for Girijā to go to the forest and perform penance. ॥6॥
2.3.22.7: Brahmā said: Thus questioned then by the two friends on Pārvatī's behalf, O best of sages, the king of mountains, after careful thought, said this: ॥7॥
2.3.22.8: Himavān said: It pleases me greatly; let it also please Menā. If this is how it is to be, what could be better than this? ॥8॥
2.3.22.9: It will surely be the fulfilment of my family; there is no doubt. If it pleases her mother too, what could be more auspicious than that? ॥9॥
2.3.22.10: Brahmā said: Having heard these words spoken by the father, the two friends, permitted by him, then went with her to the mother. ॥10॥
2.3.22.11: Going to Pārvatī's mother, O Nārada, they bowed low, joined their palms, and respectfully spoke these words: ॥11॥
2.3.22.12: The two friends said: Mother, O goddess, salutation to you; hear your daughter's words, and having heard them with full grace, you ought to fulfil them here. ॥12॥
2.3.22.13: Your daughter, wishing to perform supreme penance for Śiva's sake, having obtained her father's permission, now asks you as well. ॥13॥
2.3.22.14: She wishes to make her own form fruitful, O devoted wife; if your permission is granted, then she will perform penance accordingly. ॥14॥
2.3.22.15: Brahmā said: Having said this, the two friends then fell silent, O lord of sages. Menā, dejected at heart, did not accept their words. ॥15॥
2.3.22.16: Then Pārvatī herself, humble in spirit, with joined palms and remembering Śiva's lotus feet, spoke to her mother. ॥16॥
2.3.22.17: Pārvatī said: Mother, tomorrow morning I shall go to perform penance in order to attain Maheśvara. Permit me today to go to the penance-grove for penance. ॥17॥
2.3.22.18: Brahmā said: Hearing her daughter's words, Menā was struck with grief; then, distraught, she called her daughter to her and spoke. ॥18॥
2.3.22.19: Menā said: O Śivā, my daughter, if you are pained and longing to perform penance as before, practise penance at home today; do not go outside, Pārvatī. ॥19॥
2.3.22.20: Where are you going to perform penance? The gods are in my house, and all the sacred fords and various holy places too. ॥20॥
2.3.22.21: Do not be obstinate, daughter; you must not go outside anywhere. What did you achieve before by penance? What more will you achieve now? ॥21॥
2.3.22.22: Your body is tender, my child, but penance is hard and great. Therefore you should do your penance here; do not go outside. ॥22॥
2.3.22.23: It has never been heard that women go to a penance-grove in pursuit of a desire. So, daughter, do not set out to go for penance. ॥23॥
2.3.22.24: Brahmā said: Thus the daughter was dissuaded by her mother in many ways. Yet she said: I declare there is no happiness at all without worshipping Maheśvara. ॥24॥
2.3.22.25: Because she was forbidden by Menā with the words u mā (O, do not) from going to the forest for penance, Śivā then received the name Umā. ॥25॥
2.3.22.26: Then, knowing Śivā to be distressed, Menā, beloved of the Mountain, gave Pārvatī her consent for penance, O sage. ॥26॥
2.3.22.27: Having received her mother's permission, O best of sages, Pārvatī of fine vows, remembering Śaṅkara, then felt happiness in her heart. ॥27॥
2.3.22.28: Then Śivā joyfully bowed to her mother and father and, with her two friends, remembering Śiva, set out to perform penance. ॥28॥
2.3.22.29: Casting off her many favourite garments of various kinds, she quickly put on bark garments, having tied on a fine girdle of muñja grass. ॥29॥
2.3.22.30: Laying aside her necklace, she likewise wore an excellent deerskin, and went for penance there, towards Gaṅgāvataraṇa. ॥30॥
2.3.22.31: That plateau of Himavat, where Manobhava (Kāma) was burnt by Śambhu while he was meditating, is named Gaṅgāvataraṇa. ॥31॥
2.3.22.32: Then, O dear one, coming there, Kālī—Pārvatī, the Mother of the world—saw that plateau of the snow-mountain empty of Hara. ॥32॥
2.3.22.33: Where Śambhu had formerly stayed and performed arduous penance, there she stood for a moment and became afflicted by separation. ॥33॥
2.3.22.34: There Śivā, the mountain's daughter, weeping and crying, alas, Hara, lamented, deeply pained by grief and filled with anxiety and sorrow. ॥34॥
2.3.22.35: Then after a long while Pārvatī, daughter of Himavat, steadied her bewilderment through fortitude and was consecrated there for the observance of vows. ॥35॥
2.3.22.36: She performed penance there at the most excellent Śṛṅgitīrtha; because of her penance there, that place came to be called Gaurīśikhara. ॥36॥
2.3.22.37: There, O sage, Śivā planted beautiful, sacred trees, fruit-bearing, as a test of her penance. ॥37॥
2.3.22.38: Then the beautiful one purified the ground, built an altar, and so began a penance hard even for sages. ॥38॥
2.3.22.39: Quickly restraining all the senses together with the mind, she performed supreme penance there, in that place close at hand. ॥39॥
2.3.22.40: In summer, having kindled a fire blazing all around her day and night, she stood in its midst, continually reciting the mantra. ॥40॥
2.3.22.41: And in the rainy season, sitting firmly and constantly on the bare ground and on the surface of a rock, she was drenched by the torrents of water. ॥41॥
2.3.22.42: In the cold season she stood constantly in the midst of water, wholly intent on devotion; fasting, she performed penance there amid the snows and through the nights. ॥42॥
2.3.22.43: Thus performing penance, devoted to the recitation of the five-syllabled mantra, Śivā meditated there on Śiva, the giver of the fruits of all desires. ॥43॥
2.3.22.44: Joyfully watering, with her friends, the auspicious trees she herself had planted, she offered hospitality there every day whenever she had leisure. ॥44॥
2.3.22.45: Wind, and cold rain of many kinds, and heat too though hard to bear, were all endured by her, steady of mind. ॥45॥
2.3.22.46: The various hardships that came upon her there she did not reckon; fixing her mind on Śiva alone, she remained steadfast, O sage. ॥46॥
2.3.22.47: Performing penance first by eating fruits and then by eating leaves, the goddess gradually passed countless years. ॥47॥
2.3.22.48: Then Śivā, the daughter of Himavat, giving up even leaves, became wholly without food, the goddess absorbed in the practice of penance. ॥48॥
2.3.22.49: Because the daughter of Himavat gave up leaves as food, Śivā was therefore called by the gods by the name Aparṇā. ॥49॥
2.3.22.50: Pārvatī stood on one foot, remembering Śiva, and reciting the five-syllabled mantra she performed great penance. ॥50॥
2.3.22.51: Clad in rags and bark garments, wearing a mass of matted locks, absorbed in contemplation of Śiva, she surpassed the sages by her penance. ॥51॥
2.3.22.52: As Kālī thus practised penance, meditating on Maheśvara, three thousand years passed in the penance-grove. ॥52॥
2.3.22.53: Then, having stayed for a moment at the place where Hara had performed penance for sixty thousand years, Śivā reflected: ॥53॥
2.3.22.54: O Mahādeva, do you not know me now, abiding in my vows, that I, devoted to penance for so long, have not been sought out by you? ॥54॥
2.3.22.55: In the world and in the Veda, Giriśa is ever sung of by the sages: that Śaṅkara is indeed all-knowing, the Self of all, all-seeing, ॥55॥
2.3.22.56: the god who bestows all prosperity, who brings about all states of being, who ever grants the wishes of his devotees and removes all afflictions. ॥56॥
2.3.22.57: If, having renounced all desires, I am devoted to the bull-bannered one, then may that Śaṅkara be gracious to me here. ॥57॥
2.3.22.58: If the five-syllabled mantra taught in the Nārada Tantra has been recited by me daily with true devotion and according to rule, may Śaṅkara be gracious. ॥58॥
2.3.22.59: If, through devotion to Śiva, the Lord of all, I am utterly unwavering as has been prescribed, may Śaṅkara be gracious. ॥59॥
2.3.22.60: Thus reflecting constantly, she performed penance for a very long time, face bowed down, unwavering, wearing matted locks and bark garments. ॥60॥
2.3.22.61: Such penance was performed by her as is difficult even for sages; recalling it, the people there were struck with the highest wonder. ॥61॥
2.3.22.62: They all came together to see that penance; considering themselves blessed, they spoke thus in agreement: ॥62॥
2.3.22.63: Going to those who are advanced in dharma is declared the highest good even for the great. There is no measure for penance; dharma is always to be honoured by the wise. ॥63॥
2.3.22.64: Having heard of and seen her penance, what penance is it that others perform? Greater penance than this has never been in the world, nor will be. ॥64॥
2.3.22.65: Speaking thus, all of them, having highly praised Śivā's penance, went joyfully to their own abodes, even those who were hardened in body. ॥65॥
2.3.22.66: Now hear, O great sage, another great and most wondrous effect of the penance of Pārvatī, the Mother of the world. ॥66॥
2.3.22.67: Those creatures which came to her hermitage, though hostile by nature, then became free of enmity through its power. ॥67॥
2.3.22.68: Lions and cows, ever subject to faults such as passion, did not harm one another there, by her greatness. ॥68॥
2.3.22.69: Moreover, O best of sages, others too, such as cats and mice, enemies by nature, never behaved with hostility there. ॥69॥
2.3.22.70: There the trees bore fruit, and there were grasses of many kinds and colourful flowers, O best of sages. ॥70॥
2.3.22.71: And that whole forest then became comparable to Kailāsa; it became the very embodiment of the fulfilment of her penance. ॥71॥
2.3.22.iti: Thus ends the twenty-second adhyāya, named The description of the austerity of Pārvatī, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥22॥
2.3.23.1: Brahmā said: O lord of sages, while Pārvatī was thus performing austerities to attain Śiva, a long time passed, but Hara did not appear. ॥1॥
2.3.23.2: Then Himālaya, together with his wife, his sons and his ministers, came and spoke to Pārvatī, the supreme goddess, who had made her firm resolve. ॥2॥
2.3.23.3: Himavān said: Do not torment yourself with this austerity, O greatly fortunate Pārvatī. Rudra is not to be seen, child; he is detached from worldly attachment, there is no doubt about this. ॥3॥
2.3.23.4: You are slender, with delicate limbs, and you will become overcome by this austerity, no doubt; I tell you the truth, the truth. ॥4॥
2.3.23.5: Therefore rise and come to your own home, O fair one. What have you to do with that Rudra, by whom Smara was burnt long ago? ॥5॥
2.3.23.6: Hence, because he is free from any passion, Hara will not come to take you, excellent as you are, O queen of the gods; how will you win him by entreaty? ॥6॥
2.3.23.7: Just as the moon standing in the sky cannot be seized, so too, O sinless one, know Śambhu here to be beyond reach. ॥7॥
2.3.23.8: Brahmā said: In the same way the virtuous maiden was addressed by Menā, likewise by the Sahya mountain, by Meru, by Mandara, and likewise by Maināka. ॥8॥
2.3.23.9: So too the unperturbed Girijā was addressed in the same manner by other mountains such as Krauñca, who put forward various arguments. ॥9॥
2.3.23.10: When the slender maiden, steadfast in austerity, had been thus addressed by all, she of pure smile spoke to Himavat, laughing. ॥10॥
2.3.23.11: Pārvatī said: Father, mother, I told you before—have you forgotten it? Even now, hear my vow, O my kinsmen. ॥11॥
2.3.23.12: That Mahādeva is indeed detached, he by whom Smara was burnt in wrath; yet I will please that Śaṅkara, who is loving to his devotees, through austerity. ॥12॥
2.3.23.13: All of you, go happily each to your own abode. He will surely be pleased; there need be no deliberation about this. ॥13॥
2.3.23.14: He by whom Madana was burnt, by whom the forest of the mountain was burnt—him I shall bring right here by austerity alone. ॥14॥
2.3.23.15: By the great power of austerity Sadāśiva is easily won; know this, O fortunate ones—I tell you the truth, the truth. ॥15॥
2.3.23.16: Having thus addressed Menakā, her father Himālaya the kinsman of Maināka, together with Mandara, Girijā—Śivā, the sweet-spoken daughter of the king of mountains—quickly fell silent. ॥16॥
2.3.23.17: Thus addressed by Śivā, those wise mountains, led by the lord of the golden mountain, went back the way they had come, greatly astonished, praising Girijā again and again. ॥17॥
2.3.23.18: When they had all gone, she, surrounded by her friends and firmly resolved on the supreme goal, performed austerity even more intensely. ॥18॥
2.3.23.19: By that great austerity, O best of sages, all that moves and does not move—the three worlds with gods, asuras and humans—became heated. ॥19॥
2.3.23.20: Then all the gods and asuras, yakṣas, kinnaras and cāraṇas, siddhas and sādhyas, sages, vidyādharas and great serpents, ॥20॥
2.3.23.21: together with the Prajāpatis, the guhyakas and others too, fell into ever greater distress, and they did not know its cause. ॥21॥
2.3.23.22: All of them, led by Śakra, gathering together in agitation and having consulted their preceptor, with all their limbs scorched, went to me, Vidhi, on Sumeru for refuge. ॥22॥
2.3.23.23: Having gone there, agitated and with their splendour lost, they quickly bowed, and all of them, praising me, spoke to me with one voice. ॥23॥
2.3.23.24: The gods said: This whole world, moving and unmoving, created by you, is intensely heated—for what reason? The cause is not known, O lord. ॥24॥
2.3.23.25: So tell us the cause, O Brahmā; you should find it out for us, O lord. For the gods whose bodies are burnt, there is no protector other than you. ॥25॥
2.3.23.26: Brahmā said: Hearing their words, I remembered Śiva in my heart and, reflecting on everything in my mind, realised that it was the result of Girijā's austerity, ॥26॥
2.3.23.27: and knowing that the universe was being burnt, I went quickly, respectfully, with all of them, to the Ocean of Milk to tell this to Hari. ॥27॥
2.3.23.28: Having gone there and seen Hari resplendent on his comfortable seat, I bowed deeply, praised him well, and spoke with folded hands, together with the gods. ॥28॥
2.3.23.29: Save us, save us, O Mahāviṣṇu. We have come to you for refuge, scorched by the fierce and supreme austerity of Pārvatī, who is engaged in penance. ॥29॥
2.3.23.30: Hearing these words of us dwellers of heaven, beginning with me, the lord of Ramā, seated on Śeṣa, spoke to us. ॥30॥
2.3.23.31: Viṣṇu said: The whole cause, Pārvatī's austerity, is now known to me. Together with you, I go today to the Supreme Lord. ॥31॥
2.3.23.32: We shall entreat that Mahādeva to accept Girijā, for the purpose of taking her hand in marriage now, O immortals, for the welfare of the worlds. ॥32॥
2.3.23.33: The god of gods, the bearer of Pināka, will go there to give a boon to Śivā; and as he wishes, so we shall now do there. ॥33॥
2.3.23.34: Therefore we shall go where Rudra, the great lord, supremely auspicious, now dwells engaged in fierce austerity. ॥34॥
2.3.23.35: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of Viṣṇu, all the gods and the others, greatly afraid of the angry one who wished to burn and who causes dissolution, spoke vehemently: ॥35॥
2.3.23.36: The gods said: None of us will go to Virūpākṣa, the great lord, who is most terrifying, angry, and blazing like the fire of final destruction. ॥36॥
2.3.23.37: Just as he once burnt Madana, who was hard to overcome, so too, filled with anger, he will burn us—there is no doubt. ॥37॥
2.3.23.38: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of Śakra and the others, O sage, Hari, the lord of Ramā, consoling all those gods, spoke. ॥38॥
2.3.23.39: Hari said: O gods, all of you, listen to my words with goodwill and attention. That lord, the destroyer of the gods' fear, will not burn you. ॥39॥
2.3.23.40: Therefore, wise ones, you should go with me to the refuge of that good lord, regarding Śambhu as the bestower of welfare. ॥40॥
2.3.23.41: We go for refuge to that Śiva, the ancient Person, the supreme Lord, whose form is most worthy of choice, the supreme ancient one, who is devoted to austerity, whose form is the Supreme Self, higher than the highest. ॥41॥
2.3.23.42: Brahmā said: Thus addressed then by the mighty Viṣṇu, all the gods went with him, wishing to see the bearer of the Pināka bow. ॥42॥
2.3.23.43: First, since it lay on their way, all of them, Viṣṇu and the others, full of curiosity, went to the hermitage of the mountain's daughter to see her austerity. ॥43॥
2.3.23.44: Having seen Pārvatī's excellent austerity, and being then enveloped by her radiance, they bowed to her, the sustainer of the world, whose form was radiance and who was established in austerity. ॥44॥
2.3.23.45: Praising the austerity of her who was perfection (siddhi) embodied, the gods then went to the place where the bull-bannered Śiva was. ॥45॥
2.3.23.46: Having gone there, the gods then sent you, O sage, and stood watching from afar, fearing Hara who had reduced Kāma to ashes. ॥46॥
2.3.23.47: O Nārada, you, ever fearless and a devotee of Śiva in particular, then went to Śiva's abode and saw the Lord pleased. ॥47॥
2.3.23.48: Returning, you then carefully summoned those gods and led Viṣṇu and the others to Śaṅkara's abode, O sage. ॥48॥
2.3.23.49: Then Viṣṇu and all the others, having gone there, saw Lord Śiva seated at ease, gracious, affectionate to his devotees. ॥49॥
2.3.23.50: They saw Śambhu seated in the yoga posture with the yoga-band, surrounded by his Gaṇas, bearing the form of austerity, embodying the Supreme Lord. ॥50॥
2.3.23.51: Then Viṣṇu, I Brahmā, and the others—gods, Siddhas and chief sages—bowed and praised him with hymns drawn from the Vedas and Upaniṣads. ॥51॥
2.3.23.iti: Thus ends the twenty-third adhyāya, named The description of the consoling of Pārvatī and of the gods' sight of Śiva, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥23॥
2.3.24.1: The gods said: Obeisance to Rudra, the god, and to the one who put an end to Madana; to the one worthy of praise, to the one of abundant radiance, to the three-eyed one, obeisance, obeisance. ॥1॥
2.3.24.2: Obeisance again and again to Śipiviṣṭa, to the terrible one, to the one of terrible eyes. Obeisance to Mahādeva, the lord, the master of heaven. ॥2॥
2.3.24.3: You are the protector of all the worlds, the father and the mother; you are the Lord. You are Śambhu, Īśa, Śaṅkara; you are especially compassionate. ॥3॥
2.3.24.4: You are the creator of all the worlds; you ought to protect us, O lord. Without you, who is able to destroy our sorrow, O Maheśvara? ॥4॥
2.3.24.5: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the gods, Nandikeśvara, filled with supreme compassion, began to petition Śambhu. ॥5॥
2.3.24.6: Nandīśvara said: The hosts of gods headed by Viṣṇu and the assemblies of sages and Siddhas are especially eager just to see you, O best of gods. Seeking the fulfilment of their purpose, being harassed by the chief Asuras, they have fallen utterly into the deepest state of defeat. ॥6॥
2.3.24.7: Therefore, O lord of all, the sages and gods must indeed be protected by you. You are especially called the friend of the distressed and the one affectionate to devotees. ॥7॥
