2.3.24.8: Brahmā said: Thus earnestly petitioned by the compassionate Nandin, Śambhu slowly withdrew from meditation, opening his eyes. ॥8॥
2.3.24.9: Then the Lord Śambhu, supremely wise, the Supreme Self, having withdrawn from samādhi, spoke to all the gods. ॥9॥
2.3.24.10: Śambhu said: Why have you come to my presence, O lords of gods, all of you headed by Hari and Brahmā? Tell me that reason quickly. ॥10॥
2.3.24.11: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Śambhu, all the gods, filled with joy, looked at Viṣṇu's face so that he would make the petition. ॥11॥
2.3.24.12: Then Viṣṇu, the great devotee, the benefactor of the gods, spoke this most important task of the gods, as had been told to him by me. ॥12॥
2.3.24.13: O Śambhu, Tāraka has inflicted on the gods a most extraordinary distress, worse than the worst; all the gods have come to make this known. ॥13॥
2.3.24.14: O Śambhu, the demon Tāraka will be slain only by your own begotten son; my words are not otherwise. ॥14॥
2.3.24.15: Considering this, O Mahādeva, show mercy; obeisance to you. O master, rescue the gods from the distress caused by Tāraka. ॥15॥
2.3.24.16: Therefore, O god Śambhu, Girijā must be taken by you with your right hand. Through the very rite of taking her hand, make your own that noble one, given by the lord of mountains. ॥16॥
2.3.24.17: Hearing those words of Viṣṇu, Śiva, devoted to yoga, was pleased and spoke, showing all of them the good path. ॥17॥
2.3.24.18: Śiva said: When the goddess Girijā, beautiful in every way, is accepted by me, then all the lords of gods, the munis and the ṛṣis, then— ॥18॥
2.3.24.19: —will become full of desire and will not be capable on the supreme path. Through the marriage, that Durgā will bring Smara back to life. ॥19॥
2.3.24.20: Madana was burnt by me for the accomplishment of everyone's purpose, at Brahmā's word, O Viṣṇu; there should be no doubt about this. ॥20॥
2.3.24.21: Having thus reflected in your mind on the determination of what should and should not be done, you who are wise, O lord of gods, should not, together with all these, press me insistently. ॥21॥
2.3.24.22: With Kāma burnt by me, O Viṣṇu, a great task of the gods has been accomplished. Let all remain free of desire together with me—this is certain. ॥22॥
2.3.24.23: Just as I do, so you, all the gods, will effortlessly perform extremely difficult austerity, endowed with supreme self-control. ॥23॥
2.3.24.24: O gods, through that samādhi, without Madana, may you be endowed with supreme bliss and free from all perturbation. ॥24॥
2.3.24.25: O Vidhi, O Hari, O Mahendra, O sages and gods, let all that former event caused by Smara, which has been forgotten, be reflected upon. ॥25॥
2.3.24.26: O gods, by that very Madana, the great bowman, the meditation of all was forcibly destroyed in the past, O immortals. ॥26॥
2.3.24.27: Desire leads only to hell; from it anger arises. From anger comes delusion, and through delusion austerity is lost. ॥27॥
2.3.24.28: Desire and anger must be abandoned by you, the best of gods. And my word must be heeded by all of you, never otherwise. ॥28॥
2.3.24.29: Brahmā said: Having thus made them hear, the blessed Mahādeva, whose banner bears the bull, instructed the gods, Vidhi and Viṣṇu, and likewise the sages. ॥29॥
2.3.24.30: Śambhu became silent, resorting once more to meditation, and remained as before like a motionless pillar, surrounded by his gaṇas. ॥30॥
2.3.24.31: Śambhu contemplated his own Self by the Self within the Self alone—stainless, beyond appearance, changeless, free from affliction, ॥31॥
2.3.24.32: higher than the highest, eternal, free of possessiveness, unrestricted, beyond words, attributeless, attainable through knowledge, transcending the transcendent. ॥32॥
2.3.24.33: Thus contemplating his supreme nature, established in meditation, the creator of manifold beings became immersed in supreme bliss. ॥33॥
2.3.24.34: Seeing the lord of all established in meditation, all the heaven-dwellers, headed by Hari and Śakra, bowing down, spoke to Nandin. ॥34॥
2.3.24.35: The gods said: What shall we do now? Śambhu, detached, is established in meditation. You are Śaṅkara's friend, all-knowing, a pure servant. ॥35॥
2.3.24.36: By what means may Giriśa become pleased, O lord of gaṇas? Tell us that means; we have come to you for refuge. ॥36॥
2.3.24.37: Brahmā said: Thus petitioned then by the gods headed by Hari, O sage, Nandin, the gaṇa dear to Śambhu, replied to those gods. ॥37॥
2.3.24.38: Nandīśvara said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O Śakra, O immortals and sages, listen to my words, which will bring about Śiva's satisfaction. ॥38॥
2.3.24.39: If you are indeed insistent today on Śiva's taking a wife, then all of you, in utter humility, offer fine praise with reverence. ॥39॥
2.3.24.40: Mahādeva is won over by devotion, O gods, not by ordinary means. Through true devotion the Supreme Lord does even what ought not to be done. ॥40॥
2.3.24.41: So act, all you gods headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu; otherwise go back by the way you came, without delay. ॥41॥
2.3.24.42: Brahmā said: Having heard his words, O sage, the gods headed by Viṣṇu, thinking, so be it, praised Śaṅkara with great delight. ॥42॥
2.3.24.43: O God of gods, Mahādeva, ocean of compassion, Lord, lift us out of great distress; protect us who have come to you for refuge. ॥43॥
2.3.24.44: Brahmā said: Thus, with very piteous words, the gods praised Śaṅkara; all of them wept aloud, their minds overwhelmed by love. ॥44॥
2.3.24.45: Hari, together with me, made an earnest petition with very humble words, remembering Śambhu in his mind, filled with supreme devotion. ॥45॥
2.3.24.46: Thus intensely praised by the gods, by Hari and by me, Śambhu, the Great Lord, out of affection for his devotees, came out of meditation. ॥46॥
2.3.24.47: Hara, very gracious at heart, gladdening Hari and the others, looking upon them with a compassionate glance, Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, spoke. ॥47॥
2.3.24.48: Śaṅkara said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods headed by Śakra, all of you together — for what purpose have you come? Tell the truth before me. ॥48॥
2.3.24.49: Hari said: You are omniscient, O Maheśāna, the inner controller, lord of all. Do you not know what lies in our minds? Still, at your command, I shall speak. ॥49॥
2.3.24.50: Manifold suffering has arisen for all of us from the asura Tāraka, O Mṛḍa; it is for that reason that you have been propitiated by the gods. ॥50॥
2.3.24.51: That Śivā has been born from the mountain Himālaya for your sake. His death can come only from a son born of you in her, and not otherwise. ॥51॥
2.3.24.52: Since such a boon was given to that demon by Brahmā, he cannot die at anyone else's hands, and he oppresses the whole world. ॥52॥
2.3.24.53: At Nārada's instruction she is performing severe penance; by its fiery energy the entire three worlds, with all moving and unmoving beings, are pervaded. ॥53॥
2.3.24.54: Go, O Supreme Lord, to grant the boon to Śivā; destroy the gods' suffering, O master, and bring us happiness. ॥54॥
2.3.24.55: In the hearts of the gods and in mine there is great eagerness to behold your marriage, O Śaṅkara; therefore do what is fitting. ॥55॥
2.3.24.56: The occasion for the boon you granted to Rati has now swiftly arrived, O higher than the highest; make your promise fruitful. ॥56॥
2.3.24.57: Brahmā said: Having said this and bowed to him, Viṣṇu, the gods and the great sages, having praised him with various hymns, all stood before him. ॥57॥
2.3.24.58: Then Śaṅkara, who is subject to his devotees and guardian of the bounds of the Veda, having heard the gods' words, laughed and replied at once. ॥58॥
2.3.24.59: Śaṅkara said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods, all of you listen attentively. I shall speak what is fitting, in detail and with discernment. ॥59॥
2.3.24.60: Entering into marriage is surely not a fitting course for men; marriage, known as a great fetter, is a firm bondage. ॥60॥
2.3.24.61: There are many evil attachments in the world, and among them attachment to women is the greatest. One may be released from all bonds, but one is not freed from attachment to women. ॥61॥
2.3.24.62: Even one firmly bound with fetters of iron and wood is set free; but one tightly bound by the fetters of women and the like is never set free. ॥62॥
2.3.24.63: Sense-objects, which cause great bondage, keep on increasing; for one whose mind is overpowered by sense-objects, liberation is hard to attain even in a dream. ॥63॥
2.3.24.64: If a wise man desires happiness, he should duly renounce sense-objects. They call sense-objects poison-like, for by sense-objects one is destroyed. ॥64॥
2.3.24.65: A person falls in an instant merely through conversation with a sensualist. The teachers call sense-enjoyment an indravāruṇī (bitter colocynth) coated with sugar. ॥65॥
2.3.24.66: Although I know all this, and all knowledge in particular, nevertheless I shall make your request fruitful. ॥66॥
2.3.24.67: I am indeed dependent on my devotees; under their sway I do every deed. I am famed in the three worlds as one who does even what is not fitting. ॥67॥
2.3.24.68: The vow of Sudakṣiṇa, king and lord of Kāmarūpa, who had fallen into bondage, was made fruitful by me. ॥68॥
2.3.24.69: In the matter of Gautama's affliction I acted as Tryambaka, the bringer of happiness, and in particular I pronounced a curse on the wicked ones who had caused him that trouble. ॥69॥
2.3.24.70: Bearing the disposition of love for my devotees, I drank the poison for the sake of the gods; O gods, the gods' distress has always been removed by me with effort. ॥70॥
2.3.24.71: For my devotees' sake I have endured hardship many times with great effort; becoming Gṛhapati, I removed the sorrow of the sage Viśvānara. ॥71॥
2.3.24.72: What need of saying much, O Hari, O Vidhi? I speak the truth: you all truly know that this is my vow. ॥72॥
2.3.24.73: Whenever and wherever misfortune befalls my devotees, then I always remove it swiftly, at that very moment, completely. ॥73॥
2.3.24.74: I know the suffering that has arisen for all of you from Tāraka; I shall remove that suffering caused by the asura — truly, truly I say. ॥74॥
2.3.24.75: Although I have no desire whatever to marry, I shall marry Girijā for the purpose of begetting a son. ॥75॥
2.3.24.76: Go to your own homes, all you gods, free from fear. I shall accomplish your task; there is no need for any doubt in this. ॥76॥
2.3.24.77: Brahmā said: Having said this, Hara observed silence and became absorbed in samādhi; and all the gods headed by Viṣṇu went to their own abodes, O sage. ॥77॥
2.3.24.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fourth adhyāya, named The acceptance of marriage with Pārvatī, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥24॥
2.3.25.1: Nārada said: When those gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the rest, and all the sages had gone away gladly, what happened after that? ॥1॥
2.3.25.2: What did Śambhu do, dear father? After how long, and in what way, did he come to grant the boon? Tell me that and bring me joy. ॥2॥
2.3.25.3: Brahmā said: When those gods, Brahmā and the others, had gone to their own abodes, Bhava became absorbed in samādhi in order to test her penance thoroughly. ॥3॥
2.3.25.4: Making his own Self the object by the Self, he contemplated within his own Self that which is higher than the highest, self-abiding, free of māyā and unconstrained. ॥4॥
2.3.25.5: He, the blessed Lord bearing the bull-banner, who is himself that reality, whose ways are unknown, the source of all, is Hara, the supreme Lord. ॥5॥
2.3.25.6: Brahmā said: Then indeed, dear son, Girijā performed supreme penance; by that penance even Rudra came to great amazement. ॥6॥
2.3.25.7: He was stirred from his samādhi, being subject to his devotee, and not for any other reason. Hara, the creator, called to mind the seven sages, Vasiṣṭha and the rest. ॥7॥
2.3.25.8: All seven sages came at once, merely upon being remembered, all with cheerful faces, greatly extolling their good fortune. ॥8॥
2.3.25.9: Bowing to that great Lord, full of joy, they praised him with faltering voices, hands joined and necks bent low. ॥9॥
2.3.25.10: The seven sages said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, ocean of compassion, O Lord, we have become truly blessed, since you have now remembered us. ॥10॥
2.3.25.11: For what purpose have we been called to mind, O Lord? Give us that command. O master, show us grace befitting your own servants; salutation to you. ॥11॥
2.3.25.12: Brahmā said: Hearing this request of the sages, the treasury of compassion, his lotus-eyes blooming, spoke smiling with affection. ॥12॥
2.3.25.13: Maheśvara said: O seven sages, dear ones, listen promptly to my words. You are doers of my welfare, skilled in all knowledge. ॥13॥
2.3.25.14: Pārvatī Girijā, the queen of the gods, is now performing penance with a resolute mind on the mountain called Gaurīśikhara. ॥14॥
2.3.25.15: Wishing to obtain me as husband, she, attended by her friends, O brahmins, has abandoned all other desires and reached a supreme resolve. ॥15॥
2.3.25.16: Go there at my command, O best of sages, and test the firmness of her loving heart. ॥16॥
2.3.25.17: Your speech should be wholly full of deceit. Have no hesitation, O ones of good vows, since it is by my command. ॥17॥
2.3.25.18: Brahmā said: Thus commanded, those sages went swiftly to where the radiant Mother of the world, the mountain's daughter, was shining. ॥18॥
2.3.25.19: There they saw Śivā, like a second, embodied perfection of penance itself, of supreme brilliance, shining with great splendour. ॥19॥
2.3.25.20: Bowing to her in their hearts, those seven sages of good vows, humbly inclined and specially honoured by her, spoke these words. ॥20॥
2.3.25.21: The sages said: Listen, O goddess, daughter of the mountain: why is this penance being performed? Which god do you desire, and what is the fruit? Tell us that now. ॥21॥
2.3.25.22: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by the brahmins, the goddess Śivā, daughter of the lord of mountains, replied truthfully before them, though the matter was a deep secret. ॥22॥
2.3.25.23: Pārvatī said: O lords of sages, listen with an affectionate heart to my words. I shall tell you my own resolve, which I have pondered with my own mind. ॥23॥
2.3.25.24: You will laugh at me on hearing words about something impossible. O brahmins, I feel shy about describing it; but what can I do? ॥24॥
2.3.25.25: This mind of mine is very firm, yet beyond control, doing others' bidding; it wishes to build a great, towering wall upon water. ॥25॥
2.3.25.26: Having received the instruction of the divine sage, I perform very firm penance, cherishing the wish that Rudra may become my husband. ॥26॥
2.3.25.27: The bird of my mind, though wingless, insists on flying up into the sky. May Lord Śaṅkara, treasury of compassion, fulfil that hope. ॥27॥
2.3.25.28: Brahmā said: Hearing her words, those sages laughed, and, honouring Girijā affectionately, spoke false words full of deceit. ॥28॥
2.3.25.29: The sages said: O daughter of the mountain, though you are very wise, you have not understood the conduct of that divine sage, cruel-minded and falsely proud of his learning. ॥29॥
2.3.25.30: Nārada is a deceitful talker who churns up others' minds; by listening to his words harm comes in every way. ॥30॥
2.3.25.31: In this regard, listen with a good mind to a fine story; as we instruct you step by step with affection, take it to heart. ॥31॥
2.3.25.32: Dakṣa, the son of Brahmā, at his father's command begot ten thousand sons on his own wife and set those dear sons to penance. ॥32॥
2.3.25.33: Those sons went to Nārāyaṇa-saras in the western direction, having vowed themselves to penance; Nārada went there too. ॥33॥
2.3.25.34: There the sage Nārada made them hear a deceptive teaching, and by his direction all of them did not return to their father's house. ॥34॥
2.3.25.35: Hearing that, Dakṣa was enraged; his mind consoled by his father, he then begot sons numbering a thousand and engaged them likewise. ॥35॥
2.3.25.36: Those sons too went there for penance at their father's command; and Nārada went there again, to give his own teaching. ॥36॥
2.3.25.37: He gave them that same teaching; they went the way of their brothers, did not return to their father's house, and became devoted to the mendicant's life. ॥37॥
2.3.25.38: Such is Nārada's famous good conduct, O daughter of the mountain. Hear another deed of his, which makes men turn away from the world. ॥38॥
2.3.25.39: There was a Vidyādhara named Citraketu; formerly Nārada, having given him his own kind of teaching, made his house empty. ॥39॥
2.3.25.40: Having given his teachings to Prahlāda, this splitter of others' minds also brought great grief to Hiraṇyakaśipu. ॥40॥
2.3.25.41: Whoever is made by that sage Nārada to hear his own lore, so pleasing to the ear, quickly leaves his home and, as a rule, wanders about begging. ॥41॥
2.3.25.42: Nārada is indeed dark of mind, though always bright of body. We know him especially well, since we are his companions. ॥42॥
2.3.25.43: People describe the heron as a saint, as though it never eats fish at all; but a companion knows the character of his companions. ॥43॥
2.3.25.44: Having received his instruction, you too, though esteemed by the wise, have become foolish for nothing and are performing austerity that is hard to do. ॥44॥
2.3.25.45: He for whose sake, O girl, you perform such vast austerity is indifferent, unchanging, the enemy of Madana — there is no doubt. ॥45॥
2.3.25.46: He bears an inauspicious body, is shameless, homeless, without lineage, ill-dressed, keeps company with ghosts, spirits and the like, is naked, and carries a trident. ॥46॥
2.3.25.47: That rogue, having destroyed your discernment by his own māyā, deluded you with clever reasoning and made you perform austerity. ॥47॥
2.3.25.48: Having obtained such a husband, what happiness will there be? Consider this yourself, O goddess, O daughter of the mountain. ॥48॥
2.3.25.49: First, having married with good intent the virtuous Satī, Dakṣa's daughter, the fool did not keep up the marriage for even a few days. ॥49॥
2.3.25.50: Likewise, that lord himself, laying blame on her, abandoned her, and meditating on his own partless, sorrowless nature, he rejoiced, content. ॥50॥
2.3.25.51: He is solitary, supremely at rest, unattached and non-dual; how, O goddess, will a woman's life with him be sustained? ॥51॥
2.3.25.52: Even now, accepting our counsel, come home and give up this wrong resolve, O fortunate one, and there will be well-being for you. ॥52॥
2.3.25.53: The husband worthy of you is Viṣṇu, the lord endowed with every good quality, dweller in Vaikuṇṭha, lord of Lakṣmī, skilled in many kinds of play. ॥53॥
2.3.25.54: We will arrange your marriage with him, which will give every happiness. So give up such obstinacy and be happy, O Pārvatī. ॥54॥
2.3.25.55: Brahmā said: Hearing such words, Pārvatī, the Mother of the world, laughed and spoke again to the sages learned in knowledge. ॥55॥
2.3.25.56: Pārvatī said: What you have said from your own knowledge is true, O lords of sages; but my resolve is not given up, O twice-born. ॥56॥
2.3.25.57: Because my body is born of a mountain, hardness is natural to it. Considering this wisely, you ought not to dissuade me. ॥57॥
2.3.25.58: I shall never abandon the wholesome words of the divine sage; the knowers of the Veda know that the words of gurus are wholesome. ॥58॥
2.3.25.59: Those whose conviction is firm that the gurus' words are true have supreme happiness here and hereafter, and never unhappiness anywhere. ॥59॥
2.3.25.60: Those in whose heart there is no conviction that the gurus' words are true have sorrow both here and hereafter, and never happiness. ॥60॥
2.3.25.61: In no way should the gurus' words be abandoned, O twice-born. Whether I come to dwell in a home or it remains empty, my resolve is always a source of joy to me. ॥61॥
2.3.25.62: The words you have so well spoken, O best of sages, are otherwise in truth; I shall describe the discernment of it briefly. ॥62॥
2.3.25.63: Viṣṇu is indeed proclaimed the abode of qualities and one given to play; Sadāśiva is declared to be beyond qualities. The reason for this is now told. ॥63॥
2.3.25.64: Śiva is the changeless Brahman; he has assumed a form for the sake of his devotees, and he does not wish to display worldly lordship. ॥64॥
2.3.25.65: Therefore Śambhu, who is supreme bliss, takes on, in the form of an avadhūta, the way of life most dear to the paramahaṃsas. ॥65॥
2.3.25.66: A liking for ornaments and the like belongs to those smeared with māyā, not to Brahman. That lord is beyond qualities, unborn, free of māyā, of imperceptible course, the cosmic being (virāṭ). ॥66॥
2.3.25.67: Śambhu does not bestow grace on the basis of dharma, caste and the like, O twice-born. Only by my guru's grace do I know Śiva as he truly is. ॥67॥
2.3.25.68: If that Śiva will not marry me, O brahmins, I shall remain unmarried forever. Truly, truly I say this. ॥68॥
2.3.25.69: Even if the sun should rise in the western quarter, if Meru should move, if fire should turn cold, if a lotus should bloom on a rock on a mountain peak — my resolve will not waver. This truth I declare. ॥69॥
2.3.25.70: Brahmā said: Having said this and quickly bowed to those sages, the daughter of the mountain fell silent, remembering Śiva with an unwavering mind. ॥70॥
2.3.25.71: The sages too, thus recognising Girijā's firm resolve, uttered words of victory there and gave her an excellent blessing. ॥71॥
2.3.25.72: Then, bowing to that goddess, the sages who had tested her, glad at heart, went swiftly to Śiva's abode, O sage. ॥72॥
2.3.25.73: Having gone there, bowed to Śiva and reported that whole account, they received his leave and went respectfully to heaven. ॥73॥
2.3.25.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fifth adhyāya, named The description of the test made by the seven sages, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥25॥
2.3.26.1: Brahmā said: When those sages had gone to their own world, Śaṅkara himself, the Lord and creator, wished to test the Devī's penance. ॥1॥
2.3.26.2: On the pretext of a test, Śambhu, pleased at heart, wishing to see her, assumed the form of a matted-haired ascetic and went to Pārvatī's forest. ॥2॥
2.3.26.3: Very aged, bearing the body of a brahmin, blazing with his own splendour, delighted in mind, he became one carrying a staff and an umbrella. ॥3॥
2.3.26.4: There he saw the Devī seated on a raised altar, surrounded by her friends, pure, like an auspicious digit of the moon. ॥4॥
2.3.26.5: Having beheld that Devī, Śambhu, in the form of a celibate student, the one affectionate to his devotees, then went near her with love. ॥5॥
2.3.26.6: Seeing that brahmin arrived then, wondrous in his radiance, the Devī Śivā worshipped him with all the offerings of worship. ॥6॥
2.3.26.7: The brahmin, well honoured with due rites and worshipped with supreme joy, Pārvatī respectfully and lovingly asked about his welfare. ॥7॥
2.3.26.8: Pārvatī said: Who are you, in the form of a celibate student, and from where have you come? You illumine this forest. Tell me, O best of the knowers of the Veda. ॥8॥
2.3.26.9: The brahmin said: I am one who goes wherever he wishes, an old man in a brahmin's body, wise, an ascetic, a giver of happiness to others and a benefactor—there is no doubt. ॥9॥
2.3.26.10: Who are you? Whose daughter are you? For what purpose do you practise, in this lonely forest, a penance hard to sustain even for eminent sages? ॥10॥
2.3.26.11: You are neither a child nor old; you shine as a beautiful young woman. How is it that you practise severe penance in the forest without a husband? ॥11॥
2.3.26.12: Are you, good lady, an ascetic woman, the companion of some ascetic? Does that ascetic not support you, O Devī, and has he gone elsewhere? ॥12॥
2.3.26.13: Tell me, in whose family were you born? Who is your father, what is your name? You are the very form of great good fortune; your fondness for penance is pointless. ॥13॥
2.3.26.14: Are you the mother of the Vedas Gāyatrī, or Lakṣmī, or the lovely Sarasvatī? Which among these are you? I cannot guess. ॥14॥
2.3.26.15: Pārvatī said: I am not the mother of the Vedas, O brahmin, nor Lakṣmī, nor Sarasvatī. I am the daughter of Himācala, now named Pārvatī. ॥15॥
2.3.26.16: Formerly, in another birth, I was born as Dakṣa's daughter named Satī; I abandoned my body through yoga because my husband was reviled by my father. ॥16॥
2.3.26.17: In this birth Śiva too was attained through the power of destiny, but having burnt Manmatha to ashes he abandoned me and went away. ॥17॥
2.3.26.18: When Śaṅkara had departed, distressed by grief I came from my father's house for penance, O brahmin, firmly resolved, to the bank of the Gaṅgā. ॥18॥
2.3.26.19: Having performed severe penance for a very long time and not having obtained the beloved of my life, I was about to enter the fire; seeing you, I stopped for a moment. ॥19॥
2.3.26.20: Go now; I enter the fire, since I have not been accepted by Śiva. Wherever I take birth, I shall choose Śiva as my bridegroom. ॥20॥
2.3.26.21: Brahmā said: Having said this, Pārvatī entered the fire before him, though she was forbidden again and again by the brahmin in front of her. ॥21॥
2.3.26.22: As Pārvatī entered the fire, through her power the fire at that very instant became like sandal paste. ॥22॥
2.3.26.23: After staying within it for a moment, as the fair-bodied one was rising up toward heaven, Śiva in the brahmin's form, laughing, suddenly questioned her again. ॥23॥
2.3.26.24: The brahmin said: Ah, what is this penance of yours, good lady? Nothing at all is understood: your body was not burnt by the fire, nor has your wish been attained. ॥24॥
2.3.26.25: Therefore, O Devī, tell me truly and fully your heart's wish, before me, the best of brahmins, the giver of all joy. ॥25॥
2.3.26.26: Let it be declared by you, O Devī, properly and wholeheartedly. Friendship has arisen between us; so nothing should be concealed by you. ॥26॥
2.3.26.27: What boon do you desire, O Devī? This above all I wish to ask. For in you alone, O Devī, all fulfilment is seen. ॥27॥
2.3.26.28: And if the penance is for some other aim, it would remain mere penance; it is as if, having taken a jewel in the hand, one has thrown it away and gathered glass. ॥28॥
2.3.26.29: How have you made such beauty of yours worthless? Abandoning many garments, you have put on hides and the like. ॥29॥
2.3.26.30: Tell me truly the whole reason for this penance, so that hearing it I, the best of brahmins, may attain joy. ॥30॥
2.3.26.31: Brahmā said: Thus questioned by him, Ambikā, firm in her vows, urged her friend, and through her mouth alone had everything told. ॥31॥
2.3.26.32: Urged there by Pārvatī, her friend named Vijayā, dear as life and knowing her firm vow, spoke to the matted-haired ascetic. ॥32॥
2.3.26.33: The friend said: Listen, O good man; I shall tell you Pārvatī's excellent story and the whole reason for her penance, if you wish to hear it. ॥33॥
2.3.26.34: This friend of mine is the daughter of the king of mountains, Himālaya; she is well known by the name Pārvatī, and her mother is Menakā. ॥34॥
2.3.26.35: She has not been married by anyone, and she desires no one other than Śiva. For three thousand years she has been engaged in the practice of penance. ॥35॥
2.3.26.36: For that purpose this friend of mine has undertaken such penance. I shall tell you the reason for it here; listen, O good man, best of brahmins. ॥36॥
2.3.26.37: Passing over the gods headed by Indra, as well as Hari and Brahmā, Pārvatī wishes to obtain the Pināka-bearer as her husband. ॥37॥
2.3.26.38: This friend of mine formerly planted trees; on all of them fruits, flowers and the like have appeared, O brahmin. ॥38॥
2.3.26.39: To make her beauty fruitful, to adorn her father's family, and aiming at Maheśāna, also for the sake of favour to Kāma— ॥39॥
2.3.26.40: —my friend, on Nārada's instruction, performs terrible penance. How could her heart's wish fail to bear fruit, O ascetic? ॥40॥
2.3.26.41: O best of the twice-born, what you asked my friend about, the wish in her heart, I have told you out of affection. What else do you wish to hear? ॥41॥
2.3.26.42: Brahmā said: O sage, having heard these words of Vijayā spoken truthfully, that matted-haired ascetic, Rudra, laughing, spoke these words. ॥42॥
2.3.26.43: The matted-haired ascetic said: This was told by her friend; in that a jest is suspected. If it is true, then let the goddess speak with her own mouth. ॥43॥
2.3.26.44: Brahmā said: When this had been said then by that matted-haired twice-born, the goddess Pārvatī spoke to that brahmin with her own mouth. ॥44॥
2.3.26.iti: Thus ends the twenty-sixth adhyāya, named The dialogue of Śivā and the ascetic with matted hair, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥26॥
2.3.27.1: Pārvatī said: Listen, O best of brāhmaṇas, O matted-haired one, to my whole story. What my friend told you today is true; it is exactly so and not otherwise. ॥1॥
2.3.27.2: In mind, in word and directly in deed I have chosen Śaṅkara as my husband. I speak the truth, not falsehood. ॥2॥
2.3.27.3: I know it is a thing hard to obtain; how could it be gained by me? Even so, out of my mind's longing, I am practising austerity today. ॥3॥
2.3.27.4: Brahmā said: Having spoken these words to him, Girijā then remained silent. Hearing Pārvatī's words, the brāhmaṇa spoke there. ॥4॥
2.3.27.5: The brahmin said: Until now I had a great desire to know: what thing does the goddess long for, that she performs such very great austerity? ॥5॥
2.3.27.6: Now that I have learned it all, O goddess, hearing it from your lotus-mouth, I shall go from this place. Do as you wish. ॥6॥
2.3.27.7: If you do not tell me, our friendship would be fruitless. As the matter is, so it will turn out; it should be told freely. ॥7॥
2.3.27.8: Brahmā said: Having spoken these words, just as he wished to leave, the goddess Pārvatī bowed and spoke to that brāhmaṇa. ॥8॥
2.3.27.9: Pārvatī said: Why will you go, O chief of brāhmaṇas? Stay, and tell me what is beneficial. When she had said this, the staff-bearer stayed and spoke. ॥9॥
2.3.27.10: The brahmin said: If, O goddess, wishing to listen, you keep me here out of devotion, I shall tell you the whole truth, by which you will gain understanding. ॥10॥
2.3.27.11: I know Mahādeva thoroughly, through the tradition of my teacher. I shall tell you exactly as it is; listen attentively. ॥11॥
2.3.27.12: Mahādeva has the bull on his banner, is smeared with ash, wears matted locks, is clad in a tiger-skin garment and wrapped in an elephant's hide. ॥12॥
2.3.27.13: He carries a skull, is coiled about all his limbs with masses of serpents, is smeared with poison, eats what is not to be eaten, has odd eyes and is very terrifying. ॥13॥
2.3.27.14: His birth is unknown; he is ever without home and pleasures; he is sky-clad, ten-armed, and always accompanied by ghosts and spirits. ॥14॥
2.3.27.15: For what reason do you desire him as husband? Where has your good sense gone, O goddess? Think it over and tell me now. ॥15॥
2.3.27.16: I have heard before of his dreadful vow. Listen, I shall tell it to you now, if you have a taste for hearing it. ॥16॥
2.3.27.17: Long ago, by fate, the chaste Satī, Dakṣa's daughter, chose the bull-rider as husband; the outcome of her union with him is well known. ॥17॥
2.3.27.18: Satī was shunned by Dakṣa as the wife of the skull-bearer, and Śambhu too was excluded from receiving a share at the sacrifice. ॥18॥
2.3.27.19: Through that very insult Satī, greatly agitated with anger, gave up her dear life there, and Śaṅkara was abandoned by her. ॥19॥
2.3.27.20: You are a jewel among women; your father is king of all mountains. Why do you seek such a husband with fierce austerity? ॥20॥
2.3.27.21: Giving away a gold coin, you wish to take glass; abandoning bright sandal-paste, you wish to smear yourself with mud. ॥21॥
2.3.27.22: Forsaking the sun's brilliance, you want the glow of a firefly; giving up fine silk, you want here a garment of hide. ॥22॥
2.3.27.23: Abandoning life at home, you seek life in the forest; casting away the finest treasure, O queen of gods, you want iron. ॥23॥
2.3.27.24: Leaving aside Indra and the other world-guardians, you are devoted to Śiva. This is not well done; it appears now contrary to custom in the worlds. ॥24॥
2.3.27.25: Where are you, with eyes like lotus petals, and where is he, the three-eyed one? You have a face like the moon, while Śiva is said to be five-faced. ॥25॥
2.3.27.26: On your head is a divine braid, shining like a she-serpent; Śiva's, they say, is the well-known mass of matted locks. ॥26॥
2.3.27.27: Sandal-paste is on your limbs, and pyre-ash on Śiva's. Where is your fine silk, and where Śaṅkara's elephant hide? ॥27॥
2.3.27.28: Where are your divine ornaments, and where Śaṅkara's serpents? Where all the attendant deities around you, and where he who delights in offerings to ghosts? ॥28॥
2.3.27.29: Where the playing of the mṛdaṅga, and where that ḍamaru of his? Where the array of kettledrums, and where the inauspicious sound of the horn? ॥29॥
2.3.27.30: Where the sound made by the ḍhakkā drum, and where the inauspicious throat-noise? Your excellent beauty and Śiva's are not a fit match. ॥30॥
2.3.27.31: If he had wealth, how would he be naked? His vehicle is a bull; he has no possessions at all. ॥31॥
2.3.27.32: Of the qualities declared in bridegrooms that bring women happiness, not even one is found in Virūpākṣa. ॥32॥
2.3.27.33: Even Kāma, dear to you, was burnt by that Hara; and then his disregard for you was seen, when he left you and went elsewhere. ॥33॥
2.3.27.34: No lineage of his is to be seen, nor likewise learning or knowledge; his companions are goblins, and poison is seen in his throat. ॥34॥
2.3.27.35: He is always alone, and above all detached. So is it really fitting for you to join your mind to Hara alone? ॥35॥
2.3.27.36: Where is your necklace, and where his garland of skulls? Where your divine cosmetic, and where the pyre-ash on his body? ॥36॥
2.3.27.37: Everything, form and the rest, is at odds between you and Hara, O goddess. This does not please me; do as you wish. ॥37॥
2.3.27.38: Whatever is worthless, all that you yourself are seeking. Turn your mind away from it; if not, do as you wish. ॥38॥
2.3.27.39: Brahmā said: Hearing such words of that brāhmaṇa, Pārvatī, with an angry mind, spoke to the twice-born who was bent on reviling Śiva. ॥39॥
2.3.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of the deceiving words of the brahmacārin, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥27॥
2.3.28.1: Pārvatī said: This much I had indeed understood: that this one who came was someone else. Now everything is understood. You, above all, are not to be slain. ॥1॥
2.3.28.2: What you have said, O lord, is understood: it is false and nothing else. Had it truly been spoken by you, you would not say what is self-contradictory. ॥2॥
2.3.28.3: At times Maheśvara is seen wearing such a guise—the supreme Brahman who, in his own play, has taken on a body by his own will. ॥3॥
2.3.28.4: Intent on deceiving me in the form of a brahmacārin, you came and, with crooked reasoning, spoke words full of trickery. ॥4॥
2.3.28.5: But I know Śaṅkara's true nature very particularly; therefore, having reflected well, I shall speak of the truth of Śiva as is fitting. ॥5॥
2.3.28.6: In reality he is Brahman without attributes; he has attributes only for a purpose. How could there be a birth-lineage for him, who is attributeless yet the very self of the attributes? ॥6॥
2.3.28.7: That Sadāśiva is the very ground of all branches of knowledge; what need has he, the complete supreme Self, of learning? ॥7॥
2.3.28.8: Long ago, at the beginning of the kalpa, the Vedas were given to Viṣṇu by that Śambhu in the form of his breath. Who is so great a lord as to equal him? ॥8॥
2.3.28.9: How then can there be a measure of age for him who is the origin of all? Prakṛti was born from him; what other source could there be of his power? ॥9॥
2.3.28.10: Those who always worship with love that Śaṅkara, lord of Śakti—to such a one Śambhu grants the threefold power, ever imperishable. ॥10॥
2.3.28.11: By worshipping him alone the soul, free of fear, conquers death; hence his name Mṛtyuñjaya is famed in the three worlds. ॥11॥
2.3.28.12: By his favour alone Viṣṇu attains Viṣṇu-hood, Brahmā Brahmā-hood, and the gods their godhood. ॥12॥
2.3.28.13: When the king of the gods first goes to have sight of Śiva, he meets Bhūta and the others, the doorkeepers of Śiva, who are devoted to him; ॥13॥
2.3.28.14: his crown is struck by their staffs and battered all over. What need has he of many partisans? He himself is the great lord. ॥14॥
2.3.28.15: What would not come about here through service to him whose form is auspiciousness? What does that god lack, that Sadāśiva should desire me? ॥15॥
2.3.28.16: Even one who has been poor for seven births—if he serves Śaṅkara, by that service of his, prosperity (Lakṣmī) in the world becomes unfailing for him. ॥16॥
2.3.28.17: Before him the eight siddhis constantly dance to please him, ever with downcast faces; how then could any good be hard to obtain from him? ॥17॥
2.3.28.18: Even if auspicious things here do not attend upon Śaṅkara, still auspiciousness arises merely by remembering him. ॥18॥
2.3.28.19: He by the power of whose worship all desires are fulfilled in every way—how could there be any change in him, who is ever changeless? ॥19॥
2.3.28.20: In whose mouth the auspicious name Śiva is constantly present—by the mere sight of him others are always purified. ॥20॥
2.3.28.21: If the ash from the funeral pyre were impure, as you have said, how is it that, clinging always to his body, it is borne by the gods on their heads? ॥21॥
2.3.28.22: The god who is creator, sustainer and destroyer of the worlds, possessed of attributes, and also attributeless, called Śiva—how could he be known? ॥22॥
2.3.28.23: The attributeless form of Brahman, of Śiva the supreme Self—how could those like you, who are turned away from it, know it? ॥23॥
2.3.28.24: Those of evil conduct and sinful, who have strayed outside the Vedas, do not at all know the truth of Śiva whose form is beyond attributes. ॥24॥
2.3.28.25: The man who here reviles Śiva without knowing the truth—the merit he has gathered since birth is turned to ash. ॥25॥
2.3.28.26: Since you have here reviled Hara of boundless splendour, and I have worshipped you, I therefore incur sin. ॥26॥
2.3.28.27: On seeing a hater of Śiva, one should bathe with one's clothes on; on seeing a hater of Śiva, one should perform expiation. ॥27॥
2.3.28.28: O you wicked one, you said: I know Śaṅkara. But certainly the eternal Śiva has not been known by you. ॥28॥
2.3.28.29: Whatever Rudra may be like, or however many forms he may have, he is ever most dear to me—changeless, beloved of the good. ॥29॥
2.3.28.30: Not even Viṣṇu or Brahmā is in any way equal to that great-souled one; how then the other gods and the rest, who are always subject to time? ॥30॥
2.3.28.31: Having considered this truly with my own sound understanding, I have come to the forest for Śiva's sake and perform great austerity. ॥31॥
2.3.28.32: My longing is indeed to attain him alone—the supreme lord, lord of all, loving to his devotees, bestower of grace on the lowly. ॥32॥
2.3.28.33: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, O sage, Girijā, daughter of the lord of mountains, fell silent and meditated on Śiva with an unwavering mind. ॥33॥
2.3.28.34: Hearing the goddess's words, that brahmin brahmacārin was just beginning to speak again, ॥34॥
2.3.28.35: when Girijā, her mind wholly attached to Śiva and averse to the reviling of Śiva, quickly said to her friend Vijayā: ॥35॥
2.3.28.36: Girijā said: Friend, this vilest of brahmins must be stopped with effort; he intends to speak again and will revile Śiva. ॥36॥
2.3.28.37: Sin falls not only on the one who reviles Śiva; whoever listens to that reviling also becomes a sharer in sin here. ॥37॥
2.3.28.38: A reviler of Śiva is by all means to be slain by Śiva's servants; if he is a brahmin, he is to be shunned, and one should quickly leave that place. ॥38॥
2.3.28.39: This wicked one will revile Śiva again. If, being a brahmin, he cannot be slain, he must be shunned and not looked upon at all. ॥39॥
2.3.28.40: Leaving this place this very day, we shall go elsewhere without delay, so that there may be no further conversation with this ignorant one. ॥40॥
2.3.28.41: Brahmā said: Having said this, O sage, the moment Umā lifted her foot to leave, at that very moment Śiva himself, in person, took hold of his beloved. ॥41॥
2.3.28.42: Assuming his charming form, exactly as she had meditated on Śiva, and showing it to Śivā, Śiva spoke to her as she stood with her face cast down. ॥42॥
2.3.28.43: Śiva said: Where will you go, leaving me? You shall never again be abandoned by me. I am pleased; ask for a boon. There is nothing that cannot be given to you. ॥43॥
2.3.28.44: From today on I am your servant, bought indeed by your austerities. I am bought by your beauty; a single moment apart from you is like an age. ॥44॥
2.3.28.45: Let shyness be cast off by you; you are my eternal wife. O Girijā, O Maheśvarī, consider this with sound understanding. ॥45॥
2.3.28.46: You have been tested by me in many ways, O firm-minded one. So forgive my offence, committed by me as one following the ways of worldly play. ॥46॥
2.3.28.47: Nowhere in the three worlds do I see a loving woman like you. In every way I am subject to you; let your desire be fulfilled, O Śivā. ॥47॥
2.3.28.48: Come near me, beloved; you are my wife and I am your bridegroom. With you I shall quickly go to my own home, the finest of mountains. ॥48॥
2.3.28.49: Brahmā said: When the god of gods had spoken thus, Pārvatī was filled with joy, and she cast off all the former hardship that had arisen from her austerity. ॥49॥
2.3.28.50: All the weariness of Satī vanished, O best of sages; for when the fruit has come, a creature's earlier toil comes to an end. ॥50॥
2.3.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named Pārvatī's sight of the form of Śiva, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥28॥
2.3.29.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O Creator, O greatly fortunate one, what happened after that? I wish to hear all of it; narrate to me the glory of Śivā. ॥1॥
2.3.29.2: Brahmā said: O divine sage, listen well; I gladly narrate that story, which destroys great sins and increases devotion to Śiva. ॥2॥
2.3.29.3: Having heard the words of Hara, the Supreme Self, and having seen his bliss-giving form, Pārvatī rejoiced exceedingly, O brahmin. ॥3॥
2.3.29.4: The goddess Śivā, the great chaste lady, exceedingly happy, her face blossoming with love, replied to the Lord who stood near her. ॥4॥
2.3.29.5: Pārvatī said: You are my lord, O Lord of gods. What have you forgotten of the past—the destruction of Dakṣa's sacrifice, which you forcibly brought about for my sake? ॥5॥
2.3.29.6: You are that same one, and I, that same one, have been born of Menā to accomplish the task of the gods, O God of gods, who are afflicted by Tāraka. ॥6॥
2.3.29.7: If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, and if you show compassion, become my husband, O Īśāna; do as I ask, O Lord. ॥7॥
2.3.29.8: With your permission I shall duly go to my father's house; let that pure, supreme glory be made famous. ॥8॥
2.3.29.9: You should go, O lord, O master, to Himavat's side; then, becoming a mendicant, ask for me, you who are skilled in divine sport. ॥9॥
2.3.29.10: So should you act, proclaiming your glory in the worlds; in this way make my father's householder life wholly fruitful. ॥10॥
2.3.29.11: Lovingly instructed by the sages and surrounded by his kinsmen and retinue, my father will do as you ask; there is no doubt. ॥11॥
2.3.29.12: Formerly, when I, as Dakṣa's daughter, was given to you by my father, the marriage was not performed by you there according to the prescribed rite. ॥12॥
2.3.29.13: The planets were not worshipped by Dakṣa, my father; therefore this marriage became greatly flawed in respect of the planets. ॥13॥
2.3.29.14: Therefore, O Lord Mahādeva, you should perform the marriage with me according to the prescribed rite, for accomplishing the task of the gods. ॥14॥
2.3.29.15: As the custom of marriage is, so it must surely be carried out. Let Himavat fully know that his daughter has performed auspicious penance. ॥15॥
2.3.29.16: Brahmā said: Having heard these words, Sadāśiva, greatly pleased, spoke lovingly to Girijā, as if laughing. ॥16॥
2.3.29.17: Śiva said: Listen, O goddess, O Maheśānī, to my supreme words; do what is fitting, most auspicious and free from change. ॥17॥
2.3.29.18: The beings beginning with Brahmā are impermanent, O fair-faced one; know, O beautiful lady, that all this which is seen is perishable. ॥18॥
2.3.29.19: The One has become many; the attributeless has become endowed with attributes; he who shines by his own light has become endowed with another's light. ॥19॥
2.3.29.20: Independent as I am, I have been made dependent by you, O goddess; you alone are Prakṛti, the doer of all, Mahāmāyā. ॥20॥
2.3.29.21: This entire world, made of māyā, has been created and wholly sustained by your supreme intelligence; it is pervaded within the self by the virtuous, who are the selves of all and have the nature of the Supreme Self, and is enveloped by the guṇas. ॥21॥
2.3.29.22: What are planets, what are the groups of seasons, or what other planets are there for you? And what is it that you have now said for Śiva's sake, O goddess of fair complexion? ॥22॥
2.3.29.23: Through the distinction of guṇas and functions, we two have manifested in this world for the sake of devotees, out of love for devotees. ॥23॥
2.3.29.24: You indeed are the subtle Prakṛti, consisting of rajas, sattva and tamas, ever skilled in activity, with attributes and also without attributes. ॥24॥
2.3.29.25: I am the Self of all beings here, O slender-waisted one, changeless and desireless, assuming a form at the wish of devotees. ॥25॥
2.3.29.26: I would not go to Himālaya, your father, O mountain-born one; nor, becoming a mendicant, would I in any way beg for you. ॥26॥
2.3.29.27: Even one weighty with great virtues, even a great soul, O daughter of the mountain-king, at once falls into lightness by the word give. ॥27॥
2.3.29.28: Knowing this, O auspicious one, what do you now tell us? The task is by your command, O good lady; do as you wish. ॥28॥
2.3.29.29: Brahmā said: Though thus addressed by him, the great goddess, chaste and lotus-eyed, bowing again and again, spoke to Śaṅkara with devotion. ॥29॥
2.3.29.30: Pārvatī said: You are the Self and I am Prakṛti; there is no need for deliberation here. We two are independent yet subject to devotees, attributeless and also with attributes. ॥30॥
2.3.29.31: With effort, O Śambhu, my request must be fulfilled by you, O Lord. Ask Himagiri for me; grant me good fortune, O Śaṅkara. ॥31॥
2.3.29.32: Show compassion, O Maheśāna; I am ever your devotee. I am always your wife, O lord, birth after birth. ॥32॥
2.3.29.33: You are Brahman, the Supreme Self, attributeless, beyond Prakṛti, changeless and desireless, independent, the Supreme Lord. ॥33॥
2.3.29.34: Yet here you are also with attributes, devoted to uplifting your devotees, sporting, delighting in your own Self, skilled in manifold sports. ॥34॥
2.3.29.35: I know you in every way, O Mahādeva, O Maheśvara. What use is saying much, O all-knowing one? Show mercy. ॥35॥
2.3.29.36: Spread your glory in the world by performing a most wondrous sport, by singing of which people, O lord, easily cross the ocean of worldly existence. ॥36॥
2.3.29.37: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus to Maheśāna and bowed again and again, Girijā fell silent, with shoulders bent and palms joined. ॥37॥
2.3.29.38: Thus addressed by her, the great-souled Maheśvara, to imitate the ways of the world, thought, so be it, and laughing, became joyful, intent on doing just that. ॥38॥
2.3.29.39: Then Śambhu, greatly delighted, vanished and went to Kailāsa, his mind drawn by separation from Kālī. ॥39॥
2.3.29.40: Having gone there, Maheśāna, filled with supreme bliss, told Nandin and the others that whole account. ॥40॥
2.3.29.41: Hearing this, all the Gaṇas too, Bhairava and the rest, everywhere, became exceedingly happy and held a grand festival. ॥41॥
2.3.29.42: O Nārada, there was a great and exceedingly auspicious celebration there. The sorrow of all was destroyed, and Rudra too attained great joy. ॥42॥
2.3.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of the dialogue of Śivā and Śiva, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥29॥
2.3.30.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi (Brahmā), dear father, most fortunate one, you are blessed, a seer of the supreme truth. Through your grace I have heard this wondrous story. ॥1॥
2.3.30.2: When Hara had gone to his own mountain, what did Pārvatī, the all-auspicious one, do, and where did she go? Tell me that, O great-minded one. ॥2॥
2.3.30.3: Brahmā said: Listen with great delight, dear son, to what happened after that. When Hara had gone to his own abode — that I shall tell, remembering Śiva. ॥3॥
2.3.30.4: Pārvatī too, accompanied by her friends, having made her beauty fruitful, went to her father's house, repeating the name Mahādeva. ॥4॥
2.3.30.5: Hearing of Pārvatī's arrival, Menā and Himācala, overwhelmed with joy, mounted a divine vehicle and set out. ॥5॥
2.3.30.6: The family priest, the citizens, and her friends in great numbers, the relatives and others as well — all of them came together. ॥6॥
2.3.30.7: Then all her brothers, headed by Maināka, went, shouting cries of victory, filled with great joy. ॥7॥
2.3.30.8: Having set up an auspicious pot on the resplendent royal road, furnished with sandal, aguru, musk, fruits and branches, ॥8॥
2.3.30.9: the road adorned with excellent priests and brāhmaṇas, with sages who expound Brahman, with women and dancing girls, and beautified by lordly elephants and the like, ॥9॥
2.3.30.10: lined all around with rows of plantain stems, with groups of women who had husbands and sons, holding lamps in their hands, ॥10॥
2.3.30.11: joined by throngs of twice-born making auspicious sounds, and resounding with many kinds of instruments and the blare of conches — ॥11॥
2.3.30.12: Meanwhile Durgā came near her own city. Entering the city, the Goddess saw her parents again. ॥12॥
2.3.30.13: Seeing them, very pleased, running forward, their minds overwhelmed with joy, Kālī, greatly delighted, bowed to them together with her companions. ॥13॥
2.3.30.14: The two, giving her full blessings, pressed her to their bosoms, weeping and overwhelmed with love, saying, O dear child. ॥14॥
2.3.30.15: Then her own kinswomen, other women too, joyfully, and her brothers' wives with great affection, embraced her tightly. ॥15॥
2.3.30.16: You have properly accomplished a noble task that delivers the family; by your virtuous conduct we have all been purified. ॥16॥
2.3.30.17: Thus praising her highly, all of them, delighted, bowed to her, and joyfully worshipped Śivā with sandal paste and fine flowers. ॥17॥
2.3.30.18: At that moment the gods, standing in their aerial cars in the sky, joyfully showered auspicious flowers and, bowing to her, praised her with hymns. ॥18॥
2.3.30.19: Then all of them, the brāhmaṇas and the rest, placing her in an excellent, splendidly adorned chariot, joyfully led her into the city. ॥19॥
2.3.30.20: Then the brāhmaṇas, the priest, her friends and other women led the auspicious one Śivā into the house with great honour. ॥20॥
2.3.30.21: The women performed the waving of lamps, the brāhmaṇas bestowed blessings; Himavān and Menakā the mother rejoiced exceedingly, O lord of sages. ॥21॥
2.3.30.22: Himavān considered his household life fruitful — a daughter is better than a bad son — and he praised you, Nārada, saying, well done, well done. ॥22॥
2.3.30.23: The lord of mountains gave wealth to the brāhmaṇas and the bards, and had the twice-born recite auspicious texts — a great festival. ॥23॥
2.3.30.24: Thus, delighted by their daughter, the parents, the brothers, and the women of the family sat together in the courtyard with great affection, O sage. ॥24॥
2.3.30.25: Then Himavān, dear son, greatly delighted and serene of mind, having honoured everyone affectionately, went to the Gaṅgā to bathe. ॥25॥
2.3.30.26: Meanwhile Śambhu, delighting in sport and loving to his devotees, became a skilled dancer-actor and went into the presence of Menakā. ॥26॥
2.3.30.27: Holding a horn in his left hand and a ḍamaru drum in his right, a patched cloak on his back, clad in red, skilled in dance and song, ॥27॥
2.3.30.28: then he, in the form of a fine actor, joyfully performed in Menā's courtyard beautiful dances of many kinds and exceedingly charming songs. ॥28॥
2.3.30.29: There he played the horn and the ḍamaru with a sweet sound, and there he gave a great, varied and captivating performance. ॥29॥
2.3.30.30: To see it, all the townsfolk, men and women alike, came there at once — even children and the old, certainly. ॥30॥
2.3.30.31: Hearing that sweet song and seeing the charming dance, all were suddenly entranced, and Menā too then, O sage. ॥31॥
2.3.30.32: Durgā fell into a swoon, beholding Śaṅkara in her heart, bearing the trident and other emblems, exceedingly handsome, ॥32॥
2.3.30.33: adorned with sacred ash, delightful, wearing a garland of bones, his face radiant with three eyes, with a serpent as his sacred thread, ॥33॥
2.3.30.34: Maheśvara, fair of complexion, who was telling her to choose a boon, the friend of the afflicted, an ocean of compassion, utterly enchanting. ॥34॥
2.3.30.35: Seeing Hara thus dwelling in her heart, she bowed to him and chose a boon in her mind: Be my husband. ॥35॥
2.3.30.36: Having then lovingly granted Śivā such a boon in her heart, he vanished from it, and that mendicant again danced beautifully there. ॥36॥
2.3.30.37: Then Menā, her mind pleased by his splendour, lovingly went to give him fine jewels placed in a golden vessel. ॥37॥
2.3.30.38: He did not accept them, saying: I beg as alms that Śivā. And out of playfulness he was ready to dance and sing beautifully again. ॥38॥
2.3.30.39: Hearing his words, Menā, greatly astonished, became extremely angry; she rebuked the mendicant and wished to drive him out. ॥39॥
2.3.30.40: Meanwhile the Mountain king returned there from the Gaṅgā and saw before him the mendicant in human form standing in the courtyard. ॥40॥
2.3.30.41: Having heard that whole account from Menā's mouth, he became very angry and ordered his attendants to throw that dancer out. ॥41॥
2.3.30.42: But, O best of sages, no one was able to throw him out, for he was hard to touch like a great fire, blazing and full of splendour. ॥42॥
2.3.30.43: Then, dear one, that mendicant, skilled in many sports, showed the mountain his own infinite power. ॥43॥
2.3.30.44: There the mountain suddenly saw him bearing the form of Viṣṇu, crowned, wearing earrings, clad in yellow garments, four-armed. ॥44॥
2.3.30.45: Whatever flowers and other offerings he had given to the Mace-bearer at the time of worship, all of that he indeed saw on the mendicant's body and head. ॥45॥
2.3.30.46: Then the lord of mountains saw him as the four-faced creator of the worlds, red in colour, reciting Vedic hymns. ॥46॥
2.3.30.47: Then the king of mountains saw him for a moment in the form of the Sun, the eye of the world, causing wonder. ॥47॥
2.3.30.48: Then, dear one, he saw him in the most wondrous form of Rudra, together with Pārvatī, charming, smiling, full of splendour. ॥48॥
2.3.30.49: Then he saw him as a form of pure light, formless, stainless, free of limiting adjuncts, desireless, most wondrous and without shape. ॥49॥
2.3.30.50: Thus he saw many forms of him there; he at once became greatly astonished and filled with supreme bliss. ॥50॥
2.3.30.51: Then that best of mendicants begged from him and from her who had given birth to her for Durgā herself as alms, and accepted nothing else at all. ॥51॥
2.3.30.52: The lord of mountains, deluded by Śiva's māyā, did not agree. The mendicant took nothing and then vanished right there. ॥52॥
2.3.30.53: Then true understanding arose in Menā and the lord of mountains: The Lord Śiva has deceived us both and gone to his own abode. ॥53॥
2.3.30.54: As they reflected thus there, supreme devotion to Śiva arose in them—divine, bestowing great liberation and granting every bliss. ॥54॥
2.3.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The description of the great festival on the return of Pārvatī, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥30॥
2.3.31.1: Brahmā said: Knowing the supreme, unswerving devotion of those two, Himavat and Menā, to Śiva, all the gods led by Śakra reflected thus, O Nārada. ॥1॥
2.3.31.2: The gods said: If the mountain gives his daughter to him with single-minded devotion, he will surely attain liberation at once, here in Bhārata. ॥2॥
2.3.31.3: If he, the support of endless gems, leaves the earth and departs, the earth's name Ratnagarbhā (bearing gems in her womb) will surely become false. ॥3॥
2.3.31.4: Abandoning his immobile state and assuming a divine form, he will give his daughter to the Trident-bearer and go to Śiva's world. ॥4॥
2.3.31.5: He will gain likeness of form with Mahādeva, there is no doubt of this; having enjoyed excellent pleasures there, he will then attain liberation. ॥5॥
2.3.31.6: Brahmā said: Having thus deliberated and consulted among themselves, all the gods, greatly astonished, wished to send their preceptor there. ॥6॥
2.3.31.7: Then all the gods led by Śakra, intent on their own ends, went gladly and with humility to the preceptor's abode, O Nārada. ॥7॥
2.3.31.8: Going there and bowing to the preceptor, all the gods together with Vāsava respectfully reported the matter to that preceptor. ॥8॥
2.3.31.9: The gods said: O preceptor, go to Himālaya's house for the accomplishment of our purpose; having gone there, make an effort to speak ill of the Trident-bearer. ॥9॥
2.3.31.10: Durgā will choose no groom other than the Pināka-bearer. But if he gives his daughter unwillingly, he will quickly obtain only an ordinary fruit. ॥10॥
2.3.31.11: For the time being, let the mountain remain on the earth now; establish him, the support of many gems, on the earth, O preceptor. ॥11॥
2.3.31.12: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the gods, the preceptor put his hands over his ears; he did not accept, and remembered the name Śiva. ॥12॥
2.3.31.13: Then, remembering Mahādeva, the noble-minded Bṛhaspati spoke to the foremost gods, reproaching them again and again. ॥13॥
2.3.31.14: Bṛhaspati said: All you gods are bent on your own interest and destroy the interests of others. Indeed, if I disparage Śaṅkara, I will surely go to hell. ॥14॥
2.3.31.15: O gods, let one among you go near the mountain and accomplish what you desire by persuading the lord of mountains. ॥15॥
2.3.31.16: Having given his daughter unwillingly, let him live happily in Bhārata; whereas having given his daughter to him with devotion, he would certainly attain liberation. ॥16॥
2.3.31.17: Afterwards all the seven sages will enlighten the mountain; Durgā will choose no groom other than the Pināka-bearer. ॥17॥
2.3.31.18: Or else, O gods, go with Vāsava to Brahmā's world and tell your story; he will do your work. ॥18॥
2.3.31.19: Brahmā said: Hearing that, the gods deliberated and came to my assembly; bowing, they all respectfully reported what had happened. ॥19॥
2.3.31.20: Hearing then those words of the gods, which amounted to disparaging Śiva, I, the speaker of the Vedas, lamented and said to those gods, O sage: ॥20॥
2.3.31.21: Brahmā said: My children, I am not able to commit disparagement of Śiva, which is utterly intolerable, which is destruction of prosperity itself and the very seed of calamities. ॥21॥
2.3.31.22: O gods, go to Kailāsa and please Śaṅkara; send him quickly towards Himālaya's house. ॥22॥
2.3.31.23: Let him go near the lord of mountains and indeed disparage himself. Disparaging others is held to lead to ruin, disparaging oneself to glory. ॥23॥
2.3.31.24: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of mine, the gods joyfully bowed to me and quickly went to Kailāsa, the mountain that is lord of mountains. ॥24॥
2.3.31.25: Going there and seeing Śiva, the gods bowed with heads lowered and, with palms well joined, all praised that Hara. ॥25॥
2.3.31.26: The gods said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, mine of compassion, Śaṅkara, we have come to you for refuge; show us grace; salutation to you. ॥26॥
2.3.31.27: O Lord, you are loving to your devotees, ever accomplishing the work of devotees, uplifter of the wretched, ocean of compassion, releaser of devotees from distress. ॥27॥
2.3.31.28: Brahmā said: Having thus praised Maheśāna, all the gods with Vāsava then respectfully reported that whole matter. ॥28॥
2.3.31.29: Hearing the gods' words, Maheśvara accepted; smiling and reassuring the gods, he sent them off. ॥29॥
2.3.31.30: All the gods rejoiced; quickly going to their own abodes, they praised Sadāśiva, considering their purpose accomplished. ॥30॥
2.3.31.31: Then the blessed Śambhu, Maheśa, loving to his devotees, the Lord of Māyā, ever free of change, went to the king of mountains. ॥31॥
2.3.31.32: When the mountain himself was seated joyfully in the midst of his assembly, surrounded by his kinsfolk and accompanied by Pārvatī, ॥32॥
2.3.31.33: at that moment Sadāśiva came there, carrying a staff and an umbrella, in divine garments, bearing a shining tilaka, ॥33॥
2.3.31.34: holding a crystal rosary in his hand and a śālagrāma at his neck, devoutly repeating the name of Hari—a brahmin wearing the garb of a holy man. ॥34॥
2.3.31.35: Seeing him, Himālaya with his retinue rose up and, with devotion, prostrated on the ground like a staff before the unprecedented guest. ॥35॥
2.3.31.36: Pārvatī devoutly bowed to the lord of her life in the form of a brahmin; recognising him in her mind, the goddess praised him with supreme joy. ॥36॥
2.3.31.37: The brahmin, Śiva, lovingly bestowed blessings on all, and on Śivā especially, granting from his heart what her mind desired, dear child. ॥37॥
2.3.31.38: The brahmin gladly accepted the madhuparka and all the other offerings given with great reverence by Himavat, the overlord of mountains. ॥38॥
2.3.31.39: Having duly worshipped that best of brahmins with great affection, Himādri, the best of mountains, asked after his welfare, O sage. ॥39॥
2.3.31.40: Then the lord of mountains asked him again, who are you? The foremost brahmin promptly addressed respectful words to the king of mountains. ॥40॥
2.3.31.41: The best of brahmins said: O best of mountains, I am a Brāhmaṇa, a Vaiṣṇava, foremost among the learned. Following the profession of a match-maker, I wander over the surface of the earth. ॥41॥
2.3.31.42: By the power of my guru I move with the speed of thought, I go everywhere, and I know everything. I am a benefactor of others, pure-souled, an ocean of compassion, a remover of afflictions. ॥42॥
2.3.31.43: I have come to know that you wish to give your own daughter to Hara — this girl, like a lotus, divine, of excellent beauty, endowed with auspicious marks — ॥43॥
2.3.31.44: — to one without support, without attachment, ugly in form and devoid of qualities, who dwells in the cremation ground, who has the appearance of a snake-catcher, a yogin, ॥44॥
2.3.31.45: to one clad in the directions (naked), of ugly body, wearing serpents as ornaments, whose family and name are unknown, of bad conduct, who takes no pleasure in household life, ॥45॥
2.3.31.46: whose body is smeared with ashes, who is wrathful and lacks discernment, whose age is utterly unknown, who always bears ugly matted locks, ॥46॥
2.3.31.47: who shelters with everyone, a wanderer, wearing snakes as a necklace, a beggar, devoted to wrong paths, and who has wilfully abandoned the path of the Veda. ॥47॥
2.3.31.48: O Mountain, this intention of yours is surely not auspicious. Understand this, O best of the wise, born of the lineage of Nārāyaṇa. ॥48॥
2.3.31.49: He is not a recipient befitting you in the act of giving Pārvatī. Eminent people will smile in mockery the moment they hear of it. ॥49॥
2.3.31.50: Look, O lord of mountains: he has not a single kinsman. You are a great mine of jewels, but he has no wealth at all. ॥50॥
2.3.31.51: O lord of mountains, quickly and carefully ask your kinsmen, Menakā, your sons, and all the learned — everyone except Pārvatī. ॥51॥
2.3.31.52: O best of mountains, medicine never pleases a sick man; unwholesome diet, which always causes great harm, constantly pleases him. ॥52॥
2.3.31.53: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, that Brāhmaṇa — Śiva, the performer of many sports — having eaten, joyful and calm, quickly went to his own abode. ॥53॥
2.3.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named Śiva's māyā, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥31॥
2.3.32.1: Brahmā said: Having heard the brāhmaṇa's words, Menā, her eyes filled with tears from grief and her heart burning, spoke to Himālaya. ॥1॥
2.3.32.2: Menā said: Listen, O lord of mountains, to my words, which will bring happiness in the end. Ask all the foremost devotees of Śiva what the brāhmaṇa has said. ॥2॥
2.3.32.3: This Vaiṣṇava brāhmaṇa has spoken ill of Śambhu. Having heard that censure, my mind has become utterly disheartened, O lord of mountains. ॥3॥
2.3.32.4: O lord of mountains, I will not give my own daughter, who is endowed with good marks, to that Rudra, whose form, conduct and name are all ill-favoured. ॥4॥
2.3.32.5: If you do not heed my words, I shall die, without doubt. I shall leave the house at once, or I shall swallow poison. ॥5॥
2.3.32.6: Binding Ambikā by the neck with a rope, I shall go into the dense forest; I shall drown her in the great ocean. I will not give my daughter to him. ॥6॥
2.3.32.7: Having said this, Menā went quickly, in grief, to the chamber of anger; casting off her necklace, weeping, she lay down on the ground. ॥7॥
2.3.32.8: Meanwhile, dear one, Śambhu, his mind agitated by separation, at once called to mind those seven sages. ॥8॥
2.3.32.9: When all those sages were remembered by Śambhu, they came at once of their own accord, like so many other wish-fulfilling trees. ॥9॥
2.3.32.10: Arundhatī too came, like another Siddhi (Accomplishment) incarnate. Seeing them, radiant as the sun, Hara left off his own japa. ॥10॥
2.3.32.11: Standing before him, those excellent sages, O sage, bowed to Śiva and praised him, and then those ascetics considered themselves fulfilled. ॥11॥
2.3.32.12: Then, filled with wonder, having bowed again they stood, and with joined palms they spoke to Śiva, who is saluted by the worlds. ॥12॥
2.3.32.13: The sages said: O Supreme over all, great King, Sovereign of the dwellers of heaven, our own good fortune is now being extolled by us—what more need be said? It is the highest of all. ॥13॥
2.3.32.14: Austerity was formerly practised in three ways, excellent Vedic study was done, fires were offered oblations to, and various sacred places visited. ॥14॥
2.3.32.15: Whatever merit arose from speech, mind and body, and from remembrance of you—all of that has come to fruition today through the grace of your remembering us. ॥15॥
2.3.32.16: The man who worships you constantly becomes one who has accomplished all. What merit can be described of those whom you remember? ॥16॥
2.3.32.17: We have become the most exalted of all through your remembrance, O Sadāśiva. You never in any way come within the path of mere wishes. ॥17॥
2.3.32.18: Like a fruit reached by a dwarf, like eyes for one born blind, like speech for the mute, like the sight of a treasure for a pauper, ॥18॥
2.3.32.19: like the climbing of a great mountain by a lame man, and the giving birth by a barren woman—so has the sight of you, hard to obtain, come to us, O Lord. ॥19॥
2.3.32.20: From today onward, we lords of sages have become honoured and worshipful in the worlds, merely by the sight of you, having attained our own lofty station. ॥20॥
2.3.32.21: What use is saying much here? We have become honoured in every way through the sight of you, O Lord of gods, who are indeed the Lord of all the gods. ॥21॥
2.3.32.22: What remains to be done by those who are fulfilled? Yet if there is your supreme grace, some auspicious task befitting your servants should be given by you. ॥22॥
2.3.32.23: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of theirs, Śambhu, the great Lord, adopting worldly custom, spoke delightful words. ॥23॥
2.3.32.24: Śiva said: Sages are always worthy of worship, and you especially. It is for a purpose concerning you, O brāhmaṇas, that I called you to mind. ॥24॥
2.3.32.25: You know that my state is one of benefiting others; it must especially be accomplished for the success of the worlds. ॥25॥
2.3.32.26: Distress has arisen for the gods from the utterly wicked Tāraka; and a boon was granted to him by Brahmā. He is hard to overcome—what am I to do? ॥26॥
2.3.32.27: The eight forms that are declared to be mine, O great sages, all exist for the benefit of others, not for my own sake—that is plain. ॥27॥
2.3.32.28: So I wish to marry Śivā. She has performed severe austerity, difficult even for the great sages. ॥28॥
2.3.32.29: To her must be given the supreme fruit she desires, bringing her welfare. Such is my pledge, which clearly gives joy to devotees. ॥29॥
2.3.32.30: At Pārvatī's word, I went to the mountain's house in the form of a mendicant and purified Kālī, for I am skilled in divine play. ॥30॥
2.3.32.31: Knowing me to be the supreme Brahman, that couple, out of supreme devotion, became desirous of giving their daughter to me according to Vedic rite. ॥31॥
2.3.32.32: At the prompting of the gods I then, in the guise of a Vaiṣṇava, made censure of myself, so as to destroy their devotion. ॥32॥
2.3.32.33: Hearing that, the two became deeply disheartened and bereft of that devotion; now, O sages, they do not wish to give their daughter to me. ॥33॥
2.3.32.34: Therefore you must surely go to Himācala's house. Having gone there, enlighten the great mountain and his wife. ॥34॥
2.3.32.35: Words in accord with the Veda should be spoken with effort; that must be done in every way so that the task turns out excellently. ॥35॥
2.3.32.36: I wish to marry his daughter, O best ones. I have accepted that marriage, and such a boon has been granted by me. ॥36॥
2.3.32.37: What use is saying much here? Himālaya must be enlightened, and likewise Menā must be made to understand, so that the gods' welfare may come about. ॥37॥
2.3.32.38: Whatever procedure you devise, let it be even greater than that; this task is yours, for you are sharers in the task. ॥38॥
2.3.32.39: Brahmā said: Hearing these words, all those sages of pure heart, favoured by the Lord, attained joy. ॥39॥
2.3.32.40: They said: We have become blessed and fulfilled in every way; we have become worthy of salutation by all and especially worthy of worship. ॥40॥
2.3.32.41: He who is indeed to be worshipped by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, the accomplisher of all aims, sends us, his messengers, on a task that brings happiness to the world. ॥41॥
2.3.32.42: He is the lord of the worlds and the father; she is regarded as the mother. This alliance is fitting; may it always grow like the waxing moon. ॥42॥
2.3.32.43: Brahmā said: Having said this, the divine sages then bowed to Śiva and went by the path of the sky to where Himavat's city stands. ॥43॥
2.3.32.44: Seeing that divine city, those sages were greatly astonished, and, extolling their own good fortune, they spoke to one another. ॥44॥
2.3.32.45: The sages said: We are meritorious and blessed, having seen this city of Himavat, since we have been appointed by Śiva himself to such a task. ॥45॥
2.3.32.46: This excellent city appears superior to Alakā, to Svarga, and again to Bhogavatī, and especially to Amarāvatī. ॥46॥
2.3.32.47: The fine houses are very charming, and the courtyards are built and adorned in variety with many excellent crystals or gems. ॥47॥
2.3.32.48: In every house there are sunstones and likewise moonstones, and wonderful trees born of heaven. ॥48॥
2.3.32.49: Likewise the splendour of arched gateways is seen in every house, varied and wonderful, with parrots, swans and little aerial cars as decorations. ॥49॥
2.3.32.50: There are wonderful canopies made of cloth together with gateways, many reservoirs of water, and various long ponds. ॥50॥
2.3.32.51: There are wonderful gardens, tended by delighted people; and all the men are gods, and the women likewise are celestial nymphs. ॥51॥
2.3.32.52: In the land of action, sacrificers and those versed in the Purāṇas perform rites out of desire for heaven; all of them do so in vain, passing over the city of Himavat. ॥52॥
2.3.32.53: As long as this has not been seen, so long are men devoted to heaven; but once this is seen, O brahmins, what need is there of heaven? ॥53॥
2.3.32.54: Brahmā said: Thus describing that city, all those foremost sages went to the house of Himālaya, rich in every prosperity. ॥54॥
2.3.32.55: Seeing from afar those seven very radiant sages, resplendent like the sun, standing on the path of the sky, Himavat, astonished, said: ॥55॥
2.3.32.56: Himavān said: These seven, resplendent like the sun, are coming near me. Worship of the sages must now be performed by me with care. ॥56॥
2.3.32.57: Blessed are we householders, givers of happiness to all, since to our house such great souls come. ॥57॥
2.3.32.58: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, seeing them come down from the sky and standing on the ground before him, Himavat went forward with reverence. ॥58॥
2.3.32.59: With joined palms and bowed shoulders, he bowed deeply to the seven sages and performed their worship with great honour. ॥59॥
2.3.32.60: Those benevolent seven sages, taking hold of Himavat, lord of mountains, spoke with cheerful faces words that were an abode of auspiciousness. ॥60॥
2.3.32.61: Placing them before him, he said, blessed is my householder's life. Having said this, he brought seats and offered them with devotion. ॥61॥
2.3.32.62: When they had sat down on the seats, he himself, permitted by them, took his place; then Himavat spoke there to the radiant sages. ॥62॥
2.3.32.63: Himavān said: I am blessed indeed and have fulfilled my purpose; my life is fruitful. I am worthy to be seen in the worlds and am regarded as equal to many holy places. ॥63॥
2.3.32.64: For you, who are forms of Viṣṇu, have come to my house. What business could you, who are complete, have in the houses of poor beings? ॥64॥
2.3.32.65: Even so, kindly tell me some task befitting me, your servant, so that my birth may become fruitful. ॥65॥
2.3.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The coming of the seven sages, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥32॥
2.3.33.1: The sages said: Śiva is declared the father of the world, and Śivā is regarded as the mother of the world. Therefore you should give your daughter to the great-souled Śaṅkara. ॥1॥
2.3.33.2: By doing so, O Himālaya, your birth will become fruitful. You will surely become the guru of the guru of the world; there is no doubt. ॥2॥
2.3.33.3: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the seven sages, O lord of sages, the king of mountains bowed to them, folded his hands, and said this: ॥3॥
2.3.33.4: Himavān said: O greatly fortunate seven sages, what you have said had indeed been accepted by me as authoritative long ago, through the will of Giriśa. ॥4॥
2.3.33.5: But just now a certain brahmin, following the Vaiṣṇava dharma, came and, with great affection, spoke words contrary in praise concerning Śiva. ॥5॥
2.3.33.6: From then on, Śivā's mother has lost her good sense; she does not want her daughter's marriage with that yogin Rudra. ॥6॥
2.3.33.7: She has gone to the chamber of anger, greatly distressed, wearing soiled garments; having resolved on great obstinacy, O brahmins, she did not understand even when admonished. ॥7॥
2.3.33.8: And I too have lost my good sense — the truth is being told: I do not wish to give my daughter to Maheśa, who has the form of a beggar. ॥8॥
2.3.33.9: Brahmā said: Having said this, the king of mountains, deluded by Śiva's māyā, fell silent, remaining there in the midst of the sages, O sage. ॥9॥
2.3.33.10: All those seven sages, praising Śiva's māyā, then sent Arundhatī to Menakā. ॥10॥
2.3.33.11: Then, receiving her husband's instruction, Arundhatī, the giver of wisdom, went swiftly to where Menā and Pārvatī were. ॥11॥
2.3.33.12: Having gone, she saw Menā lying down, swooning with grief. The virtuous lady, attentive, spoke sweet and beneficial words. ॥12॥
2.3.33.13: Arundhatī said: Rise, O virtuous Menakā. I, Arundhatī, have come to your house, and the seven compassionate sages have come as well. ॥13॥
2.3.33.14: Brahmā said: Hearing Arundhatī's voice, Menakā rose quickly, bowed her head, and spoke to her, who was like Padmā (Lakṣmī) in radiance. ॥14॥
2.3.33.15: Menā said: Ah! What merit is this today for us who are of meritorious birth — that the daughter-in-law of the world's creator, the wife of Vasiṣṭha, has come here. ॥15॥
2.3.33.16: For what purpose have you come, O goddess? Tell me that in detail. I, together with my daughter, am like your maidservant; show compassion. ॥16॥
2.3.33.17: Brahmā said: When the virtuous Menakā had spoken thus, Arundhatī, having counselled her at length, came gladly with her to where those seven sages also were. ॥17॥
2.3.33.18: Then they, all skilled in speech, remembering the pair of Śiva's feet, respectfully counselled the lord of mountains. ॥18॥
2.3.33.19: The sages said: O lord of mountains, listen to our words, which are a cause of good. Give Pārvatī to Śiva; become the father-in-law of the Destroyer. ॥19॥
2.3.33.20: Brahmā earnestly entreated the Lord of all, who asks for nothing, to enter into this marital alliance for the destruction of Tāraka. ॥20॥
2.3.33.21: Śaṅkara, the best of yogins, is not eager for union with a wife; yet at the Creator's entreaty the god will accept your daughter. ॥21॥
2.3.33.22: Your daughter has performed austerities, and she has secured a promise; for these two reasons the lord of yogins will perform the marriage. ॥22॥
2.3.33.23: Brahmā said: Hearing the sages' words, Himālaya laughed, and, somewhat afraid, spoke with the utmost humility. ॥23॥
2.3.33.24: Himavān said: I see no royal possessions whatever of Śiva — no shelter, no wealth, nor any kinsman or relative. ॥24॥
2.3.33.25: I do not wish to give my daughter to an utterly detached yogin. You are the sons of the Creator of the Vedas; tell me decisively. ॥25॥
2.3.33.26: If a father gives his daughter to an unsuitable bridegroom out of desire, delusion, fear or greed, he is ruined and goes to hell. ॥26॥
2.3.33.27: I will not willingly give my daughter to the Trident-bearer. O sages, let whatever arrangement is proper be made. ॥27॥
2.3.33.28: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Himālaya, O lord of sages, Vasiṣṭha, the most skilled in speech among them, replied to him. ॥28॥
2.3.33.29: Vasiṣṭha said: Listen, O lord of mountains, to my words, which are in every way beneficial to you, not opposed to dharma, true, and bringing joy here and hereafter. ॥29॥
2.3.33.30: Speech is of three kinds, O mountain, both in worldly and in Vedic usage; one who knows the śāstras understands it all with the eye of pure knowledge. ॥30॥
2.3.33.31: What is untrue and harmful in the end, yet pleasant to hear for the present — that a clever enemy speaks; he never speaks what is beneficial. ॥31॥
2.3.33.32: What is unpleasant at first but brings happiness in the end — that a compassionate, righteous kinsman always counsels. ॥32॥
