2.3.33.33: Speech that is like nectar the moment it is heard, brings happiness at all times, has truth as its essence and is beneficial — that is the best and most desired. ॥33॥
2.3.33.34: Thus, O mountain, speech is of three kinds, as stated in the treatises on policy. Tell me: of the three, which kind of speech do you wish me to speak? ॥34॥
2.3.33.35: Śaṅkara, lord of the gods, is devoid of external wealth; his single mind is wholly immersed in the oceans of knowledge of reality. ॥35॥
2.3.33.36: What desire for external things can the Lord have, whose bliss is knowledge? Only a householder gives his daughter to one endowed with kingdom and riches. ॥36॥
2.3.33.37: A father who gives his daughter to a miserable man becomes a slayer of his daughter. But who can claim Śaṅkara is miserable, whose servant is Kubera? ॥37॥
2.3.33.38: He is able to create and destroy the universe by the mere play of a knitting of his brows. He is beyond the guṇas, the supreme Self, the highest Lord, beyond Prakṛti. ॥38॥
2.3.33.39: In the work of creation, he, the Ordainer, has a threefold form — named Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara — which brings about creation, preservation and dissolution. ॥39॥
2.3.33.40: Brahmā dwells in Brahmaloka, Viṣṇu resides in the Ocean of Milk, Hara has Kailāsa as his abode — all are manifestations of Śiva's glory. ॥40॥
2.3.33.41: And Prakṛti, born of Śiva, assumes three forms; in creation, through a portion of herself, playfully, and by a fraction of her power, she takes many forms as well. ॥41॥
2.3.33.42: From Brahmā's mouth arose Vāṇī herself, the deity presiding over speech; from Viṣṇu's chest arose Lakṣmī, the embodiment of all wealth. ॥42॥
2.3.33.43: That Śivā manifested herself from the radiant energies of the gods; having slain all the Dānavas, she gave prosperity to the gods. ॥43॥
2.3.33.44: In another kalpa she took birth in the womb of Dakṣa's wife; named Satī, she obtained Hara, and Dakṣa gave her to him. ॥44॥
2.3.33.45: Having heard her husband reviled, she abandoned her body through yoga. That same Śivā has now been born from you, out of the womb of Menā. ॥45॥
2.3.33.46: O mountain, this Śivā is Śiva's wife in birth after birth; in every kalpa she is the supreme mother of the wise, in the form of intelligence. ॥46॥
2.3.33.47: She, ever perfect, the giver of siddhi and the embodiment of siddhi, is born again and again. Hara himself devotedly bears Satī's bones and the ashes of her pyre. ॥47॥
2.3.33.48: Therefore give your auspicious daughter to Hara of your own will; otherwise, she herself will go to her beloved's abode, even if you do not give her. ॥48॥
2.3.33.49: Having made a promise, and having seen the countless hardships of your daughter, the Lord of the gods came to her place of penance in the form of a brahmin. ॥49॥
2.3.33.50: Having consoled her and granted a boon, he went to his own abode. Moved by her entreaty, Śambhu asked you for Śivā, O mountain. ॥50॥
2.3.33.51: That was accepted by you both, with minds devoted to Śiva. Tell us, O lord of mountains, why has your mind turned contrary? ॥51॥
2.3.33.52: Therefore we sages, and Arundhatī too, have been quickly sent to you by the Lord, who was entreated by the gods. ॥52॥
2.3.33.53: We indeed counsel you: give Pārvatī to Rudra. If this is done, O mountain, great joy will be yours. ॥53॥
2.3.33.54: O king of mountains, if you do not give Śivā to Śiva of your own will, their marriage will take place here anyway, by the force of destiny. ॥54॥
2.3.33.55: Dear one, that Śaṅkara granted a boon to Śivā while she was performing penance. What the Lord has promised can never turn out otherwise. ॥55॥
2.3.33.56: Ah! The promise of the virtuous who abide by the Lord is hard to transgress among all the worlds; how much more, O mountain, that of the Lord himself. ॥56॥
2.3.33.57: Mahendra alone playfully cut off the wings of the mountains, and Pārvatī playfully broke the peak of Meru. ॥57॥
2.3.33.58: O lord of mountains, all one's possessions should not be destroyed for the sake of one; one should give up one for the sake of the family — this is the eternal scriptural teaching. ॥58॥
2.3.33.59: King Anaraṇya, lord of kings, having fallen into fear of a brahmin, gave his own daughter to the brahmin and thus protected his own possessions. ॥59॥
2.3.33.60: Men versed in the science of polity, his preceptors and the best of his kinsmen, quickly counseled him, who was terrified of a brahmin's curse. ॥60॥
2.3.33.61: O king of mountains, you too in the same way give your daughter to Śiva, protect all your kinsfolk, and bring even the gods under your sway. ॥61॥
2.3.33.62: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Vasiṣṭha, he smiled and, with an aching heart, asked about the story of the king. ॥62॥
2.3.33.63: Himavān said: O brahmin, in whose lineage was that king Anaraṇya born? And how did he, having given away his daughter, protect all his possessions? ॥63॥
2.3.33.64: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the mountain, Vasiṣṭha, with a serene mind, told that mountain the pleasing story of the king. ॥64॥
2.3.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The consoling of the mountain, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥33॥
2.3.34.1: Vasiṣṭha said: King Anaraṇya, lord of kings, was born in the lineage of Manu, namely of the fourteenth Manu, called Indrasāvarṇi. ॥1॥
2.3.34.2: Anaraṇya, best of kings, ruler of the earth with its seven continents, was especially devoted to Śambhu; born of Maṅgalāraṇya, he was mighty. ॥2॥
2.3.34.3: Making Bhṛgu his priest, he performed a hundred sacrifices; yet he did not accept the status of Indra even when the gods offered it. ॥3॥
2.3.34.4: That king had a hundred sons, O Himālaya, and one daughter, beautiful, named Padmā, equal to Padmālayā (Lakṣmī). ॥4॥
2.3.34.5: Whatever affection the king had for his hundred sons, greater than that was his affection for the daughter, O best of mountains. ॥5॥
2.3.34.6: The king had five wives, queens dearer than life, most beloved, foremost among all women, all endowed with good fortune. ॥6॥
2.3.34.7: That girl reached youth in her father's house; he sent out letters to bring a fine bridegroom. ॥7॥
2.3.34.8: Once the sage Pippalāda, eager to go to his own hermitage, saw a Gandharva in a lonely place of austerity. ॥8॥
2.3.34.9: He saw him with a woman, his mind immersed in the ocean of the erotic sentiment, sporting with great love, skilled in the science of love. ॥9॥
2.3.34.10: Seeing him, that tiger among sages became filled with desire; his mind no longer given to austerities, he thought of taking a wife. ॥10॥
2.3.34.11: While that good sage Pippalāda was thus disposed, his mind churned by desire, some time passed there. ॥11॥
2.3.34.12: Once, going to bathe in the Puṣpabhadrā, the lord of sages saw the young Padmā, charming like Padmā (Lakṣmī). ॥12॥
2.3.34.13: Who is this girl? Thus the sage asked the people standing nearby. The people, bowing and held in check by fear of a curse, told him. ॥13॥
2.3.34.14: The people said: This is indeed Anaraṇya's daughter, named Padmā, a second Ramā, fair-hipped, an abode of virtues, sought after by the best of kings. ॥14॥
2.3.34.15: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of the truthful people, the sage was greatly agitated in mind and became eager to obtain her. ॥15॥
2.3.34.16: The sage, having bathed and duly worshipped Śiva, his chosen deity, went, full of desire, to Anaraṇya's court on the pretext of alms, O mountain. ॥16॥
2.3.34.17: The king, seeing the sage, quickly bowed down, anxious with fear, and offering madhuparka and the rest, worshipped him with devotion. ॥17॥
2.3.34.18: Having accepted everything, the sage out of desire asked for the girl. The king fell silent, unable to say anything. ॥18॥
2.3.34.19: The sage demanded the girl: Give her to me, O lord of kings; otherwise I shall reduce everything to ashes in an instant. ॥19॥
2.3.34.20: All the attendants were overwhelmed by his radiance, O sage. The king with his retinue wept, seeing the brahmin worn by old age. ॥20॥
2.3.34.21: All the queens wept, unable to decide what should be done; the chief queen, the girl's mother, overcome by grief, fainted. ॥21॥
2.3.34.22: All the sons became stricken with grief; everything connected with the king was plunged in sorrow, O lord of mountains. ॥22॥
2.3.34.23: Meanwhile the wise brahmin, his unsurpassed preceptor, and the intelligent family priest came into the king's presence. ॥23॥
2.3.34.24: The king bowed to them, worshipped them, and wept before the two; he told them everything and promptly asked what was proper. ॥24॥
2.3.34.25: Then the king's preceptor, a learned brahmin, and the priest, both knowers of scripture and of right conduct, counselled the king, ॥25॥
2.3.34.26: and the grief-stricken queens, the princes and the girl, relying on the highest counsel, beneficial to all. ॥26॥
2.3.34.27: The guru and the family priest said: Listen, O king of great wisdom, to our words that bring true welfare. Do not grieve, you and your family; set your mind rightly on scripture. ॥27॥
2.3.34.28: Whether today or at the end of a year, a daughter must be given away, O king, to a worthy recipient — especially a brahmin — or to someone else. ॥28॥
2.3.34.29: In the three worlds we see no worthier recipient than a brahmin. Give your daughter to the sage and protect all your prosperity. ॥29॥
2.3.34.30: O king, through a single cause all prosperity perishes; by giving up that one, one protects everything — unless that one has come seeking refuge. ॥30॥
2.3.34.31: Vasiṣṭha said: Hearing the words of the wise and lamenting again and again, the king adorned the girl and gave her to the lord of sages. ॥31॥
2.3.34.32: Taking the lovely Padmā, lotus-like, and marrying her with due rites, O mountain, the sage joyfully went to his abode. ॥32॥
2.3.34.33: The king, having given his daughter to the old man, renounced everyone and, with dejection settled in his heart, went to the forest for austerities. ॥33॥
2.3.34.34: When her lord of life had gone to the forest, O mountain, his beautiful wife gave up her life from grief for her husband and daughter. ॥34॥
2.3.34.35: The elders, the sons and the servants fainted without the king; all the other people, learning of it, grieved, sighing heavily. ॥35॥
2.3.34.36: Anaraṇya went to the forest, performed intense austerities, and having propitiated Śaṅkara with devotion, attained Śiva's world, free from affliction. ॥36॥
2.3.34.37: Then the king's eldest son, the righteous one named Kīrtimān, protected the subjects as if they were his sons and ruled the kingdom. ॥37॥
2.3.34.38: Thus I have told you, O mountain, the auspicious story of Anaraṇya — how by giving away his daughter he protected his lineage and all his wealth. ॥38॥
2.3.34.39: O king of mountains, you too, likewise giving your daughter to Śiva, protect your entire family, and bring all under your sway — even the gods. ॥39॥
2.3.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The story of Anaraṇya, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥34॥
2.3.35.1: Nārada said: Having heard the story of Anaraṇya together with the account of the giving of his daughter, what did the best of mountains do, dear one? Tell me that. ॥1॥
2.3.35.2: Brahmā said: Having heard the story of Anaraṇya together with the giving away of his daughter, the lord of mountains, with joined palms, questioned Vasiṣṭha again. ॥2॥
2.3.35.3: Himavān said: O Vasiṣṭha, tiger among sages, son of Brahmā, treasure of compassion, you have told the most wondrous story of Anaraṇya. ॥3॥
2.3.35.4: Since Anaraṇya's daughter obtained the sage Pippalāda as husband, what did she do? Tell me that delightful story. ॥4॥
2.3.35.5: Vasiṣṭha said: Pippalāda, the excellent sage, greatly worn with age, having gone to his own hermitage with that woman, the daughter of Anaraṇya, ॥5॥
2.3.35.6: dwelt there with great delight, an ascetic not excessively lustful; there in the forest on that excellent mountain he constantly performed his own dharma. ॥6॥
2.3.35.7: Then that daughter of Anaraṇya served the sage with devotion, in deed, mind and speech, as Lakṣmī serves Nārāyaṇa. ॥7॥
2.3.35.8: Once, as she, sweetly smiling, was going to bathe in the heavenly river, Dharma, having assumed the form of a king by illusion, saw her on the path. ॥8॥
2.3.35.9: Seated in a beautiful jewelled chariot, adorned with various ornaments, in fresh youth, splendid, his radiance equal to Kāmadeva's. ॥9॥
2.3.35.10: Seeing that beautiful Padmā, the mighty Vṛṣa (Dharma) spoke, in order to know the inner disposition of that sage's wife. ॥10॥
2.3.35.11: Dharma said: O beautiful one, truly a Lakṣmī, worthy of a king, charming, in the very prime of youth, O lovely woman of lasting youth, ॥11॥
2.3.35.12: I tell you the truth, slender one: beside the old sage Pippalāda, afflicted by age, you do not shine at all. ॥12॥
2.3.35.13: Abandoning that brahmin devoted to austerities, unfeeling, facing death, look at me, a lord of kings, a hero in love, tormented by desire. ॥13॥
2.3.35.14: A beautiful woman obtains her beauty from the merit of a former birth; all of that becomes fruitful through the embrace of a passionate lover. ॥14॥
2.3.35.15: Abandoning that husband, O beloved, make me your servant, me who am the lover of a thousand beauties and expert in the science of love. ॥15॥
2.3.35.16: In lonely, delightful forests, on mountain after mountain, on river banks, sport with me; make this birth fruitful. ॥16॥
2.3.35.17: Vasiṣṭha said: To him who had spoken thus and, descending from his chariot, was eager to seize her by the hand, the devoted wife said: ॥17॥
2.3.35.18: Padmā said: Go far away, go far away. You are most sinful, O king. If you look at me with lust, you will perish at once. ॥18॥
2.3.35.19: Abandoning Pippalāda, the best of sages, whose body is purified by austerity, how could I resort to you, conquered by women and greedy for pleasure? ॥19॥
2.3.35.20: By the mere touch of one conquered by women all merit perishes; one conquered by women is a great sinner, and even the sight of him brings sin. ॥20॥
2.3.35.21: Even if he performs good rites, that man who is conquered by a woman is always impure; the ancestors, the gods and all humans censure him. ॥21॥
2.3.35.22: What use to him are knowledge, good austerity, japa, oblations and worship? What use is learning or charity to one whose mind has been stolen by women? ॥22॥
2.3.35.23: Since you speak to me, who am like a mother, regarding me as a woman to be enjoyed, therefore, in time, decline will come upon you through my curse. ॥23॥
2.3.35.24: Vasiṣṭha said: Hearing the chaste woman's curse, Dharma, lord of gods, cast off the king's form, assumed his own form, and trembling, spoke. ॥24॥
2.3.35.25: Dharma said: O mother, know me to be Dharma, the teacher of the teacher of the wise, who always regards others' wives as mothers, O chaste one. ॥25॥
2.3.35.26: I came into your presence to know your inner nature. I know your mind, yet I was impelled by destiny. ॥26॥
2.3.35.27: The chastisement inflicted on me, O virtuous lady, is not wrong; it is fitting. Punishment for those on the wrong path has been ordained by the Lord. ॥27॥
2.3.35.28: Salutation to that Śiva who himself is able to bestow on all happiness, sorrow and boons, prosperity and adversity. ॥28॥
2.3.35.29: Salutation to that Śiva who is able to make foe and friend, love and strife, and to create and destroy the creation. ॥29॥
2.3.35.30: Salutation to that Śiva by whom of old milk was made white, coolness placed in water, and fire made burning. ॥30॥
2.3.35.31: Salutation to that Śiva by whom Prakṛti was created, the principles beginning with Mahat, and Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa and the rest. ॥31॥
2.3.35.32: Brahmā said: Having said this, Dharma, preceptor of the world, stood before her; astonished and pleased by her wifely fidelity, he said nothing more. ॥32॥
2.3.35.33: Then Padmā too, that king's daughter, beloved of Pippalāda, the virtuous one, recognising him as Dharma, spoke in amazement, O mountain. ॥33॥
2.3.35.34: Padmā said: You indeed, O Dharma, are the witness of all the deeds of all beings. Why, O lord, do you mock me to know my mind? ॥34॥
2.3.35.35: Whatever was done, O holy one, no fault was mine; yet you were cursed by me in ignorance, out of a woman's nature, needlessly, O Vṛṣa. ॥35॥
2.3.35.36: What remedy can there be for it? I am now pondering this. May that understanding flash in my mind by which I may obtain peace. ॥36॥
2.3.35.37: Even if this sky, all the directions and the winds should perish, still the curse of a chaste woman never fails. ॥37॥
2.3.35.38: In the Satya age you are complete with four feet, like the moon on the full-moon day; you shine, O king of gods, at all times, day and night. ॥38॥
2.3.35.39: If you were to perish, then creation would be destroyed. Bewildered about what ought to be done, I speak, even if in vain. ॥39॥
2.3.35.40: In the Tretā age there will be the loss of one foot, O best of gods; another foot in the Dvāpara, and the third also in the Kali, O lord. ॥40॥
2.3.35.41: At the end of the Kali age all your feet will be cut off. When the Satya age comes again, you will be whole once more. ॥41॥
2.3.35.42: In the Satya age you are all-pervading, and in the other ages only here and there; according to the order of the ages, you will be as each age requires. ॥42॥
2.3.35.43: Thus let this word of mine prove true and bring you happiness. I go to serve my husband; you go to your own home, O lord. ॥43॥
2.3.35.44: Brahmā said: Hearing her words, Dharma was indeed pleased. O son of Vidhi, he spoke to that chaste woman who had spoken thus. ॥44॥
2.3.35.45: Dharma said: You are blessed, you are devoted to your husband; may it be well with you, O faithful wife. Accept a boon. For the sake of your protection, your husband— ॥45॥
2.3.35.46: May your husband become young, valiant in love and righteous, handsome, virtuous, eloquent, with youth that is ever constant. ॥46॥
2.3.35.47: May he be long-lived, surpassing Mārkaṇḍeya, O auspicious one; richer than Kubera and more lordly than Śakra. ॥47॥
2.3.35.48: May he be a devotee of Śiva equal to Hari, a perfected one surpassing Kapila, equal to Bṛhaspati in intellect, and equal to Vidhi in equanimity. ॥48॥
2.3.35.49: May you be endowed with the good fortune of having your husband for as long as you live; and likewise, O fortunate lady, may you be of lasting youth. ॥49॥
2.3.35.50: You will be the mother of ten sons, virtuous, long-lived and surpassing their own father—there is no doubt. ॥50॥
2.3.35.51: O virtuous woman, may your houses be filled with every kind of wealth, ever radiant, surpassing the mansion of Kubera. ॥51॥
2.3.35.52: Vasiṣṭha said: Having spoken thus, that Dharma stood still, O best of mountains. She circumambulated him, bowed, and went to her own home. ॥52॥
2.3.35.53: Dharma, having thus given blessings, went to his own abode, and with affection praised that Padmā in assembly after assembly. ॥53॥
2.3.35.54: She delighted constantly in private with her young husband. Afterwards good sons were born, surpassing their father in virtues. ॥54॥
2.3.35.55: All prosperity came to the couple, increasing their happiness, bringing growth of every joy, for their welfare both here and hereafter. ॥55॥
2.3.35.56: O lord of mountains, this whole ancient history of that couple has been told, and you have heard it with love and the highest respect. ॥56॥
2.3.35.57: Having understood the truth, give your daughter Pārvatī to Īśvara; give up your ill resentment, O lord of mountains, together with your wife Menā. ॥57॥
2.3.35.58: When a week has passed, at a rare and most auspicious moment, when the lord of the ascendant stands in the ascendant and the Moon is joined with its own son Budha, ॥58॥
2.3.35.59: the Moon being joyful and conjoined with Rohiṇī, the Moon and stars being pure, in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, on a Monday free from all defects, ॥59॥
2.3.35.60: the moment being associated with all benefic planets and free from the aspect of malefic planets, with Jupiter granting good progeny and the good fortune of a husband, ॥60॥
2.3.35.61: —having given the maiden Girijā, the Mother of the world, the primordial Prakṛti, the sovereign Goddess, to the Father of the world, become fulfilled, O mountain. ॥61॥
2.3.35.62: Brahmā said: Having said this, Vasiṣṭha, tiger among sages and best of the wise, fell silent, remembering Śiva, the Lord who performs many divine sports. ॥62॥
2.3.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The story of Padmā and Pippalāda, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥35॥
2.3.36.1: Brahmā said: Having heard Vasiṣṭha's words, Himālaya, the lord of mountains, astonished, together with his retinue and his wife, spoke to the mountains. ॥1॥
2.3.36.2: Himavān said: O Meru, king of mountains, Sahya, Gandhamādana, Mandara, Maināka, Vindhya, O lords of mountains, all of you, listen to my words. ॥2॥
2.3.36.3: Vasiṣṭha speaks thus; what should I do? Let it be considered. Having decided everything in your minds, tell me how matters stand. ॥3॥
2.3.36.4: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, those mountains headed by Sumeru, having carefully decided, spoke affectionately to Himālaya. ॥4॥
2.3.36.5: The mountains said: What need now of deliberation? The matter is already settled just so. O fortunate one, she has been born solely for the purpose of the gods' task. ॥5॥
2.3.36.6: She must be given to Śiva, for she has incarnated for Śiva's sake. Rudra has been propitiated by her, and Rudra himself has spoken to her. ॥6॥
2.3.36.7: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Meru and the others, Himācala became exceedingly pleased, and Girijā laughed in her heart. ॥7॥
2.3.36.8: And Arundhatī enlightened that Menā about the reason, with many kinds of words and various ancient tales. ॥8॥
2.3.36.9: Then Menakā, the mountain's wife, having understood, with a cheerful mind fed the sages, Arundhatī and the mountain, and then ate herself. ॥9॥
2.3.36.10: Then the wise best of mountains, having served those sages well, spoke with joined palms, affectionately, his mind serene and his confusion gone. ॥10॥
2.3.36.11: Himavān said: O fortunate Seven Sages, hear my words. All my astonishment is gone, now that I have heard the story of Śiva and Śivā. ॥11॥
2.3.36.12: My body, my wife Menā, my daughter, my sons, prosperity, success and everything else belong to Śiva alone, not otherwise. ॥12॥
2.3.36.13: Brahmā said: Having said this, he then looked at his daughter, and respectfully adorning her limbs, seated her on the lap of the sages. ॥13॥
2.3.36.14: And the king of mountains again spoke affectionately to the sages then: This portion is to be given by me to him — this is decided. ॥14॥
2.3.36.15: The sages said: Śaṅkara is the mendicant coming to you; you yourself, O mountain, are the giver; and the alms is the goddess Pārvatī — what could be more excellent than this? ॥15॥
2.3.36.16: O Himavat, because of this your state is equal to the loftiness of your peaks. Blessed are you, lord of all mountains, excellent in every way. ॥16॥
2.3.36.17: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, the pure-minded sages gave their blessing to the maiden: Be a giver of happiness to Śiva. ॥17॥
2.3.36.18: Touching her there with their hands they said: Welfare will be yours. As the moon in the bright fortnight, so may your virtues grow. ॥18॥
2.3.36.19: Having said this, all the sages joyfully gave the mountain flowers along with fruits, and thereby made the pledge of betrothal then. ॥19॥
2.3.36.20: Then there the fair-faced Arundhatī, that supreme chaste lady, joyfully enticed Menā with the description of Śiva's virtues. ॥20॥
2.3.36.21: Following worldly custom, he smeared the mountain's beard with turmeric and saffron, an excellent auspicious rite. ॥21॥
2.3.36.22: Then, having fixed an excellent auspicious moment on the fourth day, and being mutually satisfied, they went to Śiva's presence. ॥22॥
2.3.36.23: Going there, bowing to Śiva and praising him with various hymns, all the sages headed by Vasiṣṭha spoke to the Supreme Lord. ॥23॥
2.3.36.24: The sages said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Supreme Lord, great master, hear graciously our account of what has been done by your servants. ॥24॥
2.3.36.25: The king of mountains and Menā have been instructed with various sayings and ancient tales, O Maheśāna; he is fully awakened, no doubt. ॥25॥
2.3.36.26: Pārvatī has been promised to you by the lord of mountains, it is not otherwise. Go forth for the marriage, accompanied by your gaṇas and the gods. ॥26॥
2.3.36.27: Go quickly, O Mahādeva, O Lord, to Himācala's house, and marry Pārvatī according to custom, for the birth of your own offspring. ॥27॥
2.3.36.28: Brahmā said: Hearing their words, Maheśāna, intent on worldly custom, delighted at heart, laughed and said this. ॥28॥
2.3.36.29: Maheśa said: O fortunate ones, a marriage has been neither seen nor heard of by me. Its procedure, as practised of old, should be explained by you in detail. ॥29॥
2.3.36.30: Brahmā said: Hearing that auspicious, worldly speech of Maheśa, they laughingly replied to Sadāśiva, the God of gods. ॥30॥
2.3.36.31: The sages said: Summon quickly Viṣṇu especially, together with his retinue, Brahmā with his sons, lovingly, and likewise the god Śatakratu (Indra); ॥31॥
2.3.36.32: likewise all the hosts of sages, the Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Kinnaras, the Siddhas and Vidyādharas, and also the hosts of Apsarases. ॥32॥
2.3.36.33: Bring all these and others here respectfully, O Lord; they will accomplish all your work, no doubt. ॥33॥
2.3.36.34: Brahmā said: Having said this, the Seven Sages, receiving his permission, joyfully all went to their own abode, praising Śaṅkara's ways. ॥34॥
2.3.36.iti: Thus ends the thirty-sixth adhyāya, named The words of the seven sages, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥36॥
2.3.37.1: Nārada said: Dear father, O wise one, tell me now: when the seven sages had gone, what did the Himālaya mountain do? Show me your grace, O lord, and tell me that. ॥1॥
2.3.37.2: Brahmā said: O lord of sages, when all seven of those sages, together with Arundhatī, had gone, I shall tell you what Himavān did. ॥2॥
2.3.37.3: Then, having consulted his brothers Meru and the others, the great-hearted Himavān, lord of mountains, rejoiced together with his sons and his wife. ॥3॥
2.3.37.4: Then, so instructed by them, Himavān lovingly and with great delight had the letter fixing the auspicious marriage time written by Garga, his own family priest. ॥4॥
2.3.37.5: Then he sent that letter to Śiva, along with articles of many kinds, through his own people, who were joyful at heart. ॥5॥
2.3.37.6: Those people went there to Kailāsa into Śiva's presence, applied the tilaka to him, and gave the letter to Śiva. ॥6॥
2.3.37.7: Specially honoured by the Lord, as was fitting, they all came back, glad at heart, into the presence of the mountain. ॥7॥
2.3.37.8: Seeing his people return, specially honoured by Maheśa and overjoyed, the mountain rejoiced exceedingly in his heart. ॥8॥
2.3.37.9: Then, delighted, he sent invitations, a source of happiness, to all his kinsmen dwelling in various lands. ॥9॥
2.3.37.10: Then he carefully had a store of fine food gathered, and materials of many kinds suited to performing the wedding. ॥10॥
2.3.37.11: He made many mountains of rice, and likewise of flattened rice, of jaggery, of sugar, and likewise of salt; ॥11॥
2.3.37.12: he made pools of milk, of ghee and of curd, and likewise heaps of flour of barley and other grains, and of laḍḍus; ॥12॥
2.3.37.13: and of śaṣkulī cakes, svastika sweets and likewise sugar; and there he made pools of nectar-like sugarcane juice. ॥13॥
2.3.37.14: He made many pools of fresh butter and likewise of fermented drinks, and heaps of various cooked foods, and likewise very tasty juices; ॥14॥
2.3.37.15: various savoury dishes beneficial to the gaṇas and gods, and priceless garments of many kinds, such as were purified by fire; ॥15॥
2.3.37.16: kinds of jewels and gems, gold and silver: having gathered these and other articles according to rule, ॥16॥
2.3.37.17: the mountain began to perform the auspicious rites on an auspicious day. The mountain-women had the purificatory rite of Pārvatī performed. ॥17॥
2.3.37.18: Adorned themselves with ornaments, they joyfully performed the auspicious rite; the delighted brāhmaṇa women of the city carried out the customary folk observances, ॥18॥
2.3.37.19: various rites there with festivity, preceded by great auspiciousness. Himālaya too, glad at heart, having performed the very auspicious customary rite, ॥19॥
2.3.37.20: was wholly delighted and eager for the arrival of his kinsfolk. Meanwhile his kinsmen, who had been invited, ॥20॥
2.3.37.21: came, delighted, with their wives, sons and retinues. Listen attentively, O divine sage, to that very arrival of the mountains. ॥21॥
2.3.37.22: I shall describe it briefly, for the increase of love for Śiva. The great mountain that is the abode of the gods Meru, bearing a divine form, ॥22॥
2.3.37.23: with his company shining with many gems, together with his retinue, having carefully brought the choicest of many jewels and great gems, ॥23॥
2.3.37.24: adorned with fine attire, the glorious one went to Himālaya. Mandara, the mountain rich in every splendour, with his wife and sons, ॥24॥
2.3.37.25: went, taking various fine gifts. Astācala too, divine-natured and noble-minded, bearing gifts, ॥25॥
2.3.37.26: came full of joy, endowed with great splendour. Udayācala, bringing fine gems and jewels too, ॥26॥
2.3.37.27: came most happy, with a most excellent retinue. Malaya, king of mountains, honoured, with his retinue, ॥27॥
2.3.37.28: came, adorned with very divine arrangements and with a large, fine army. And promptly the one named Dardura, joyful, with his wife, ॥28॥
2.3.37.29: full of great splendour, dear one, went to the house of the Himālaya mountain. Niṣada too, glad at heart, came with his retinue; ॥29॥
2.3.37.30: with his sons and womenfolk he lovingly went to the house of the Himālaya mountain. The greatly fortunate mountain Gandhamādana came, ॥30॥
2.3.37.31: and likewise Karavīra, endowed with great wealth. Mahendra, best of mountains, came to Himālaya, ॥31॥
2.3.37.32: with his attendants, sons and wife, endowed with great splendour. Pāriyātra, glad at heart, laden with mines of jewels and gems, ॥32॥
2.3.37.33: came to the Himālaya mountain with his attendants and retinue. Krauñca, king of mountains, with a retinue of great strength, the best of mountains, came respectfully with gifts. ॥33॥
2.3.37.34: The Puruṣottama mountain too, respectful, with his retinue, came to the Himālaya mountain bringing a great gift. ॥34॥
2.3.37.35: Nīla, playful, with his sons and wife, laden with goods, came full of joy to the house of the snow mountain. ॥35॥
2.3.37.36: Trikūṭa, Citrakūṭa too, Veṅkaṭa and likewise Śrīgiri, Gokāmukhī and Nārada came to Himālaya's home. ॥36॥
2.3.37.37: And Vindhya, best of mountains, endowed with manifold riches, auspicious, came glad at heart with his wife and sons. ॥37॥
2.3.37.38: Kālañjara, the great mountain, filled with great joy, lovingly came to the Himālaya mountain with many of his own attendants. ॥38॥
2.3.37.39: And Kailāsa, the great mountain, filled with great joy, the lord shining above all, came out of kindness. ॥39॥
2.3.37.40: O brāhmaṇa, the other mountains that are in other continents too, and all the mountains that are here as well, came to Himālaya. ॥40॥
2.3.37.41: O sage, the mountains whom he had joyfully invited there beforehand all came with affection, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā. ॥41॥
2.3.37.42: Then indeed all of them, Śoṇabhadra and the others, came, greatly splendid, with great affection, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā. ॥42॥
2.3.37.43: All the rivers came, adorned with various ornaments and bearing divine forms, with affection, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā. ॥43॥
2.3.37.44: Godāvarī and Yamunā, and likewise Brahmā's consort Sarasvatī and Veṇikā came to the Himālaya mountain, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā. ॥44॥
2.3.37.45: Gaṅgā, with very great joy, adorned with various ornaments and divine in form, came with affection, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā. ॥45॥
2.3.37.46: Narmadā, the daughter of Rudra and best of rivers, full of great delight, came quickly with great affection, thinking, it is the wedding of Śiva and Śivā. ॥46॥
2.3.37.47: Then, with all of them arriving from every side at the Himālaya mountain, the divine city, endowed with every splendour, became crowded. ॥47॥
2.3.37.48: It was full of great festivity, abounding in gleaming banners, flags and arched gateways; the sun was screened off by canopies, and it shone with manifold brilliance. ॥48॥
2.3.37.49: Himālaya too, with great affection and respect of many kinds, honoured them — the mountains and the rivers — each as was fitting. ॥49॥
2.3.37.50: He lodged them all separately in fine quarters and satisfied them completely with abundant provisions. ॥50॥
2.3.37.iti: Thus ends the thirty-seventh adhyāya, named The sending of the wedding letter, the gathering of provisions and the coming of the mountains, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥37॥
2.3.38.1: Brahmā said: Then, O best of sages, Himavān, the lord of mountains, pleased, adorned his own city wonderfully for a supreme festival. ॥1॥
2.3.38.2: Its roads were sprinkled with water, cleaned, and adorned with the highest splendours; and at every door there were auspicious decorations of plantains and the like, furnished with auspicious articles. ॥2॥
2.3.38.3: He arranged the courtyard with plantain-trunk pillars, bound together with silk cords and decorated with mango sprouts, ॥3॥
2.3.38.4: furnished with garlands of mālatī jasmine, resplendent with shining arches, and adorned with auspicious articles placed in the four directions. ॥4॥
2.3.38.5: In the same way, filled with supreme joy, the king of mountains did everything for the sake of his own daughter, placing the greatly powerful Garga at the front, doing all that was fitting for the occasion and highly auspicious. ॥5॥
2.3.38.6: Having summoned Viśvakarman, he respectfully had him build a very spacious pavilion, charming with altars and the like. ॥6॥
2.3.38.7: O celestial sage, it extended over ten thousand yojanas, possessed of many excellent features and filled with various wonders. ॥7॥
2.3.38.8: All things there, moving and unmoving, were charmingly made in the likeness of the real ones; it was on every side a treasury of marvels, astonishing with various objects. ॥8॥
2.3.38.9: There the moving was especially surpassed by the unmoving, and the unmoving too was surpassed by the moving. ॥9॥
2.3.38.10: There dry ground was outdone by water, and water not otherwise by ground; no experts at all could tell what was water and what was land. ॥10॥
2.3.38.11: In some places there were artificial lions, in some rows of cranes, and in some places charming artificial peacocks. ॥11॥
2.3.38.12: In some places artificial women were dancing with men, bewitching all people; and likewise artificial women were gazing on. ॥12॥
2.3.38.13: Likewise, in the same manner, there were charming doorkeepers holding bows raised in their hands, motionless yet seeming alive. ॥13॥
2.3.38.14: At the door stood a wondrous artificial Mahālakṣmī, possessed of all auspicious marks, as if she had come directly from the ocean of milk. ॥14॥
2.3.38.15: There were adorned artificial elephants, like real ones; likewise horses with their riders, and elephants with elephant-riders. ॥15॥
2.3.38.16: Chariots drawn by charioteers, full of great wonder; likewise other vehicles and foot-soldiers, all artificial. ॥16॥
2.3.38.17: Thus, O sage, all this was made by Viśvakarman with a delighted heart, for the purpose of enchanting the gods and the sages. ॥17॥
2.3.38.18: At the main gate, O sage, an artificial Nandin was made, resembling pure crystal; he was exactly like Nandin himself. ॥18॥
2.3.38.19: Above it was a very divine Puṣpaka aerial car, decked with jewels, gleaming with bright sprouts and beautifully adorned with chowries. ॥19॥
2.3.38.20: On the left side were two elephants, the colour of pure saffron, four-tusked, sixty years old, in rut, greatly resplendent. ॥20॥
2.3.38.21: Likewise he made two horses, radiant like the sun, greatly brilliant, divine, adorned with chowries and decked with divine ornaments. ॥21॥
2.3.38.22: Likewise the guardians of the worlds, armoured and rich in fine jewels, and all the gods, were made by Viśvakarman true to life. ॥22॥
2.3.38.23: So too all the sages, Bhṛgu and the others rich in austerity, and other demigods likewise, and other Siddhas too, were made. ॥23॥
2.3.38.24: Likewise an artificial Viṣṇu was fashioned, accompanied by all his attendants headed by Garuḍa, of supremely wondrous form. ॥24॥
2.3.38.25: In the same way, O Nārada, an artificial image of me was fashioned, surrounded by my sons, the Vedas and the Siddhas, reciting hymns. ॥25॥
2.3.38.26: Likewise an artificial Śakra was fashioned, mounted on the elephant Airāvata, accompanied by his retinue, resembling the full moon. ॥26॥
2.3.38.27: What need of saying much, O divine sage? The whole assembly of the gods was swiftly fashioned by Viśvakarman, urged on by the Snow Mountain. ॥27॥
2.3.38.28: Such was the pavilion made by him: of divine form, full of many wonders, vast, bewildering even to the gods. ॥28॥
2.3.38.29: Then, commanded by the lord of mountains, the highly intelligent Viśvakarman carefully built the respective worlds for the residence of the gods and others. ॥29॥
2.3.38.30: And right there great couches, very bright, supremely wondrous, comfortable and divine, were made for them by Viśvakarman. ॥30॥
2.3.38.31: Likewise, in a moment, he created a wondrous Satyaloka, endowed with supreme radiance, for the residence of the Self-born (Brahmā). ॥31॥
2.3.38.32: In the same way he created in a moment for Viṣṇu another abode called Vaikuṇṭha, greatly brilliant, divine, full of various wonders. ॥32॥
2.3.38.33: Likewise that Viśvakarman created the divine, wondrous and excellent mansion of the lord of the immortals (Indra), endowed with every splendour. ॥33॥
2.3.38.34: He likewise gladly created beautiful houses for the guardians of the worlds, divine, wondrous and great. ॥34॥
2.3.38.35: And likewise, in due order, wonderful dwellings were made by him for all the other immortals. ॥35॥
2.3.38.36: Viśvakarman of great intellect, who had obtained a great boon from Śambhu, created everything in a moment, solely for the satisfaction of Śiva. ॥36॥
2.3.38.37: Likewise he made Śambhu's mansion: supremely wonderful, greatly brilliant, very radiant, well worshipped by the foremost gods, bearing the emblems of the Mountain-Lord (Śiva), set as in Śivaloka, beautifully adorned. ॥37॥
2.3.38.38: Such was the construction made by Viśvakarman for Śiva's satisfaction: varied, supremely wondrous and greatly brilliant. ॥38॥
2.3.38.39: Having thus done all this, along with the worldly customs, Himācala joyfully awaited the arrival of Śambhu. ॥39॥
2.3.38.40: Thus, O divine sage, the delightful account of Himālaya has been told in full. What more do you wish to hear? ॥40॥
2.3.38.iti: Thus ends the thirty-eighth adhyāya, named The building of the pavilion and the rest, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥38॥
2.3.39.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi (Brahmā), dear father, greatly wise one, disciple of Viṣṇu, salutation to you. This wondrous story has been heard by us from you, O treasure of compassion. ॥1॥
2.3.39.2: Now I wish to hear the marriage-story of the moon-crested Śiva, most auspicious, destroying all floods of sin. ॥2॥
2.3.39.3: What did Mahādeva do on receiving the auspicious letter? Narrate to me that divine story of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self. ॥3॥
2.3.39.4: Brahmā said: Listen, dear child, greatly wise one, to the supreme glory of Śaṅkara — what Mahādeva did on receiving the auspicious letter. ॥4॥
2.3.39.5: Then Śambhu, taking that auspicious letter with joy, laughed, delighted at heart; the all-pervading Lord showed honour to them the messengers. ॥5॥
2.3.39.6: Having had it read out properly, he accepted it according to rule; and, respectful, he sent those people off after honouring them greatly. ॥6॥
2.3.39.7: He said to those groups of sages: The task has been done well and auspiciously. You must come to my wedding; the marriage has been accepted by me. ॥7॥
2.3.39.8: Hearing these words of Śambhu, they, overjoyed, bowed to him, circumambulated him and went to their abodes, extolling their own supreme good fortune. ॥8॥
2.3.39.9: Then Śambhu, lord of the gods, the Lord who performs great sports, following worldly custom, quickly remembered you, O sage. ॥9॥
2.3.39.10: You came with great love, praising your supreme good fortune, bowing, with lowered shoulders, humble in spirit, with joined palms. ॥10॥
2.3.39.11: You praised him, uttering cries of victory again and again, requesting his command and extolling your good fortune, O sage. ॥11॥
2.3.39.12: Then Śambhu, delighted at heart, displaying the worldly way, spoke to you, O best of sages, gladdening you with auspicious words. ॥12॥
2.3.39.13: Śiva said: Listen with love, O best of sages; today I tell you from myself. I tell you this because you are dear to me, the crest-jewel among the kings of devotees. ॥13॥
2.3.39.14: Great austerity was performed by the goddess Pārvatī at your instruction. Pleased, I granted her the boon of having me as husband. ॥14॥
2.3.39.15: And I shall marry her, for I am subject to her through her devotion. The auspicious moment has been fixed by the seven sages and verified by them. ॥15॥
2.3.39.16: It will take place on the seventh day from today, O Nārada. Following the worldly way, I shall hold a great festival. ॥16॥
2.3.39.17: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self, you, dear son, with a glad mind, bowed to the Lord and spoke these words. ॥17॥
2.3.39.18: Nārada said: This indeed is your vow: you are regarded as subject to your devotees. And you have rightly fulfilled what Pārvatī desired in her heart. ॥18॥
2.3.39.19: Some task fit for me should be told by you, O Lord. Regarding me as your own servant, show me grace; salutation to you. ॥19॥
2.3.39.20: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by you, Śambhu Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, glad at heart, replied to you respectfully, O lord of sages. ॥20॥
2.3.39.21: Śiva said: On my word, O sage, invite without fail the gods headed by Viṣṇu, the sages and the Siddhas, and others too, from everywhere. ॥21॥
2.3.39.22: Let all come eagerly, adorned with every splendour, with their wives, sons and retinues, out of love and out of regard for my command. ॥22॥
2.3.39.23: Those gods and others who do not come here to my wedding festival, O sage, shall surely not be regarded by me as my own. ॥23॥
2.3.39.24: Brahmā said: Then you, beloved of Śaṅkara, bearing the Lord's command, quickly went to each one and invited them all, O sage. ॥24॥
2.3.39.25: After that invitation, you, the best of sages, quickly came back to Śambhu's presence and, receiving his permission, remained there, O Nārada. ॥25॥
2.3.39.26: Śiva too waited eagerly, longing for their arrival, with all his Gaṇas festive and dancing in every direction. ॥26॥
2.3.39.27: At that very time Acyuta (Viṣṇu), having arrayed himself in his attire, quickly came to Kailāsa with his retinue. ॥27॥
2.3.39.28: Having joyfully bowed to Śiva with true devotion, together with his wife and his host, and receiving his permission, he stayed in a fine place, pleased at heart. ॥28॥
2.3.39.29: Likewise I quickly and joyfully went to Kailāsa with my attendants, and having bowed to the Lord, I stayed there, delighted, accompanied by my followers. ॥29॥
2.3.39.30: Indra and the other guardians of the worlds came with their retinues, all likewise adorned, festive, and with their wives. ॥30॥
2.3.39.31: In the same way the sages, Nāgas, Siddhas and Upasuras, and others too, duly invited, came here festively. ॥31॥
2.3.39.32: Then Maheśvara joyfully honoured each of all the gods and others who had come there, one by one. ॥32॥
2.3.39.33: Then there was a great, supremely wondrous festival on Kailāsa; the celestial women then performed dances and the like, as was fitting. ॥33॥
2.3.39.34: At this time all the gods headed by Viṣṇu who had assembled stayed there, O sage, in order to conduct Śambhu's wedding procession. ॥34॥
2.3.39.35: Then all of them, commanded by Śiva and bound by the thought, this is our own task, did all this work of Śiva as service to Śiva. ॥35॥
2.3.39.36: The Seven Mothers there, filled with joy, performed the supreme rite of adorning Śiva, again as was fitting. ॥36॥
2.3.39.37: Then, by the will of that Supreme Lord, the glorious master, O best of sages, his natural attire itself became his adornment. ॥37॥
2.3.39.38: The moon then took its place as the crown, and the beautiful third eye became an auspicious tilaka. ॥38॥
2.3.39.39: And the two serpents known as his ear-ornaments became his earrings, set with many kinds of gems, O sage. ॥39॥
2.3.39.40: The serpents on his other limbs became ornaments for those limbs, exceedingly lovely and made of many kinds of gems. ॥40॥
2.3.39.41: The sacred ash became a body-ointment made from sandal and the like, and the elephant hide and the rest became that beautiful divine silken garment. ॥41॥
2.3.39.42: Such a beautiful form came about, extremely hard to describe. The Lord himself, in person, attained majesty of his own accord. ॥42॥
2.3.39.43: Then all the gods and dānavas, the nāgas, birds, apsarases and great sages, all gathering at that time in Śiva's presence, in great festive mood and full of joy, exclaimed, Aho! ॥43॥
2.3.39.44: They all said: Go, go, Mahādeva, O Maheśvara, for your marriage with Girijā, the great goddess; together with us, show your grace. ॥44॥
2.3.39.45: Then Viṣṇu, his mind gladdened by understanding, bowed to Śaṅkara with devotion and spoke these words suited to the occasion. ॥45॥
2.3.39.46: Viṣṇu said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, loving to those who come for refuge, accomplisher of the tasks of your devotees, O Lord, hear my request. ॥46॥
2.3.39.47: O Śambhu, O Śaṅkara, you should perform here the rite of your own marriage with the goddess, daughter of the lord of mountains, according to the procedure laid down in the Gṛhya texts. ॥47॥
2.3.39.48: And when the marriage rite is being performed by you, O Hara, that very procedure will thereby gain full renown throughout the world. ॥48॥
2.3.39.49: O Lord, gladly have the erection of the pavilion and the Nāndīmukha rite performed according to that family custom, proclaiming your own glory in the world. ॥49॥
2.3.39.50: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Viṣṇu, Śambhu, the supreme Lord, intent on worldly custom, then did that according to the rules. ॥50॥
2.3.39.51: Authorized by him, I, together with the sages, gladly and respectfully performed there everything fitting for the auspicious occasion, that whole rite. ॥51॥
2.3.39.52: Kaśyapa, Atri and Vasiṣṭha, Gautama, Bhāguri, the preceptor Bṛhaspati's kin? — rather: Gautama, Bhāguri, Guru, Kaṇva, Bṛhaspati, Śakti, Jamadagni, Parāśara, ॥52॥
2.3.39.53: Mārkaṇḍeya, Śilāpāka, Aruṇapāla, Akṛtaśrama, Agastya, Cyavana, Garga and Śilāda, O great sage, ॥53॥
2.3.39.54: Dadhīci and Upamanyu, Bharadvāja, Akṛtavraṇa, Pippalāda, Kuśika, Kautsa, and Vyāsa with his disciples— ॥54॥
2.3.39.55: These and many others came to Śiva's presence; well urged by me, they performed the rite there according to rule. ॥55॥
2.3.39.56: All of them, masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, performed the protective rite for Maheśa by the Vedic procedure, after carrying out the auspicious kautuka wedding-thread ceremony. ॥56॥
2.3.39.57: With hymns of the Ṛg, Yajus and Sāman, and likewise with various other excellent ones, all the sages gladly performed many auspicious rites. ॥57॥
2.3.39.58: Together with Śambhu and me, they gladly performed the worship of the planets and of all the gods stationed in the maṇḍala, for the removal of obstacles. ॥58॥
2.3.39.59: Then Śiva, well pleased, having done everything properly—both worldly and Vedic rites—joyfully bowed to the brāhmaṇas. ॥59॥
2.3.39.60: Then the Lord of all, placing the brāhmaṇas and gods in front, joyfully set out from that Kailāsa, the best of mountains. ॥60॥
2.3.39.61: Outside the Kailāsa mountain Śambhu, the Lord, stood joyfully together with the gods and brāhmaṇas, accepting various honours. ॥61॥
2.3.39.62: Then a great festival took place there, held by the gods and others for Maheśa's delight, with singing, instrumental music and fine dancing. ॥62॥
2.3.39.iti: Thus ends the thirty-ninth adhyāya, named The invitation of the gods, the coming of the gods and Śiva's journey, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥39॥
2.3.40.1: Brahmā said: Then Śambhu, having summoned all the gaṇas headed by Nandin, joyfully commanded them to go there together with himself. ॥1॥
2.3.40.2: Śiva said: You too, come along with me to the mountain's city, leaving some gaṇas here, with great festivity. ॥2॥
2.3.40.3: Brahmā said: Then, thus permitted, the lords of the gaṇas set out joyfully, each taking his own force; I shall describe them in some measure. ॥3॥
2.3.40.4: Śaṅkhakarṇa, lord of gaṇas, went forth with a crore of gaṇas to proceed with Śiva toward the city of Himācala. ॥4॥
2.3.40.5: Kekarākṣa, full of great festive joy, went with ten crores of gaṇas, and Vikṛta, leader of gaṇas, with eight crores of gaṇas. ॥5॥
2.3.40.6: Viśākha, leader of gaṇas, went with four crores of gaṇas, and Pārijāta, foremost of gaṇas, with nine crores. ॥6॥
2.3.40.7: The glorious Sarvāntaka went with sixty crores, and likewise Vikṛtānana; Dundubha, leader of gaṇas, with eight crores of gaṇas. ॥7॥
2.3.40.8: Likewise the gaṇa-lord named Kapāla went with five crores, and the heroic Sandāraka with six crores of gaṇas, O sage. ॥8॥
2.3.40.9: Here Kanduka and likewise Kuṇḍaka went with crores upon crores, and Viṣṭambha, a gaṇa-chief, likewise with eight crores of gaṇas. ॥9॥
2.3.40.10: The gaṇa-chief Pippala went joyfully with a thousand crores, and so did the heroic gaṇa-lord Sanādaka, O best of sages. ॥10॥
2.3.40.11: Likewise Āveśana, leader of gaṇas, went with eight crores; the gaṇa-chief Mahākeśa went with a thousand crores. ॥11॥
2.3.40.12: Kuṇḍa went with twelve crores, and likewise Parvataka, O sage; the heroic Candratāpana went along with eight crores. ॥12॥
2.3.40.13: Kāla, Kālaka, and Mahākāla went with a hundred crores, and likewise the gaṇa-lord named Agnika. ॥13॥
2.3.40.14: Agnimukha, leader of gaṇas, went with a crore; and Ādityamūrdhan with a crore, and likewise Ghanāvaha. ॥14॥
2.3.40.15: Sannāha went with a hundred crores, and likewise the gaṇa-chief Kumuda; Amogha and Kokila, overlords of gaṇas, with a hundred crores. ॥15॥
2.3.40.16: Sumantra, leader of gaṇas, went with crores upon crores; Kākapādodara with sixty crores, and likewise Santānaka. ॥16॥
2.3.40.17: Mahābala with nine crores, and Madhupiṅga and Kokila; Nīla with ninety crores, and likewise Pūrṇabhadra. ॥17॥
2.3.40.18: Caturvaktra went with seven crores, Karaṇa with twenty crores, and the gaṇa-lord Ahiromaka went with ninety crores. ॥18॥
2.3.40.19: Yajvākṣa, Śatamanyu and Meghamanyu, O Nārada—all these gaṇa-lords went, each separately, with as many crores. ॥19॥
2.3.40.20: Kāṣṭhāṅguṣṭha, leader of gaṇas, went with sixty-four crores; also Virūpākṣa, Sukeśa, and the eternal Vṛṣabha, ॥20॥
2.3.40.21: Tālaketu, Ṣaḍāsya, the eternal Cañcvāsya, Saṃvartaka, likewise Caitra, Lakulīśa the self-ruling lord, ॥21॥
2.3.40.22: Lokāntaka, the radiant-souled Dīptātman, likewise Daityāntaka, O sage, the divine and glorious Bhṛṅgiriṭi, and likewise Devadevapriya, ॥22॥
2.3.40.23: Aśani and Bhānuka, each with sixty-four crores by thousands, went festively with Śiva for Śiva's wedding. ॥23॥
2.3.40.24: The Pramathas went with a thousand crores of bhūtas and three crores more; Vīrabhadra with sixty-four crores and three crores of the Romajas (born of his hair). ॥24॥
2.3.40.25: Surrounded by twenty hundreds of thousands of crores of crores, the gaṇa-chiefs headed by Nandin went there to Śaṅkara's festival. ॥25॥
2.3.40.26: Kṣetrapāla and Bhairava, accompanied by crores upon crores of gaṇas, came lovingly in great festivity, thinking, it is Śaṅkara's wedding. ॥26॥
2.3.40.27: These and other countless, mighty gaṇa-chiefs went there with great love and enthusiasm to Śaṅkara's festival. ॥27॥
2.3.40.28: All were thousand-handed, wearing crowns of matted hair, adorned with the crescent moon, blue-throated and three-eyed. ॥28॥
2.3.40.29: All wore rudrākṣa ornaments and holy ash, and were adorned with necklaces, earrings, armlets, crowns and the like. ॥29॥
2.3.40.30: Resembling Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Indra, endowed with powers such as aṇimā, and shining like crores of suns, the lords of gaṇas looked splendid there. ॥30॥
2.3.40.31: Some moved on the earth, some in the netherworld, some in the sky, and some in the seven heavens, O sage. ॥31॥
2.3.40.32: What need of saying more, O divine sage? Śambhu's own gaṇas, dwelling in all the worlds, came lovingly to Śaṅkara's festival. ॥32॥
2.3.40.33: Thus, accompanied by the gods, the gaṇas and others, Lord Śaṅkara went to the city of Himagiri for his own wedding. ॥33॥
2.3.40.34: When the Lord of all went for his wedding with the gods and others, what happened there—hear that, O lord of sages. ॥34॥
2.3.40.35: Becoming Rudra's sister, Caṇḍī, full of festive spirit, came there with great delight, bringing great terror to others. ॥35॥
2.3.40.36: Mounted on a corpse as her seat, adorned with serpent ornaments, carrying on her head a full golden pitcher of great brilliance, ॥36॥
2.3.40.37: accompanied by her own retinue, with blazing face and blazing eyes, playing about in sport, filled with joy, of mighty strength. ॥37॥
2.3.40.38: There, O sage, divine hosts of bhūtas, misshapen, by crores and of many kinds, then shone in great numbers. ॥38॥
2.3.40.39: Joined by them, Caṇḍī of distorted face went in front, full of playfulness, delighted, causing playful mischief out of affection. ॥39॥
2.3.40.40: Then all the gaṇas of Rudra, numbering eleven crores, fierce and dear to Rudra, were placed behind by Caṇḍī. ॥40॥
2.3.40.41: Then the three worlds were filled with the booming of ḍamaru drums, with the clanging sound of bherī drums, and with the blare of conches. ॥41॥
2.3.40.42: Likewise, with the thunder of dundubhi drums, a tumultuous sound arose, bringing auspiciousness to the world and dispelling whatever was inauspicious. ॥42॥
2.3.40.43: Following behind the gaṇas, all the gods, full of eagerness, went along, together with all the Siddhas and the guardians of the worlds and others, O sage. ॥43॥
2.3.40.44: Then the Lord of Ramā (Viṣṇu), moving in the middle, seated on Garuḍa, shone with a great parasol held over him, O sage. ॥44॥
2.3.40.45: He was being fanned with chowries, surrounded by his own attendants and by radiant companions, and adorned in the manner of his own ornaments. ॥45॥
2.3.40.46: So too I Brahmā shone forth, moving along the path, resplendent, accompanied by the embodied Vedas, the Śāstras, the Purāṇas and the Āgamas, ॥46॥
2.3.40.47: and by Sanaka and the other great Siddhas, and by my sons together with the Prajāpatis; joined with my retinue, I was intent on serving Śiva. ॥47॥
2.3.40.48: Śakra, lord of the gods, in the midst of his own army, mounted on the elephant Airāvata and exceedingly adorned with various ornaments, shone as he went. ॥48॥
2.3.40.49: Then those many sages, going along, shone forth, exceedingly eager for Śiva's wedding. ॥49॥
2.3.40.50: Śākinīs, Yātudhānas, Vetālas, Brahmarākṣasas, Bhūtas, Pretas and Piśācas, and likewise others, the Pramathas and the rest, went along. ॥50॥
2.3.40.51: Tumburu, Nārada, Hāhā and Hūhū and other excellent Gandharvas, and the Kinnaras, went joyfully, sounding their instruments. ॥51॥
2.3.40.52: All the Mothers of the world and the daughters of the gods from every side, Gāyatrī and Sāvitrī, Lakṣmī and other celestial women, ॥52॥
2.3.40.53: these and others—the wives of the gods, mothers of the world—all went filled with joy, thinking, it is Śaṅkara's wedding. ॥53॥
2.3.40.54: The bull, shining like pure crystal and beautiful in every way, who is called Dharma by the Vedas, the Śāstras, the Siddhas and the great sages— ॥54॥
2.3.40.55: mounted on that bull, Mahādeva, who loves Dharma, shone exceedingly as he went, attended by all the gods and sages. ॥55॥
2.3.40.56: Accompanied by these and by the great sages whose aims were fulfilled, Maheśa, richly adorned in many ways, shone as he proceeded to the abode of the mountain named Himālaya for the taking of Śivā's hand in marriage. ॥56॥
2.3.40.57: Thus has been told the story of Śambhu—his journey, a supreme festival. Now hear, O Nārada, the noble account of what took place in the city of Himālaya. ॥57॥
2.3.40.iti: Thus ends the fortieth adhyāya, named Śiva's journey, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥40॥
2.3.41.1: Brahmā said: Then, having consulted together and having received Śaṅkara's command, Hari, O sage, sent you first to the abode of the mountain. ॥1॥
2.3.41.2: Then, having bowed to the Lord of all, you, Nārada, urged affectionately by Hari, went ahead towards the house of Himācala. ॥2॥
2.3.41.3: Having gone there, O sage, you saw yourself—an artificial likeness fashioned there by Viśvakarman—and, astonished, you were filled with embarrassment. ॥3॥
2.3.41.4: O great sage, you were wearied by that artificial self of yours; you became intent on gazing at the handiwork of Viśvakarman. ॥4॥
2.3.41.5: You entered the pavilion of that Himādri, adorned with jewels, furnished with golden pitchers and greatly beautified with plantain trees and the like, ॥5॥
2.3.41.6: furnished with a thousand pillars, wonderful and supremely marvellous; and seeing the altar likewise, O sage, you fell into amazement. ॥6॥
2.3.41.7: Then, O sage Nārada, greatly astonished in mind, with your understanding lost and your intellect bewildered, you said to the lord of mountains: ॥7॥
2.3.41.8: Have the gods headed by Viṣṇu arrived now? And likewise all the great sages, the Siddhas and the demigods? ॥8॥
2.3.41.9: Has Mahādeva, mounted on the bull and surrounded by the Gaṇas, come for the wedding? Tell the truth, O lord of mountains. ॥9॥
2.3.41.10: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of yours, whose mind was astonished, O sage, that mountain Himavat spoke truthful words to you. ॥10॥
2.3.41.11: Himavān said: O Nārada, most wise one, Śiva has not yet come for the marriage of Pārvatī, with his Gaṇas and the wedding party. ॥11॥
2.3.41.12: Know with a clear mind, Nārada, that this is a marvel made by Viśvakarman. Give up your amazement, O divine sage; be at ease and remember Śiva. ॥12॥
2.3.41.13: Having eaten and rested, well pleased, show me kindness and go to Śaṅkara together with Maināka and the other mountains. ॥13॥
2.3.41.14: Accompanied by these mountains, O great-minded one, entreat Śiva and quickly bring him here, together with the gods and the hosts of great sages—he whose tender lotus-feet are worshipped by gods and demons. ॥14॥
2.3.41.15: Brahmā said: Saying, so be it, you, high-minded one, having duly finished your tasks there and having eaten, went quickly at once with those sons of the mountain and others to the presence of Śiva. ॥15॥
2.3.41.16: There the radiant Mahādeva, surrounded by the gods and others, was seen, and was saluted with devotion by you and by those mountains. ॥16॥
2.3.41.17: Then, together with me and Viṣṇu, all the gods with Vāsava, O sage, and likewise all the attendants of Rudra questioned you, ॥17॥
2.3.41.18: astonished and with minds troubled by doubt on seeing the mountains Maināka, Sahya, Meru and the rest, adorned with various ornaments. ॥18॥
2.3.41.19: The gods said: O Nārada, most wise, you appear astonished. Were you honoured by the Himālaya or not? Tell us in detail. ॥19॥
2.3.41.20: Why have these excellent mountains come here—Maināka, Sahya, Meru and the others—most majestic and finely adorned? ॥20॥
2.3.41.21: Will that mountain give his daughter to Śambhu or not, Nārada? What is happening today in Himālaya's house, dear one? Tell us that. ॥21॥
2.3.41.22: Speak to us gods, whose minds are thus in doubt and who are asking you; remove our doubt, O you of good vows. ॥22॥
2.3.41.23: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of the gods led by Viṣṇu, O sage, you, astonished by the magic of Tvaṣṭṛ, spoke to them. ॥23॥
2.3.41.24: Taking us aside, O sage, you spoke these words to me, to Viṣṇu, and to Śacī's lord, ruler of all the gods, the wing-cutter, the old enemy of the mountains. ॥24॥
2.3.41.25: Nārada said: That strange, wondrous display made by Tvaṣṭṛ is bewildering to all the gods; by it he wishes to bewilder all the gods, through a contrivance, out of sheer affection. ॥25॥
2.3.41.26: Formerly you dealt him a bewildering blow; you have entirely forgotten all that, O lord of Śacī. Therefore he surely wishes to get the better of you in the house of that great-souled mountain. ॥26॥
2.3.41.27: I was bewildered by him with a shining replica of myself; likewise Viṣṇu was made by him, and Brahmā and Śakra too in the same way. ॥27॥
2.3.41.28: What need of much talk, O lord of gods? All the hosts of gods have been made artificially as images; nothing has been left out. ॥28॥
2.3.41.29: To bewilder everyone, and the gods especially, an illusion made of images has been created, producing jest and mischief. ॥29॥
2.3.41.30: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, the lord of gods, his body shaken with fear, quickly spoke then to Viṣṇu, Hari: ॥30॥
2.3.41.31: Indra said: O God of gods, lord of Ramā, Tvaṣṭṛ will kill me. Burning with grief for his son, he will do it by this pretext, not otherwise. ॥31॥
2.3.41.32: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, Janārdana, the God of gods, laughing, spoke then, reassuring Śakra: ॥32॥
2.3.41.33: Viṣṇu said: Formerly, O lord of Śacī, you were bewildered by the Nivātakavacas, Dānavas and old enemies, through the power of great magic. ॥33॥
2.3.41.34: This mountain Himavat and all the other mountains were made wingless by you, O Vāsava, at my word. ॥34॥
2.3.41.35: These foolish mountains, remembering that and seeing you, wish to conquer you by illusion; but there is no need to fear even an enemy such as this. ॥35॥
2.3.41.36: Śaṅkara, kind to his devotees, is the Lord of us all; he will bring about well-being in every way, Śakra, without doubt. ॥36॥
2.3.41.37: Brahmā said: Śakra, his mind disturbed, was conversing thus, and Hari had spoken; then Giriśa, adopting the manner of the world, spoke. ॥37॥
2.3.41.38: Īśvara said: O Hari, O lord of gods, what are you two saying to each other now? Having said this to the two, Maheśāna then addressed you, O sage: ॥38॥
2.3.41.39: What does the great mountain say? Tell it truly, Nārada. Relate the whole account; you should not keep anything secret. ॥39॥
2.3.41.40: Does the mountain give his own daughter or not? Tell me that quickly. What did you see, and what was done when you went there? Tell all of it gladly and at once, dear one. ॥40॥
2.3.41.41: Brahmā said: Thus addressed there by Śambhu, O sage, you, who have vision of the divine, told the whole secret: what had been seen there in the pavilion. ॥41॥
2.3.41.42: Nārada said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, listen to my auspicious words. There is no fear of any obstacle at all in the marriage, O Lord. ॥42॥
2.3.41.43: The lord of mountains will certainly give you the maiden. These mountains have come to fetch you; there is no doubt. ॥43॥
2.3.41.44: But a wondrous illusion has been fashioned to bewilder the immortals, for amusement, O all-knowing one; there is no possibility of any obstacle. ॥44॥
2.3.41.45: At his command, O Lord, Viśvakarmā, the great master of illusion, made in his house a marvellous pavilion full of many wonders. ॥45॥
2.3.41.46: And a bewildering assembly of all the gods was fashioned there. Seeing it, I was struck with amazement, deluded by that illusion. ॥46॥
2.3.41.47: Brahmā said: Hearing those words, dear one, the Lord Śambhu, who acts according to worldly custom, laughingly addressed Hari and all the other gods. ॥47॥
2.3.41.48: Īśvara said: If the mountain Himācala is going to give me the maiden, what have I to do with illusion? Tell me truly, O Viṣṇu. ॥48॥
2.3.41.49: O Brahmā, Śakra, sages and gods, tell me truly: what have I to do with illusion, if the mountain is going to give the maiden? ॥49॥
2.3.41.50: The goal is to be achieved by some means or other—so say the learned who know sound reasoning. Therefore let all of you, seeking the aim, led by Viṣṇu, go quickly. ॥50॥
2.3.41.51: Brahmā said: Conversing thus with the gods, Śambhu, though self-controlled, then became as if brought under the sway of Smara, like an ordinary man. ॥51॥
2.3.41.52: Then, at Śambhu's command, all the immortals headed by Viṣṇu, and the great-souled sages, went to that place which brings delusion and bewilderment. ॥52॥
2.3.41.53: Placing you, O sage, and those mountains at the front, they, full of wonder, then went to the supremely marvellous mansion of Himādri. ॥53॥
2.3.41.54: Then Hara, joined by Viṣṇu and the others and accompanied by his own delighted hosts, came joyfully near the city of the Snowy Mountain. ॥54॥
2.3.41.iti: Thus ends the forty-first adhyāya, named The building of the pavilion, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥41॥
2.3.42.1: Brahmā said: Then Himālaya, lord of the mountains, hearing that the all-pervading Lord had arrived near his own city, rejoiced exceedingly. ॥1॥
2.3.42.2: Then, having gathered all the requisites, he sent out the mountains and also the brahmins, all of them, to greet and converse with the Lord. ॥2॥
2.3.42.3: The mountain himself went with true devotion to see the Lord, dear to him as life, his mind melting with devotion, joyfully praising his own good fortune. ॥3॥
2.3.42.4: Seeing then the army of the gods, Himavat was filled with wonder, and he went forward to meet it there, thinking, I am blessed. ॥4॥
2.3.42.5: The gods too, seeing his host, were struck with supreme wonder; and the gods as well as the mountains attained supreme joy. ॥5॥
2.3.42.6: O sage, the great host of the mountains and that of the gods, meeting together, shone like the eastern and western oceans joining. ॥6॥
2.3.42.7: Meeting one another, the gods and the mountains considered themselves fulfilled, with supreme joy. ॥7॥
2.3.42.8: Then, seeing the Lord before him, Himālaya bowed; all the mountains and the brahmins bowed to Sadāśiva — ॥8॥
2.3.42.9: — seated on the bull, with a gracious face, adorned with various ornaments, illuminating the regions of space with the loveliness of his divine limbs; ॥9॥
2.3.42.10: his body resplendent in very fine, new, excellent silk garments, his crown gleaming with fine jewels, smiling, of pure radiance; ॥10॥
2.3.42.11: his limbs bearing serpents that served as ornaments, with wondrous radiance of limbs, of divine lustre, attended by the lords of the gods with chowries in their hands; ॥11॥
2.3.42.12: the Lord with Acyuta standing on his left, Brahmā (Vidhi) on his right side, Hari behind him, and the gods and others behind and at his sides; ॥12॥
2.3.42.13: praised by gods and beings of many kinds, the benefactor of the worlds, who assumed a body by his own will, Brahman, lord of all, giver of boons; ॥13॥
2.3.42.14: with attributes and also without attributes, subject to his devotees, a mine of compassion, beyond both Prakṛti and Puruṣa, whose nature is being, consciousness and bliss. ॥14॥
2.3.42.15: On the Lord's right side he saw Hari Acyuta, mounted on the son of Vinatā (Garuḍa), adorned with various ornaments. ॥15॥
2.3.42.16: And on the Lord's left side, O sage, he saw me, the four-faced one, of great splendour, accompanied by my retinue. ॥16॥
2.3.42.17: Seeing these two lords of the gods, ever very dear to Śiva, the lord of mountains bowed with reverence along with his retinue. ॥17॥
2.3.42.18: Likewise, seeing the gods and others shining behind Śiva and at his two sides, that lord of the best of mountains bowed to them. ॥18॥
2.3.42.19: At Śiva's command the mountain went ahead to his own city; Śeṣa, Hari and the Self-born (Brahmā) followed quickly, with the sages, the gods and others. ॥19॥
2.3.42.20: O Nārada, all the sages, gods and others, going along with the Lord, delighted, praised the mountain's city greatly. ॥20॥
2.3.42.21: Having lodged the gods and others on a lovely, specially constructed peak, Himavat went to where the ritual altar stood. ॥21॥
2.3.42.22: Having had a square pavilion specially made, furnished with arches, and having performed bathing, gift-giving and the like, he then made an inspection of the preparations. ॥22॥
2.3.42.23: Likewise Hima, king of mountains, sent his own sons to the presence of Śiva, who was accompanied by the full company headed by Viṣṇu. ॥23॥
2.3.42.24: Full of great joy, the king of the snowy mountains, together with all his kinsmen, wished to perform the bridegroom's reception rite with a great festival. ॥24॥
2.3.42.25: Then those sons of the mountain went there, bowed to him together with his company, and conveyed the message of the lord of mountains, ending with his request. ॥25॥
2.3.42.26: Then, by his leave, the sons of the mountain returned to their home and joyfully told the king of mountains: They are coming. ॥26॥
2.3.42.27: Then, O sage, hearing the mountain's request, the gods, Viṣṇu and all the others, along with the Lord, were overjoyed and rejoiced exceedingly. ॥27॥
2.3.42.28: All the gods, sages, Gaṇas and others too, having dressed themselves finely, set out with the Lord for the house of the king of mountains. ॥28॥
2.3.42.29: At that moment Menā became eager to see Śiva, and, O sage, she summoned you, the best of sages, from the Lord's side. ॥29॥
2.3.42.30: You went there then, O sage, urged on by the Lord, who in his mind wished to fulfil that purpose dear to Śiva's heart. ॥30॥
2.3.42.31: Bowing to you, O sage, Menā, her mind full of wonder, spoke, wishing to see the form of Lord Śaṅkara, which dispels pride. ॥31॥
2.3.42.iti: Thus ends the forty-second adhyāya, named The meeting of the gods and the mountain, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥42॥
2.3.43.1: Menā said: O sage, I shall first look at that husband of Girijā. What kind of form does Śiva have, for whose sake she performed supreme penance? ॥1॥
2.3.43.2: Brahmā said: Thus, given over to ignorance, she came at once with you, O sage, to the upper terrace in order to see Śiva. ॥2॥
2.3.43.3: Then Śiva too, the Lord, knowing the pride in her, performed a wondrous sport and spoke to Viṣṇu and to me, dear son. ॥3॥
2.3.43.4: Śiva said: By my command, you two dear ones, together with the gods, go separately to the mountain's door; we shall come afterwards. ॥4॥
2.3.43.5: Brahmā said: Hearing this, Hari summoned everyone and told them; and all the gods, absorbed in him, eagerly set out quickly just as instructed. ॥5॥
2.3.43.6: O sage, the Lord of the universe, through you, showed Menā, who stood in the upper chamber, the procession in just such a way that her heart would be confounded. ॥6॥
2.3.43.7: At this time Menā, observing the supreme and auspicious army, O sage, was delighted on seeing it as a whole. ॥7॥
2.3.43.8: First of all the Gandharvas came then, handsome and charming, rich in fine garments and adorned with various ornaments, ॥8॥
2.3.43.9: furnished with various vehicles, intent on various musical instruments, with colourful banners, and accompanied by hosts of Apsarases. ॥9॥
2.3.43.10: Then, seeing Vasu there, their lord, of supreme majesty, Menā was overjoyed and said, this is Śiva. ॥10॥
2.3.43.11: These are Śiva's attendants; this is not Śiva, the husband of Śivā — thus you then told her, O best of sages. ॥11॥
2.3.43.12: Hearing this, Menā then became absorbed in thought: He who is even greater than this—what will he be like? ॥12॥
2.3.43.13: Meanwhile the Yakṣas, Maṇigrīva and the others—their army was seen by her, twice as splendid and so on. ॥13॥
2.3.43.14: And seeing their lord Maṇigrīva, full of splendour, Menā said in delight, this is Rudra, Śivā's lord. ॥14॥
2.3.43.15: This is not Rudra, Śivā's lord; he is a servant of Śiva—thus you told the mountain's wife. Meanwhile Agni arrived. ॥15॥
2.3.43.16: Seeing his splendour, twice even that, she said, this is Rudra, Girijā's lord; then you said, no. ॥16॥
2.3.43.17: Meanwhile Yama arrived, twice as radiant even as that; seeing him, Menā said in delight, this is Rudra. ॥17॥
2.3.43.18: You told her, no. Meanwhile Nirṛti arrived, the auspicious lord of the Puṇyajanas (Rākṣasas), bearing twice the splendour. ॥18॥
2.3.43.19: Seeing him, Menā said in delight, this is Rudra. You told her, no. Meanwhile Varuṇa arrived. ॥19॥
2.3.43.20: Seeing his splendour, twice even that, she said, this is Rudra, Girijā's lord; then you said, no. ॥20॥
2.3.43.21: Meanwhile Vāyu arrived, twice as radiant even as that; seeing him, Menā said in delight, this is Rudra. ॥21॥
2.3.43.22: You told her, no. Meanwhile Dhanada (Kubera), lord of the Guhyakas, arrived, bearing a splendour twice even that. ॥22॥
2.3.43.23: Seeing him, Menā said in delight, this is Rudra. You told her, no. Meanwhile Īśāna arrived. ॥23॥
2.3.43.24: Seeing his splendour, twice even that, she said, this is Rudra, Girijā's lord; then you said, no. ॥24॥
2.3.43.25: Meanwhile Indra arrived, twice as radiant even as that—the foremost of all immortals, shining with various divine lustres, lord of the threefold heaven. ॥25॥
2.3.43.26: Seeing him, Menakā said, this is that Śaṅkara. Then you said, this is Śakra, lord of the gods—not he. ॥26॥
2.3.43.27: Meanwhile the Moon arrived, bearing splendour twice that; seeing him she said, this is Rudra, but you told her, no. ॥27॥
2.3.43.28: Meanwhile the Sun arrived, bearing splendour twice that; seeing him she said, this is he, but you told her, no. ॥28॥
2.3.43.29: Meanwhile there arrived the lords of sages, Bhṛgu and the others, all masses of radiance, accompanied by their hosts of disciples. ॥29॥
2.3.43.30: Seeing Vāgīśa (Bṛhaspati) in their midst, Menakā said, this is Rudra, Girijā's lord; then you said, no. ॥30॥
2.3.43.31: Meanwhile Brahmā arrived, the supreme mass of radiance, together with his sons, the foremost sages, praised as if he were dharma itself embodied. ॥31॥
2.3.43.32: Seeing me then, O sage, Menā, full of great joy, said, this is he, the husband of Śivā, but you told her, no. ॥32॥
2.3.43.33: Meanwhile the god Viṣṇu arrived there, endowed with every splendour, glorious, dark as a rain-cloud, four-armed, ॥33॥
2.3.43.34: with the beauty of a crore of Kandarpas, wearing yellow garments, self-ruling, lotus-eyed, serene, whose excellent mount is the king of birds, ॥34॥
2.3.43.35: bearing the marks of the conch and the rest, adorned with a crown and other ornaments, with the Śrīvatsa on his chest, lord of Lakṣmī, endowed with immeasurable radiance. ॥35॥
2.3.43.36: Seeing him, her eyes grew wide with wonder, and in great joy she said, this is the husband of Śivā, Śiva himself—there is no doubt of it. ॥36॥
2.3.43.37: Then you, the helper, hearing Menakā's words, said, this is not the husband of Śivā; rather, this is Keśava, Hari. ॥37॥
2.3.43.38: He is in charge of all Śaṅkara's affairs and dear to him. The excellent one greater than him is to be known as Śiva, the lord of Pārvatī. ॥38॥
2.3.43.39: O Menā, his splendour cannot be described by me at all. He alone is the lord of the entire cosmos, lord of all, self-ruling. ॥39॥
2.3.43.40: Brahmā said: Hearing his words thus, Menā considered her daughter auspicious, greatly rich, fortunate, a bringer of happiness to three families. ॥40॥
2.3.43.41: And with a cheerful face and a heart full of affection she spoke, describing again and again her own great good fortune. ॥41॥
2.3.43.42: Menā said: Now I have become blessed in every way through the birth of Pārvatī. Blessed today is the lord of mountains too; everything of mine is most blessed. ॥42॥
2.3.43.43: Whichever gods I have seen, leaders endowed with great splendour—he who is the lord of all these will here be her husband. ॥43॥
2.3.43.44: What can be said of her fortune? Even in hundreds of years it could not be described, seeing that she has won that Lord. ॥44॥
2.3.43.45: Brahmā said: Thus spoke Menā, her mind overflowing with love. Meanwhile Rudra, the Lord, worker of wondrous deeds, arrived. ॥45॥
2.3.43.46: O dear one, he of wondrous nature came, and his gaṇas, removers of Menā's pride, displaying himself as untouched by māyā and free from change. ॥46॥
2.3.43.47: Then, O sage Nārada, perceiving that he had arrived, you spoke to Menā with great delight, pointing out to her that husband of Śivā. ॥47॥
2.3.43.48: Nārada said: This is Śaṅkara himself; behold him, O beautiful lady—he for whose sake Śivā performed exceedingly great austerity in the forest. ॥48॥
2.3.43.49: Brahmā said: When this was said, delighted Menā joyfully beheld that Lord, Īśāna, of wondrous form, with wondrous followers, himself wondrous. ॥49॥
2.3.43.50: Just then Rudra's most wondrous army arrived, joined by bhūtas, pretas and the like, accompanied by many kinds of gaṇas. ॥50॥
2.3.43.51: Some bore the form of whirlwinds, with sounds like the rustling of banners; some there had crooked snouts, and others likewise were misshapen. ॥51॥
2.3.43.52: Some were dreadful and bearded; some lame, and some eyeless; some carried staffs and nooses, some had clubs in their hands. ॥52॥
2.3.43.53: Some rode strange mounts, sounding with blasts of horns; some were playing ḍamarus, some were playing gomukha trumpets. ॥53॥
2.3.43.54: Some gaṇas were faceless, some had distorted faces, some had many faces; some were handless, some had deformed hands, some had many hands. ॥54॥
2.3.43.55: Eyeless and many-eyed, headless and ugly-headed, earless and many-eared—gaṇas wearing all kinds of guises. ॥55॥
2.3.43.56: Thus, O dear one, there were many mighty gaṇas of such deformed shapes, countless, great heroes and terrifying. ॥56॥
2.3.43.57: Then, O sage, pointing out Rudra's gaṇas to her with your finger, you said: Behold the servants of Hara, and Hara too, O fair-faced lady. ॥57॥
2.3.43.58: Seeing the countless gaṇas, bhūtas, pretas and the rest, O sage, Menakā was at that very moment overwhelmed with fear. ॥58॥
2.3.43.59: And in their midst she saw Śaṅkara—beyond attributes yet supremely endowed with qualities, seated on a bull, five-faced, three-eyed, adorned with ash, ॥59॥
2.3.43.60: with matted locks, the moon on his crest, ten-armed, bearing a skull, with a tiger-skin as upper garment, holding the excellent Pināka bow in his hand, ॥60॥
2.3.43.61: bearing a trident, odd-eyed, of deformed and wild appearance, clad in an elephant's hide—seeing him, Śivā's mother trembled with fear. ॥61॥
2.3.43.62: To her—startled, trembling, distraught, her mind reeling—you said, pointing with your finger: This is Śiva. ॥62॥
2.3.43.63: Hearing those words of yours, the virtuous Menā, laden with grief, quickly fell to the ground like a creeper struck by the wind. ॥63॥
2.3.43.64: What is this monstrosity? Seeing it, I have been deceived through this stubborn insistence. Having said this, Menakā fainted there in an instant. ॥64॥
2.3.43.65: Then, tended by her friends with various efforts, Menā, beloved of the mountain-lord, slowly regained consciousness. ॥65॥
