2.3.43.iti: Thus ends the forty-third adhyāya, named Śiva's wondrous sport, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥43॥
2.3.44.1: Brahmā said: Then Menā, the chaste beloved of the Mountain, regained consciousness. Greatly agitated, she lamented and then began to hurl reproaches. ॥1॥
2.3.44.2: There, faltering again and again, she first reviled her own sons; then she spoke harsh words to her daughter. ॥2॥
2.3.44.3: Menā said: O sage, earlier you declared, Śivā will choose Śiva. Afterwards you set Himavat to the task of arranging worship of him. ॥3॥
2.3.44.4: Then the fruit was truly seen—perverse and worthless. O evil-minded sage, wretched I have been utterly deceived by you. ॥4॥
2.3.44.5: Moreover, she performed austerities that are hard even for sages; and this is the fruit she obtained from them—a source of grief to those who see it. ॥5॥
2.3.44.6: What shall I do? Where shall I go? Who will dispel my grief? My family and all else are ruined, and so has my life been dealt with. ॥6॥
2.3.44.7: Where have those divine seers gone? I will pluck out their beards. And that ascetic wife of Vasiṣṭha who came of her own accord—she is a cheat. ॥7॥
2.3.44.8: Through whose offence has everything of mine now been ruined? Having said this and looking at her daughter, she spoke bitter words. ॥8॥
2.3.44.9: O wicked daughter, what grievous deed have you done to me? Giving away gold, you, wicked one, have yourself brought home glass. ॥9॥
2.3.44.10: Abandoning sandal paste, you have instead smeared yourself with mud; letting the swan fly away, you have caught a crow in the cage of your hand. ॥10॥
2.3.44.11: Casting holy water far away, you have drunk well water; abandoning the sun, you have painstakingly grasped a firefly. ॥11॥
2.3.44.12: Likewise, abandoning rice grains, you have eaten husks; throwing away ghee, you have eagerly consumed kāraṇḍa oil. ॥12॥
2.3.44.13: Likewise, giving up service to a lion, you have served a jackal; giving up knowledge of Brahman, you have listened to a vile tale. ॥13॥
2.3.44.14: Casting far away the most auspicious sacrificial ash of the household, you, O daughter, have taken up the inauspicious ash of the funeral pyre. ॥14॥
2.3.44.15: Forsaking all the foremost gods, Viṣṇu and the other supreme lords, you, with your perverse mind, performed such austerity for Śiva's sake. ॥15॥
2.3.44.16: Fie on you and on your intellect! Fie on your beauty and your conduct! Fie on the one who instructed you, and fie likewise on your two friends! ॥16॥
2.3.44.17: Fie also on us two, O daughter, who brought about your birth! Fie on your intellect, O Nārada, and on the seven seers, givers of evil counsel! ॥17॥
2.3.44.18: Fie on the family! Fie on skill in rites! Fie on everything you have done! This house has been set on fire—this is nothing but my death. ॥18॥
2.3.44.19: Let this king of mountains not come near me; let the seven seers themselves never show me their faces. ॥19॥
2.3.44.20: What has been achieved? All of them together have destroyed the family. Why did I not become barren? Why was the embryo not miscarried? ॥20॥
2.3.44.21: Or why did I not die? Why did my daughter not die? Or why was she not devoured in the sky by rākṣasas and the like? ॥21॥
2.3.44.22: I will cut off your head today. What shall I do with these bodies? Abandoning you, where could I go? Alas, alas, my life is ruined! ॥22॥
2.3.44.23: Brahmā said: Having said this, Menā fell to the ground unconscious. Distraught with grief, anger and the like, she did not go into her husband's presence. ॥23॥
2.3.44.24: At that time, O lord of sages, there arose a great cry of lament. All the gods came there one after another into her presence. ॥24॥
2.3.44.25: Earlier, O divine sage, I myself had come there then; and seeing me, you, O best of seers, spoke these words to her: ॥25॥
2.3.44.26: Nārada said: You have not known Śiva's true, beautiful form. This form has been assumed by Śiva in play; it is not his true one. ॥26॥
2.3.44.27: Therefore, giving up anger, be composed, O faithful wife. Abandon obstinacy, do what must be done, and give Śivā to Śiva. ॥27॥
2.3.44.28: Brahmā said: Hearing your words, Menā said to you: Get up and go far from here. You are the foremost of the wicked and vile. ॥28॥
2.3.44.29: When she had said this, all the gods led by Indra, and the guardians of the quarters, came one after another and spoke these words. ॥29॥
2.3.44.30: The gods said: O Menā, daughter of the Pitṛs, listen gladly to our words. This is indeed the supreme Śiva himself, the bringer of highest bliss. ॥30॥
2.3.44.31: Seeing your daughter's most unbearable austerity, Śambhu, who is loving to his true devotees, out of compassion granted her his vision and a boon. ॥31॥
2.3.44.32: Brahmā said: Then Menā, lamenting bitterly again and again, said to the gods: My daughter shall not be given by me to Giriśa of fearsome form. ॥32॥
2.3.44.33: Why have all of you gods been led astray, and set yourselves to render her supreme beauty futile? ॥33॥
2.3.44.34: When she had said this, the seven seers, Vasiṣṭha and the others, came there and spoke, O lord of sages. ॥34॥
2.3.44.35: The seven sages said: We have come to accomplish this task, O daughter of the Pitṛs, beloved of the Mountain. How could we consider anything contrary in this fitting matter? ॥35॥
2.3.44.36: This indeed is the supreme gain—the sight of Śaṅkara. Becoming the recipient of your gift, he has come to your house. ॥36॥
2.3.44.37: Brahmā said: Addressed thus by them, Menā set the sages' words at naught; angry and weak in understanding, she replied to those seers. ॥37॥
2.3.44.38: Menā said: I will have her killed with weapons or the like, but I will not give her to Śaṅkara. Go far away, all of you; do not come near me. ॥38॥
2.3.44.39: Brahmā said: Having said this, she quickly fell silent, lamenting and utterly distraught. Because of that event, O sage, a great cry of lament arose there. ॥39॥
2.3.44.40: Then Himālaya came there, greatly perturbed, and, to bring her to understanding, spoke to her affectionately, revealing the truth. ॥40॥
2.3.44.41: Himavān said: Listen to my words today, Menā. Why are you so distressed, my dear? Who are these who have come to our house, and why do you revile them? ॥41॥
2.3.44.42: You know Śaṅkara, yet you are agitated on seeing his form — the fierce form of that Śambhu, who indeed has many forms and names. ॥42॥
2.3.44.43: That Śaṅkara is known to me as the protector of all. He is indeed the most worshipful among the worshipful, the one who bestows grace and punishment. ॥43॥
2.3.44.44: Do not be obstinate; give up your grief, O you dear as life, O sinless one. Get up quickly; you should do what has to be done, O lady of good vows. ॥44॥
2.3.44.45: Formerly Śambhu came to our door bearing a fierce form and performed various sports; I remind you of that very episode. ॥45॥
2.3.44.46: Having seen his supreme greatness, you and I then agreed to give him the girl, O goddess; make that agreement good, my dear. ॥46॥
2.3.44.47: Brahmā said: Having said this, the lord of mountains then fell silent, O sage. Hearing that, Menā, the mother of Śivā, spoke to Himālaya. ॥47॥
2.3.44.48: Menā said: Let my words be heard, lord; you should act thus: take this daughter Pārvatī and, tying a stone to her neck, ॥48॥
2.3.44.49: throw her down without hesitation; I will not give her to Hara. Or else, lord, go and throw this daughter into the ocean — ॥49॥
2.3.44.50: drown her, casting off pity, and then, lord of mountains, be happy; if you give the daughter to Rudra of hideous form, then, my lord, I will certainly give up my body. ॥50॥
2.3.44.51: Brahmā said: When these words had been spoken there by Menā out of obstinacy, Pārvatī came of her own accord and spoke charming words. ॥51॥
2.3.44.52: Pārvatī said: Mother, your mind has become perverse, bringing misfortune. Though you stand on dharma, how can you abandon dharma? ॥52॥
2.3.44.53: This Rudra is the unsurpassed Lord in person, the source of all, Śambhu, beautiful, giver of happiness, described in all the Vedas. ॥53॥
2.3.44.54: He is Maheśa and Śaṅkara, lord of all the gods, self-ruling, of many forms and names, O mother; he is Hari the remover, served by Brahmā and the others. ॥54॥
2.3.44.55: That Lord is the foundation of all, the creator and the destroyer, changeless, lord of the three gods, imperishable and eternal. ॥55॥
2.3.44.56: For his sake all the gods have come, made into servants, and are at your door today in festive mood — what greater happiness is there than this? ॥56॥
2.3.44.57: So rise with effort and make your life fruitful. Give me to this Śiva and make your household meaningful. ॥57॥
2.3.44.58: Give me to the supreme Lord Śaṅkara, O mother! Accept this humble plea of mine, mother; I am telling you. ॥58॥
2.3.44.59: If you do not give me to him, I will not choose any other groom. How could a deceitful jackal obtain the lion's share? ॥59॥
2.3.44.60: In mind, speech and deed, mother, Hara himself has been chosen by me — truly chosen. Do as you wish. ॥60॥
2.3.44.61: Brahmā said: Hearing Śivā's words, Menā, beloved of the lord of mountains, lamenting bitterly and greatly enraged, seized her body, ॥61॥
2.3.44.62: and, grinding her teeth, distraught and filled with extreme fury, she beat that daughter with fists and elbows. ॥62॥
2.3.44.63: The sages who were there, dear one — you and others, O sage — wrested her from Menā's hands and then took her far away. ॥63॥
2.3.44.64: Seeing them act thus, she scolded them again and again, and once more spoke harsh words, making them all hear. ॥64॥
2.3.44.65: Menā said: What shall I do with this wickedly obstinate Śivā? I will give her strong poison, or surely throw her into a well. ॥65॥
2.3.44.66: Or I will hack Kālī into many pieces with weapons and missiles, or indeed drown my own daughter Pārvatī in the sea. ॥66॥
2.3.44.67: Or else I will surely give up my own body at once. I will not give the girl Durgā to Śambhu of hideous form. ॥67॥
2.3.44.68: What kind of dreadful groom is this that this wicked girl has won? She has made me a laughing-stock, and the mountain and our family too. ॥68॥
2.3.44.69: He has no mother, no father, no brother, no kinsman, not even anyone of his lineage; no beauty, no skill, nor any house whatsoever. ॥69॥
2.3.44.70: No clothes, no ornaments, no companions at all has he; no fine vehicle, no youth, and no wealth either. ॥70॥
2.3.44.71: No purity, no learning — and what a body, causing distress. Seeing what in him should I give my daughter to him, that she may be truly blessed? ॥71॥
2.3.44.72: Brahmā said: Having lamented much in this and similar ways, Menakā then wept loudly, O sage, overwhelmed with grief and sorrow. ॥72॥
2.3.44.73: Then I came quickly and explained to that Menakā the supreme truth of Śiva, excellent and dispelling wrong understanding. ॥73॥
2.3.44.74: Brahmā said: O Menā, listen gladly to my auspicious words; by hearing them with love, your wrong thinking will be destroyed. ॥74॥
2.3.44.75: Śaṅkara is the creator, sustainer and destroyer of the world. You do not know his true form; why do you court grief? ॥75॥
2.3.44.76: The Lord has many forms and names and performs various sports; he is master of all, independent, ruler of Māyā, free of all dualistic notions. ॥76॥
2.3.44.77: Knowing this, Menā, give Śivā to Śiva. Give up this wrong obstinacy and wrong understanding, which ruins every undertaking. ॥77॥
2.3.44.78: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by me, Menā, lamenting again and again, slowly cast off a little of her shame, O sage, and spoke to me. ॥78॥
2.3.44.79: Menā said: Why, O Brahmā, do you make her surpassing beauty go to waste? Why should this Śivā not rather be killed outright? ॥79॥
2.3.44.80: And you should not say, let her be given to Śiva. I will not give this daughter of mine, dear to me as my life, to Śiva. ॥80॥
2.3.44.81: Brahmā said: When she had spoken thus, O great sage, the Siddhas, Sanaka and the others, came together and with great affection spoke these words. ॥81॥
2.3.44.82: The siddhas said: This is indeed the supreme Śiva himself, the bringer of highest bliss. Out of compassion the Lord has granted his sight to your daughter. ॥82॥
2.3.44.83: Brahmā said: Then Menā, lamenting again and again, said to them: She certainly shall not be given by me to Giriśa of terrible form. ॥83॥
2.3.44.84: Why are all of you Siddhas, crafty as you are, bent on rendering her supreme beauty futile? ॥84॥
2.3.44.85: When she had said this there, O sage, I was astonished; all — gods, Siddhas, seers and men — were filled with wonder. ॥85॥
2.3.44.86: At this time, hearing of her firm and great obstinacy, Viṣṇu, beloved of Śiva, quickly came and said this. ॥86॥
2.3.44.87: Viṣṇu said: You are the beloved mind-born daughter of the Pitṛs, endowed with virtues, the wife of Himavat himself; yours is the excellent lineage of Brahmā. ॥87॥
2.3.44.88: Such are your supporters in the world; you are blessed indeed — what more shall I say? You are the very foundation of dharma; how then can you abandon dharma? ॥88॥
2.3.44.89: Is anything contrary to the truth being spoken by the gods and the seers, by Brahmā or likewise by me? Let it be carefully considered by you yourself. ॥89॥
2.3.44.90: You do not know Śiva: he is both without attributes and with attributes; he is of misshapen form and also of beautiful form; he is to be served by all, the refuge of the good. ॥90॥
2.3.44.91: By him alone was created the goddess, the sovereign primordial Prakṛti; and then beside her he created the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama). ॥91॥
2.3.44.92: From those two came I and likewise Brahmā; and then Rudra himself, the benefactor of the worlds, descended in the form of a guṇa. ॥92॥
2.3.44.93: Then the Vedas and the gods, and whatever world is seen, moving and unmoving — all of that came forth from Śaṅkara. ॥93॥
2.3.44.94: By whom has his form been described, or by whom can it be known? Even by me and by Brahmā his end has never been found. ॥94॥
2.3.44.95: Whatever world is seen, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass, know all that to be Śiva; there should be no doubt about this. ॥95॥
2.3.44.96: He himself, having descended in such a form through his own sport, has come to your door by the power of Śivā's penance. ॥96॥
2.3.44.97: Therefore, O wife of Himavat, give up your grief and worship Śiva. There will be great joy, and your distress will come to an end. ॥97॥
2.3.44.98: Brahmā said: O sage, when Menakā had been thus admonished, her mind, awakened by Viṣṇu, became somewhat softened. ॥98॥
2.3.44.99: But she did not give up her great obstinacy; Menā, deluded by Śiva's māyā, did not then consent to give the maiden to Hara. ॥99॥
2.3.44.100: Having heard Viṣṇu's pleasing words, Menā, the beloved of the Mountain and mother of Girijā, somewhat awakened, spoke to Hari. ॥100॥
2.3.44.101: If he takes on a handsome body, then my daughter may be given by me — not otherwise, even with millions of efforts. I speak a true and firm word. ॥101॥
2.3.44.102: Brahmā said: Having spoken these words, Menā, firm in her resolve, fell silent — the blessed one, impelled by Śiva's will, which thus deludes all. ॥102॥
2.3.44.iti: Thus ends the forty-fourth adhyāya, named The enlightening of Menā, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥44॥
2.3.45.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, O sage, urged by Viṣṇu, you quickly went near Śambhu to make him favourable. ॥1॥
2.3.45.2: Having gone there, you praised that Rudra with hymns of many kinds and duly prompted him, wishing to accomplish the gods' task. ॥2॥
2.3.45.3: Hearing your words, Śambhu gladly assumed a wondrous, supreme, divine form, and displayed his compassion. ॥3॥
2.3.45.4: Seeing that beautiful Śambhu, whose form surpassed Manmatha's, the supreme abode of loveliness, you, O sage, were overjoyed. ॥4॥
2.3.45.5: Having praised him with hymns of many kinds, filled with supreme bliss, you came, O sage, to where Menā stood with everyone. ॥5॥
2.3.45.6: Arriving there, very pleased and overflowing with love, O sage, you spoke these words, delighting Menā, the mountain's wife. ॥6॥
2.3.45.7: Nārada said: O Menā, O wide-eyed one, behold Śiva's unsurpassed form. Śiva himself, compassionate by nature, has shown great grace. ॥7॥
2.3.45.8: Brahmā said: Hearing those words, Menā, the mountain's beloved, was astonished and beheld that form of Śiva which bestows supreme bliss. ॥8॥
2.3.45.9: It was radiant like ten million suns, beautiful in every limb, in wonderful garments, adorned with many ornaments, ॥9॥
2.3.45.10: very gracious, sweetly smiling, exceedingly lovely, captivating, fair-hued, shining, adorned with the crescent moon, ॥10॥
2.3.45.11: lovingly attended by all the hosts of gods headed by Viṣṇu, shaded on the head by the Sun as an umbrella, and made splendid by the Moon. ॥11॥
2.3.45.12: He was charming in every way; the great splendour of the vehicle of him, adorned with ornaments, simply cannot be described. ॥12॥
2.3.45.13: Gaṅgā and Yamunā held fine chowries, and the eight Siddhis danced beautifully before him. ॥13॥
2.3.45.14: Then I, Viṣṇu, and the immortals headed by Indra, each well adorned in his own attire, moved along together with Giriśa. ॥14॥
2.3.45.15: Likewise the Gaṇas of many forms, crying victory, well adorned and in great joy, moved ahead of Girīśa. ॥15॥
2.3.45.16: The Siddhas, all the demigods, and the sages in great happiness went along with Śiva, much delighted, and likewise all the others. ॥16॥
2.3.45.17: Thus all the gods and others, full of eager curiosity, adorned and accompanied by their wives, went extolling the supreme Brahman. ॥17॥
2.3.45.18: There the Gandharvas led by Viśvāvasu, together with the troupes of Apsarases, sang before him the supreme glory of Śaṅkara. ॥18॥
2.3.45.19: Thus, O best of sages, a great festival of many kinds took place there as Maheśa proceeded to the mountain's door. ॥19॥
2.3.45.20: Who, O lord of sages, can describe in detail the splendour of the Supreme Self there at that time? ॥20॥
2.3.45.21: Seeing him in such a form, Menā stood for a moment as if painted in a picture; then, O sage, she lovingly spoke these words. ॥21॥
2.3.45.22: Menā said: Blessed is my daughter, who performed great austerity, by whose power you, O great lord, have come here to my house. ॥22॥
2.3.45.23: The grievous censure of Śiva which I committed earlier, forgive it, O lord of Śivā; be well pleased now. ॥23॥
2.3.45.24: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus and praised the moon-browed one, Menā, the mountain's beloved, bowed with joined palms and became overcome with bashfulness. ॥24॥
2.3.45.25: Meanwhile the women of the city came in great numbers, abandoning their many pursuits, eager to see Śiva. ॥25॥
2.3.45.26: One who was bathing went off with the bath-powder still on her, full of curiosity to see Śaṅkara, Girijā's bridegroom. ॥26॥
2.3.45.27: Another, with her friend, left off serving her husband and gladly went, chowry in hand, to see Śambhu. ॥27॥
2.3.45.28: Another, leaving her child who was eagerly drinking at her breast and not yet satisfied, went, longing for the sight, to see Śaṅkara. ॥28॥
2.3.45.29: One who was tying her girdle went with it in her hand; another went off wearing her garment inside out. ॥29॥
2.3.45.30: A loving wife, leaving her husband seated for his meal, went gladly, thirsting and curious, to see Śivā's bridegroom. ॥30॥
2.3.45.31: Another lady, holding the collyrium stick in her hand, having applied collyrium to only one eye, went to see the mountain-daughter's bridegroom. ॥31॥
2.3.45.32: Another lovely woman, dyeing her feet with lac, heard the uproar, left that, and came to see. ॥32॥
2.3.45.33: Thus, abandoning various tasks and their homes, the women went; and seeing Śaṅkara's form, they were then overcome with infatuation. ॥33॥
2.3.45.34: Then, stirred with love and thrilled at seeing Śiva, they placed his image in their hearts and spoke these words. ॥34॥
2.3.45.35: The women of the city said: The eyes of the dwellers of Himavat's city have borne fruit; whoever saw this form, his birth is truly meaningful. ॥35॥
2.3.45.36: His alone is a fruitful birth, his alone are fruitful deeds, by whom Śiva, destroyer of all sins, has been seen face to face. ॥36॥
2.3.45.37: Pārvatī has accomplished everything through the austerity she performed for Śiva's sake; blessed is she, fulfilled is she, Śivā, having won Śiva as her husband. ॥37॥
2.3.45.38: If Brahmā had not joyfully united this pair, Śiva and Śivā, then all his labour would have been fruitless. ॥38॥
2.3.45.39: It has been done well, and this excellent pair has been united here; everyone's life has become meaningful, the source of all accomplishments. ॥39॥
2.3.45.40: Without austerity, the sight of Śambhu is hard for men to obtain; through the very sight of Śaṅkara all have attained fulfilment. ॥40॥
2.3.45.41: Just as Lakṣmī long ago obtained Nārāyaṇa as her lord, so this goddess Pārvatī, well adorned, shines having obtained Hara. ॥41॥
2.3.45.42: And just as Sarasvatī obtained Brahmā as her lord, so this goddess Pārvatī, well adorned, shines having obtained Hara. ॥42॥
2.3.45.43: Blessed are we all, the women, and all the excellent men — whoever behold Śaṅkara, the Lord of all, the husband of Girijā. ॥43॥
2.3.45.44: Brahmā said: Having spoken these words, they worshipped Śiva with sandal paste and unbroken rice grains, and showered parched grain on him with reverence. ॥44॥
2.3.45.45: All the women stood there eagerly with Menā, extolling the great good fortune of Menā and of the mountain Himavat too. ॥45॥
2.3.45.46: Hearing such auspicious words spoken by those women, the Lord, O sage, became delighted then, together with all, Viṣṇu and the others. ॥46॥
2.3.45.iti: Thus ends the forty-fifth adhyāya, named Śiva's beautiful form and the festivity of the townspeople, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥45॥
2.3.46.1: Brahmā said: Then Śambhu, delighted at heart, went eagerly to the mountain's abode together with the messenger, with his own gaṇas, the gods, and all the others. ॥1॥
2.3.46.2: Menā too, the beloved wife of the excellent Himācala, rising from there with those groups of women, went into the interior of her own house. ॥2॥
2.3.46.3: Holding a lamp-vessel in her hand for the waving of lights (nīrājana) before Śambhu, the virtuous lady went respectfully to the door together with the hosts of the wives of all the sages. ॥3॥
2.3.46.4: There Menā lovingly beheld the arrived Maheśāna, Śaṅkara, the bridegroom of Girijā, attended by all the gods. ॥4॥
2.3.46.5: He was radiant with the hue of a lovely campaka flower, five-faced, three-eyed, his face bright with a gentle smile, adorned with jewels, gold and the like; ॥5॥
2.3.46.6: wearing a garland of mālatī flowers, resplendent with a crown of fine gems, with a fine necklace, adorned with lovely bracelets and armlets; ॥6॥
2.3.46.7: greatly splendid in a pair of priceless, wondrous garments, fire-purified, matchless, extremely fine and beautiful; ॥7॥
2.3.46.8: adorned with sandal, aguru, musk and lovely saffron, holding a jewelled mirror in his hand, his eyes bright with collyrium; ॥8॥
2.3.46.9: enveloped in the radiance of his whole being, exceedingly charming, exceedingly youthful and delightful, and adorned with ornamented limbs; ॥9॥
2.3.46.10: beloved of women, composed, his lotus-face bright as a crore of moons, the lustre of his body surpassing a crore of Kāmas, beautiful in every limb. ॥10॥
2.3.46.11: Seeing that lord, the excellent god of such a kind, her son-in-law, standing before her, Menā, filled with joy, cast off her grief. ॥11॥
2.3.46.12: She praised her own good fortune, Girijā, the mountain her husband and the family; she considered herself fulfilled and rejoiced again and again. ॥12॥
2.3.46.13: With beaming face the virtuous Menā performed the nīrājana there, joyfully intent on gazing at her son-in-law. ॥13॥
2.3.46.14: Recalling what Girijā had said, Menā was struck with wonder, and, her lotus-face blooming with delight, said this within her mind: ॥14॥
2.3.46.15: Whatever Pārvatī told me earlier on that occasion, I now see the beauty of the Supreme Lord to be greater than that. ॥15॥
2.3.46.16: The exquisite loveliness of Maheśa is now beyond words. Thus overcome with wonder, Menā returned to her house. ॥16॥
2.3.46.17: The young women praised her: Blessed, blessed is the mountain's daughter! Some maidens said, she is Durgā, the Bhagavatī. ॥17॥
2.3.46.18: Such a bridegroom, worthy of the gift of a bride, has never been seen by us; truly blessed is Goddess Girijā, said some maidens. ॥18॥
2.3.46.19: The foremost Gandharvas sang and the hosts of Apsarases danced; and all the deities, seeing Śaṅkara's form, were delighted. ॥19॥
2.3.46.20: The musicians, with devotion, played various kinds of instruments sweetly, with manifold skill. ॥20॥
2.3.46.21: Himācala too, delighted, then performed the door-rite (dvārācāra); and Menā too, with all the women, amid great festivity, ॥21॥
2.3.46.22: performed the parapṛcchā (welcoming inquiry) rite and, joyful, went to her house. Śiva, with the gaṇas and gods, went to the place assigned to him. ॥22॥
2.3.46.23: Meanwhile the attendants of the mountain's inner apartments went outside, taking Durgā with them to worship the family deity. ॥23॥
2.3.46.24: There the gods, unblinking, joyfully beheld her, shining with the hue of deep-blue collyrium, adorned by her own limbs, ॥24॥
2.3.46.25: her eyes honoured fixed by the Three-eyed One, her gaze turned away from others, her face bright with a gentle smile, with side-long glances, enchanting; ॥25॥
2.3.46.26: with a very lovely mass of braided hair, beautified with charming leaf-designs on her face, adorned with a dot of vermilion along with dots of musk; ॥26॥
2.3.46.27: her bosom shining with a necklace of the finest jewels, wearing jewelled armlets and bracelets, decked with jewelled wristlets; ॥27॥
2.3.46.28: her lovely cheeks glowing with ear-rings of fine gems, resplendent with rows of teeth that rob the lustre of gems and jewels; ॥28॥
2.3.46.29: her lips sweet and red like bimba fruit, tinged with jewel-like lac, holding a jewelled mirror in her hand, adorned with a play-lotus; ॥29॥
2.3.46.30: richly anointed with sandal, aguru, musk and saffron, with tinkling anklets on her feet, and shining with reddened soles. ॥30॥
2.3.46.31: Seeing the Goddess, the primal one of the world and mother of the world, all the gods and others, full of devotion, bowed their heads to her along with Menakā. ॥31॥
2.3.46.32: The Three-eyed One, filled with joy, looked at her from the corner of his eye; seeing in her the form of Satī, Śiva cast off the fever of separation. ॥32॥
2.3.46.33: Śiva, his eyes fixed on Śivā, forgot everything; with all his limbs thrilling with horripilation, he gazed at Gaurī in delight. ॥33॥
2.3.46.34: Then Kālī, having gone outside the city and worshipped the family mother-goddess, entered the lovely mansion of her father along with the wives of the brāhmaṇas. ॥34॥
2.3.46.35: Śaṅkara too, with the gods, with Hari and likewise Brahmā, joyfully went to his own lodging assigned by Himācala. ॥35॥
2.3.46.36: There all stayed happily, serving Śaṅkara as befitting, honoured by the Lord of the Mountains with riches of many kinds. ॥36॥
2.3.46.iti: Thus ends the forty-sixth adhyāya, named The arrival of the bridegroom and the rest, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥46॥
2.3.47.1: Brahmā said: Then that best of mountains, with affection and enthusiasm, had the sacred-thread ceremony of Durgā performed with Vedic mantras, and that of Śiva as well. ॥1॥
2.3.47.2: Then the gods headed by Viṣṇu and the sages, full of eagerness, entered the inner apartments of the mountain at Himācala's request. ॥2॥
2.3.47.3: Having duly carried out the Vedic custom and the worldly custom, they adorned Śivā with the ornaments given by Śiva. ॥3॥
2.3.47.4: First they bathed her, then adorned her in every way; and she was waved with lights (nīrājana) by her friends and by the wives of the brahmins. ॥4॥
2.3.47.5: Adorned with a pair of new, unworn garments, the fair-complexioned daughter of the great mountain, beloved of Śaṅkara, shone forth. ॥5॥
2.3.47.6: O sage, a supreme, divine, wondrous bodice set with many jewels was worn by that goddess, and it gleamed exceedingly. ॥6॥
2.3.47.7: She likewise wore a necklace set with divine gems, and very precious bracelets of pure gold. ॥7॥
2.3.47.8: Staying right there, meditating on Śiva in her mind, the auspicious daughter of the great mountain, mother of the three worlds, shone exceedingly. ॥8॥
2.3.47.9: Then there was a great festival on both sides, bringing joy; various gifts were given to the brahmins. ॥9॥
2.3.47.10: And to others too there was a great and varied gift of wealth; and there was entertainment with song and instrumental music as part of the festival. ॥10॥
2.3.47.11: Then Viṣṇu, I the Creator, the immortals headed by Śakra, and all the sages, festive and joyful with great delight, ॥11॥
2.3.47.12: having bowed deeply to Śivā with devotion and remembering Śiva's lotus feet, obtained the permission of Himagiri and returned each to his own place. ॥12॥
2.3.47.13: Meanwhile Garga, expert in the science of astrology, spoke these words there to Himavat, that lord of mountains. ॥13॥
2.3.47.14: Garga said: O Himācala, lord of the earth, master, O lord, bring Śambhu, the husband of Kālī, to your own mansion for the taking of the hand. ॥14॥
2.3.47.15: Brahmā said: Then the mountain, knowing the time suitable for giving away the bride, as announced by Garga, rejoiced greatly in his heart. ॥15॥
2.3.47.16: Joyfully and with great affection, the mountain sent mountains, brahmins and others too, desiring to bring Śiva. ॥16॥
2.3.47.17: Those mountains and brahmins, holding all auspicious articles in their hands, went festively and gladly to where the god Maheśvara was. ॥17॥
2.3.47.18: Then, with the sound of instruments and abundant Vedic chanting, accompanied by song and dance, there was great jubilation there. ॥18॥
2.3.47.19: Hearing the resounding of the instruments, all the attendants of Śaṅkara, together with the hosts of gods and sages, rose up joyfully all at once. ॥19॥
2.3.47.20: With minds brimming with delight they said to one another: The mountains are coming here, wishing to take Śiva along. ॥20॥
2.3.47.21: Surely the time for the taking of the hand has now arrived. We think great good fortune has come to all here. ॥21॥
2.3.47.22: We are especially blessed: we shall certainly behold with supreme joy the wedding of Śiva and Śivā, the abode of auspiciousness for the worlds. ॥22॥
2.3.47.23: Brahmā said: While this conversation was taking place among them there with respect, all the ministers of the lord of mountains arrived. ॥23॥
2.3.47.24: Having come, they requested Śiva and also Viṣṇu and the others: The time suitable for giving away the bride is at hand; please come. ॥24॥
2.3.47.25: O sage, hearing that, all those gods, Viṣṇu and the rest, rejoiced exceedingly in their hearts and quickly said to the mountain: Victory! ॥25॥
2.3.47.26: Śiva too, longing to obtain Kālī, rejoiced greatly; he of wondrous form kept that sign of joy hidden within his mind. ॥26॥
2.3.47.27: Then a bath with auspicious substances was taken by the trident-bearer, highly pleased, who bestows grace upon the worlds. ॥27॥
2.3.47.28: Bathed and clad in fine garments, surrounded by all of them, he was placed on the bull's back and well attended by the guardians of the worlds. ॥28॥
2.3.47.29: Placing the Lord in front, all went to Himagiri's house, playing instruments and making merry. ॥29॥
2.3.47.30: The brahmins sent by Himavat and those best of mountains went ahead of Śambhu, full of eagerness. ॥30॥
2.3.47.31: Maheśvara shone with a great parasol held over his head, fanned with chowries, and with a canopy above. ॥31॥
2.3.47.32: I, Viṣṇu, Indra and likewise the guardians of the worlds, going in front, shone exceedingly, endowed with supreme splendour. ॥32॥
2.3.47.33: Then conches, kettledrums, paṭahas, ānakas, gomukhas and other instruments were sounded again and again at the great festival. ॥33॥
2.3.47.34: Likewise all the singers sang most auspicious songs, and all the dancing girls danced to various rhythms. ॥34॥
2.3.47.35: Accompanied by these, the sole kinsman of the world then proceeded with the radiance of the Supreme Lord, well served by all the lords of the gods and showered with flowers by the delighted beings. ॥35॥
2.3.47.36: Then Śambhu, the Supreme Lord, duly worshipped and praised with many hymns, entered the sacrificial pavilion. ॥36॥
2.3.47.37: The best of mountains helped Maheśa down from the bull and joyfully led him into the house amid great festivity. ॥37॥
2.3.47.38: Himālaya too, having bowed with devotion according to rule to the Lord who had arrived with the hosts of gods, then performed the waving of lights (nīrājana). ॥38॥
2.3.47.39: Having bowed to all the gods, the sages and the others amid great festivity, he honoured them, joyfully praising his own good fortune. ॥39॥
2.3.47.40: That mountain led Īśāna together with Acyuta and the group of chief gods into his own abode, preceded by fine water for the feet and arghya offerings. ॥40॥
2.3.47.41: He seated them all in the courtyard on jewelled thrones: Viṣṇu, me, the Lord Śiva, and the distinguished ones with special honour. ॥41॥
2.3.47.42: Menā, together with her friends, the brahmin women and other matrons, joyfully and lovingly performed the waving of lights (nīrājana). ॥42॥
2.3.47.43: By the priest, knower of rites, every rite such as the madhuparka that was to be done for the great-souled Śaṅkara was joyfully performed. ॥43॥
2.3.47.44: Urged by me there, the priest then performed the auspicious rite befitting the occasion, O sage. ॥44॥
2.3.47.45: Having entered with great joy, along with Himādri, into the inner altar area, where the maiden Pārvatī, adorned with all ornaments, ॥45॥
2.3.47.46: the slender-limbed one, was seated on the altar, shining splendidly—there Mahādeva was led by Viṣṇu and by me. ॥46॥
2.3.47.47: Those led by Vācaspati watched for the auspicious moment suitable for the giving of the bride; there great festivities took place. ॥47॥
2.3.47.48: Garga sat where the water-clock was; as long as a ghaṭī remained, the praṇava (Om) was recited. ॥48॥
2.3.47.49: Proclaiming puṇyāham (auspicious day), Garga joyfully joined Pārvatī's palms; and Pārvatī, her palms full of unbroken rice, showered it upon Śiva. ॥49॥
2.3.47.50: Rudra was worshipped there by her, the most noble Pārvatī of lovely face, with curd, unbroken rice, kuśa grass and water. ॥50॥
2.3.47.51: Gazing at that Śambhu for whose sake she had earlier performed supreme austerity with great love, Śivā shone exceedingly. ॥51॥
2.3.47.52: Then, O sage, told by me and by the sages beginning with Garga, Śambhu, devoted to worldly custom, worshipped Śivā in return. ॥52॥
2.3.47.53: Thus Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord, who pervade the world, worshipping each other at that time, shone forth. ॥53॥
2.3.47.54: Enveloped by the splendour of the three worlds and gazing at each other, they were then specially honoured with the waving of lights by Lakṣmī and other women. ॥54॥
2.3.47.55: Likewise other brahmin wives and the women of the city performed the waving of lights; and gazing at Śivā and Śambhu, all of them attained joy—a great festival. ॥55॥
2.3.47.iti: Thus ends the forty-seventh adhyāya, named The festivity of Śiva's going into the house of the Himālaya mountain, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥47॥
2.3.48.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, there, urged on by the preceptor Garga, Himavān, together with Menā, began to give away their daughter. ॥1॥
2.3.48.2: Taking a golden pitcher, the most fortunate Menā, adorned with garments and ornaments, took her place at Himādri's side. ॥2॥
2.3.48.3: Then the mountain, delighted, together with his family priest, honoured that bridegroom with water for the feet and the other offerings, and with garments, sandal paste and ornaments. ॥3॥
2.3.48.4: Then the brāhmaṇas were told by Himādri: Now that this moment has come, let the formula for proclaiming the lunar day and the rest be pronounced. ॥4॥
2.3.48.5: Being so addressed, all those excellent brāhmaṇas, knowers of auspicious time, said, so be it, and, supremely content, gladly performed the proclamation of the lunar day and the rest. ॥5॥
2.3.48.6: Then Himācala, prompted in his heart by Śambhu, the Supreme Lord who was directing everything, laughing, gladly spoke to Śambhu: ॥6॥
2.3.48.7: Let your gotra be stated, O Śambhu, and your pravara and family likewise, your name, your Veda and your śākhā. Do not let the auspicious time pass. ॥7॥
2.3.48.8: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Himādri, Śaṅkara, though of gracious countenance, at once turned his face away; though not one to be pitied, he came into a pitiable state. ॥8॥
2.3.48.9: When the blessed Maheśa was seen in such a state, with no answer on his face, by the foremost gods, the sages, and likewise the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakṣas and Siddhas, then there, O Nārada, you burst into a hearty laugh. ॥9॥
2.3.48.10: Then, O Nārada, you, knower of Brahman, prompted there inwardly by Śiva, with your mind fixed on Śambhu, played the vīṇā. ॥10॥
2.3.48.11: Then you, wise one, were forcibly restrained by the lord of mountains, and by Viṣṇu, by me, by the gods and by all the sages as well. ॥11॥
2.3.48.12: When you, by Śaṅkara's will, did not stop, then the mountain told you: Do not play the vīṇā now. ॥12॥
2.3.48.13: When you, O wise divine sage, were firmly and forcibly forbidden by him, you, keeping Maheśvara well in mind, replied to that lord of the mountains: ॥13॥
2.3.48.14: Nārada said: You have fallen into delusion and know nothing at all. In what may be said about Maheśa, you are utterly turned away from the truth. ॥14॥
2.3.48.15: Hara himself has been questioned by you about stating his own gotra; at this moment such speech is utterly laughable. ॥15॥
2.3.48.16: O mountain, even Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the others here do not know his gotra, family or name; what then is to be said of others? ॥16॥
2.3.48.17: O mountain, he in a single day of whom a crore of Brahmās has gone to dissolution—that very Śaṅkara is seen by you today through the power of Kālī's austerity. ॥17॥
2.3.48.18: He is formless, the supreme Brahman, without attributes, beyond Prakṛti, shapeless, changeless, the master of Māyā, higher than the highest. ॥18॥
2.3.48.19: He is without gotra, family or name, independent, loving to his devotees; by his own will he becomes endowed with attributes, of fair body, bearing many names. ॥19॥
2.3.48.20: He has a noble gotra yet is without gotra; he is without family yet of noble family. Through Pārvatī's austerity he is today your son-in-law—there is no doubt. ॥20॥
2.3.48.21: By him who sports in play, the whole world, moving and unmoving, is deluded. No one, however wise, knows Śiva, O best of mountains. ॥21॥
2.3.48.22: Who has seen the top of Maheśa in the form of the liṅga? No one. Even Viṣṇu, going down to Pātāla, did not then reach him and was astonished. ॥22॥
2.3.48.23: What need of many words, O best of mountains? Śiva's Māyā is hard to cross; the three worlds are subject to it, and so are Hari, Brahmā and the others. ॥23॥
2.3.48.24: Therefore, O father of Śivā, having reflected carefully and with effort, you should not entertain the slightest doubt here about such a bridegroom. ॥24॥
2.3.48.25: Brahmā said: Having said this, O sage, you, the knowing one, the accomplisher of Śiva's will, spoke again to that lord of mountains, delighting him with your words: ॥25॥
2.3.48.26: Nārada said: Listen to my words, dear great mountain, father of Śivā; having heard them, give your daughter, the goddess, to Śaṅkara. ॥26॥
2.3.48.27: Know that the gotra and family of Maheśa with attributes, who assumes a form in play, is Nāda (primordial sound) alone. ॥27॥
2.3.48.28: Truly Śiva consists of Nāda, and Nāda likewise consists of Śiva; there is no difference between the two, Nāda and Śiva. ॥28॥
2.3.48.29: Because Nāda was the first-born in creation from Śiva, who assumes a form with attributes in play, therefore, O lord of mountains, it is the most excellent of all. ॥29॥
2.3.48.30: That is why, O Himālaya, the vīṇā was played by me today, prompted inwardly by Śaṅkara, the Lord of all. ॥30॥
2.3.48.31: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of yours, O sage, Himādri, the lord of mountains, became satisfied, his mind freed of perplexity. ॥31॥
2.3.48.32: Then Viṣṇu and the others, the gods and likewise the sages, all freed of perplexity, exclaimed: Well said, well said! ॥32॥
2.3.48.33: Understanding the profundity of Maheśvara, all the discerning ones, full of wonder and great joy, said to one another: ॥33॥
2.3.48.34: He by whose command this vast universe came into being, higher than the highest, whose form is his own awareness, Śarva, who moves by his own free will and is reached through supreme devotion—that very lord of the three worlds has today been clearly seen by us. ॥34॥
2.3.48.35: Then those foremost mountains, Meru and the others, agitated, spoke with one voice to Himavān, the lord of mountains: ॥35॥
2.3.48.36: The mountains said: Hold firm now to the giving of your daughter, O lord of mountains. Why ruin your own purpose through further talk? We speak the truth: no deliberation should be made here. Therefore let the daughter be given to the Lord. ॥36॥
2.3.48.37: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of his friends, Himālaya, impelled by Providence, performed the gift of his daughter to Śiva: ॥37॥
2.3.48.38: I give this maiden to you, O Supreme Lord. Accept her as your wife; be gracious, O Lord of all. ॥38॥
2.3.48.39: With this mantra Himācala gave his own daughter Pārvatī, mother of the three worlds, to that great Rudra. ॥39॥
2.3.48.40: Having thus placed Śivā's hand in Śiva's hand, the mountain rejoiced greatly in his mind, having crossed the great ocean of his desire. ॥40॥
2.3.48.41: With a Vedic mantra Giriśa, the Supreme Lord, well pleased, quickly took the lotus-hand of Girijā in his own hand. ॥41॥
2.3.48.42: O sage, touching the earth, Śaṅkara joyfully recited the mantra kāmasya ko'dāt (Who gave this? ... of Kāma), showing the worldly custom. ॥42॥
2.3.48.43: There was a great festival everywhere, bringing delight; shouts of victory arose in heaven, on earth and in the sky. ॥43॥
2.3.48.44: All, exceedingly delighted, cried well done and homage; the Gandharvas sang sweetly with joy and the hosts of Apsarases danced. ॥44॥
2.3.48.45: The citizens of Himācala rejoiced greatly in their hearts; there was indeed great auspiciousness, accompanied by a grand festival. ॥45॥
2.3.48.46: I, Viṣṇu, Śakra, the gods and all the sages became exceedingly delighted, our lotus-faces blooming. ॥46॥
2.3.48.47: Then Himācala, best of mountains, very pleased, gave to Śiva the accompaniments of the gift of the maiden, fully as was proper. ॥47॥
2.3.48.48: Then his kinsmen, having worshipped Śivā with devotion, gave excellent articles to Śiva according to various rites and procedures. ॥48॥
2.3.48.49: Himālaya, with a contented mind, gave there many kinds of articles for the pleasure of Pārvatī and Śiva, O lord of sages. ॥49॥
2.3.48.50: He gave him dowry gifts, various gems, and various vessels made of beautiful jewels. ॥50॥
2.3.48.51: He gave a hundred thousand cows, likewise a hundred caparisoned horses, and a hundred thousand devoted maidservants adorned with fine ornaments. ॥51॥
2.3.48.52: And, O sage, ten million elephants, and likewise chariots inlaid with gold, fashioned of the finest jewels. ॥52॥
2.3.48.53: Thus, having duly given his own daughter Girijā Śivā to Śiva, the Supreme Lord, Himālaya attained fulfilment. ॥53॥
2.3.48.54: Then the best of mountains, with joined palms, joyfully praised the Supreme Lord in noble words with the hymn taught in the Mādhyandina recension. ॥54॥
2.3.48.55: Then, instructed by him who knew the Vedas, the hosts of sages, full of great festivity, performed the anointing of Śivā's head. ॥55॥
2.3.48.56: Pronouncing the name of the deity, they performed the rite of sprinkling around; and then, O sage, there was a great festival producing great bliss. ॥56॥
2.3.48.iti: Thus ends the forty-eighth adhyāya, named The giving away of the bride, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥48॥
2.3.49.1: Brahmā said: Then, at my instruction, the Lord had the fire installed by the brāhmaṇas and, seating Pārvatī on his lap, performed the homa there. ॥1॥
2.3.49.2: Śiva poured oblations into the fire with mantras of the Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma Vedas. Kālī's brother, named Maināka, offered the handful of parched grain. ॥2॥
2.3.49.3: Then Kālī and Śiva, both of them, joyfully and according to rule circumambulated the fire, dear son, also observing the customs of the world. ॥3॥
2.3.49.4: There the Lord of Girijā enacted a wondrous deed. Listen to just that, O divine sage; out of affection for you I shall tell it. ॥4॥
2.3.49.5: At that moment I, deluded by Śiva's māyā, saw the charming moon-like toenail on the Goddess's foot. ॥5॥
2.3.49.6: By the sight of it, O divine sage, I then became possessed by Madana, my mind greatly agitated. ॥6॥
2.3.49.7: Infatuated by Smara, I gazed again and again at her body; then, from that sight, my seed at once fell to the ground. ॥7॥
2.3.49.8: Ashamed at that oozing semen, I, the Grandsire, O sage, crushed what had fallen with my feet, trying to hide it. ॥8॥
2.3.49.9: Knowing this, Mahādeva became exceedingly angry, O Nārada, and at once wished to kill me, Vidhi, infatuated by lust. ॥9॥
2.3.49.10: A great cry of alarm arose there on every side, O Nārada; all the people trembled, and even the sustainer of the universe was struck with fear. ॥10॥
2.3.49.11: Then the immortals headed by Viṣṇu, O sage, praised that Śambhu, who was blazing with wrath and radiance and poised to kill. ॥11॥
2.3.49.12: The gods said: O God of gods, all-pervading one, Supreme Lord, Sadāśiva, Lord of the world, Master of the world, you who consist of the world, be gracious. ॥12॥
2.3.49.13: You are the self, the cause and the ruler of all beings; changeless, imperishable, eternal, beyond distinctions, undecaying, supreme. ॥13॥
2.3.49.14: That from which come the beginning and end of this world, its middle, this and the other, the I and the outside — being imperishable, he is none of these; that truth, Brahman, consciousness, is you. ॥14॥
2.3.49.15: Sages firm in their vows, longing for liberation, abandon attachment on both sides and worship only your lotus feet. ॥15॥
2.3.49.16: You are Brahman — full, immortal, free from sorrow, without qualities, supreme, pure bliss, unperturbed, changeless, without individual self. ॥16॥
2.3.49.17: You are indeed the cause of the arising, sustenance and withdrawal of the universe; in relation to it you are the lord of selves, yet the all-pervading one is ever independent. ॥17॥
2.3.49.18: You alone are the one, the existent and the non-existent, the dual and the non-dual; just as gold, whether worked or unworked, has no difference in substance. ॥18॥
2.3.49.19: Since distinction in you is perceived by people through ignorance, the remedy is only for the delusion; for you, who are free of limiting adjuncts, there is none in yourself. ॥19॥
2.3.49.20: We are blessed, O Maheśāna, merely by seeing you. O Śambhu, giver of bliss to your steadfast devotees, show compassion. ॥20॥
2.3.49.21: You are the beginning and you are beginningless; you are the Person beyond Prakṛti, Lord of the universe, Master of the world, changeless, higher than the highest. ॥21॥
2.3.49.22: This Brahmā, the Grandsire, who through rajas is the form of the universe, and Viṣṇu, the Supreme Person, through sattva, exist by your grace, O Lord. ॥22॥
2.3.49.23: Through tamas you are Kālāgnirudra; yet you are the Supreme Self beyond the guṇas, Sadāśiva, Maheśāna, all-pervading Maheśvara. ॥23॥
2.3.49.24: The manifest, Mahat, the source of elements (ahaṃkāra), the subtle elements and the senses are all presided over by you alone, O Maheśvara whose form is the universe. ॥24॥
2.3.49.25: O Mahādeva, Supreme Lord, mine of compassion, Śaṅkara, be gracious, O Lord of the gods of gods; be gracious, O Supreme Person. ॥25॥
2.3.49.26: The seven oceans are your garments, the directions your mighty arms; heaven is your head, O all-pervading one, the sky your navel, and the wind your nose. ॥26॥
2.3.49.27: Fire, sun and moon are your eyes, the clouds your hair, O Lord; the lunar mansions, stars and the rest, and the planets are your ornaments. ॥27॥
2.3.49.28: How shall I praise you, O Lord of gods, all-pervading Supreme Lord? You are beyond the reach of words, and of the mind too, O Śaṅkara. ॥28॥
2.3.49.29: Salutation to you, the five-faced Rudra, whose forms number five hundred million, lord of the three worlds, most excellent, the very essence of knowledge. ॥29॥
2.3.49.30: Salutations again and again to the indescribable, the eternal, the one with form like a lightning flame, fire-hued, the god Śaṅkara. ॥30॥
2.3.49.31: Salutations again and again to him who abides in this world, having assumed a most beautiful eight-cornered form shining like ten million lightnings. ॥31॥
2.3.49.32: Brahmā said: Hearing their words thus, the Supreme Lord, affectionate to his devotees, was pleased and quickly granted fearlessness to me, Brahmā. ॥32॥
2.3.49.33: Then all the gods there, headed by Viṣṇu, and the sages likewise, broke into smiles, dear son, and held a great celebration. ॥33॥
2.3.49.34: From that semen of mine, dear son, crushed again and again, there arose there a great many particles, exceedingly radiant. ॥34॥
2.3.49.35: From those particles of seed, blazing with their own radiance, many sages were born — the Bālakhilyas, by the thousands. ॥35॥
2.3.49.36: Then all those sages approached me, O sage, with great love, and said: Father, father. ॥36॥
2.3.49.37: Those Bālakhilyas were then addressed there by Nārada, prompted by the Lord's will, with an angry mind. ॥37॥
2.3.49.38: Nārada said: Go together, all of you, to Mount Gandhamādana. You must not stay here, for you have no purpose here. ॥38॥
2.3.49.39: Having performed intense austerity there, you will become lords among sages, disciples of the Sun. This I have told you at Śiva's own command. ॥39॥
2.3.49.40: Brahmā said: Thus addressed, all those Bālakhilyas then bowed to Śaṅkara and swiftly went to Mount Gandhamādana. ॥40॥
2.3.49.41: Then, O lord of sages, I was comforted by Viṣṇu and the others, those great-souled ones impelled by the Supreme Lord, and I became free of fear. ॥41॥
2.3.49.42: And I praised Śaṅkara, the Lord of all, affectionate to his devotees, knowing him to be the accomplisher of all deeds and the remover of the pride of the wicked. ॥42॥
2.3.49.43: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O ocean of compassion, O Lord, you alone are in every way the creator, sustainer and destroyer of all. ॥43॥
2.3.49.44: By your will indeed the whole universe, moving and unmoving, is held in place, like bullocks tied to a rope; this I have come to know especially. ॥44॥
2.3.49.45: Having spoken thus, I, with joined palms, made obeisance; and all the others too, Viṣṇu and the rest, praised that Maheśvara. ॥45॥
2.3.49.46: Then, having heard the pure praise offered by me in humility, and that of Viṣṇu and all the others, Maheśvara became pleased. ॥46॥
2.3.49.47: With a delighted mind he granted me the supreme boon of fearlessness. All attained great happiness, and I, O sage, attained great joy. ॥47॥
2.3.49.iti: Thus ends the forty-ninth adhyāya, named The bewilderment of Vidhi, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥49॥
2.3.50.1: Brahmā said: Then, O Nārada, at Śiva's command, I, together with the hosts of sages, lovingly performed the remaining rites of the marriage of Śiva and Śivā. ॥1॥
2.3.50.2: Then the anointing of their heads took place with reverence; and the brahmins respectfully had them view the pole star (Dhruva). ॥2॥
2.3.50.3: After that came the rite of touching the heart, and, O best of brahmins, the recitation of blessings accompanied by great festivity. ॥3॥
2.3.50.4: At the brahmins' bidding Śambhu placed vermilion on Śivā's head; at that moment Girijā's splendour became wondrous and indescribable. ॥4॥
2.3.50.5: Then, at the brahmins' bidding, the two, seated together on one seat, attained supreme beauty that brought joy to the hearts of devotees. ॥5॥
2.3.50.6: Then, O sage, coming to their own place, the two performers of wondrous sport joyfully partook of the remnant of the oblation at my direction. ॥6॥
2.3.50.7: When the marriage sacrifice had thus been completed according to rule, Lord Śiva gave the full vessel (pūrṇapātra) to me, Brahmā, the maker of the worlds. ॥7॥
2.3.50.8: Then Śambhu duly gave a gift of cows to the officiating teacher, and lovingly gave the great gifts that bestow auspiciousness. ॥8॥
2.3.50.9: Then he gave a hundred gold pieces to each brahmin separately, and to many, crores of gems and various goods in abundance. ॥9॥
2.3.50.10: Then all the immortals and other beings, moving and unmoving, rejoiced greatly at heart, and a loud cry of victory arose. ॥10॥
2.3.50.11: Auspicious sounds and songs rose abundantly on all sides; and the delightful sound of musical instruments arose, increasing everyone's joy. ॥11॥
2.3.50.12: Then Hari, along with me, the gods, the sages and all the others, taking leave of the Mountain with great affection, quickly went to their own places. ॥12॥
2.3.50.13: Then in the Mountain's city the delighted women, bringing the excellent pair Śiva and Śivā, went to the bridal chamber (kuhavara). ॥13॥
2.3.50.14: There those honoured women carried out the worldly customs; then great festivity, bringing delight, spread everywhere. ॥14॥
2.3.50.15: Then those women, bringing the couple, the benefactors of people, to the very divine bed-chamber, joyfully performed the customary rites. ॥15॥
2.3.50.16: Then the women of the lord of mountains' city came near, completed the auspicious rite, and brought the couple into the house. ॥16॥
2.3.50.17: Raising cries of victory, they performed the untying of the knot and other rites, smiling, casting sidelong glances, their bodies thrilled with joy. ॥17॥
2.3.50.18: Entering the bed-chamber, those excellent ladies were entranced, praising their own good fortune as they gazed at the Supreme Lord— ॥18॥
2.3.50.19: —of exceedingly beautiful form and attire, endowed with all loveliness, in fresh youth, captivating the hearts of women, ॥19॥
2.3.50.20: his face bright with a gentle smile, casting sidelong glances, most handsome, wearing very fine garments and adorned with various jewels. ॥20॥
2.3.50.21: Then sixteen celestial women came near, with great eagerness, to see that couple. ॥21॥
2.3.50.22: Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī, Sāvitrī and likewise Jāhnavī, Aditi and Śacī, Lopāmudrā and Arundhatī, ॥22॥
2.3.50.23: Ahalyā, Tulasī, Svāhā, Rohiṇī and Vasundharā, Śatarūpā, Saṃjñā and Rati—these were the celestial women. ॥23॥
2.3.50.24: Charming daughters of gods, of Nāgas, of sages—who is able to count all those who were present there? ॥24॥
2.3.50.25: When they had offered him a jewelled seat, Śiva sat there joyfully; and the goddesses in turn spoke to him sweet words with lovely smiles. ॥25॥
2.3.50.26: Sarasvatī said: O Mahādeva, now you have joyfully obtained Satī, dearer than life. Seeing your beloved's moon-like face, O lover, give up your anguish. ॥26॥
2.3.50.27: O Lord of Time, pass your time in Satī's embrace; there will be no separation for you, for she has taken refuge in you for all time. ॥27॥
2.3.50.28: Lakṣmī said: O Lord of gods, abandon shyness and remain holding Satī to your bosom. What shyness toward her, without whom your life-breaths depart? ॥28॥
2.3.50.29: Sāvitrī said: O Śambhu, having fed Satī, eat quickly yourself; do not be weary. Then, after rinsing your mouth, lovingly give her betel with camphor. ॥29॥
2.3.50.30: Jāhnavī said: Holding her gold-lustred hand, comb the woman's hair; for a loving wife there can be no happiness of a husband's favour greater than this. ॥30॥
2.3.50.31: Aditi said: O Śivā, at the end of the meal, respectfully and with great love give Śambhu water for rinsing his mouth; the love of a married couple is hard to find. ॥31॥
2.3.50.32: Śacī said: You who, for her sake, lamenting and holding Śivā on your chest, wandered ceaselessly in delusion—what shyness can you have toward your beloved? ॥32॥
2.3.50.33: Lopāmudrā said: O Śiva, it is the women's custom: having eaten in the bed-chamber and given betel to Śivā, you should go to bed. ॥33॥
2.3.50.34: Arundhatī said: Satī was given to you through me, persuading Menā, who was unwilling to give her to you; having coaxed her in various ways, you should make delightful love. ॥34॥
2.3.50.35: Ahalyā said: Giving up the state of old age, become very youthful indeed, so that Menā, whose heart is devoted to her daughter, may approve of you. ॥35॥
2.3.50.36: Tulasī said: Satī was abandoned by you; Kāma was formerly burnt by you. How then, O Lord, was Vasiṣṭha now sent to ask for her? ॥36॥
2.3.50.37: Svāhā said: O Mahādeva, stay steady now under the women's words; at a wedding it is the custom for matrons to be bold. ॥37॥
2.3.50.38: Rohiṇī said: O expert in the science of love, fulfil Pārvatī's desire; being yourself a lover, carry her across the ocean of the beloved's longing. ॥38॥
2.3.50.39: The Earth said: O knower of feelings, you know the feelings of women afflicted by love; O Śambhu, such a woman does not always merely cherish her own husband as a lord. ॥39॥
2.3.50.40: Śatarūpā said: One tormented by hunger is not satisfied by eating without divine food; O Śambhu, it is proper to do that by which a woman's satisfaction arises. ॥40॥
2.3.50.41: Saṃjñā said: Quickly and lovingly send Śaṅkara off with Pārvatī, after preparing in a secluded place a jewelled lamp, betel, and a bed. ॥41॥
2.3.50.42: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of the women, Śiva himself, the Lord free from all perturbation, the preceptor of the preceptors of the lords of yogins, spoke to them. ॥42॥
2.3.50.43: Śaṅkara said: O goddesses, do not speak such words in my presence. You are mothers of the worlds and chaste ladies; how can there be such frivolity toward a son? ॥43॥
2.3.50.44: Brahmā said: Hearing Śaṅkara's words, the wives of the gods were ashamed and, out of embarrassment, fell silent like figures in a painting. ॥44॥
2.3.50.45: Having eaten the sweet food and rinsed his mouth, Maheśa, delighted at heart, partook of betel with camphor together with his wife. ॥45॥
2.3.50.iti: Thus ends the fiftieth adhyāya, named The jesting, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥50॥
2.3.51.1: Brahmā said: At that moment Rati, knowing the time to be favourable and greatly pleased, spoke to Śaṅkara, who is tender towards the afflicted. ॥1॥
2.3.51.2: Rati said: By taking Pārvatī as your wife you have obtained extremely rare good fortune. Why then was my lord of life reduced to ashes, though he sought nothing for himself? ॥2॥
2.3.51.3: Revive my husband here; let the working of desire be active in yourself, and remove my anguish caused by separation. ॥3॥
2.3.51.4: At this wedding festival all people are happy; I alone, O Maheśāna, am miserable without my husband. ॥4॥
2.3.51.5: Make me one who has a protector, O god; be gracious, O Śaṅkara. Make your own words come true, O friend of the afflicted, O supreme Lord. ॥5॥
2.3.51.6: Apart from you, who in the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings is able to destroy my grief? Knowing this, show compassion. ॥6॥
2.3.51.7: In this festive wedding of yours, which bestows joy on all, make me too joyful, O Lord, O source of mercy to the afflicted. ॥7॥
2.3.51.8: When my lord is revived, your delightful sport with your beloved Pārvatī will indeed be complete; there is no doubt. ॥8॥
2.3.51.9: You are able to do everything, since you are the supreme Lord. What is the use of many words here, O Lord of all? Quickly revive my husband. ॥9॥
2.3.51.10: Brahmā said: Having said this, she gave him Kāma's ashes tied up in a knotted bundle, and wept before Śambhu, crying, O lord, O lord. ॥10॥
2.3.51.11: Hearing Rati's weeping, the women headed by Sarasvatī—all the goddesses—wept and spoke very piteous words. ॥11॥
2.3.51.12: The goddesses said: You bear the name loving to devotees; you are the friend of the afflicted, a treasure of compassion. Revive Kāma, make Rati joyful again; salutation to you. ॥12॥
2.3.51.13: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of theirs, Maheśvara became pleased; the Lord, an ocean of compassion, quickly cast a merciful glance. ॥13॥
2.3.51.14: By the nectar-like glance of the trident-bearer, Smara came forth from the ashes, with the same form, dress and marks as before, handsome and of wondrous appearance. ॥14॥
2.3.51.15: Seeing her husband of that same form and shape, smiling, with bow and arrows, Rati bowed to Maheśvara. ॥15॥
2.3.51.16: She became fulfilled, and with joined palms, together with her revived husband, she praised again and again the god Śiva, who had given back her lord of life. ॥16॥
2.3.51.17: Hearing the praise of Kāma together with his wife, Śaṅkara became exceedingly pleased and, his mind moist with compassion, spoke. ॥17॥
2.3.51.18: Śaṅkara said: I am pleased with your praise, O mind-born one, offered together with your wife. O self-born one, name a boon; whatever you wish, I shall give you. ॥18॥
2.3.51.19: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Śambhu, Smara, filled with great joy, then spoke with joined palms, humbly, in a voice choked with emotion. ॥19॥
2.3.51.20: Kāma said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, ocean of compassion, O Lord, if you are pleased, O Lord of all, be the giver of joy to me. ॥20॥
2.3.51.21: Forgive the offence that I committed before, O Lord. Grant me supreme affection for your own people and devotion to your feet. ॥21॥
2.3.51.22: Brahmā said: Hearing Smara's words, the supreme Lord, a treasure of compassion, was pleased; saying Om, he smiled and spoke to him. ॥22॥
2.3.51.23: Īśvara said: O Kāma, I am pleased; abandon fear, O wise one. Go near Viṣṇu and stay in the place outside. ॥23॥
2.3.51.24: Brahmā said: Hearing that, he bowed his head, circumambulated the all-pervading Lord while praising him, went outside, saluted Hari and the gods, and attended upon them. ॥24॥
2.3.51.25: The gods, having conversed with Kāma, gave him auspicious blessings; Viṣṇu and the others, pleased, spoke while remembering Śiva in their hearts. ॥25॥
2.3.51.26: The gods said: Blessed are you, Smara: burnt by Śiva, yet favoured by him. The Lord of all has revived you with his compassionate glance born of his sattva portion. ॥26॥
2.3.51.27: There is no other giver of happiness and sorrow, since a person experiences the fruit of his own deeds. Protection, marriage and conception at their appointed time—by whom can they be prevented? ॥27॥
2.3.51.28: Brahmā said: Having said this and honoured him, the immortals, Viṣṇu and the rest, all with their wishes fulfilled, then remained there happily. ॥28॥
2.3.51.29: He too, delighted, dwelt there by Śiva's command. Cries of victory, salutation and excellent arose. ॥29॥
2.3.51.30: Then Śambhu, in the bridal chamber, seated Pārvatī on his left and fed her sweet food, and she, full of joy, fed him too. ॥30॥
2.3.51.31: Then Śambhu, following worldly custom, having performed the rites there, took leave of Menā and the Mountain and went to the lodging of the bridegroom's party. ॥31॥
2.3.51.32: Then there was a great festival and the sound of the Vedas arose, O sage; and people played the four kinds of musical instruments. ॥32॥
2.3.51.33: Śambhu, having come to his own place, then saluted the sages, Hari and me, according to worldly custom, and was saluted by the gods and others. ॥33॥
2.3.51.34: Then arose the cry of victory and likewise salutation, and the auspicious sound of the Vedas that shatters all obstacles. ॥34॥
2.3.51.35: Then Viṣṇu, I, Śakra, all the gods with the sages, the Siddhas, the Upasuras and the Nāgas praised him each separately. ॥35॥
2.3.51.36: The gods said: Victory to you, Śambhu, support of all! Victory indeed, Maheśvara! Victory, Rudra, Mahādeva! Victory, O Lord, sustainer of the universe! ॥36॥
2.3.51.37: Victory, O husband of Kālī, O master! Victory, O increaser of bliss! Victory, Tryambaka, Lord of all! Victory, O all-pervading Lord of Māyā! ॥37॥
2.3.51.38: Victory, O attributeless, desireless one, beyond causes, all-pervading! Victory, O support of all through your sport, who have assumed form; salutation to you. ॥38॥
2.3.51.39: Victory, O Lord who grants the good desires of your devotees, O source of compassion! Victory, O you whose form is being and bliss! Victory, O you who take form through the guṇas of Māyā! ॥39॥
2.3.51.40: Victory to you, O fierce one, O gracious one (Mṛḍa), O Self of all, O friend of the afflicted, O treasure-house of compassion! Victory to you, O changeless one, O lord of Māyā, whose form is beyond speech and mind! ॥40॥
2.3.51.41: Brahmā said: Having thus praised the great lord, the master, the consort of Girijā, Viṣṇu and the others served him with supreme affection, as was fitting. ॥41॥
2.3.51.42: Then Śambhu, the great lord, the Īśvara who had assumed a body in play, bestowed honour and boons upon all of them there, O Nārada. ॥42॥
2.3.51.43: All of them, Viṣṇu and the others, O dear one, having received the command of the supreme lord, greatly delighted, with cheerful faces and honoured, went to their own abodes. ॥43॥
2.3.51.iti: Thus ends the fifty-first adhyāya, named The revival of Kāma, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥51॥
2.3.52.1: Brahmā said: Then, dear child, Himavat, the best of mountains, most fortunate of all and wise, arranged the courtyard for the feast. ॥1॥
2.3.52.2: He had it properly swept and plastered, and he respectfully adorned it with fragrances and various articles. ॥2॥
2.3.52.3: Then the Mountain, through his sons and other mountains as well, invited all the gods, together with the Lord, and others too, to the feast. ॥3॥
2.3.52.4: Hearing the Mountain's invitation, O sage, the Lord, with Acyuta (Viṣṇu) and all the gods and others, joyfully went there for the meal. ॥4॥
2.3.52.5: The Mountain, having duly honoured the Lord and all of them according to rule, joyfully seated them on fine seats inside the house. ॥5॥
2.3.52.6: Having served many excellent dishes, he then, with folded hands, made a humble request that they begin the meal. ॥6॥
2.3.52.7: Then the gods, led by Viṣṇu, thus honoured there, placing Sadāśiva at their head, all ate. ॥7॥
2.3.52.8: Then all of them, gathered together at once in every way, sitting in rows, ate, laughing, each group separately. ॥8॥
2.3.52.9: Nandin, Bhṛṅgin, Vīrabhadra and Vīrabhadra's attendants ate separately — those illustrious ones, full of merriment. ॥9॥
2.3.52.10: The gods with Indra, and the guardians of the worlds, resplendent in many ways, those illustrious ones ate amid many kinds of humour. ॥10॥
2.3.52.11: All the sages, brahmins and seers headed by Bhṛgu likewise all ate with delight, seated then in separate rows. ॥11॥
2.3.52.12: Likewise all Caṇḍī's attendants ate and finished their meal, joyfully making merry and cracking many jokes. ॥12॥
2.3.52.13: Thus, having eaten and rinsed their mouths, all of them, Viṣṇu and the rest, full of joy, gladly went each to his own lodging to rest. ॥13॥
2.3.52.14: At Menā's bidding, the virtuous women devoutly entreated Śiva and lodged him in the house called the bridal chamber (vāsa), amid great festivity. ॥14॥
2.3.52.15: Śambhu, seated on the charming jewelled throne given by Menā, joyfully beheld the bridal chamber. ॥15॥
2.3.52.16: It was lit up splendidly by hundreds of blazing jewelled lamps, filled with jewelled vessels and jars, and gleaming with pearls and gems, ॥16॥
2.3.52.17: rich in the beauty of jewelled mirrors, adorned with white chowries, festooned with fine garlands of pearls and gems, supremely opulent, ॥17॥
2.3.52.18: incomparable, greatly divine, wondrous, most charming, delighting the mind, its spaces laid out in many designs, ॥18॥
2.3.52.19: displaying the unequalled, supreme power of the boon granted by Śiva, radiant, and bearing the name Śivaloka, ॥19॥
2.3.52.20: perfumed with many fragrant substances, brilliantly bright, furnished with sandal and aguru, and provided with a bed of flowers, ॥20॥
2.3.52.21: rich with many wondrous paintings, built by Viśvakarman, and studded with excellent ornaments made of the finest gems. ॥21॥
2.3.52.22: In one place was depicted the most charming Vaikuṇṭha, fashioned by the gods; in another, Brahmaloka; elsewhere, the city of the world-guardians; ॥22॥
2.3.52.23: in one place lovely Kailāsa, in another Śakra's (Indra's) palace, and in another Śivaloka, shining above all. ॥23॥
2.3.52.24: Seeing the whole house, such a marvel, Maheśvara praised the lord of the snowy mountains and was greatly pleased. ॥24॥
2.3.52.25: There, on a most delightful, excellent jewelled couch, the Supreme Lord joyfully lay down in sport. ॥25॥
2.3.52.26: Himācala fed all his own kinsmen completely, and all the others too with great affection, and attended to the remaining duties. ॥26॥
2.3.52.27: While the lord of mountains was thus occupied and the beloved Lord slept, the whole night passed and morning came. ॥27॥
2.3.52.28: Then at daybreak the people, full of resolve and enthusiasm, played many kinds of musical instruments. ॥28॥
2.3.52.29: All the gods, Viṣṇu and the rest, rose up in great joy; remembering their beloved Lord of the gods, they made themselves ready in haste. ॥29॥
2.3.52.30: Having readied their own vehicles, eager to go to Kailāsa, they sent Dharma to Śiva. ॥30॥
2.3.52.31: Then Dharma, the yogin, coming to the bridal chamber at Nārāyaṇa's command, spoke words fitting the occasion to Śaṅkara, the lord of yogins. ॥31॥
2.3.52.32: Dharma said: Arise, arise. May it be well with you, O Bhava, our lord of the Pramathas. Come to the guests' lodging and make them there fulfilled. ॥32॥
2.3.52.33: Brahmā said: Hearing Dharma's words, Maheśvara laughed, looked on him with a compassionate glance, and left his bed. ॥33॥
2.3.52.34: Laughing, he said to Dharma: You go ahead there; I too shall come very soon, no doubt. ॥34॥
2.3.52.35: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by Śaṅkara, he went to the guests' lodging; and Lord Śambhu himself also intended to go there. ॥35॥
2.3.52.36: Learning of this, the group of women came there in great festivity and sang auspicious songs, gazing at Śambhu's two feet. ॥36॥
2.3.52.37: Then Śambhu, following worldly custom, performed his morning rites, took leave of Menā and the Mountain, and went to the guests' lodging. ॥37॥
2.3.52.38: Then there was a great festival; the sound of the Vedas arose, O sage, and the people played instruments of the four kinds. ॥38॥
2.3.52.39: Śambhu, reaching his own quarters, then saluted the sages, and, following worldly custom, Hari and me; and he was saluted by the gods and others. ॥39॥
2.3.52.40: Then arose cries of victory and likewise cries of salutation; the auspicious sound of the Vedas too, and a great tumult arose. ॥40॥
2.3.52.iti: Thus ends the fifty-second adhyāya, named The feast of the bridegroom's party and Śiva's sleep, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥52॥
2.3.53.1: Brahmā said: Then the gods headed by Viṣṇu, and the sages rich in austerity, having performed their obligatory rites, made preparations for the departure from the mountain's city. ॥1॥
2.3.53.2: Then the best of mountains, having bathed and carefully worshipped his chosen deity, summoned the citizens and kinsmen and joyfully went to the guests' lodging. ॥2॥
2.3.53.3: There, having worshipped the Lord, he joyfully made an earnest request: Stay for some days in my house together with everyone. ॥3॥
2.3.53.4: O Śambhu, by the sight of you I am fulfilled, there is no doubt; and blessed am I, into whose house you have come with the gods. ॥4॥
2.3.53.5: Brahmā said: Having spoken much in this way, the lord of mountains, with joined palms and bowing, invited the Lord together with Viṣṇu, the gods and the others. ॥5॥
2.3.53.6: Then the sages and gods, having mentally consulted together with Śiva, delighted, replied respectfully, along with Viṣṇu, the gods and the rest. ॥6॥
2.3.53.7: The gods said: Blessed are you, O tiger among mountains; your fame is very great. In the three worlds there is no one equal to you, no person more meritorious. ॥7॥
2.3.53.8: At whose door Maheśāna, the supreme Brahman, the refuge of the good, loving to his devotees, has come out of compassion together with his attendants. ॥8॥
2.3.53.9: The lodging is very delightful, and varied honour has been shown; and the dishes are unprecedented, beyond description, O lord of mountains. ॥9॥
2.3.53.10: Surely there is nothing to wonder at where the goddess Śivā Ambikā dwells; everything is complete without remainder, and we are blessed that we have come. ॥10॥
2.3.53.11: Brahmā said: Thus there was excellent mutual praise there; a festival of many kinds arose, with sounds of Vedic chanting, well done and victory. ॥11॥
2.3.53.12: There was auspicious singing, and the troop of Apsarases danced; the bards (Māgadhas) and others sang praises, and gifts of wealth were given in abundance. ॥12॥
2.3.53.13: Then, having invited the lord of gods, the mountain went to his own house and began the festive feast according to various prescribed procedures. ॥13॥
2.3.53.14: For the meal he lovingly and fittingly brought the Lord, Īśvara, together with his retinue, amid great excitement. ॥14॥
2.3.53.15: Having washed with great reverence the feet of Śambhu, of Viṣṇu and of me, and duly those of all the immortals and the sages, ॥15॥
2.3.53.16: and of the others who had come, the lord of mountains, accompanied by his kinsmen, seated each of them with great affection inside the pavilion. ॥16॥
2.3.53.17: The mountain satisfied them with delicious and varied foods; all of them ate, together with Śambhu, Viṣṇu and me. ॥17॥
2.3.53.18: At that time the women of the city joyfully sang teasing abuse-songs, laughing with gentle voices and gazing intently at them. ॥18॥
2.3.53.19: Having eaten and duly rinsed their mouths, and taken leave of the mountain, O Nārada, they all went to their own quarters, delighted and fully satisfied. ॥19॥
2.3.53.20: Thus on the third day too, O sage, they were duly honoured by the lord of mountains with gifts, honours, respect and the like. ॥20॥
2.3.53.21: When the fourth day arrived, the Caturthī rite was duly performed with purity—without which that marriage remains incomplete. ॥21॥
2.3.53.22: There was a festival of many kinds with cries of well done and victory, abundant gifts, fine singing, and dancing of various kinds as well. ॥22॥
2.3.53.23: When the fifth day came, all the gods, full of joy, with great affection made a request to the mountain regarding their departure. ॥23॥
2.3.53.24: Hearing that, the lord of mountains, with joined palms, said to the gods: Let the gods stay some more days and show me grace. ॥24॥
2.3.53.25: Having said this, out of affection he made them—the Lord, Viṣṇu, me and the others—stay for many days, always with great respect. ॥25॥
2.3.53.26: Thus many days passed for them as they dwelt there; then the gods sent the seven sages to the lord of mountains. ॥26॥
2.3.53.27: They counselled him and Menā as befitted the occasion, and joyfully, duly praising, explained the supreme truth of Śiva. ॥27॥
2.3.53.28: Through their various counsels, O sage, it was accepted by the lord of mountains; and Śambhu, with the gods and others, went to the lord of mountains to take leave for the journey. ॥28॥
2.3.53.29: As Śiva, the lord of gods, accompanied by the gods, was setting out for his own mountain, Menā wept loudly and spoke to that treasure of compassion. ॥29॥
2.3.53.30: Menā said: O treasure of compassion, showing compassion, you will cherish Śivā; being easily pleased, you will forgive Pārvatī's thousand faults. ॥30॥
2.3.53.31: My child has been devoted to your lotus feet birth after birth; in dream or in waking awareness she has no remembrance of anything but the Lord Mahādeva. ॥31॥
2.3.53.32: Merely on hearing of devotion to you she is filled with tears of joy and thrilling of the hair; at slander of you she becomes silent, as if dead, O Mṛtyuñjaya. ॥32॥
2.3.53.33: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, Menakā then entrusted her own daughter to him, and weeping very loudly, fainted before the two of them. ॥33॥
2.3.53.34: Then, having consoled Menā and taken leave of her and likewise of the mountain, Śiva set out on the journey with the gods, amid a great festival. ॥34॥
2.3.53.35: Then all the immortals, with the Lord and his own Gaṇas, silently set out on the journey toward the mountain, keeping Śiva in mind. ॥35॥
2.3.53.36: In a garden outside the city of Himācala the delighted gods, together with the Lord and in festive mood, halted and awaited the coming of Śivā. ॥36॥
2.3.53.37: Thus has been told Śiva's auspicious journey with the gods, O lord of sages; now hear of Śivā's journey, attended by the festivity mingled with separation. ॥37॥
2.3.53.iti: Thus ends the fifty-third adhyāya, named Śiva's journey, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥53॥
2.3.54.1: Brahmā said: Then those Seven Sages said to the lord of the Himālaya mountain: O mountain, have the departure of your daughter, the goddess, carried out today, as is fitting. ॥1॥
2.3.54.2: Hearing this, the lord of the mountains, realising the great separation from her that was coming, became dejected for some time out of his great love, O lord of sages. ॥2॥
2.3.54.3: After some time the king of mountains regained his composure; then, saying in words, so be it, he gave the message to Menā. ॥3॥
2.3.54.4: Hearing the mountain's message, O sage, Menā, overcome by joy and sorrow, made arrangements for the send-off and became ready to carry it out. ॥4॥
2.3.54.5: O sage, Menā, beloved of the mountain, duly performed the customs of the Vedas and of her own family, and held various festivities there. ॥5॥
2.3.54.6: She adorned Girijā with excellent garments set with various jewels, with the twelve ornaments, and with adornments befitting royalty. ॥6॥
2.3.54.7: Understanding Menā's wish, a certain virtuous brahmin lady instructed Girijā in the supreme vow of wifely devotion. ॥7॥
2.3.54.8: The brahmin's wife said: O Girijā, listen with good will to my words, which increase righteousness, bring joy here and hereafter, and give happiness to those who hear them. ॥8॥
2.3.54.9: Blessed is the woman devoted to her husband; no other is so especially worthy of honour. She purifies all the worlds and destroys the mass of all sins. ॥9॥
2.3.54.10: She who serves her husband with love as if he were the Supreme Lord, O Śivā, enjoys all pleasures here and at the end attains the auspicious goal together with her husband. ॥10॥
2.3.54.11: Devoted wives were Sāvitrī, Lopāmudrā, Arundhatī, Śāṇḍilyā, Śatarūpā, Anasūyā, Lakṣmī, Svadhā, Satī, ॥11॥
2.3.54.12: Saṃjñā, Sumati, Śraddhā, Menā and likewise Svāhā; and many other virtuous women too, who are not mentioned for fear of prolixity. ॥12॥
2.3.54.13: Through the virtue of wifely devotion alone they attained universal honour, and became revered even by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Hara and the great sages. ॥13॥
