2.3.54.14: Therefore your husband, Lord Śaṅkara, should always be served by you; he bestows grace on the afflicted, is to be served by all, and is the refuge of the good. ॥14॥
2.3.54.15: Great is the dharma of the devoted wife, enjoined in the Śrutis and Smṛtis. As this is described as the best, certainly no other is equal to it. ॥15॥
2.3.54.16: Intent on wifely devotion, she should eat after her beloved husband has eaten; O Śivā, O virtuous one, the woman should stand when he is standing, in every way. ॥16॥
2.3.54.17: She should always sleep when he sleeps, but the wise one should wake first. Guileless in conduct, the beloved should always do what is good for him. ॥17॥
2.3.54.18: O Śivā, she should never show herself to him unadorned; when he has gone abroad on business, she should remain without ornaments. ॥18॥
2.3.54.19: A devoted wife should never utter her husband's name; even when scolded she should not scold back, and even when struck she should remain gracious. She should say: Let me be struck, O master, but show me mercy. ॥19॥
2.3.54.20: When called, she should leave her household tasks and go quickly to him, with joined palms, lovingly; bowing deeply, she should say thus: ॥20॥
2.3.54.21: For what purpose have I been called, O lord? Let that favour be shown to me. Then, as instructed by him, she should do the task with a cheerful mind. ॥21॥
2.3.54.22: She should not stand long at the door, nor go to another's house; taking anything whatsoever of his, she should never give it to anyone. ॥22॥
2.3.54.23: Without being told, she should herself prepare all the requisites for worship, awaiting the occasion and doing what is beneficial and suited to the time. ॥23॥
2.3.54.24: She should never go on a pilgrimage without her husband's permission; she should keep far away from watching social gatherings and festivals. ॥24॥
2.3.54.25: A woman who desires the merit of holy places should drink the water of her husband's feet; in it are all the holy places and sacred sites, there is no doubt. ॥25॥
2.3.54.26: The devoted wife should eat her husband's leftovers, whatever food and the like is pleasing, given by her husband, calling it great prasāda. ॥26॥
2.3.54.27: She should not eat without sharing among gods, ancestors and guests, among the servants, cows and groups of mendicants. ॥27॥
2.3.54.28: With household goods well kept, skilful, cheerful, averse to extravagance, that lady should always be devoted to the vow of wifely loyalty. ॥28॥
2.3.54.29: Without her husband's permission she should not undertake fasts, vows and the like; otherwise they bear no fruit, and she goes to hell in the next world. ॥29॥
2.3.54.30: She should never rouse her husband when he is comfortably seated at ease or enjoying himself as he pleases, even for household matters. ॥30॥
2.3.54.31: Whether her husband is impotent, in bad circumstances, sick or old, happy or unhappy, she should not transgress her one husband. ॥31॥
2.3.54.32: During her menses, for three nights she should not show her face, nor let her voice be heard, until she is purified by bathing. ॥32॥
2.3.54.33: Having bathed well, she should look at her husband's face and never at another's; or else, meditating on her husband in her mind, she should look at the sun. ॥33॥
2.3.54.34: Turmeric, kuṅkuma, vermilion, collyrium and the like, the bodice, betel, the auspicious ornaments and so on, ॥34॥
2.3.54.35: the dressing of the hair, the braid, and ornaments of the hands, ears and so on—a devoted wife who desires long life for her husband should not set these aside. ॥35॥
2.3.54.36: She should never make friends with a washerwoman, an unchaste woman, a female ascetic, or an ill-fated woman. ॥36॥
2.3.54.37: She should never converse with a woman who hates her husband. She should never stay alone anywhere, nor ever bathe naked. ॥37॥
2.3.54.38: A chaste woman should never sit on a mortar, a pestle, a broom, a grinding stone, a mill, or the threshold. ॥38॥
2.3.54.39: Except at the time of intimacy she should never behave boldly; wherever her husband's liking lies, there she should be loving. ॥39॥
2.3.54.40: She should be joyful when he is joyful and dejected when her beloved's face is dejected. O Devī, the beloved wife should be devoted to her husband (pativratā), always seeking her husband's welfare. ॥40॥
2.3.54.41: The virtuous woman should remain the same in prosperity and in adversity. Holding firm to fortitude, she should never let herself be thrown out of balance. ॥41॥
2.3.54.42: Even when ghee, salt, oil and the like have run out, the devoted wife should not tell her husband there is none; she should not burden him with troubles. ॥42॥
2.3.54.43: For a devoted wife, her husband alone is held to be greater than Brahmā, Viṣṇu or even Hara. O Queen of the gods, her own husband is indeed Śiva. ॥43॥
2.3.54.44: She who undertakes vows, fasts and observances in disregard of her husband takes away her husband's lifespan, and after death goes to hell. ॥44॥
2.3.54.45: The woman who, when spoken to, answers back, given to anger, is reborn as a bitch in a village or a she-jackal in a desolate forest. ॥45॥
2.3.54.46: A woman should not occupy a high seat, nor go near wicked people, nor ever speak words of distress to her husband. ॥46॥
2.3.54.47: She should not speak slander; she should keep far away from quarrels. In the presence of elders she should never speak loudly nor laugh. ॥47॥
2.3.54.48: Seeing her husband coming from outside, with promptly offered food, water and refreshments, with betel, with garments, and with massaging of his feet and the like, ॥48॥
2.3.54.49: and likewise with sweet words and other excellent means of removing fatigue — she who, herself pleased, gladdens her beloved, by her the three worlds are gladdened. ॥49॥
2.3.54.50: A father gives in measure, a brother gives in measure, a son gives in measure; she should always honour her husband, who is the giver of the immeasurable. ॥50॥
2.3.54.51: The husband is her god, the husband is her guru, he is her dharma, holy places and vows. Therefore, abandoning all else, she should worship her husband alone. ॥51॥
2.3.54.52: The evil-minded woman who abandons her husband and roams about in secret is reborn as a cruel owl, dwelling in the hollow of a tree. ॥52॥
2.3.54.53: If, when struck, she wishes to strike back, she becomes a tigress or a she-cat; she who casts side-glances at another man becomes squint-eyed. ॥53॥
2.3.54.54: She who, leaving out her husband, eats sweet food by herself becomes a sow in the village, or else a bat that eats its own excrement. ॥54॥
2.3.54.55: She who addresses her beloved disrespectfully with tu (you) is surely born mute; she who is always jealous of a co-wife is ill-fated again and again. ॥55॥
2.3.54.56: She who, evading her husband's gaze, looks at some other man is born one-eyed, with a turned-away face, and ugly. ॥56॥
2.3.54.57: Just as a body devoid of life becomes impure in a moment, so a woman devoid of her husband is always impure, even when well bathed. ॥57॥
2.3.54.58: Blessed in the world is that mother, blessed is that father who begot her, and blessed is that husband in whose home there is a noble devoted wife. ॥58॥
2.3.54.59: Three generations each of the father's line, the mother's line and the husband's line enjoy happiness in heaven through the merit of a devoted wife. ॥59॥
2.3.54.60: Women of bad conduct, through breach of virtue, cause the three families — of father, mother and husband — to fall, and they suffer both here and hereafter. ॥60॥
2.3.54.61: Wherever the foot of a devoted wife touches the ground, there that ground becomes destructive of sin and highly purifying. ॥61॥
2.3.54.62: Even the mighty Sun makes contact with a devoted wife, as do the Moon and the Wind, for their own purification and for no other reason. ॥62॥
2.3.54.63: The waters always long for the touch of a devoted wife, thinking: Today the destruction of our coldness has come about; today we are purifiers of others. ॥63॥
2.3.54.64: The wife is the root of the householder; the wife is the root of happiness; the wife is for attaining the fruit of dharma; the wife is for the increase of progeny. ॥64॥
2.3.54.65: Are there not in every house women proud of their beauty and charm? But a devoted wife is obtained only through devotion to the Lord of the universe. ॥65॥
2.3.54.66: The other world and this world — both are won through a wife. A man without a wife is not entitled to rites such as worship of the gods, ancestors and guests. ॥66॥
2.3.54.67: He alone should be known as a true householder in whose home there is a devoted wife; others are devoured day by day, as if by the demoness Old Age. ॥67॥
2.3.54.68: Just as the body becomes pure by bathing in the Gaṅgā, so by seeing a devoted wife everything becomes pure. ॥68॥
2.3.54.69: There is no difference between the Gaṅgā and the woman for whom her husband is her deity. Such a couple are directly equal to Umā and Śiva; therefore the wise should worship them both. ॥69॥
2.3.54.70: The husband is the Praṇava (Om), the wife is the Veda; she is forbearance, he is austerity itself; the husband is the fruit, she is the good deed. Blessed, O Śivā, is such a couple. ॥70॥
2.3.54.71: Thus, O daughter of the king of mountains, the dharma of the devoted wife has been described to you. Now hear from me, with great delight and attention, its divisions. ॥71॥
2.3.54.72: O Devī, devoted wives are said to be of four kinds, distinguished as the best and so on; they remove the sins of those who remember them. ॥72॥
2.3.54.73: The best, the middling, the inferior and the very inferior — I shall tell their characteristics; listen attentively. ॥73॥
2.3.54.74: She whose mind, even in dreams, always sees only her own husband and never another man, O gentle one, is declared the best. ॥74॥
2.3.54.75: She who with a pure mind looks upon another man as a father, brother or son is called the middling devoted wife, O daughter of the mountain. ॥75॥
2.3.54.76: She who, understanding her own dharma in her mind, does not commit infidelity is called the inferior one, yet she is of good conduct, O Pārvatī. ॥76॥
2.3.54.77: She who refrains from infidelity out of fear of her husband and of the family is called the lowest devoted wife by the sages of old. ॥77॥
2.3.54.78: O Śivā, all four kinds of devoted wives destroy sin; they purify all the worlds and are joyful both here and hereafter. ॥78॥
2.3.54.79: Through the power of her wifely devotion, the wife of Atri, at the request of the three gods, brought back to life a certain brāhmaṇa who had died through the curse of Vārāha. ॥79॥
2.3.54.80: Knowing this, O Śivā, O daughter of the mountain, you should always serve your husband with love, for this service always bestows all desires. ॥80॥
2.3.54.81: You are the Mother of the world, the great Goddess, and Śiva himself is your husband. Indeed, by remembering you women become devoted to their husbands. ॥81॥
2.3.54.82: O Goddess, what purpose is there in telling this before you? Still, O Śivā, I have told it today in keeping with the custom of the world. ॥82॥
2.3.54.83: Brahmā said: Having said this and bowed deeply to Śivā, that Brahmin woman fell silent. Pārvatī, beloved of Śaṅkara, attained great joy. ॥83॥
2.3.54.iti: Thus ends the fifty-fourth adhyāya, named The dharma of a devoted wife, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥54॥
2.3.55.1: Brahmā said: Then that Brahmin woman, having taught the goddess that vow, addressed Menā and said: Arrange her departure. ॥1॥
2.3.55.2: Saying, so be it, she became overwhelmed by love. Gathering her composure, she called Kālī, distressed at the pain of separation. ॥2॥
2.3.55.3: Embracing her again and again, she wept very loudly. Pārvatī too wept loudly, uttering words of tenderness. ॥3॥
2.3.55.4: The mountain's beloved Menā and Śivā too, afflicted by grief, fell into a swoon; and at Pārvatī's weeping the wives of the gods also swooned. ॥4॥
2.3.55.5: All the women wept; everything became senseless. The lord of yogins himself wept as he was going — what other lord could be higher? ॥5॥
2.3.55.6: Meanwhile Himālaya quickly came there, with all his sons, his ministers and eminent Brahmins. ॥6॥
2.3.55.7: He himself wept out of affection, holding his darling child to his breast, crying again and again, where are you going, and feeling everything empty. ॥7॥
2.3.55.8: Then the family priest, most wise, together with the Brahmins, compassionately comforted everyone gently with spiritual knowledge. ॥8॥
2.3.55.9: Pārvatī bowed with devotion to her mother, father and preceptor; the Great Māyā, following worldly custom, wept loudly again and again. ॥9॥
2.3.55.10: At Pārvatī's very weeping all the women wept — above all her mother Menā, and likewise her female kin and brothers. ॥10॥
2.3.55.11: Again and again Śivā's mother, the kinswomen and other women, the brothers and the father, bound by affection, wept out of love. ॥11॥
2.3.55.12: Then the Brahmins came and respectfully consoled them, and announced the auspicious moment for the journey, supremely favourable. ॥12॥
2.3.55.13: Then Himālaya, having steadied Menā and himself with discernment, had a palanquin brought for Śivā to mount. ॥13॥
2.3.55.14: The Brahmin women seated Śivā in it; and all of them, the father, mother and the Brahmins likewise, gave her blessings. ॥14॥
2.3.55.15: Menā and the mountain gave her the requisites befitting a great queen, and a heap of various auspicious goods hard for others to obtain. ॥15॥
2.3.55.16: Śivā, having bowed to all her elders, to her father and mother, to the Brahmins, the family priest, the kinswomen and other women, departed, O sage. ॥16॥
2.3.55.17: The wise Himācala too, moved by affection, went along with his sons, and arrived where the Lord was with the gods, bearing delight. ॥17॥
2.3.55.18: All rejoiced lovingly amid a great festival; they bowed to the Lord with devotion and, praising him, entered the city. ॥18॥
2.3.55.19: Śiva said: I remind you, who remember your former births — if you remember, tell me. O queen of the gods, in my play you are ever dear to me as my life. ॥19॥
2.3.55.20: Brahmā said: Hearing this from Maheśa, her own lord, Pārvatī — the chaste one, ever dear to Śaṅkara — spoke with a smile. ॥20॥
2.3.55.21: Pārvatī said: I remember everything, O lord of my life; be silent about it. Now quickly do what befits the occasion. Salutation to you. ॥21॥
2.3.55.22: Brahmā said: Hearing his beloved's words, like a hundred streams of nectar, the Lord of the universe, intent on worldly custom, rejoiced greatly. ॥22॥
2.3.55.23: Śiva, having gathered provisions, fed the gods headed by Nārāyaṇa with many delightful things. ॥23॥
2.3.55.24: Likewise the Lord lovingly fed all the others who had come to his wedding with tasty food of many kinds. ॥24॥
2.3.55.25: Then, having eaten, all those gods, adorned with various jewels, with their wives and attendants, bowed to the moon-crested Śiva. ॥25॥
2.3.55.26: Having praised him with pleasing words and circumambulated him, full of joy and praising the wedding, they then went to their own abodes. ॥26॥
2.3.55.27: O sage, Śiva himself, adopting worldly custom, bowed to Nārāyaṇa and to me, just as Viṣṇu bows to Kaśyapa. ॥27॥
2.3.55.28: I embraced him and gave him my blessing; then, before Śiva, regarding him as the supreme Brahman, I offered an excellent hymn of praise. ॥28॥
2.3.55.29: Taking leave of him, Viṣṇu together with me, with folded hands before Śiva and Śivā, joyfully praising their wedding, went to his own supreme abode. ॥29॥
2.3.55.30: Śiva too stayed on his own mountain, sporting joyfully with Pārvatī; all the Gaṇas, worshipping the divine pair, attained great happiness. ॥30॥
2.3.55.31: Thus, dear one, has the most auspicious wedding of Śiva been narrated: it destroys grief, brings joy, prolongs life and increases wealth. ॥31॥
2.3.55.32: Whoever, pure and with mind fixed on it, listens to this regularly, or recites it to others with discipline, would attain Śiva's world. ॥32॥
2.3.55.33: This wondrous narrative that has been told is an abode of auspiciousness, allaying all obstacles and destroying all diseases. ॥33॥
2.3.55.34: It brings fame, heaven and long life, supremely grants sons and grandsons, bestows all desires here, and always gives enjoyment and liberation. ॥34॥
2.3.55.35: It averts untimely death, brings great peace, is auspicious, removes all bad dreams, and is a means to intelligence, wisdom and the like. ॥35॥
2.3.55.36: At all festivals of Śiva it should be recited with care and love by people desiring good, for it is a cause of Śiva's satisfaction. ॥36॥
2.3.55.37: One should recite it especially at the time of installing images of gods and others, and with great delight at the beginning of every undertaking connected with Śiva. ॥37॥
2.3.55.38: Or, having become pure, one should listen to the auspicious story of Śiva and Śivā; all undertakings succeed — truly, truly, without doubt. ॥38॥
2.3.55.iti: Thus ends the fifty-fifth adhyāya, named Śiva goes to Kailāsa, in the third khaṇḍa, the Pārvatī-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥55॥
